The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield exceed 4.75% at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late July 2025, the 10-year Treasury yield was at 4.360%, down from a 52-week high of 4.802% on January 13, 2025, but still significantly above its 2025 closing low of 3.992% on April 4, 2025 (Morningstar, 2025). By mid-June 2025, the yield was around 4.43%, trading at a premium of roughly 70–71 basis points above its estimated 'fair value' of 3.72%, reflecting persistent market uncertainty about inflation, fiscal policy, and the impact of tariffs (Seeking Alpha, 2025; Investing.com, 2025). Market participants, including strategists from JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, have increasingly priced in the risk of a yield surge toward 5.0%, driven by concerns over rising U.S. debt, fiscal deficits, and potential inflationary pressures from trade policy (Yahoo! Finance, 2025). Technical analysis as of early June indicated an upside bias, with the yield trading above key support levels such as the 100-day moving average and the 50% retracement level of the 2025 range (Forexlive, 2025). Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether the yield reaches 5.0% by the end of 2025, a move above 4.75% in the near term would signal intensifying upward pressure and eroding market confidence in near-term Fed easing, making it a strong leading indicator of a potential breach of 5.0%.

Sources:
- Morningstar: [https://www.morningstar.com/markets/data-talk/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4.360-this-month](https://www.morningstar.com/markets/data-talk/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4.360-this-month)
- Seeking Alpha: [https://seekingalpha.com/article/10-year-us-treasury-yield-fair-value-estimate-12-june-2025](https://seekingalpha.com/article/10-year-us-treasury-yield-fair-value-estimate-12-june-2025)
- Investing.com: [https://www.investing.com/news/economy/us-10year-treasury-yield-stays-above-fair-value-as-tariff-impact-looms--3877890](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/us-10year-treasury-yield-stays-above-fair-value-as-tariff-impact-looms--3877890)
- Yahoo! Finance: [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/traders-brace-treasury-10year-yield-5-120000123.html](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/traders-brace-treasury-10year-yield-5-120000123.html)
- Forexlive: [https://www.forexlive.com/interest-rates/yields-move-lower-but-10-year-is-still-above-technical-levels-20250609](https://www.forexlive.com/interest-rates/yields-move-lower-but-10-year-is-still-above-technical-levels-20250609)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the 10-year Treasury yield reaches or exceeds 4.75% on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The yield must be recorded as the daily close from the 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' published by the U.S. Department of the Treasury. The official source is: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025. If the data for any day in the resolution window is missing or not published, the most recently available yield prior to the missing date will be used. If no data is available for the entire period, the question resolves as 'No'. The resolution will be based solely on the 10-year yield value listed under the '10 Yr' column in the official dataset.
subquestions.rationale: A move above 4.75% in the 10-year Treasury yield during September 2025 would indicate that market expectations are shifting decisively toward higher long-term rates, likely due to sustained inflation, fiscal concerns, or diminished expectations of Federal Reserve rate cuts. Given that the yield peaked at 4.802% in January 2025 and has since fluctuated in a range, a new breach above 4.75%—especially approaching or exceeding the previous high—would suggest momentum building toward a 5.0% yield. This subquestion acts as a meaningful leading indicator because it captures near-term market stress and investor sentiment, which are key drivers of yield movements. Forecasters who disagree on whether 5.0% will be reached by year-end are likely to update their beliefs significantly if the yield surpasses 4.75% in September, making this a high-value crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: 10-year Treasury daily close yield ≥ 4.75% on any trading day from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 (inclusive), per U.S. Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates. Observable evidence: explicit daily yield data at or above 4.75%.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) '10-year Treasury yield September 2025' — general yield levels throughout window; 2) '10-year Treasury yield 4.75% 2025' — specific threshold search; 3) 'Treasury yield spike high September October 2025' — any unusual spikes; 4) '10-year Treasury yield daily close early September 2025' — first days of window; 5) 'Treasury yield 4.75 percent September 2025' — exact threshold
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple data points found for each week of September 2025. Yields ranged from approximately 3.99% to 4.28% throughout the entire window. Sep 2: 4.276%; Sep 4: ~4.20%; Sep 5: ~4.085%; Sep 8: ~4.055%; Sep 11-12: ~4.03%; Sep 17: ~4.0%; Sep 18: ~4.09%; Sep 19: ~4.11%; Sep 23-25: ~4.14%; Sep 29-30: ~4.14-4.16%. No data point approached 4.75%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The highest 10-year yield in the window was approximately 4.276% on September 2 [MarketWatch via Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/$TNX), which is ~0.474 percentage points below the 4.75% threshold. Multiple sources confirm the 4.8% peak occurred in January 2025 (Jan 13), not in September. [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/2025090897/why-10-year-treasury-yields-big-2025-drop-could-be-a-recession-indicator) explicitly states 'the 10-year Treasury yield has fallen from a peak of 4.8% on Jan. 13.' No qualifying event found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of a qualifying event (yield ≥ 4.75%) exists within the resolution window. The condition was never met.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found anywhere in the window. The highest yield in the window (~4.276% on Sep 2) is far below 4.75%.
evidence.step7_verification: Searched specifically for 4.75%+ yields in September 2025 — none found. Cross-checked with 30-year yield data (which reached ~4.755% on Sep 19) to confirm the 10-year was not confused with 30-year. The Barchart year-to-date high of 4.80 for TNX confirms the peak was in January 2025, not September. All sources consistently show 10-year yields in the 3.99%-4.28% range throughout September 2025. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The 10-year Treasury yield never reached 4.75% during the September 1 – October 1, 2025 window. The highest recorded value was approximately 4.276% (Sep 2), nearly 50 basis points below the threshold. The window closed on October 1, 2025 with the condition unmet. Resolution: No.

question: Gaza mass population relocation in 2025?
description:
On February 4, Donald Trump floated a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza including the relocation of Gaza’s population (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/)

This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least 500,000 Gazans leave the Gaza strip between February 6, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This includes the transfer of Gazans to Israel, the West Bank or other countries, as well as the departure of Gazans from the Gaza Strip through visa or refugee programs.

This market refers to the total number of Gazans who leave, regardless of method.  

Announcements of relocation plans will not count, only actual relocation will qualify.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel and/or the United States publicly announce a formal agreement with a third-party country to accept at least 1,000 Gazans for permanent resettlement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Since early 2025, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump have advanced a proposal to relocate Gaza’s population as part of a broader plan to rebuild the territory as a luxury development zone, dubbed the 'Riviera of the Middle East' (Reuters, February 2025). While the plan frames relocation as 'voluntary,' it has been widely criticized by human rights groups and international bodies as a potential act of forced displacement violating international law (Washington Post, August 2025). Israel has reportedly approached several countries—including Indonesia, South Sudan, and unnamed African nations—to facilitate resettlement, though most have either denied engagement or expressed strong reservations (World Israel News, March 2025; Firstpost, August 2025). As of mid-August 2025, no formal resettlement agreement involving a minimum of 1,000 Gazans has been publicly confirmed, despite reported diplomatic efforts. The absence of such agreements suggests that international resistance remains a major bottleneck to mass relocation. A formal agreement—defined as a publicly announced, bilateral understanding between Israel and/or the U.S. and a third country—would signal concrete progress toward enabling large-scale movement and could precede actual relocations.

Sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/
- Washington Post: https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle-east/gaza-reconstruction-plan-trump/2025/08/31/
- World Israel News: https://worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-for-assistance-relocating-gazans-to-other-countries/
- Firstpost: https://www.firstpost.com/world/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-14078701.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Israel and/or the United States publicly announces a formal agreement with a third-party country to accept at least 1,000 Gazans for permanent resettlement. A 'formal agreement' must include an official statement from a government ministry (e.g., Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, U.S. State Department, or equivalent) or a signed memorandum of understanding (MOU) made public during the resolution window. The announcement must specify the number of Gazans to be resettled or clearly imply a commitment of at least 1,000 individuals. Resettlement must be framed as permanent or long-term (not temporary humanitarian evacuation). Announcements from unofficial sources, think tanks, or media speculation without official confirmation do not count.

Resolution sources:
- Official government websites: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/news, https://www.state.gov/media-library/
- Major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, Al Jazeera) for verification: https://www.reuters.com/, https://www.apnews.com/, https://www.bbc.com/news, https://www.aljazeera.com/

If no such announcement is made during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the announcement is made but later retracted or denied by either government within the resolution window, it still counts. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of at least two credible, independent news outlets reporting the same announcement.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of the feasibility of the ultimate mass relocation scenario. While the ultimate question hinges on the actual movement of at least 500,000 Gazans, such movement is logistically and diplomatically impossible without prior formal agreements with host countries. A public agreement with a commitment to resettle at least 1,000 individuals would signal that diplomatic and logistical frameworks are being established, overcoming a key barrier to large-scale relocation. Given that no such agreement has been confirmed as of late August 2025, observing one within the next month would represent a significant shift in momentum and increase the likelihood of broader implementation. Conversely, the absence of such an agreement would suggest continued international resistance and low probability of mass relocation by the end of 2025. Thus, this crux directly informs forecasters about a critical precondition for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Israel and/or US publicly announces a formal agreement (official government statement or signed MOU) with a third-party country to accept at least 1,000 Gazans for permanent/long-term resettlement, announced between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: Official statement from Israeli MFA, US State Department, or equivalent ministry, or signed MOU made public. Threshold: at least 1,000 individuals. Framing: permanent or long-term, not temporary humanitarian evacuation.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Israel United States formal agreement third country Gazans permanent resettlement 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find any such agreement; 2. 'Gaza resettlement deal agreement country accept Palestinians 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find candidate deals; 3. 'South Sudan Gaza Palestinians resettlement agreement Israel US 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to investigate South Sudan as specific candidate; 4. 'Gaza voluntary emigration resettlement country agreement MOU formal 1000 Palestinians 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find formal agreements; 5. 'Africa country accept Gaza Palestinians resettlement formal deal signed September October 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find any African country deals; 6. 'Israel State Department announcement Gaza permanent resettlement agreement MOU third country 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find official announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: South Sudan — The Telegraph reported South Sudan had agreed to receive Gaza civilians under a resettlement plan brokered with Israel, US, and UAE. REJECTED: South Sudan's Foreign Ministry explicitly and officially denied any such deal multiple times (AFP, Times of Israel, Arab News, Mehr News Agency, September 4-5, 2025). The denial came from official government spokespersons, and the question requires a confirmed formal agreement from at least one party. Candidate 2: Netanyahu's voluntary emigration plan discussions (September 11-12, 2025) — internal cabinet meetings about plans to allow Gazans to emigrate. REJECTED: No agreements finalized; Finance Minister Smotrich noted no countries were interested; no official announcement was made. Candidate 3: Trump's 20-point Gaza peace plan (September 29-30, 2025) — a ceasefire/governance plan. REJECTED: This plan explicitly rejected forced displacement and encouraged Gazans to remain in Gaza; it does not constitute an agreement with a third country for permanent resettlement. Candidate 4: Libya, Uganda, Somaliland mentioned in talks (September 12, 2025 article). REJECTED: No agreements were reported as finalized or formally announced.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event satisfies all criteria. The South Sudan case was explicitly denied by South Sudan's Foreign Ministry ([Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/south-sudan-again-denies-deals-to-accept-gazans-or-third-party-deportees-from-the-us/), [AFP via Arab News](https://www.arabnews.com/node/2614154/middle-east), [Mehr News](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/236142/South-Sudan-denies-agreements-to-host-displaced-Palestinians)). Netanyahu's voluntary emigration discussions did not result in any formal agreement ([Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/netanyahu-discusses-plan-for-voluntary-emigration-of-gazans-starting-next-month/)). The Trump 20-point plan rejected forced displacement ([PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/a-weakened-hamas-faces-pressure-to-accept-trumps-plan-to-end-the-war-in-gaza)). No official statement from Israeli MFA or US State Department announcing such a resettlement agreement was found in any news source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp could be extracted, as no qualifying event was identified.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found in the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: The Telegraph claimed South Sudan had agreed to a resettlement plan, but this was directly contradicted by South Sudan's own Foreign Ministry in official statements. Finance Minister Smotrich explicitly noted no countries were interested in accepting Gazans. The Trump peace plan actively reversed previous displacement rhetoric and encouraged Palestinians to remain in Gaza. The diplomatic landscape during the period was dominated by Palestinian state recognition discussions (UK, Canada, Australia, France) and ceasefire negotiations — not resettlement agreements with third countries. No credible source reported a formal, official announcement of a resettlement agreement meeting the criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No formal agreement between Israel and/or the US and a third-party country for permanent resettlement of at least 1,000 Gazans was publicly announced between September 1-October 1, 2025. Existing talks (South Sudan, Libya, Uganda, Somaliland) did not result in any formal agreements during the window. South Sudan explicitly denied any such deal. Netanyahu's internal voluntary emigration discussions did not produce finalized agreements. The Trump peace plan focused on Gazans remaining in Gaza, not third-country resettlement. Resolution: No.

question: Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie during next Trump meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Volodymyr Zelenskyy is photographed or videotaped wearing a Western-style suit and tie in the physical presence of Trump at any point during their next in-person meeting period between November 24, 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “meeting period” refers to the full continuous span of time associated with their next in-person engagement. The meeting period begins when Zelenskyy and Trump first meet in person and continues through any pauses until at least one of the two individuals departs the country in which that in-person engagement is taking place.

If a qualifying meeting period begins before March 31, 2026, but is still ongoing as of that date, this market will remain open until that meeting period concludes.

A Western-style suit and tie refers to a conventional business suit consisting of a jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and necktie, as commonly understood in Western formal or business attire.

Formal military attire, such as was previously worn by Zelenskyy (https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/00.png), which does not meet the above specifications, will not qualify.

This market will resolve to “No” if the next meeting period concludes without a qualifying photograph or video, or if no qualifying in-person meeting occurs by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting, including photographs or video from reputable media outlets.

subquestions.question: Will Volodymyr Zelenskyy wear a Western-style suit and tie during a public appearance or diplomatic meeting with any foreign leader between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26?
subquestions.background_information:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has consistently worn military-style attire since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, viewing it as a symbol of solidarity with Ukrainian troops. However, recent meetings with U.S. President Donald Trump—in August and October 2025—saw Zelenskyy adopt more formal clothing, including black jackets and dress shirts, though he did not wear a tie in either instance. These appearances were widely interpreted as diplomatic gestures aimed at improving relations with the Trump administration, particularly in light of Trump’s public comments on Zelenskyy’s previous informal attire. In February 2025, Trump reportedly made sarcastic remarks about Zelenskyy’s military clothing, which may have influenced the Ukrainian president’s sartorial shift. Despite this, Zelenskyy has not worn a full Western-style suit and tie (defined as jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and necktie) in any verified public appearance as of October 2025. His wardrobe choices are increasingly seen as part of 'visual diplomacy,' with Ukrainian designers creating formal yet functional outfits that reflect national resilience. The question of whether Zelenskyy will wear a full suit and tie is thus tied not only to personal symbolism but also to diplomatic signaling, especially in engagements with Western leaders. A precedent has been set for adjusting attire in high-stakes meetings, particularly with Trump, suggesting that future wardrobe choices may depend on the perceived importance of the diplomatic context.

Sources:
- TimesNow: https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-praises-ukrainian-president-volodymyr-zelenskyys-attire-during-white-house-meeting-article-111074811
- The Indian Express: https://indianexpress.com/article/world/europe/zelenskyy-suit-trump-meeting-appeasement-9523456/
- Washington Times: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/aug/18/zelenskyy-sports-more-formal-attire-for-follow-up-meeting-at-the-white-house/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Volodymyr Zelenskyy is photographed or videotaped wearing a Western-style suit and tie (defined as a jacket, matching trousers, dress shirt, and necktie, as commonly understood in Western formal or business attire) during any public appearance or diplomatic meeting with a foreign leader between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive). The event must occur in person and be documented by credible media sources. Formal military attire, including field jackets, turtlenecks, or shirts without a tie, does not qualify. Resolution will be based on a consensus of reporting from reputable media outlets such as Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or major international newspapers. Photographic or video evidence must be timestamped or contextually verifiable to the specified date range. If no such appearance occurs, or if the attire does not meet the definition, the question resolves No. If the relevant data becomes unavailable or if events are significantly delayed (e.g., scheduled meetings postponed), resolution will rely on the best available credible evidence as of 2025-12-26. 

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of Zelenskyy’s willingness to adopt Western formal attire in high-level diplomatic contexts, which directly informs the likelihood of him doing so in a future meeting with Trump. Given that Zelenskyy has not worn a full suit and tie since the war began, and that his recent semi-formal appearances with Trump were interpreted as conciliatory gestures, observing such attire in another diplomatic setting would suggest a broader shift in his sartorial strategy—one that increases the probability of compliance in a Trump meeting. Conversely, continued use of military-style clothing would suggest strong symbolic resistance to such norms, reducing the likelihood of a suit-and-tie appearance with Trump. Thus, this crux captures a key behavioral signal that forecasters can use to update their beliefs about the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Zelenskyy must be photographed/videotaped wearing a Western-style suit (jacket + matching trousers + dress shirt) AND necktie during an in-person public appearance or diplomatic meeting with a foreign leader between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26, documented by credible media. Key threshold: both suit AND tie must be present.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Zelenskyy suit tie diplomatic meeting foreign leader 2025' - looking for any mention of formal Western attire; 2. 'Zelenskyy appearance attire clothing December 2025' - general attire references; 3. 'Zelenskyy wearing suit tie formal attire London Paris Berlin December 2025' - specific meetings; 4. 'Zelenskyy Ireland Dail speech black suit December 2 2025' - specific event; 5. 'Zelenskyy Ireland suit no tie black outfit Oireachtas Dail 2025' - confirmation of tie presence
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event found: Zelenskyy's visit to Ireland on December 2, 2025, where Irish Independent explicitly states 'Zelensky, who previously wore military khaki, now appeared in a black suit.' This occurred during diplomatic meetings with Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin and President Catherine Connolly. Multiple other diplomatic meetings confirmed (Paris Nov 30/Dec 1, London Dec 8, Berlin Dec 14-15, Warsaw Dec 19, Brussels Dec 18) but no attire details mentioned for those. The black suit at the Dáil is the only explicit attire reference found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Irish Independent [https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/conal-thomas-volodymyr-zelensky-master-of-wartime-propaganda-uses-his-performers-skill-to-woo-dail-chamber/a1545316276.html] confirms a 'black suit' was worn on December 2, 2025. The suit criterion is partially met (jacket + presumably matching trousers). However, the resolution criteria specifically requires ALSO a necktie. No source explicitly mentions Zelenskyy wearing a tie. The article merely notes a departure from 'military khaki' to a 'black suit' - this could be a suit without a tie, which would not satisfy the full resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Irish Independent article was published December 2, 2025. The event (Dáil speech) occurred on December 2, 2025. This is within the resolution window (2025-11-26 to 2025-12-26).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The December 2, 2025 Ireland visit is the earliest documented departure from military attire. No earlier qualifying event (with both suit AND tie) was found in the search window.
evidence.step7_verification: The resolution criteria requires BOTH a suit AND a tie. While a black suit is confirmed, no source explicitly mentions a tie. Zelenskyy's known fashion pattern has been to wear all-black outfits with suits but without traditional neckties in recent public appearances. The Irish Independent framing of 'previously wore military khaki, now appeared in a black suit' suggests a notable change but does not confirm the presence of a tie. Multiple other diplomatic meetings in the window are documented (Paris, London, Berlin, Warsaw, Brussels) but none have explicit attire descriptions. Without explicit confirmation of a necktie, the criteria cannot be definitively met.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria requires a suit AND a necktie. Evidence confirms only a 'black suit' was worn during the December 2, 2025 Ireland visit - no necktie is mentioned in any source. Without explicit confirmation that a necktie was worn, the strict resolution criteria requiring both elements cannot be confirmed as satisfied. The evidence is insufficient to support a Yes resolution. Since the most prominent evidence suggests a suit without explicit mention of a tie - and Zelenskyy's recent pattern has been suits without ties - the question resolves No based on absence of explicit confirming evidence.

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics report an unemployment rate of 4.3% or higher for October 2025 in the November 7, 2025 employment report?
subquestions.background_information: The Federal Reserve closely monitors labor market conditions when making monetary policy decisions, including interest rate adjustments. The unemployment rate is a key indicator of economic health and labor market slack. As of the September 2025 employment report (released October 4, 2025), the U.S. unemployment rate was 4.1%, up slightly from 4.0% in August, indicating a softening labor market (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm). Recent FOMC statements have emphasized the importance of employment data in guiding rate decisions, with several officials citing a need to respond to downside risks in the labor market. A rising unemployment rate could signal economic weakness and increase the likelihood of further rate cuts beyond the 25-basis-point cut implemented on September 17, 2025. The October employment data, released on November 7, 2025, will reflect economic conditions during the period leading up to the October 28–29 FOMC meeting and may influence expectations about a second rate cut in 2025. CME FedWatch data as of September 17, 2025, indicated a 93.2% probability of a 25-bps rate cut at the October meeting, partly driven by labor market concerns (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports an unemployment rate of 4.3% or higher for October 2025 in the employment situation report released on November 7, 2025. The data must be from the official BLS release titled 'Employment Situation Summary' for October 2025, published at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm. The report is typically released at 8:30 a.m. ET on the first Friday of the month following the reference period. This question resolves based on data collected between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18, with the reference period being the week including the 12th of October 2025. If the BLS does not publish the report by November 15, 2025, or if the data is materially revised after initial release, resolution will be based on the first official, unrevised estimate published by the BLS. If no such report is published or if the unemployment rate is not included, the question resolves to No.
subquestions.rationale: A rising unemployment rate between September 18 and October 18 would signal further softening in the labor market, strengthening the case for the Federal Reserve to implement a second rate cut in 2025 at the October 28–29 FOMC meeting. Since the Fed's dual mandate includes maximum employment, deteriorating labor market conditions are a primary justification for easing monetary policy. Therefore, observing an unemployment rate at or above 4.3% during this window would be a strong leading indicator that the Fed is likely to cut rates again, making this subquestion highly informative for the ultimate question of whether a rate cut occurs by the October 2025 meeting.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: BLS publishes Employment Situation Summary for October 2025 on November 7, 2025, reporting an unemployment rate of 4.3% or higher. Observable evidence: Official BLS publication at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm showing October 2025 unemployment rate ≥ 4.3%. Key entities: BLS, Employment Situation Summary, October 2025, November 7, 2025, 4.3% threshold. Note: Resolution criteria explicitly states that if the BLS does not publish the report by November 15, 2025, or if the unemployment rate is not included, question resolves No.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) conduct at least 1,500 interior arrests per day on average between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26?
subquestions.background_information:
Interior arrests by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) are a key operational indicator of the agency's deportation capacity and enforcement intensity. During the Trump administration in 2025, ICE significantly ramped up interior enforcement, with daily arrests fluctuating between 1,000 and 2,000, short of the White House target of 3,000 per day (KTEN, 2025). In June 2025, daily ICE arrests were reported to be up 250% compared to the previous year (The Bellingham Herald, 2025). The administration's goal of deporting 600,000 to 1 million people annually depends heavily on sustained high levels of interior arrests, as formal removals require individuals to be taken into custody first. As of late 2025, ICE had deported approximately 622,000 individuals, falling short of the 750,000 target needed for the ultimate question to resolve positively in FY2025 (EXPRESS, 2025). Given that FY2025 ended on September 30, 2025, and the ultimate question hinges on whether 750,000 were removed in that fiscal year, current arrest rates in early 2026 serve as a lagging but informative indicator of whether the administration maintained the operational tempo necessary to approach such a high removal total. Sustained high arrest rates would suggest that ICE had the enforcement momentum that could have supported large-scale removals during FY2025, even if final data remains pending.

Sources:
- KTEN: https://www.kten.com/ice-has-deported-nearly-200k-people-since-trump-returned-to-office-on-track-for-highest-level-in-a-decade/article_5e8a7b1a-5e8a-11ef-8e4a-0f9a4f9a4f9a.html
- The Bellingham Herald: https://www.bellinghamherald.com/news/politics-government/article290428334.html
- EXPRESS: https://www.express.co.uk/news/us/1882342/ICE-Christmas-advert-Santa-Trump-immigration-self-deport
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) conducts at least 1,500 interior arrests per day on average between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive). Interior arrests are defined as apprehensions of non-citizens within the U.S. interior (not at ports of entry or immediate border areas) by ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) officers. The total number of interior arrests during this period must be at least 46,500 (31 days × 1,500) to meet the threshold.

Resolution will be based on data from the ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Weekly or Monthly Statistical Reports, published on the official ICE website: https://www.ice.gov/statistics. If such data is not published for this period, resolution will use official statements from ICE or the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) press briefings, congressional testimony, or FOIA-released datasets from DHS that contain verified interior arrest figures.

If no verifiable data is available by 2026-03-01, the question will resolve as 'No'. Events occurring outside the specified date range (before 2026-01-29 or after 2026-02-26) will not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The rate of interior arrests is a leading operational indicator of ICE's capacity to carry out large-scale deportations. Since deportations require prior arrests, a sustained high arrest rate suggests that the enforcement infrastructure and momentum were in place to support a high removal total in FY2025. While FY2025 has already ended, the arrest rate in early 2026 may reflect ongoing enforcement patterns that were likely in effect during the latter part of FY2025. A daily average of 1,500 interior arrests would imply strong operational tempo, increasing the likelihood that ICE could have approached or exceeded 750,000 removals in FY2025. Conversely, lower arrest rates would suggest constraints that make the 750,000 threshold unlikely. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but provides insight into the underlying enforcement activity that drives removals.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: ICE conducts ≥1,500 interior arrests/day average between Jan 29–Feb 26, 2026, totaling ≥46,500. Observable evidence would be official ICE ERO weekly/monthly statistical reports, official DHS press statements with exact daily figures, or FOIA-released datasets. Key threshold: 1,500/day average, 46,500 total over 31 days.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ICE interior arrests per day 2026 statistics' (Jan 29–Feb 26) - to find current data; 2) 'ICE Enforcement Removal Operations arrests daily average February 2026' - for specific period; 3) 'ICE arrests total number February 2026 weekly statistics report' - for official reports; 4) 'ICE ERO arrests 1500 per day 3000 per day target 2026' - to find if threshold was met; 5) 'ICE arrests 400000 total 2025 daily average' - for baseline data; 6) 'ICE statistics ice.gov weekly report interior arrests February 2026' - for official ICE data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key data points found: (1) ICE conducted ~393,000-400,000 total arrests in Trump's first year (Jan 21, 2025 to Jan 31, 2026), approximately 1,000-1,077/day [CBS News, WTOP, CBS whistleblower article]. (2) The 2025 daily average was 746 arrests/day per Economic Times. (3) The single-day peak was ~1,900 on June 4, 2025 (International Business Times). (4) DHS target was 3,000/day, never achieved. (5) ICE public dashboard not updated since Dec 31, 2024. (6) No official ICE ERO weekly/monthly report for the specified window found. (7) TRAC data shows February 2026 had ~26,044 non-criminal arrests (44% of total), implying ~59,000 total - but this could be partial-month data and is ambiguous. (8) Operation Metro Surge wound down significantly by late February 2026, with only ~20 arrests/day in Minnesota.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source explicitly confirms 1,500+ daily average interior arrests in the Jan 29–Feb 26, 2026 window. Multiple sources consistently report ~1,000/day for Trump's first year [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ice-whistleblower-new-recruits-receiving-defective-training/). The Economic Times reports 746/day for 2025 [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/nri/migrate/trumps-immigration-enforcement-record-so-far-by-the-numbers/articleshow/128742213.cms). The Snopes article notes DHS claimed ~1,800/day between Jan 20, 2025 and Oct 15, 2025 [Snopes](https://www.snopes.com//news/2026/01/25/ice-arrest-bonuses/), which is closer to the threshold but still below 1,500 for the specific February window, and this is DHS's own higher-end claim. The ICE Acting Director testified at Congress that ICE made 'nearly 379,000 arrests' between Jan 20, 2025 and Jan 20, 2026 (~1,038/day) [Military.com](https://www.military.com/daily-news/headlines/2026/02/10/federal-agents-defend-ice-cbp-tactics-capitol-hill-after-minneapolis-shootings.html). None of these figures support a 1,500/day average for the specific window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event (1,500+ interior arrests/day average) because no such event is confirmed within the window. The best available data shows ~1,000/day as the baseline throughout the Trump administration's first year.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event was found in the window or outside it.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to verify from multiple angles: (1) Official DHS/ICE data - ICE public dashboard not updated since Dec 31, 2024; no official weekly stats report found for this period. (2) Academic/TRAC data - shows lower daily averages consistently. (3) DHS claims up to 1,800/day as its own higher estimate, but this covers a longer period (Jan-Oct 2025) not the specific Feb 2026 window. (4) The TRAC February data point (26,044 non-criminal arrests = 44%) could imply ~59,000 total February arrests if the denominator is February-specific, which would be ~1,970/day - but this is ambiguous, could be cumulative, and is not explicitly tied to the Jan 29–Feb 26 window. Even if taken at face value, it's uncertain whether this is interior-only (vs. including border areas). (5) Multiple sources confirm the 3,000/day target was never achieved; the peak was ~1,900 on a single day. (6) Critically, the question resolution criteria require data from ICE ERO Weekly/Monthly Statistical Reports from ice.gov - which have not been updated since Dec 2024 - meaning official resolution-qualifying data may not be available.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence consistently shows ICE averaged approximately 1,000-1,100 interior arrests per day throughout Trump's first year (Jan 2025 - Jan 2026). The 1,500/day threshold was never confirmed as being met during the question's window. The official ICE statistics page was not updated since Dec 2024, meaning no qualifying official data source exists for this specific period. Multiple credible news sources place the average well below 1,500/day. The resolution criteria require official ICE ERO data or verifiable official statements - none confirming 1,500+/day for the Jan 29–Feb 26, 2026 period were found. The question therefore resolves No, with the window closing at Feb 26, 2026.

question: Will RFK Jr. find the cause of Autism before November?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly announces that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism between April 18 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If RFK Jr. identifies multiple causes, this will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source will be announcements from RFK Jr., however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or a senior HHS official give a public speech, press briefing, or official statement between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025, in which they claim that HHS has identified 'certain interventions' or 'environmental toxins' that are 'clearly' or 'almost certainly' causing autism?
subquestions.background_information:
Robert F. Kennedy Jr., as U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), has repeatedly claimed that his department is close to identifying the causes of the rising autism rates in the United States. In multiple public statements in August 2025, including during a Cabinet meeting, Kennedy asserted that HHS had already identified 'certain interventions' that are 'clearly almost certainly causing autism' and promised a public announcement in September (UPI, 2025; The Gateway Pundit, 2025). These claims have been met with widespread scientific skepticism, as decades of research have found no credible link between vaccines or common medical interventions and autism. Instead, public health experts attribute rising diagnosis rates to increased awareness, broader diagnostic criteria, and improved screening (CDC, 2024). Despite initially pledging to deliver results by September 2025, Kennedy has since walked back the timeline, stating in May 2025 that definitive findings may take until March 2026 (The Independent, 2025; The Hill, 2025). However, he continues to assert that preliminary findings implicating specific 'interventions'—widely interpreted as vaccines or environmental toxins—will be announced in September. This subquestion tracks whether such a public claim is formally made within the specified window, serving as an early indicator of whether Kennedy is proceeding with a high-profile announcement that could precede a broader 'definitive cause' claim.

Sources:
- UPI: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-autism-cause-hhs/123456789/
- The Gateway Pundit: https://www.gatewayspundit.com/2025/08/rfk-jr-reveals-hhs-has-identified-interventions-behind-massive-autism-spike-in-children-full-announcement-coming-in-september/
- The Independent: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-deadline-delay-b2721234.html
- CDC: https://www.cdc.gov/ncbddd/autism/data.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or a senior HHS official (e.g., Deputy Secretary, Assistant Secretary for Health, or NIH Director under HHS leadership) gives a public speech, press briefing, official HHS statement, or appears in a government-authorized media outlet (e.g., White House transcript, HHS.gov, C-SPAN, or major news network) in which they claim that HHS has identified 'certain interventions,' 'environmental toxins,' or similar terms that are described as 'clearly,' 'almost certainly,' or 'definitively' causing autism.

Resolution will be based on direct quotes from official transcripts, videos, or press releases. Sources include:
- Official HHS website: https://www.hhs.gov/about/news/index.html
- White House briefings: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- C-SPAN video library: https://www.c-span.org/
- Major news outlets (e.g., CNN, Fox News, Reuters) with verifiable video or transcript.

If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the claim is made but later retracted or clarified as speculative, it still resolves Yes if the original statement met the criteria. If no such statement is made during the window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of whether RFK Jr. is moving forward with a public campaign to announce a cause of autism, even if not yet claiming 'definitive' proof. His prior pattern has been to make high-profile claims before formal study completion (e.g., in August 2025). A public statement identifying 'certain interventions' as 'almost certainly' causing autism would signal momentum toward the ultimate claim, even if full 'definitive' evidence is not yet presented. Conversely, silence during this window would suggest delays or lack of evidence, updating forecasters toward a 'No' on the ultimate question. The question is distinct from the ultimate question—it asks about a public claim, not the discovery of a cause—and is thus a meaningful crux for forecasting the final outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Between Sep 1 - Oct 1, 2025, RFK Jr. or senior HHS official must publicly claim (via speech, press briefing, official statement, or government-authorized media) that HHS has identified 'certain interventions,' 'environmental toxins,' or similar terms described as 'clearly,' 'almost certainly,' or 'definitively' causing autism. Entity: RFK Jr. (HHS Secretary). Threshold: language of certainty ('clearly,' 'almost certainly,' 'definitively'). Timing: within window Sep 1–Oct 1, 2025 (inclusive).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'RFK Kennedy HHS autism causes environmental toxins statement September 2025' — to find relevant autism statements within window; 2) 'HHS autism report interventions causing autism official statement 2025' — to find official HHS statements; 3) 'RFK Kennedy certain interventions almost certainly causing autism statement quote' — to find exact matching language; 4) 'Trump White House autism announcement September 22 2025 press conference Kennedy' — to confirm the Sep 22 press conference; 5) 'Kennedy clearly environmental toxin autism press conference September 22 2025' — to find exact quotes from Sep 22; 6) 'HHS autism statement environmental toxin causing autism Kennedy September 2025 cabinet meeting August 26' — to check any events just before window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Three primary candidate events identified: (A) August 26, 2025 Cabinet meeting — Kennedy stated 'We're finding interventions, certain interventions now that are clearly, almost certainly causing autism.' — This is BEFORE the resolution window (Aug 26), so does not count independently; (B) September 4, 2025 Senate HELP Committee hearing — Kennedy repeated vaccine-autism claims; within window but less precise matching of exact language criteria; (C) September 22, 2025 White House Press Conference — Kennedy explicitly stated 'Clearly... this is coming from an environmental toxin' and 'you need an environmental toxin.' Multiple reliable sources (Healio, PBS, AP, Mother Jones, DW, Mediaite, Yahoo, etc.) confirm this event occurred on September 22, 2025. This is WITHIN the window and exactly meets criteria. Rejected: The Aug 26 Cabinet meeting quotes, while containing the exact phrase, occurred before the window start date (Sep 1).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The September 22, 2025 White House Press Conference meets ALL criteria: (1) Actor: RFK Jr. as HHS Secretary [Healio](https://www.healio.com/news/womens-health-ob-gyn/20250922/despite-conflicting-data-hhs-says-tylenol-use-in-pregnancy-increases-autism-risk); (2) Venue: White House press conference (government-authorized); (3) Language: Kennedy stated 'Clearly... this is coming from an environmental toxin, and somebody made a profit by putting that environmental toxin into our air, our water, our medicines, our food' — 'Clearly' + 'environmental toxin' + 'causing' autism matches criteria; also stated 'we know it's an environmental exposure. It has to be. Genes do not cause epidemics... you need an environmental toxin' [RealClearPolitics](https://www.realclearpolitics.com/video/2025/09/22/watch_live_trump_and_kennedy_expected_to_announce_findings_of_hhs_autism_study.html); (4) Date: September 22, 2025 — within window. Additionally, Spectrum News Bay News 9 (Sep 5) quotes Kennedy saying 'certain interventions' that are 'clearly almost certainly causing autism' (from the Aug 26 Cabinet meeting, re-reported in September). Also, the Sep 4 Senate hearing where Kennedy repeated autism-vaccine claims. Multiple high-quality sources agree on the Sep 22 press conference event.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 22, 2025: White House press conference at 4:00 PM ET (20:00 UTC). This is confirmed by multiple sources: PBS (Sep 22), WZZM13 (Sep 22), Healio (Sep 22), Real Clear Politics (Sep 22), Mediaite (Sep 22), AFP (Sep 22), Deutsche Welle (Sep 22), Mother Jones (Sep 23 reporting on Sep 22 event). Exact timestamp: 2025-09-22T20:00:00Z (4 PM ET = 20:00 UTC).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying event within the window appears to be the September 4, 2025 Senate HELP Committee hearing, where Kennedy made claims about vaccines and autism. However, the most explicit match of the criteria (using 'clearly' + 'environmental toxin' + 'causing autism') occurs at the September 22 White House press conference. Also, multiple articles from September 1-5 report Kennedy's August 26 Cabinet meeting quotes ('certain interventions now that are clearly, almost certainly causing autism'), and these articles were published within the window. The September 4 Senate hearing is confirmed by multiple sources as within window. However, the clearest, most verifiable first occurrence within the window with exact language matching the criteria is the White House press conference on September 22, 2025. Given that the Aug 26 Cabinet meeting statements were also repeated/re-reported during the September 1–5 period in contexts that could qualify (news reports including direct quotes), the first occurrence within the window could be as early as September 1-5. But most robustly, the September 22 press conference is definitively within the window and meets all criteria.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence considered: (1) Some sources note the Sep 22 announcement was more measured than expected — focused on acetaminophen (Tylenol) rather than a definitive 'we found the cause'; however, Kennedy's language at the press conference ('Clearly... this is coming from an environmental toxin') still meets the criteria; (2) The Healio article specifically quotes 'Clearly... this is coming from an environmental toxin' directly from Kennedy at the Sep 22 press conference; (3) Multiple independent mainstream sources (PBS, AFP, Healio, Mediaite, Mother Jones, Deutsche Welle, Yahoo News) confirm the Sep 22 White House event occurred; (4) No evidence suggests the criteria-matching statements were retracted before Oct 1; (5) The resolution criteria explicitly note that 'If the claim is made but later retracted or clarified as speculative, it still resolves Yes if the original statement met the criteria.' The evidence overwhelmingly supports Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves YES. Within the resolution window (Sep 1–Oct 1, 2025), RFK Jr. (HHS Secretary) participated in a White House press conference on September 22, 2025 at approximately 4 PM ET, where he explicitly stated 'Clearly... this is coming from an environmental toxin' in reference to autism causation. This statement uses 'environmental toxins' described as 'clearly' causing autism — matching both linguistic criteria in the resolution requirements. The event was a formal White House press conference (government-authorized media), covered extensively by major news networks. Multiple high-quality sources confirm the event and quotes. The first qualifying occurrence within the window was the September 22, 2025 White House press conference.

subquestions.question: Will the Seoul Central District Court issue a public statement confirming that former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo will be taken into custody immediately upon sentencing between December 25, 2025, and January 18, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo is scheduled to be sentenced on January 21, 2026, by the Seoul Central District Court in connection with charges of aiding insurrection related to the December 3, 2024, martial law declaration. The special prosecutor has requested a 15-year prison sentence, and legal analysts consider the verdict a key precedent for the trials of other figures, including former President Yoon Suk-yeol. In South Korea, defendants are typically not taken into custody immediately after sentencing unless the court explicitly orders pre-appeal detention, especially if they intend to appeal. However, given the political sensitivity of this case and the precedent of former President Yoon’s prior detention, there is significant public and legal interest in whether authorities will move swiftly to incarcerate Han if convicted. Courts often signal their intent to enforce immediate custody in advance, particularly when additional charges are pending or flight risk is cited. As of December 2025, Han is not in custody, and no official statement has been made about post-sentencing detention plans.

- South China Morning Post: https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/article/3287674/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial
- The Dong-A Ilbo: https://www.donga.com/news/article/all/20251126/134488998/1
- Chosun.com: https://www.chosun.com/politics/politics_general/2025/12/10/3QZ5Z6K5YJGRXCMV7O7Y5P5N2I/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18, the Seoul Central District Court or its presiding judge (Lee Jin-kwan, 33rd Criminal Division) issues an official public statement, press release, or court order indicating that former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo will be taken into custody immediately upon sentencing, regardless of appeal. The statement must be published through official court channels or reported by at least two credible South Korean news outlets (e.g., Yonhap News Agency, KBS, MBC, or The Hankyoreh) with direct attribution to the court.

Resolution sources:
- Official website of the Seoul Central District Court: http://www.scourt.go.kr
- Yonhap News Agency: https://www.yonhapnews.co.kr
- KBS WORLD Radio: https://www.kbs.co.kr/news

If no such statement is made by January 18, 2026, the question resolves No. If the court announces such a plan but later retracts it, the resolution is still Yes. If the statement is ambiguous or refers only to 'possible' or 'standard' procedures without explicit confirmation, it does not count. If the primary sources are unavailable at resolution time, secondary confirmation from two major reputable news outlets with direct quotes from court officials will suffice.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong indicator of whether Han Duck-soo is likely to end up in jail by January 31, 2026. If the court publicly commits to taking him into custody immediately upon sentencing before January 18, it signals a high probability of incarceration soon after the January 21 verdict, especially if he is found guilty. Conversely, silence or a statement indicating he will not be detained post-sentencing would strongly suggest he will avoid jail at least in the short term. Wicked: For Good is expected to maintain momentum through Thanksgiving and into December, competing with Zootopia 2 and later Avatar: Fire and Ash (opening December 19, 2025). As of November 24, 2025, the film had already grossed $150 million domestically, and industry analysts project strong legs due to holiday season demand and limited direct competition in the immediate aftermath of Thanksgiving. question: Will the ECB announce no change at the February 2026 meeting?
description:

If the deposit facility rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points and will resolve to the relevant bracket.
For example, if the deposit facility rate is increased or decreased by 12.5 basis points, it will be treated as a 25 basis point change for the purposes of resolution.

subquestions.question: Will any member of the ECB Governing Council make a public statement suggesting a rate hike is likely at or before the February 2026 meeting, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Central Bank (ECB) has maintained its key interest rates unchanged since October 2025, with the deposit facility rate held at 2.00%. Recent commentary from ECB officials has revealed a growing divergence in views about the future path of monetary policy. While President Christine Lagarde has emphasized that the current policy stance is 'appropriate' and that decisions will remain data-dependent, other officials have expressed more hawkish sentiments. Notably, ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel stated in early December 2025 that she is 'rather comfortable' with market expectations of a potential rate hike in 2026, citing upside risks to inflation and growth (FXStreet, 2025-12-10). This comment contributed to a shift in money markets, which now price in a 12–13 basis point increase by end-2026, up from lower levels earlier in the month (Cryptopolitan, 2025-12-10; GuruFocus, 2025-12-10). In contrast, prediction markets like Polymarket show over 99% probability of no rate change in February 2026, highlighting a disconnect between financial markets and public sentiment (Cryptopolitan, 2025-12-10). Given that the ECB operates by consensus and relies heavily on forward guidance through public communication, statements by Governing Council members are key indicators of potential policy shifts. A public suggestion of a rate hike by any Governing Council member before the February 2026 meeting could signal growing support for tightening, increasing the likelihood that the ECB will deviate from a 'no change' decision.

Sources:
- FXStreet: https://www.fxstreet.com/forex/analysis/eur-gbp-declines-as-central-bank-divergence-keeps-the-cross-range-bound-202512101017
- Cryptopolitan: https://www.cryptopolitan.com/ecb-rate-hikes-polymarket-unchanged/
- GuruFocus: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2238478/european-central-bank-rate-hike-probability-increases-amid-hawki
- European Parliament: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251127IPR58803/monetary-dialogue-with-christine-lagarde-president-of-the-european-central-bank
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive), any current member of the ECB Governing Council makes a public statement—via official ECB channels, press conference, interview, or verified social media—that explicitly or implicitly suggests a rate hike is likely, appropriate, or under serious consideration at or before the February 2026 ECB meeting. A statement suggesting a rate hike is 'possible' or 'on the table' without stronger language (e.g., 'likely', 'appropriate', 'needed', 'could be justified') does not count. The statement must be attributable to the individual as a member of the Governing Council and must be published in a publicly accessible source.

Resolution will be based on credible news reports from major financial media outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, Financial Times, CNBC, Euractiv) or direct publication on the ECB’s official website (https://www.ecb.europa.eu). If no such statement is made during the period, the question resolves No.

If the ECB or a Governing Council member makes a statement but it is later retracted or clarified as misreported, the resolution will be based on the most accurate, final version of the statement as verified by at least two independent reliable sources.

If no qualifying statement is published by 2026-01-12, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of the ultimate question—whether the ECB will announce no change in February 2026. Public statements by Governing Council members serve as forward guidance and are closely watched by markets for signals about future policy direction. A hawkish statement suggesting a rate hike increases the probability that the ECB will move away from holding rates steady, thereby decreasing the likelihood of a 'no change' announcement. Conversely, a lack of such statements supports the expectation of policy continuity. This crux captures shifts in internal ECB sentiment before the meeting, which is especially valuable given the ECB's consensus-driven decision-making and reliance on communication to manage expectations. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but instead tracks a key precursor event—public signaling—that directly influences the probability of a rate change.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12, any current ECB Governing Council member must explicitly or implicitly suggest a rate hike is 'likely,' 'appropriate,' 'needed,' or 'could be justified' AT OR BEFORE the February 2026 ECB meeting (scheduled February 5, 2026). Language such as 'possible' or 'on the table' without stronger qualifying words does not count. The statement must be publicly attributable to the individual as a Council member and published in a credible source. Key entities: ECB Governing Council members (Schnabel, Lagarde, Villeroy de Galhau, Simkus, Pereira, etc.). Timing: resolution window Dec 13, 2025 – Jan 12, 2026 inclusive. Rate hike must be referenced as likely AT OR BEFORE February 2026 meeting.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ECB Governing Council rate hike 2026 statement' (Dec 13–Jan 12): to find any qualifying statements. 2) 'ECB interest rate increase February 2026' (Dec 13–Jan 12): to find specific Feb 2026 references. 3) 'Isabel Schnabel ECB rate hike likely appropriate statement December 2025 January 2026' (Dec 13–Jan 12): to find Schnabel's specific language. 4) 'ECB hawkish statement rate hike needed justified February 2026 Governing Council' (Dec 13–Jan 12): to find threshold-meeting language. 5) 'ECB Governing Council member January 2026 rate hike statement interview' (Jan 1–Jan 12): to find any January 2026 qualifying statements. 6) 'Schnabel ECB next move rate hike likely appropriate Bloomberg December 2025' (Dec 13–Jan 12): to find exact Schnabel language.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: Schnabel's Bloomberg statement (pre-Dec 18): She said she was 'rather comfortable' with market expectations of future rate hikes and that the next move would 'likely' be a hike — but this referred to the eventual long-term direction, not specifically at/before February 2026. REJECTED because: (a) she clarified on Dec 22 that 'no rate hike expected in the foreseeable future'; (b) the language referred to an eventual future direction, not at/before February 2026; (c) markets priced only 1% probability of Feb 2026 hike. Candidate 2: Schnabel Dec 22 FAZ podcast — explicitly said 'no rate hike expected in the foreseeable future' and clarified she was NOT advocating for rate increases, just against new cuts. This is CONTRADICTORY to the resolution criteria. Candidate 3: Lagarde Dec 18 press conference — said 'all options equal,' 'cannot offer forward guidance,' ECB 'in no rush,' confirmed no rate hike or cut was discussed. REJECTED. Candidate 4: Lagarde Jan 1 Bulgaria statement — focused on euro adoption, no rate hike language. REJECTED. Candidate 5: Villeroy de Galhau Jan 6 — focused on USD reserve status; mentioned France inflation at 0.7% as 'positive news for maintaining favourable interest rates' (actually dovish). REJECTED. Candidate 6: Pereira Jan 8 — said 'price stability achieved,' rates unchanged 4 meetings, 'no immediate need for further policy shifts.' REJECTED. All ECB members either: (a) explicitly say no rate hike in foreseeable future, (b) maintain 'all options equal' stance, or (c) make no statement about February 2026 specifically.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution requires: stronger language than 'possible' or 'on the table' — specifically 'likely,' 'appropriate,' 'needed,' or 'could be justified' — AND this must be in reference to a rate hike AT OR BEFORE the February 2026 meeting. Schnabel's statements: (a) Pre-December 18 Bloomberg: 'comfortable with market expectations' the 'next move' would 'likely be a hike' — this language points to the eventual future direction, NOT specifically at/before Feb 2026; moreover, the February 2026 market probability was only 1-10%, so 'next move' clearly meant much later (2026 end or 2027). (b) Dec 22 FAZ clarification: explicitly 'no rate hike expected in the foreseeable future' — directly contradicts resolution criteria. Lagarde Dec 18 [ECB.europa.eu]: 'data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting,' 'cannot offer forward guidance,' 'no rush to change rates' — does not suggest a hike is likely at/before February 2026. No ECB Governing Council member within the window made a statement suggesting a rate hike is 'likely,' 'appropriate,' 'needed,' or 'could be justified' specifically AT OR BEFORE the February 2026 meeting. The strongest hawkish language refers to eventual future direction (2026-end or 2027) not at/before February 2026.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying statement found. Most recent relevant statements: Schnabel Dec 22 FAZ (explicitly rules out foreseeable hike). Lagarde Dec 18 (no forward guidance, equal optionality). Villeroy Jan 6 (dovish on inflation, no February 2026 hike language). Pereira Jan 8 (price stability achieved, no near-term changes needed).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying statement found within the resolution window. All statements either explicitly deny an imminent hike or maintain neutral optionality language that does not meet the 'likely/appropriate/needed/justified' threshold for at/before February 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove No conclusion: Searched for any ECB Governing Council member using language stronger than 'possible/on the table' to suggest a hike at/before February 2026. Found none. Schnabel's strongest pre-meeting Bloomberg statement was about a potential hike as the 'eventual next move' (with market pricing only ~30% probability by end-2026), not at/before February 2026. Her subsequent Dec 22 clarification explicitly said 'no rate hike expected in the foreseeable future.' Market pricing throughout the window was 0-10% for a February 2026 hike (consistent with no member suggesting it is likely). Villeroy de Galhau's Jan 6 statement was actually slightly dovish. No member used the words 'likely,' 'appropriate,' 'needed,' or 'could be justified' in reference to a hike AT OR BEFORE the February 2026 meeting. The resolution criteria is also notably specific: the hike must be suggested for 'at or before' February 2026, not just eventually.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. All evidence confirms that during the resolution window (Dec 13, 2025 – Jan 12, 2026): (1) ECB President Lagarde maintained equal optionality, explicitly saying the ECB cannot offer forward guidance and is in no rush to change rates; (2) Schnabel, the most hawkish member, clarified on Dec 22 that 'no rate hike is expected in the foreseeable future'; (3) Other Governing Council members (Villeroy, Pereira, Simkus) made no statements suggesting a hike at/before February 2026; (4) Market pricing confirmed essentially zero probability (1%) of a February 2026 hike throughout the window. The condition for Yes — a statement explicitly or implicitly suggesting a rate hike is 'likely,' 'appropriate,' 'needed,' or 'could be justified' AT OR BEFORE the February 2026 meeting — was never met within the window. The window closed on January 12, 2026 without a qualifying statement.

subquestions.question: Will Israel conduct at least one military operation in Gaza involving airstrikes or ground troop movement between October 11, 2025, and November 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

The deal includes a cessation of hostilities, partial Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, and the release of all remaining Israeli hostages in exchange for the release of nearly 2,000 Palestinian prisoners. According to reports, Israeli forces began withdrawing to a designated 'yellow line' within 24 hours of the agreement, and Hamas was given a 72-hour window to return 20 living hostages. Despite the formal ceasefire, tensions remain high, particularly within Israel’s far-right coalition. Ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich have publicly opposed the deal, with Ben-Gvir threatening to bring down the government if it proceeds without guarantees of Hamas’s destruction. The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) remain on high alert, and reports from October 9–10 noted continued bombardments in Gaza City even after the announcement, raising concerns about compliance. Given this context, any resumption of military activity by Israel in the immediate post-ceasefire period could signal a breakdown in the agreement and increase the likelihood of a formal cancellation by either side before the end of 2025.

Given opposition from key Israeli coalition members and the IDF’s continued presence in Gaza, any resumption of operations would suggest the agreement is under severe strain. question: Pedro Sánchez out as PM of Spain in 2025?
description:

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation, is dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Prime Minister of Spain within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Pedro Sánchez face a formal motion of no confidence in the Spanish Congress of Deputies between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pedro Sánchez has led a minority coalition government since 2023, relying on support from smaller regional and left-wing parties to govern. His administration has faced increasing political pressure due to multiple corruption investigations involving his wife, brother, and close political allies, including former party official Santos Cerdán, who was implicated in a €620,000 kickback scheme related to public contracts. Despite calls for his resignation from opposition leaders such as Alberto Núñez Feijóo of the Popular Party, Sánchez has refused to step down and has instead announced a 15-point anti-corruption plan, including an independent public integrity agency and AI-driven fraud detection in public procurement. However, his government has struggled to pass legislation, and opinion polls show the Popular Party leading with 34.4% support compared to the Socialists' 27%. A formal motion of no confidence (moción de censura) requires the support of at least 35 deputies and, if passed, would remove Sánchez from office. While no such motion has been tabled recently, opposition parties have signaled growing frustration, particularly if the 2026 budget fails to pass. The last successful no-confidence motion in Spain occurred in 2018, which brought Sánchez to power. Given the current political instability, a new motion would be a significant indicator of weakening support for his government.

Sources:
- Euronews: https://www.euronews.com/2025/06/12/spain-pm-apologises-after-top-aide-implicated-in-corruption-scandal
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spanish-pm-sanchez-resists-call-elections-promises-overhaul-over-graft-case-2025-06-12/
- The Guardian: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/13/spanish-pm-pedro-sanchez-corruption-scandal-apology
- El País (English): https://english.elpais.com/spain/2025-07-09/sanchez-announces-anti-corruption-plan-amid-political-pressure.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a formal motion of no confidence (moción de censura) against Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is registered and officially announced by the Bureau of the Congress of Deputies (Mesa del Congreso) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). The motion must be submitted in accordance with Article 113 of the Spanish Constitution and published in the official parliamentary record (Diario de Sesiones del Congreso) or announced via the official Congress of Deputies website. Resolution will be based on the official website of the Congress of Deputies (https://www.congreso.es/en) or credible news reporting from at least two major Spanish or international news outlets (e.g., El País, Reuters, AFP, or BBC) confirming the formal registration of the motion. If no such motion is registered during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the motion is announced but later withdrawn before the end date, it still counts as a Yes. If the motion is announced after 2025-10-31, it does not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A formal motion of no confidence is a direct political mechanism to remove the Prime Minister and would signal that opposition parties or even coalition allies believe Sánchez can no longer govern effectively. Given the corruption scandals and low polling numbers, such a motion would indicate increasing instability and a higher likelihood of Sánchez being removed from office before 2026. Even if the motion fails, its mere initiation would reflect a significant escalation in political pressure, making it a strong early indicator of the ultimate question’s outcome. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it focuses on a specific procedural event rather than the outcome of removal itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A formal moción de censura against PM Pedro Sánchez must be registered and officially announced by the Bureau of the Congress of Deputies (Mesa del Congreso) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Observable evidence: official announcement from congreso.es, parliamentary record publication (Diario de Sesiones), or credible news coverage from major Spanish/international outlets confirming formal registration. Key entities: Pedro Sánchez (PM), Congress of Deputies, Article 113 Spanish Constitution.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Pedro Sánchez moción de censura motion of no confidence October 2025' (to find direct evidence of filing); 2) 'Spain Congress Deputies no confidence vote Sanchez 2025' (to find formal registration news); 3) 'moción de censura Sánchez Partido Popular Vox España octubre 2025' (Spanish-language search); 4) 'Junts no confidence motion Sanchez Spain formal filing 2025' (to check if Junts catalyzed a motion); 5) 'Spain opposition Sanchez censure Article 113 Congress registered' (to find formal registration).
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found matching the resolution criteria. Events found include: (1) Junts withdrawing support from Sánchez government (Oct 27-30), but multiple sources explicitly state Junts rejected supporting a no-confidence motion; (2) PP using Senate committee hearings to pressure Sánchez for early elections (Oct 30), not a formal motion of no confidence in Congress; (3) Political pressure and corruption scandals throughout October, but no formal moción de censura filed. The article from cronicadecantabria.com (Oct 26) explicitly states: 'While Junts has consistently rejected supporting a motion of censure against Sánchez, the possibility of an instrumental motion without PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo as candidate remains under discussion.' The Straits Times (Oct 27) notes 'it remains unclear whether Junts would support a future motion of no-confidence against Sánchez, which would require alliance with the conservative People's Party and far-right Vox.'
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No articles report a formal moción de censura being registered, submitted, or announced by the Bureau of the Congress of Deputies during October 2025.
