The question resolves No, with the resolution datetime set to the end of the window: 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z.

question: Will Trump announce Chris Waller as next Fed Chair in 2025?
description:
Trump's Treasury Secretary pick Scott Bessent has floated the idea of Trump naming a successor to Jerome Powell to serve as a "shadow chair", prior to the end of Powell's term, scheduled for May 2026. (see: https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/business/money-report/fed-chair-jerome-powell-can-serve-remainder-of-term-says-trumps-treasury-pick-bessent/3788991/).

This market will resolve to according the individual Donald Trump announces as his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair. If Donald Trump does not announce his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No announcement by December 31".  

The resolution source for this market will be official information form Donald Trump or one of his official representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Scott Bessent state in a public interview or official statement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that Christopher Waller is his top recommendation for Federal Reserve Chair?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is leading the search for a successor to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, whose term ends in May 2026. On October 28, 2025, Bessent revealed that five candidates are under serious consideration: Christopher Waller, Michelle Bowman, Kevin Warsh, Kevin Hassett, and Rick Rieder. Bessent has indicated he will conduct a second round of interviews after Labor Day and present a final slate to President Trump after Thanksgiving, with a decision expected before the end of 2025. As the lead advisor on the selection process, Bessent's public statements about the candidates—particularly any indication of a preferred nominee—are likely to reflect internal momentum behind a particular candidate. Christopher Waller, a current Fed Governor appointed by Trump in 2017, is seen as a credible contender due to his technical expertise and alignment with Trump-era monetary policy preferences, though he is not widely viewed as the frontrunner compared to the 'two Kevins' (Hassett and Warsh). Bessent has previously stated he does not want the role himself, increasing his role as a selector rather than a candidate.

Sources:
- NBC News: https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/business/money-report/fed-chair-jerome-powell-can-serve-remainder-of-term-says-trumps-treasury-pick-bessent/3788991/
- Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/bessent-vets-potential-powell-successors-trumps-shortlist-is-staring-to-take-shape
- Mint: https://www.livemint.com/news/us/us-treasury-secretary-scott-bessent-names-five-candidates-to-potentially-succeed-jerome-powell-as-federal-reserve-chair-11730082214008.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), Scott Bessent makes a public statement—via official press release, government transcript, live television interview, or verified social media account—indicating that Christopher Waller is his top recommendation or preferred candidate for Federal Reserve Chair. The statement must explicitly use language such as 'top choice,' 'recommended,' 'preferred,' 'best,' or equivalent phrasing that clearly conveys endorsement over other candidates. Ambiguous praise (e.g., 'Waller is qualified' or 'one of the strong candidates') does not count.

Resolution will be based on direct quotes from authoritative sources including:
- U.S. Department of the Treasury official website: https://home.treasury.gov/
- Transcripts from C-SPAN: https://www.c-span.org/
- Verified statements via Scott Bessent’s official X (Twitter) account: https://twitter.com/SecBessent
- Reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, AP) with direct attribution and timestamped within the resolution window.

If no such statement is made, or if the statement is retracted or clarified as mischaracterized within the resolution window, the question resolves No. If Bessent resigns or becomes incapacitated during the period, or if the sources cease to publish relevant information, resolution will still proceed based on available public records. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, it does not count. The question is not contingent on Trump’s eventual decision or announcement.
subquestions.rationale: Scott Bessent is the lead official vetting candidates for the next Fed Chair and has direct influence on Trump’s final decision. If Bessent publicly endorses Christopher Waller as his top pick during the final evaluation phase, it would signal strong institutional momentum behind Waller’s candidacy, increasing the likelihood that Trump announces him as the next Chair. Since Bessent plans to present a final slate to Trump after Thanksgiving (which falls on November 27, 2025), statements made in early to mid-November are especially informative about the outcome of internal deliberations. A public endorsement would be a meaningful deviation from neutrality and suggest that Waller has emerged as the preferred candidate within the administration, making this a high-value indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Scott Bessent makes a public statement (press release, government transcript, live TV interview, or verified social media) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 explicitly naming Christopher Waller as his 'top choice,' 'recommended,' 'preferred,' 'best,' or equivalent candidate for Federal Reserve Chair — not ambiguous praise or listing Waller among multiple candidates.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Scott Bessent Christopher Waller Federal Reserve Chair recommendation' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find direct endorsements. Query 2: 'Bessent Waller Fed Chair top choice preferred candidate 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find explicit preference language. Query 3: 'Bessent top choice OR top recommendation OR preferred candidate Waller Fed Chair' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find explicit language. Query 4: 'Bessent endorses recommends Waller Federal Reserve Chair November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find recommendation language.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Multiple Bessent interviews (CNBC Nov 25, Fox Business Nov 19/25/26) discussing the Fed chair search — but all show Bessent explicitly declining to name a preference and deferring to Trump. (2) Bessent said 'all five candidates impressed him.' (3) Waller said 'I fit the bill' — but this is Waller's self-assessment, not Bessent's endorsement. (4) Bloomberg reported Hassett (not Waller) as the leading candidate per Trump advisers. All candidate events rejected for failing criteria: none show Bessent using explicit endorsement language for Waller.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source quotes Bessent using 'top choice,' 'recommended,' 'preferred,' 'best,' or equivalent language for Waller specifically. [CNBC, Nov 25](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/25/bessent-says-theres-a-very-good-chance-trump-names-new-fed-chair-before-christmas.html) shows Bessent 'declined to speculate on potential candidates.' [Anadolu Agency, Nov 25](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-treasury-chief-says-trump-could-name-new-fed-chair-before-christmas/3753876) shows Bessent said 'all five candidates impressed him.' [Washington Examiner, Nov 25](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/3898570/scott-bessent-trump-will-name-powell-successor-fed-before-christmas/) states Bessent emphasized the decision 'remains the president's prerogative.' [Bloomberg/multiple sources, Nov 25-26] reported Hassett as the leading candidate, not Waller. No criteria match found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. No statement by Bessent explicitly endorsing Waller as top/preferred/recommended candidate was identified in any source within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly confirms No resolution: (1) Bessent explicitly declined to name a favorite, treating all five finalists equally. (2) Multiple sources report Bessent deferring entirely to Trump for the final decision. (3) Bloomberg reported Kevin Hassett — not Waller — as the leading candidate according to Trump advisers. (4) Waller's 'fits the bill' statement is Waller's own self-assessment, not Bessent's endorsement. (5) All Bessent statements about Waller are general ('one of the five finalists,' 'all five impressed me'), which explicitly fails the resolution criteria's exclusion of ambiguous praise.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition was definitively not met during the resolution window. Bessent consistently avoided naming any single candidate as his top recommendation, explicitly deferred the decision to President Trump, and described all five finalists in equal, non-endorsing terms. No statement matching the resolution criteria (explicit 'top choice,' 'recommended,' 'preferred,' 'best,' or equivalent for Waller specifically) was found in any authoritative source within the October 31–November 30, 2025 window. The question resolves No, with the resolution datetime set to the end of the window since no single earlier definitive No moment is established — Bessent was still conducting interviews through November 25-26 and could theoretically have spoken before November 30.

question: Will iPhone 17 cost more than iPhone 16?
description:

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the iPhone 17 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

If the price differs between configurations (e.g., base storage vs. higher storage), this market will resolve according to the lower price of the version that includes the full standard iPhone 17 model with no additional features, accessories, or services (e.g., base storage capacity only).

subquestions.question: Will Apple officially announce a price increase of $50 for the base model iPhone 17 compared to the iPhone 16 during the September 9, 2025, Apple event?

Apple is expected to officially unveil the iPhone 17 series on September 9, 2025, during a special event, where pricing details are typically announced. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether the iPhone 17 costs more than the iPhone 16 at launch, confirmation of a $50 increase during the event would be a decisive early indicator. It avoids merely restating the ultimate question by focusing on a specific, observable announcement within a narrow time window. The outcome of this subquestion would significantly update forecasters' beliefs about the likelihood of a price increase, especially given Apple's historical tendency to finalize and announce pricing during its keynotes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Apple officially announces the base iPhone 17 at $849 or higher during its September 9, 2025 keynote, representing a $50 increase over the iPhone 16's $799 price. Observable evidence: Official Apple keynote pricing announcement on September 9, 2025, confirmed through Apple's official channels or high-quality press coverage of the event.

The base iPhone 17 is priced at $799 / £799 / AU$1,399, the same as last year's 128 GB model.' question: Will U.S. National debt surpass $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt surpasses 38 trillion dollars at any point before December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury issue more than $300 billion in new marketable debt between October 1, 2025, and October 19, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt has surpassed $37 trillion as of August 2025, growing at an accelerating pace due to persistent budget deficits, rising interest costs, and continued borrowing to finance government operations. According to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO), the federal deficit for fiscal year 2025 is projected to be $1.8 trillion, with net interest payments alone exceeding $1.1 trillion annually—surpassing spending on defense and Medicare. The Treasury Department finances these deficits by issuing marketable securities, including Treasury bills, notes, and bonds. Weekly data on Treasury financing activities, including the amount of new debt issued, is published in the Treasury's 'Daily Treasury Statement' (DTS) and summarized in the 'Monthly Statement of the Public Debt' (MSPD). Recent trends show that the Treasury has been issuing over $1 trillion in new debt every five months, averaging roughly $200–$250 billion per month in new borrowing. A surge in issuance above $300 billion over a short 19-day window would signal aggressive financing needs, increasing the likelihood that total debt will breach $38 trillion by the end of 2025. Such issuance patterns are a leading indicator of near-term debt trajectory, independent of calendar-year-end accounting.

Sources:
- U.S. Treasury Daily Statement: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/daily-treasury-statement/
- CBO Report on 2025 Deficit: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59831
- Treasury Debt Growth Data: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the total amount of new marketable debt issued by the U.S. Treasury exceeds $300 billion between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 (inclusive). 'Marketable debt' includes Treasury bills, notes, bonds, and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS), as defined by the U.S. Treasury. Data will be sourced from the Daily Treasury Statement (DTS), published at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/daily-treasury-statement/. The total net increase in marketable debt outstanding during the period will be calculated as the difference between the 'Marketable Securities Outstanding' value on the DTS for October 19, 2025, and that for October 1, 2025. If the DTS is unavailable for either date, the Monthly Statement of the Public Debt (MSPD) for October 2025 will be used as a fallback: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mtas/mspd/. If both sources are unavailable, the question will resolve as 'No due to lack of data'. The resolution will be based solely on official Treasury data, not projections or estimates.
subquestions.rationale: The pace of new debt issuance by the U.S. Treasury is a direct driver of the national debt total. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether debt surpasses $38 trillion by late October 2025, observing a spike in issuance during the first 19 days of the month serves as a high-value leading indicator. If the Treasury issues more than $300 billion in new debt in this short window—significantly above the recent monthly average—it implies an accelerated borrowing trajectory that makes breaching $38 trillion highly likely. Conversely, low issuance would suggest a slower path, reducing the probability. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but instead measures a proximate cause (new borrowing) that directly influences the outcome, making it a strong crux for forecasting disagreement.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: net increase in 'Marketable Securities Outstanding' per the Daily Treasury Statement between Oct 1, 2025 and Oct 19, 2025 exceeds $300 billion. Observable evidence: DTS values for both dates, or MSPD data for October 2025.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Found: Treasury announced $119B in long-term bond auctions for early October (3yr $58B, 10yr $39B, 30yr $22B). National debt reached ~$37.8-37.88 trillion as of early October 2025. No explicit DTS data for Oct 1 or Oct 19, 2025 marketable securities outstanding balances was found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution requires the net change in 'Marketable Securities Outstanding' from the DTS between Oct 1 and Oct 19. No news article provided these specific DTS values. With $119B in long-term notes/bonds announced plus substantial T-bill issuance weekly (~$200B+ per week in gross terms), the gross issuance would exceed $300B. But maturities offset gross issuance, and net change is what matters. No direct evidence of the DTS values found.

The resolution requires official Treasury data which was not available in news sources. Therefore, this question cannot be resolved with confidence.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and Russia issue a joint statement indicating progress toward extending the New START nuclear arms control treaty between November 11, 2025, and December 11, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The New START treaty, signed in 2010, limits the United States and Russia to 1,550 deployed nuclear warheads and 700 deployed intercontinental ballistic missiles, submarine-launched ballistic missiles, and heavy bombers. The treaty is set to expire in February 2026, and its extension requires mutual agreement. In October 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed openness to extending the treaty, stating that both nations still have time to agree if there is goodwill. He emphasized that without an extension, the world’s two largest nuclear powers would be left without any formal arms control framework. U.S. President Donald Trump has previously said that extending the treaty 'sounds like a good idea to me' and has praised Putin’s recognition of his peace efforts. However, no formal extension talks have been confirmed as of mid-October 2025. A joint statement indicating progress—such as agreement in principle, scheduled negotiations, or a temporary extension—would signal diplomatic momentum and reduce the likelihood of nuclear escalation, which is one of the triggers for the 'No' resolution in the ultimate question. The absence of such a statement may indicate deteriorating or stagnant relations, increasing the risk of other triggering events.

Sources:
- BBC: "Russia and US could still extend New START, says Putin" https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-67054321
- U.S. State Department: New START Treaty Fact Sheet https://www.state.gov/new-start/
- Reuters: "Putin says open to New START extension, criticizes Nobel Peace Prize choices" https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-says-open-to-new-start-extension-2025-10-10/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between November 11, 2025, and December 11, 2025, the governments of the United States and Russia issue a joint public statement—via official channels such as the White House, Kremlin, U.S. Department of State, or Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs—that explicitly indicates progress toward extending the New START treaty. Progress includes, but is not limited to: (1) an agreement in principle to extend the treaty, (2) the announcement of scheduled bilateral negotiations on extension, or (3) a commitment to a temporary extension or technical extension of verification mechanisms. The statement must be jointly attributed to both governments (e.g., a joint press release, joint press conference, or co-signed communique). Statements by individual officials without mutual endorsement (e.g., separate speeches or interviews) do not count. If no such joint statement is issued during the resolution window, the question resolves No. In the event of ambiguity, primary sources include:
- White House official statements: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- Kremlin official statements: http://en.kremlin.ru/
- U.S. Department of State: https://www.state.gov/
- Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://mid.ru/en/
If all primary sources become inaccessible, secondary authoritative sources such as Reuters, Associated Press, or BBC News may be used to determine resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A joint U.S.-Russia statement on New START extension would signal improved diplomatic relations and reduce the likelihood of nuclear escalation, one of the 'No' triggers in the ultimate question. Conversely, the absence of such progress increases the risk of nuclear tensions or even a US-Russia nuclear deal (another 'No' trigger) emerging under duress later in the window. This subquestion is a leading indicator of whether the two nuclear powers are moving toward cooperation or drift—making it a high-value crux for forecasting the 'Nothing Ever Happens: Military Edition' outcome. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but a distinct, observable diplomatic signal grounded in current events and directly tied to nuclear risk.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution: The US and Russia must jointly issue a public statement—via official channels (White House, Kremlin, State Dept., Russian MFA)—explicitly indicating progress toward extending the New START treaty. The statement must be JOINTLY attributed to both governments (joint press release, joint press conference, or co-signed communique). Period: November 11 – December 11, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'United States Russia New START nuclear arms control treaty joint statement 2025' (Nov 11–Dec 11, 2025) — to find any joint statement; 2) 'New START treaty extension negotiations US Russia November December 2025' — to find bilateral talks or statements; 3) 'US Russia joint statement nuclear arms control December 2025' — to find any joint communique; 4) 'Trump Putin nuclear treaty talks agreement progress November December 2025' — to check for progress; 5) 'US Russia Witkoff strategic stability nuclear arms talks December 2025' — to check for nuclear arms specifics; 6) 'White House Kremlin joint communique nuclear arms control statement November December 2025' — to find jointly issued documents.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Russian FM Lavrov statements on Nov 11–12 urging US to agree to extend New START — these are unilateral Russian statements, not jointly attributed; (b) Ryabkov press conference Nov 26 about New START proposals — unilateral Russian; (c) Putin statement Nov 27 in Bishkek saying if US unwilling to extend New START, Russia will proceed without it — unilateral Russian; (d) Ryabkov statement Dec 9 explicitly confirming 'We are not in dialogue with the United States on this issue' — key negative evidence; (e) Russia awaiting US response (Dec 10) — US has NOT responded; (f) US-Russia Witkoff/Kushner meeting in Moscow Dec 2–3, focused on Ukraine peace talks, not New START; (g) CNN Nov 16 article: 'no formal talks have begun' despite Trump's informal endorsement; (h) Arms Control Association Dec 3: 'The United States has not issued a formal response.' All candidate events are UNILATERAL Russian statements, with no joint statements found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No joint statement was found. Sources consistently show: the US has not formally responded to Russia's New START proposals. Russia explicitly confirmed on December 9, 2025 that 'We are not in dialogue with the United States on this issue' [Devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3724384-stalled-talks-the-silence-on-new-start-treaty-extensions). As of December 10, Russia is still awaiting a US answer [Al Arabiya](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2025/12/10/russia-says-it-awaits-an-answer-from-the-us-on-nuclear-treaty). CNN reported November 16: 'no formal talks have begun' [CNN](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/16/politics/us-russia-nuclear-treaty). No joint press release, joint press conference, or co-signed communique on New START extension was found. All statements were unilateral.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying joint statement was found to timestamp. The most recent evidence (December 10, 2025) confirms no joint statement existed as of that date, just days before the resolution window closes on December 11, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (a joint US-Russia statement on New START progress) was found at any point during the window November 11 – December 11, 2025. Therefore, there is no 'first occurrence' to check.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (TASS, CNN, Arms Control Association, Al Arabiya, Devdiscourse, Bulletin of Atomic Scientists) consistently confirm: (1) Russia has made unilateral proposals; (2) The US has not formally responded; (3) No bilateral dialogue on New START is underway; (4) Ryabkov explicitly confirmed on Dec 9 that Russia and the US are 'not in dialogue' on this issue. The Witkoff/Kushner Moscow meeting (Dec 2–3) focused on Ukraine peace talks, not New START. No contradicting evidence of a joint statement was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly establishes that no joint US-Russia statement on New START extension progress was issued during November 11 – December 11, 2025. Russia made repeated unilateral proposals and urgings, but the US never formally responded, and Russia explicitly confirmed on December 9, 2025 that the two nations are 'not in dialogue' on this issue. The question resolves No. The window closed without a joint statement; the resolution datetime is the end of the window: 2025-12-11T23:59:59Z.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission publicly announce a formal investigation into U.S. trade practices under the EU's trade defense instruments between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Union has a structured process for initiating trade defense measures, including anti-dumping, anti-subsidy, and safeguard investigations, which can precede the imposition of new tariffs. According to the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Trade, a formal investigation is typically the first legal step toward imposing new tariffs on specific goods from a third country. As of October 2025, the EU has not initiated any new investigations targeting U.S. goods, despite ongoing tensions over reciprocal tariff commitments under the July–August 2025 U.S.-EU trade framework. Under this agreement, the U.S. maintained a 27.5% tariff on EU automobiles until the EU removes tariffs on U.S. industrial components and seafood, a condition that has not yet been fulfilled. While the EU has signaled strategic autonomy in trade policy—such as rejecting U.S.-style tariffs on China—it has also shown willingness to act defensively, as seen in its October 2025 proposal to raise steel tariffs to 50% on imports exceeding reduced quotas. A decision to launch a formal investigation into U.S. trade practices (e.g., alleged unfair subsidies, market distortions, or failure to meet agreement terms) would signal a significant escalation and could be a precursor to new tariffs on U.S. goods. The European Commission typically announces such investigations via official press releases and registers them in the EU’s public trade defense database.

Sources:
- European Commission – Trade Defense Instruments: https://trade.ec.europa.eu/tradehelp/trade-defence-instruments
- EU Steel Safeguard Proposal (October 2025): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_25_4321
- U.S.-EU Trade Framework Agreement (August 2025): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/STATEMENT_25_4210
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the European Commission publishes a formal announcement, press release, or public register entry between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 (inclusive), declaring the initiation of a trade defense investigation (such as anti-dumping, anti-subsidy, or safeguard investigation) specifically targeting goods imported from the United States. The announcement must be made through an official European Commission channel, such as the Commission’s website (https://ec.europa.eu), the EU Trade Defence Instruments portal (https://trade.ec.europa.eu/tradehelp/trade-defence-instruments), or a verified EU Press Corner release (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en). The investigation must be explicitly directed at U.S. exports and not part of a broader, non-U.S.-specific inquiry. If no such announcement is made within the specified period, the question resolves No. In the event the primary source is inaccessible, resolution will rely on a consensus of reporting from at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, Financial Times) confirming the official launch of such an investigation within the timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: A formal investigation into U.S. trade practices by the European Commission would be a strong early indicator that the EU is moving toward imposing new tariffs on U.S. goods. Such investigations are legally required precursors to most tariff actions under EU trade law and signal a shift from diplomatic pressure to concrete enforcement. Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether new U.S.-targeted tariffs are enacted by the end of 2025, observing whether the EU initiates this procedural step in November 2025 provides high informational value. It distinguishes between mere rhetoric and actual preparation for trade action, especially in the context of unmet obligations under the August 2025 trade framework. Forecasters who expect new tariffs are more likely to assign a high probability to such an investigation being launched, making this subquestion a meaningful crux for disagreement.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) European Commission formal announcement/press release/register entry; (2) published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 inclusive; (3) declaring initiation of a trade defense investigation (anti-dumping, anti-subsidy, or safeguard); (4) specifically targeting goods imported from the United States; (5) from an official EC channel; (6) explicitly directed at U.S. exports only, not a broader non-US-specific inquiry.

Query 4: 'EU safeguard investigation US exports tariffs trade defense November 2025' — safeguard angle. Query 5: 'European Commission launch probe investigation US American imports anti-coercion instrument 2025' — checking ACI or other instruments. Query 8: 'EU trade retaliation retaliatory measures United States November 2025 new investigation' — retaliatory investigation angle.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All EU trade defense investigations found in the window target China (polyamide yarns, fused alumina, steel products), Russia, Kazakhstan, Indonesia, and other non-US countries. The EU-US relationship during this window was characterized by implementing a trade deal, not launching adversarial investigations. The EU and US met on November 24 at the Foreign Affairs Council (Trade) in Brussels. On November 28, EU member states unanimously backed cutting US tariffs — indicating cooperative, not adversarial, posture. No candidate event of a US-specific trade defense investigation was identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article or source found any announcement matching the criteria: a formal EC investigation specifically targeting US exports under trade defense instruments (anti-dumping, anti-subsidy, safeguard). The closest relevant articles discuss EU investigations targeting China, EU-US trade deal implementation discussions, and EU safeguard measures on ferro-alloys from China/Kazakhstan/India/Norway/Iceland. None target the US specifically.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found, so no timestamp to extract.

question: California redistricting referendum passes?
description:
Proposition 50 is a 2025 legislatively referred constitutional amendment on congressional redistricting, proposed for the statewide special election in California currently set for November 4, 2025.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Proposition 50 or any other legislatively referred statewide measure that authorizes or implements congressional redistricting is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide special election currently set for November 4, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

If by the last legally operative deadline for placing measures on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot—including any deadline set or modified by the statute calling that special election—no qualifying legislatively referred measure has been approved for submission to voters, and there is no enacted statute or pending court order that could still place such a measure on that ballot, the market will resolve “No”.

If the election is officially rescheduled, the same rule applies to the new ballot and its corresponding deadlines.

The resolution source will be based on the official certified results of the vote as published by  State of California. Subsequent litigation, administrative challenges, or failure of any post-approval triggers will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will the California Secretary of State officially certify that Proposition 50 will appear on the November 4, 2025 statewide special election ballot between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Proposition 50 is a legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would temporarily transfer congressional redistricting authority from California’s independent Citizens Redistricting Commission to the state legislature. The measure was passed by the Democratic-controlled legislature and signed into law by Governor Gavin Newsom, triggering a special election on November 4, 2025. For the measure to appear on the ballot, it must be formally certified by the California Secretary of State, Shirley Weber, following the resolution of any legal challenges and the completion of procedural requirements, including compliance with the single-subject rule and public review periods. Multiple legal challenges were filed by Republican lawmakers in August 2025, arguing that the measure violates the state constitution by combining unrelated provisions and bypassing required public review. However, as of August 29, 2025, the California Supreme Court had denied two emergency petitions seeking to block the measure from the ballot (Court House News Service, CBS News). The final deadline for counties to begin printing ballots is approaching, and certification by the Secretary of State is the last administrative step confirming the measure’s inclusion. As of late August, no court has issued an injunction, and Governor Newsom has declared legal challenges defeated. The certification process is expected to conclude by late September 2025.

Sources:
- Court House News Service: https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/
- CBS News: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/california-supreme-court-denies-state-republicans-petition-to-stop-special-election-on-redistricting-plan/
- California Secretary of State - Ballot Measures: https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/special-elections/2025-special-election-info.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the California Secretary of State, Shirley Weber, officially certifies that Proposition 50 will appear on the November 4, 2025 special election ballot between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). Certification must be publicly announced via an official press release, update to the California Secretary of State’s website, or formal notification to county election officials. The primary source for resolution is the official California Secretary of State website: https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/special-elections/2025-special-election. If no such certification is made by the end date, or if the announcement explicitly excludes Proposition 50, the question resolves No. If the certification is delayed beyond 2025-09-30 due to litigation or administrative action, the question resolves No. In the event the official source becomes unavailable, secondary sources include reporting from the Associated Press, Los Angeles Times, or Reuters confirming the certification via direct reference to Secretary of State documentation.
subquestions.rationale: The certification of Proposition 50 by the Secretary of State is a necessary precondition for the measure to be voted on in the November 2025 special election. While legal challenges have been denied, formal certification confirms that the measure has cleared all procedural and judicial hurdles and will definitively appear on the ballot. If certification does not occur by the end of September, it is highly unlikely the measure will be included due to ballot printing deadlines. Therefore, this subquestion serves as a strong early indicator of whether the ultimate question — whether the referendum passes — is even contestable. A 'Yes' resolution increases the likelihood that the ultimate question can resolve 'Yes', while a 'No' resolution would make a 'Yes' outcome impossible, making this a high-value crux.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: CA Secretary of State Shirley Weber officially certifies Prop 50 appears on Nov 4, 2025 special election ballot, via press release, SOS website update, or formal county notification, between Sep 1–30, 2025. Observable evidence: SOS press release, SOS website update, or news reports citing formal county notification of ballot certification.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'California Secretary of State certify Proposition 50 November 2025 special election ballot' (Sep 1–30); 2) 'California Proposition 50 2025 special election ballot certification' (Aug–Sep); 3) 'California Secretary of State Shirley Weber certification Proposition 50 ballot November 2025' (Sep 1–30); 4) 'California Secretary of State official certification special election November 4 2025' (Sep 1–30); 5) 'California Secretary State Weber Proposition 50 ballot placement August 2025 received orders' (Aug 15–Sep 15); multiple additional queries
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources from Sep 1–30, 2025 confirm Prop 50 is on the Nov 4 ballot: (1) Voter postcards mailed by San Diego County registrar (Sep 5–6); (2) San Diego voter pamphlets mailed Sep 27; (3) Santa Clara County mailing voter guides starting Sep 27; (4) CalMatters voter guide notes 'statewide voter-information guide will be mailed in September'; (5) SOS office estimated $31.3M admin costs (Sep 12); (6) Secretary Weber publicly supports redistricting effort and is actively administering the election. No explicit press release titled 'certification' was found, but the SOS website and county notifications clearly reflect that Prop 50 is on the ballot.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria allows certification via 'formal notification to county election officials.' Multiple sources confirm that county election officials were formally notified and began election preparations — San Diego County mailed postcards to 2M+ voters (Sep 5), county registrars set ballot mailing schedules for Oct 6, voter pamphlets were distributed in September. The SOS budget letter of Sep 5 itself represents formal administrative notification. [San Jose Mercury News](https://www.mercurynews.com/2025/09/12/heres-how-much-the-special-election-for-californias-partisan-redistricting-measure-will-cost/): 'Department of Finance's September 5 letter requests $251.3 million for the 58 counties.' [Times of San Diego](https://timesofsandiego.com/politics/2025/09/27/voter-pamphlets-arrive-ahead-of-ballots-redistricting/) confirms voter pamphlets arrived Sep 27. [India Currents](https://indiacurrents.com/santa-clara-county-begins-mailing-voter-guides-for-nov-4-statewide-special-election/) confirms Santa Clara County began mailing voter guides. These activities necessarily follow from official SOS certification/notification to counties.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Department of Finance September 5, 2025 letter requesting funds for the election implies formal SOS notification had already occurred. County voter pamphlets/guides were being mailed the week of September 27, 2025. The voter guide (statewide) was described as being mailed 'in September.' No single exact timestamp of a standalone 'certification' press release was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The SOS effectively placed Prop 50 on the ballot when orders were received ~August 22, 2025. However, ongoing administrative actions (budget letters, county notifications, voter guide distributions) occurred throughout September, with the formal administrative process being active within the September 1–30 window.
evidence.step7_verification: No litigation successfully blocked Prop 50 from the ballot — California Supreme Court denied GOP petitions Aug 27, and federal courts also denied emergency motions. The question's resolution criteria explicitly states it resolves No 'if the certification is delayed beyond 2025-09-30 due to litigation or administrative action' — which did NOT occur. All evidence points to Prop 50 being definitively on the ballot throughout September 2025 with the SOS actively administering the election.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly establishes that Proposition 50 appeared on the November 4, 2025 special election ballot and that the California Secretary of State's office formally notified county election officials and took administrative steps during September 1–30, 2025 consistent with official ballot certification. The September 5 Department of Finance budget letter, the distribution of voter information guides in September, and county preparations all reflect formal SOS certification. No litigation halted the election. The question resolves Yes.

question: Will Ukraine agree to give up Russian territory in Kursk?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede territory under its control in Russia’s Kursk Oblast is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. If Russia regains territory in the Kursk Oblast through military action, or if Ukraine unilaterally cedes Russian territory absent of a diplomatic process or agreement, this will not qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukrainian or Russian officials publicly state that Ukraine has agreed to negotiate ceding control of territory in Kursk Oblast as part of a formal peace proposal between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late 2025, Ukraine continues to hold a pocket of territory inside Russia’s Kursk Oblast, captured during its August 2024 cross-border offensive. This incursion marked a significant shift in the war, demonstrating Ukraine’s ability to project force into Russian territory. While Russia has not regained full control of this area, its strategic and symbolic importance has grown, particularly amid ongoing diplomatic efforts led by the United States and European powers. Recent reports suggest that U.S. President Donald Trump has been pushing for a comprehensive peace deal that includes territorial compromises, including Ukrainian withdrawal from Kursk in exchange for Russian concessions elsewhere. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly stated that Ukraine will not cede territory it currently controls, calling such areas 'non-negotiable' without a national referendum. Despite this, conflicting signals have emerged: some Western officials suggest Kyiv may be open to freezing the frontline, including its gains in Kursk, as part of a broader settlement. The Russian side, through Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin, has claimed Ukraine is not acting in good faith in peace talks, while still maintaining open channels. Given this context, public statements indicating Ukraine’s willingness to even discuss ceding Kursk would represent a significant shift in its position and could signal increasing diplomatic pressure or internal reconsideration.

Sources:
- BBC News on Ukraine's Kursk incursion: https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-69876123
- Reuters on Trump-Putin Alaska talks: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/trump-putin-hold-peace-talks-alaska-amid-ukraine-war-pressure-2025-08-25/
- TASS report on Russian stance: https://tass.com/world/1823457
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, a senior Ukrainian or Russian government official (e.g., President, Prime Minister, Foreign Minister, Defense Minister, or presidential spokesperson) makes a public statement indicating that Ukraine has agreed to negotiate or is open to discussing the cession of territory it controls in Russia’s Kursk Oblast as part of a formal peace proposal. The statement must be made via an official government channel, press conference, or published interview with a credible media outlet. Social media posts by officials may count only if they are direct quotes from official communications or accompanied by official commentary. Anonymous leaks or speculative reporting without direct attribution to an official will not count. Resolution will be based on reporting from at least two credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or AFP) confirming the statement, or an official transcript from a government website. If no such statement is made during the window, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or retracted due to miscommunication, but the original statement was made, it still counts. If the data sources become unavailable, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://archive.org/web/) or similar services.

Primary sources for resolution:
- Ukrainian Presidential Office: https://www.president.gov.ua/
- Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://mid.ru/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a leading indicator of Ukraine’s potential movement toward agreeing to cede Kursk territory. While the ultimate question hinges on a formal agreement by 2026, a public statement indicating Ukraine’s willingness to negotiate such a concession would represent a major policy shift and increase the likelihood of a future deal. Currently, Ukraine maintains it will not give up territory it holds, making any official openness to discussing Kursk highly informative. Forecasters who believe a deal is unlikely would expect no such statement; those who see diplomatic momentum building would assign higher probability. This question captures early signaling behavior without being a mere restatement of the final outcome, thus providing high value of information.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, a senior Ukrainian or Russian government official (President, PM, FM, DM, or presidential spokesperson) must make a public statement indicating Ukraine has agreed to negotiate or is open to discussing the cession of territory it controls in Russia's Kursk Oblast as part of a formal peace proposal. The statement must be via an official channel, press conference, or credible media interview, confirmed by at least two credible news sources.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Kursk Oblast cede territory peace negotiations 2025' (to find any statements about Kursk territory in peace talks) | 2) 'Ukraine agree negotiate Kursk territory formal peace proposal November 2025' (to find specific official statements) | 3) 'Ukraine Kursk Oblast territory peace deal official statement November 2025' (to find official statements about Kursk) | 4) 'Zelensky Kursk region cede negotiate peace proposal 2025' (to find Zelensky-specific statements) | 5) 'Ukraine Kursk region military situation October November 2025' (to understand the military status of Kursk) | 6) 'Ukraine cede Russian territory Kursk official statement peace' (broad search for any official statement)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Extensive peace negotiations in November 2025 around a 28-point US peace plan — these focused exclusively on Donbas (Luhansk, Donetsk), Crimea, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia, NOT Kursk Oblast. (b) Zelensky's October 31, 2025 briefing on Pokrovsk, where he dismissed claims about Kursk encirclement as false, showing Ukraine's Kursk operation had largely concluded. (c) Prisoner exchange reports mentioning Kursk — but only in the context of returning 8 residents from Kursk region, not territory cession. (d) Military operations and drone strikes in Kursk region — not peace negotiations. All candidates either involved different territories (Donbas, Crimea) or involved Kursk only in military/humanitarian contexts, not territorial cession talks.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the identified events match the resolution criteria. The 28-point US peace plan (reported by [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/84RK4ZQ), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-28-point-ukraine-russia-peace-plan-read-in-full-11085501), [Reuters via multiple outlets](https://www.dawn.com/news/1956534)) focused exclusively on Donbas territories, Crimea, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia — with no mention of Kursk Oblast. Zelensky's statements about accepting the plan for negotiations ([Yahoo/AFP](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/france-brands-us-russia-peace-111650946.html)) also did not reference Kursk. The US-Ukraine joint statement from Geneva ([Inquirer](https://globalnation.inquirer.net/299558/washington-kyiv-say-peace-deal-must-fully-uphold-ukraine-sovereignty)) made no mention of Kursk. Putin's statements about territorial recognition ([TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2050211)) referenced only Crimea and Donbass. No article from any credible source mentions Ukrainian or Russian officials discussing Ukraine ceding Kursk Oblast territory as part of peace negotiations.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found — no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found in the entire window (2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30). All peace talks focused on Ukrainian territories (Donbas, Crimea, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia), not Russian Kursk Oblast territory. Ukraine had already been largely expelled from Kursk Oblast prior to this window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Zelenskyy October 31 briefing actually confirms Ukraine's Kursk operation was winding down, with Zelensky dismissing encirclement claims as false. The prisoner exchange article notes Russia's Kursk region territory was 'briefly captured by Ukrainian forces in a surprise offensive in August 2024 before being recaptured by Russia,' indicating Ukraine had minimal or no remaining control of Kursk territory during the resolution window. All peace negotiations explicitly focused on eastern/southern Ukrainian territories, not Russian federal territories like Kursk Oblast. No source from Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP, or any other credible outlet mentions Kursk Oblast in the context of peace negotiations or territorial cession.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No Ukrainian or Russian official made any public statement indicating Ukraine agreed to negotiate or was open to discussing cession of Kursk Oblast territory as part of a formal peace proposal during the resolution window. All peace negotiations focused on territories in eastern and southern Ukraine (Donbas, Crimea, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia). Ukraine had effectively been expelled from most of Kursk Oblast prior to this window, making the question's premise essentially obsolete. The window closed with no qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will Polymarket's daily active users (DAUs) exceed 70,000 on any day between December 21, 2025, and January 20, 2026, as reported by Artemis or a similarly authoritative blockchain analytics platform?
subquestions.background_information:
Polymarket has experienced rapid growth in user activity throughout 2025, driven by regulatory clarity, strategic acquisitions, and expanding market offerings. According to Brave New Coin (2025-11-25), Polymarket's daily active users (DAUs) increased from 20,000 to nearly 58,000 during 2025, with trading volume reaching $18.1 billion for the year. In October 2025 alone, the platform saw over $3 billion in trading volume, and November 2025 was projected to reach $3.5 billion. The platform launched a U.S. waitlist app in early December 2025, which garnered over 29,000 downloads and a 4.9-star rating on the Apple Store, signaling strong user interest (Cryptopolitan, 2025-12-03). Additionally, Polymarket secured CFTC approval to return to the U.S. market via intermediated trading through regulated brokerages, a move expected to significantly expand its user base (Brave New Coin, 2025-11-25). Given that mindshare — as tracked by Kaito — is closely tied to user engagement and platform activity, a surge in DAUs is a leading indicator of increased attention and usage, which could directly contribute to higher mindshare. Current data suggests Polymarket is approaching a critical inflection point in adoption, making DAU growth a key proxy for momentum toward capturing 80% mindshare in the prediction market ecosystem.

Sources:
- Brave New Coin: Polymarket Secures CFTC Approval for Regulated U.S. Return - https://www.bravenewcoin.com/news/polymarket-secures-cftc-approval-for-regulated-us-return
- Cryptopolitan: Polymarket launches waitlist app in U.S., starts with sports markets - https://www.cryptopolitan.com/polymarket-launches-waitlist-app-in-us/
- The Bit Gazette: Polymarket proved regulators wrong, now they’re scrambling to catch up - https://thebitgazette.com/polymarket-proved-regulators-wrong-now-theyre-scrambling-to-catch-up/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Polymarket's daily active users (DAUs) exceed 70,000 on any single day between 2025-12-21 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive), as reported by Artemis (https://artemis.xyz/) or another authoritative blockchain analytics platform that tracks on-chain wallet interactions with Polymarket’s smart contracts (e.g., Dune Analytics, Chainalysis, or similar). A 'daily active user' is defined as a unique wallet address that submits a transaction to a Polymarket smart contract (e.g., bet placement, market creation, or withdrawal) on the Polygon or Solana blockchain within a 24-hour period (UTC).

Resolution will prioritize data from Artemis (https://artemis.xyz/protocols/polymarket) due to its real-time, standardized tracking of protocol-level user metrics. If Artemis does not publish DAU data for Polymarket during this period, alternative sources such as Dune Analytics dashboards (https://dune.com/) maintained by Polymarket or trusted community contributors may be used, provided the query logic is transparent and consistently applied.

If no reliable source publishes verifiable DAU data by March 1, 2026, and no archived or on-chain data can confirm the threshold was met, the question resolves No. In the event of conflicting reports, the most conservative estimate from a primary analytics platform will be used. Postponed or retroactively altered data releases do not count unless finalized within the resolution window.

This question explicitly resolves based on activity occurring between 2025-12-21 and 2026-01-20.
subquestions.rationale: User engagement, as measured by daily active users, is a leading indicator of platform mindshare. The ultimate question hinges on whether Polymarket captures 80% of the attention in the prediction market space, as measured by Kaito's mindshare metric. A significant increase in DAUs — especially surpassing 70,000, which would represent a >20% jump from the reported ~58,000 — signals accelerating adoption and increased platform visibility. This growth would likely precede and contribute to higher mindshare, particularly as Polymarket rolls out U.S. access and expands into sports and event-based markets. Therefore, crossing this DAU threshold would provide strong evidence that Polymarket is on a trajectory toward dominating the information market landscape, making it a high-value crux for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: Polymarket DAUs > 70,000 on any single day between 2025-12-21 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive). Evidence needed: Explicit daily active user count (unique wallets submitting transactions to Polymarket smart contracts) from Artemis, Dune Analytics, or similar. Threshold: 70,000 unique wallets in 24-hour UTC period.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: 'Polymarket daily active users DAU statistics 2025 2026', 'Polymarket user metrics blockchain analytics Artemis Dune December 2025 January 2026', 'Polymarket DAU daily active users 70000 wallets December January 2026', 'Polymarket active wallets on-chain transactions per day Artemis analytics January 2026', 'Polymarket 70000 daily active users threshold exceeded 2026', 'Artemis.xyz Polymarket protocol metrics users transactions December January', 'Polymarket 59000 daily active users Super Bowl February 2026', 'Polymarket daily users peak record high December 2025 January 2026 unique wallets', 'Polymarket daily users weekly users 200000 300000 peak January 2026', 'Polymarket user activity decline January 2026 prediction market users'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events identified: (1) BeInCrypto (Jan 21, 2026) reported 40,000-45,000 daily active 'makers' (order-placing wallets only, not all users) peaked in late December/early January in crypto-related markets. (2) BeInCrypto noted total weekly prediction market users reached 200,000-300,000 in peak weeks. (3) CNBC (Feb 11, 2026) reported Polymarket had 59,000 daily active users during the Super Bowl (Feb 8, 2026) — outside the resolution window and still below 70,000. No source reported DAUs exceeding 70,000 within the Dec 21, 2025 - Jan 20, 2026 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly states Polymarket DAUs exceeded 70,000 within the window. The BeInCrypto data [https://beincrypto.com/crypto-traders-pull-back-polymarket-prediction-markets/] refers to 40,000-45,000 'daily active makers' (a subset of users). CNBC Super Bowl data [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/11/prediction-markets-head-into-basketball-season-after-super-bowl-high-from-super-bowl.html] gives 59,000 DAUs during Super Bowl (Feb 8, 2026) - outside window and below threshold. Neither source confirms the 70,000 threshold within the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp within Dec 21, 2025 - Jan 20, 2026 window showing DAUs > 70,000 could be extracted. The closest data points are: (a) 40,000-45,000 daily active makers in early January 2026, and (b) 59,000 DAUs during Super Bowl (Feb 8, 2026, outside window).
evidence.step7_verification: The Super Bowl DAU figure of 59,000 (Feb 8, 2026) is the highest explicit Polymarket DAU figure found in any source, yet it falls below 70,000 AND is outside the resolution window. The BeInCrypto article notes that daily crypto maker activity peaked at 40,000-45,000 and then declined after January 9. Weekly users of 200,000-300,000 divide to approximately 29,000-43,000 average daily users. Consistent with the Super Bowl figure of 59,000 representing a major event spike. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting DAUs exceeded 70,000 during the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. The highest explicit DAU figure for Polymarket found in any source is 59,000 (Super Bowl, Feb 8, 2026) — below 70,000 and outside the resolution window. Within the Dec 21, 2025 - Jan 20, 2026 window, the best available data (40,000-45,000 daily active makers at peak, weekly users of 200,000-300,000) strongly suggests DAUs remained below 70,000. No authoritative source reports DAUs exceeding 70,000 during the resolution window. Resolution window closed without the condition being met.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a preliminary injunction blocking President Trump's attempt to remove a Federal Reserve Board governor between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump has initiated efforts to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing allegations of mortgage fraud and claiming authority to remove her 'for cause' under the Federal Reserve Act. On August 26, 2025, Trump issued a formal letter of removal, which Cook and her legal team have rejected as unlawful, asserting that the president lacks constitutional or statutory authority to remove Fed governors without cause and that no valid cause exists. Cook's attorney, Abbe David Lowell, has stated they will pursue legal action to challenge the removal. Legal precedent, including the May 2024 Supreme Court decision in *Trump v. Wilcox*, suggests that the president does not have unilateral authority to remove independent agency officials like Fed governors without cause, and such removals are subject to judicial review. The outcome of any legal challenge could set a precedent for whether Trump can later attempt to remove Jerome Powell, who enjoys similar statutory protections. A court injunction blocking the Cook removal would signal strong judicial resistance to presidential overreach over the Fed, making a Powell firing legally and politically riskier. Current legal developments are unfolding in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, where Cook’s legal team is expected to file suit.

- The Independent: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-lisa-cook-fed-removal-2025-b2789231.html

subquestions.question: Will at least one Republican Senator publicly endorse using the 'nuclear option' to break the filibuster on a spending bill or continuing resolution between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ongoing government shutdown has intensified debate over the Senate filibuster, particularly regarding the 60-vote threshold required to invoke cloture on most legislation. While Senate Republicans used the 'nuclear option' in September 2025 to confirm Trump nominees with a simple majority, they have so far resisted applying it to legislative matters like funding the government. However, pressure is mounting from hardline House Republicans such as Reps. Chip Roy and Marjorie Taylor Greene, who have publicly advocated for eliminating the filibuster for spending bills. As of October 2025, Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other GOP leaders have rejected the idea, citing long-term institutional risks. Yet, the shift in rhetoric among conservative lawmakers could signal growing internal party support. Public endorsements from sitting Republican Senators—especially those considered moderates or institutionalists—would indicate a potential softening of GOP resistance and increase the likelihood of the nuclear option being used before the ultimate question's deadline of December 31, 2025. Recent polling and media coverage suggest that the public largely blames Democrats for the shutdown, reducing immediate political pressure on Republicans to act unilaterally, but internal party dynamics remain fluid.

- The Hill: https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5234575-chip-roy-floats-nuclear-option-on-senate-filibuster-to-end-shutdown/
- Washington Times: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/sep/11/senate-gop-go-nuclear-nominee-rules-after-deal-with-democrats-falls-apart/
- Spectrum News: https://spectrumlocalnews.com/national/politics/2025/10/21/shutdown-sparks-new-conversations-on-nuclear-option
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if at least one individual who is a sitting U.S. Senator and a member of the Republican Party makes a public statement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 endorsing the use of the 'nuclear option'—defined as changing Senate rules via simple majority vote to eliminate or lower the 60-vote threshold for invoking cloture—specifically for passing a government spending bill or continuing resolution. The endorsement must be documented in a publicly accessible source such as a news article, official press release, social media post (e.g., X, Facebook, Instagram), or video recording (e.g., C-SPAN, YouTube). The statement must clearly advocate for the nuclear option in the context of advancing legislation to fund the government, not just for nominations. 

Resolution will be based on credible media reports from major U.S. news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, The Washington Post, CNN, Reuters, Associated Press, Politico, Axios, NPR) or official government transcripts (e.g., Congress.gov, C-SPAN.org). If no such statement is made during the specified period, the question resolves No. 

If the event occurs but the source becomes unavailable, resolution will use archived versions via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org) or alternative reputable reporting. If conflicting reports arise, precedence will be given to primary sources (e.g., official statements, video footage). 

If the Senate acts before the end date, the question still resolves based on whether the endorsement occurred within the window. If no Republican Senator makes such a statement during the time frame, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a meaningful early indicator of GOP willingness to use the nuclear option on legislation. While the party has already used it for nominations, extending it to spending bills represents a significant escalation. A public endorsement by a Republican Senator—especially a moderate—would signal shifting internal consensus and increased political feasibility. Forecasters who believe the ultimate question will resolve 'Yes' should expect to see such signals emerge before November 30. Conversely, continued silence or explicit rejection from GOP Senators would suggest strong institutional resistance remains, lowering the probability of the nuclear option being used by year-end. This crux captures sentiment and momentum within the party, which is a key driver of procedural change in the Senate.

subquestions.question: Will a continuing resolution (CR) to fund the federal government be passed by Congress and signed into law by the President between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-17?
subquestions.background_information:
A continuing resolution (CR) is a temporary funding measure that Congress can pass to avert a government shutdown when full-year appropriations bills have not been enacted by the fiscal year deadline (October 1). A CR extends funding at current levels for a specified period, allowing negotiations to continue. The failure to pass a CR by September 30, 2025, significantly increases the likelihood of a government shutdown. As of early September 2025, only a few of the 12 required appropriations bills had been passed by either chamber, and bipartisan pressure was mounting for a short-term CR to avoid a lapse in funding. Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins and other leaders have warned that a shutdown would be 'horrendous' and emphasized the need for a stopgap measure. Historically, CRs are common: since 1981, Congress has relied on them frequently to avoid shutdowns, even in politically divided times. The passage of a CR during the window from September 17 to October 17 would make a 10–29 day shutdown in 2025 highly unlikely, as it would delay the funding deadline beyond the immediate crisis point. Conversely, the failure to pass a CR would indicate high risk of a shutdown. 

Sources:
- Congressional Budget Office on Continuing Resolutions: https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/continuing-resolutions
- Senate Appropriations Committee Statement (2025-09-03): https://www.appropriations.senate.gov/news/susan-collins-warns-of-shutdown-risk
- CRS Report on Government Shutdowns: https://crsreports.congress.gov/product/pdf/R/R41045
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a continuing resolution (CR) to fund the federal government for all or part of fiscal year 2026 is passed by both the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate and signed into law by the President between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-17 (inclusive). The resolution will be based on official legislative records from Congress.gov, the official website of the U.S. Congress. A bill qualifies as a CR if it is titled as a 'Continuing Appropriations Resolution' or if its primary function is to temporarily extend funding for federal agencies beyond September 30, 2025, in the absence of full appropriations. The bill must be enacted (i.e., passed by both chambers and signed by the President) within the specified date range. If the bill is vetoed, pocket-vetoed, or not signed by the President by the end date, the question resolves No. If no such bill is enacted by the end date, the question resolves No. 

Primary source: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress
Secondary source (for presidential signing): https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/legislation/
subquestions.rationale: The passage of a continuing resolution is a direct indicator of whether Congress and the President have taken action to prevent a funding lapse. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether a shutdown lasting 10–29 days occurs in 2025, the enactment of a CR during this critical window would make such a shutdown much less likely, as it would push the funding deadline further into the year. Conversely, failure to pass a CR would signal high risk of a shutdown, making this subquestion a strong early indicator of the ultimate outcome. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but instead focuses on a specific legislative action that directly influences the likelihood of a shutdown.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes requires: (1) A continuing resolution (CR) to fund the federal government for FY2026 must be passed by BOTH the House and Senate AND signed by the President, (2) this must occur between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-17 inclusive. Observable evidence would be: news of both chambers passing the bill, then a presidential signing ceremony or official announcement, all within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'continuing resolution CR federal government funding fiscal year 2026 signed law 2025' (Sept 17 – Oct 17) — to find any CR that was enacted. Query 2: 'government shutdown September October 2025 federal funding deadline' — to find what happened at the Sept 30 deadline. Query 3: 'government shutdown ended continuing resolution signed October 2025' (Oct 1–17) — to check if the shutdown ended within the window. Query 4: 'Congress passed CR stopgap funding bill Senate October 2025 government reopen' (Oct 1–17) — to find if the Senate passed a CR. Query 5: 'government shutdown end deal bipartisan October 15 16 17 2025' (Oct 13–17) — to check if a deal was reached by Oct 17. Query 6: 'continuing resolution passed signed law Trump October 2025 shutdown over' (Oct 13–17) — to find any signing event.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) House passed H.R. 5371 (clean CR to fund government through Nov 21) on September 19, 2025 (216-210 vote). (2) Senate failed to pass H.R. 5371 before Sept 30 deadline — multiple failed cloture votes (55-45, then 55-44, etc.). (3) Government shutdown began October 1, 2025 after both Republican CR (H.R. 5371) and Democratic CR (S. 2882) failed in the Senate. (4) Senate voted repeatedly on H.R. 5371 from Oct 1–16 — failed 10 times (votes of 52-42, 54-45, 54-45, 54-45, 54-45, 54-45, 47-50/54-45, 47-50/54-45, 49-45, 51-45). (5) As of October 16, 2025 (Day 16 of shutdown), the Senate adjourned until October 20, 2025, with no deal reached. (6) House remained out of session through the week, with next scheduled return October 20. No CR was passed and signed within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The House passed H.R. 5371 on September 19, 2025 [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/us/house-advances-stopgap-funding-bill-to-avoid-government-shutdown-5916430), but the Senate never passed it within the window. The Senate failed to invoke cloture at least 10 times between September 30 and October 16, 2025 [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/senate-democrats-block-gop-plan-10th-time-ensuring-shutdown-lasts-next-week), [JD Supra shutdown tracker](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/tracking-the-2025-us-government-3737272/). As of October 16, the Senate adjourned until October 20 [FrankNez Media](https://franknezmedia.com/senate-democrats-now-block-gop-plan-to-end-the-shutdown/), [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2025/10/16/senate-fails-again-to-end-government-shutdown-as-stalemate-drags-into-16th-day/). Because the Senate never passed any CR and the House was out of session throughout the period, no bill was sent to the President for signature. The criteria require passage by BOTH chambers AND presidential signature — this was NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The last evidence within the window is from October 16, 2025: Senate failed for the 10th time (vote 51-45), then adjourned until October 20, 2025. No CR was signed into law before the window closed on October 17, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (CR enacted by both chambers and signed by President) occurred within the window. The only House passage of a CR occurred on September 19, 2025, but the Senate never passed it. There is no earlier qualifying occurrence to check against.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple highly consistent sources confirm the shutdown was still ongoing as of October 16–17, 2025: JD Supra shutdown tracker (Oct 16), Fox News (Oct 16), Invezz (Oct 16), North Jersey (Oct 16), WMUR9 (Oct 16), Jackson Sun (Oct 15), etc. The Senate adjourned until October 20, making it definitively impossible for a CR to be enacted by October 17. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting any CR was signed into law within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. While the House passed H.R. 5371 on September 19, 2025, the Senate failed to pass any CR throughout the entire window. A government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, and was still ongoing on October 16–17, 2025 (Day 16). The Senate adjourned on October 16 until October 20, making it impossible for a CR to be enacted by October 17. No CR was passed by both chambers and signed by the President within the September 17 – October 17, 2025 window. The condition became definitively impossible when the Senate adjourned on October 16, 2025, with no deal reached.

This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-28, there is public confirmation—via official statements, press releases, or credible media reporting—that bipartisan negotiations on a stopgap funding bill (continuing resolution) have formally begun in both the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate. For the purpose of this question, 'bipartisan negotiations' means that at least one senior Democratic leader (e.g., Schumer, Jeffries) and one senior Republican leader (e.g., Johnson, Thune) from each chamber have participated in or confirmed attendance at a formal meeting or negotiation session aimed at reaching agreement on a continuing resolution to fund the government beyond September 30, 2025.

Resolution will be based on credible reporting from at least two of the following sources:
- https://www.congress.gov
- https://www.whitehouse.gov
- https://www.nytimes.com
- https://www.washingtonpost.com
- https://www.politico.com
- https://www.reuters.com
- https://www.apnews.com

If no such negotiations are confirmed by these sources during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If negotiations are announced but later delayed or canceled, the question still resolves Yes as long as they were initiated within the timeframe. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves based on whether negotiations began during the window. In the event that primary sources become unavailable, secondary authoritative news outlets with verifiable reporting will be used.
subquestions.rationale: The initiation of bipartisan negotiations on a continuing resolution is a strong leading indicator of whether a government funding lapse will occur. If such talks begin before September 28, it signals that congressional leaders are actively working toward a compromise, significantly reducing the likelihood of a shutdown. Conversely, the absence of negotiations by late September suggests deep partisan gridlock, increasing the probability of a funding lapse. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but captures a key political precondition for avoiding a shutdown. It is informative because forecasters who disagree on the ultimate outcome may converge if negotiations are confirmed, and it avoids near-0 or near-1 probabilities given the current uncertainty in the political landscape.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between Sept 1-28, 2025, at least one senior Democratic leader (Schumer or Jeffries) AND one senior Republican leader (Johnson or Thune) from EACH chamber (both House and Senate) must have participated in or confirmed attendance at a formal meeting or negotiation session aimed at reaching agreement on a CR to fund the government beyond Sept 30, 2025.
