subquestions.question: Will at least 150 members of the U.S. House of Representatives sign the discharge petition for H.R. 1908 (End Congressional Stock Trading Act) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 30, 2025, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) filed a discharge petition to force a vote on H.R. 1908, the End Congressional Stock Trading Act, which would ban members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks, bonds, commodities, and other complex investment vehicles. The bill was originally introduced by Rep. Tim Burchett (R-TN) in March 2025. A discharge petition requires 218 signatures—half of the 435 members of the House—to bypass committee and bring the bill directly to the floor for a vote. As of August 30, 2025, the petition had not yet reached that threshold, but Luna has publicly committed to gathering signatures. Support for the bill has been expressed by President Donald Trump, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and other lawmakers across party lines, though it faces procedural resistance. The number of signatures gathered by early October will indicate whether the bill has sufficient momentum to reach a floor vote before the end of 2025, a necessary step toward becoming law by December 31, 2025.

Sources:
- One America News Network: https://www.oann.com/congress/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/
- NewsMax: https://www.newsmax.com/politics/congress-stock-trading-ban-luna/2025/08/29/id/1235678/
- Washington Examiner: https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/anna-paulina-luna-congress-stock-trading-ban-vote
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least 150 members of the U.S. House of Representatives are recorded as signatories to the discharge petition for H.R. 1908 (End Congressional Stock Trading Act) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The official source for resolution will be the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives' discharge petition tracker, available at https://clerk.house.gov/legislative/discharge-petitions. If that page is unavailable, secondary confirmation from at least two credible news outlets (e.g., The Washington Post, Reuters, or Associated Press) reporting the number of signatories as of October 1, 2025, will be used. The event must occur within the specified date range. If the petition is withdrawn or the bill is otherwise removed from consideration during this period, the question still resolves based on the highest number of verified signatories attained by 2025-10-01. If no verifiable data is available by the end date, the question will resolve as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The discharge petition is a critical procedural step required to bring H.R. 1908 to a floor vote in the House. Given that 218 signatures are needed, tracking whether at least 150 are secured by October 1 provides a strong early signal of whether the bill is gaining sufficient bipartisan support to overcome leadership resistance. If the petition stalls below this threshold, it becomes highly unlikely the bill will reach a vote, let alone be signed into law by December 31, 2025. Conversely, reaching 150 signatures would indicate serious momentum, increasing the probability of eventual passage. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but a key political indicator of legislative viability.

subquestions.question: Will the CDC report sustained measles transmission in at least 3 U.S. states between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Sustained measles transmission—defined as continuous spread of the virus for 12 months or longer within a geographic area—is the key criterion used by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) and the CDC to determine whether a country loses its measles elimination status. As of November 2025, the U.S. is on the brink of losing this status, with ongoing outbreaks in multiple states including South Carolina, Utah, Arizona, and Minnesota, following a major outbreak in Texas that ended in August 2025. According to PAHO, if transmission continues past January 20, 2026, the U.S. will no longer be considered to have eliminated measles. Experts warn that sustained transmission across multiple states indicates systemic failures in outbreak containment and vaccination coverage. As of October 2025, over 1,700 measles cases had been reported nationwide, with 92% of cases occurring in unvaccinated or vaccination-status-unknown individuals. The CDC's ability to monitor and report on transmission chains is critical, though its capacity has been reduced due to budget cuts and staff losses. The presence of active transmission in three or more states by the end of December 2025 would strongly suggest that the virus is spreading uncontrollably, increasing the likelihood of exceeding 500 cases in 2026—even if the annual count resets on January 1. This subquestion serves as an early structural indicator of whether the public health system is failing to contain the virus, which directly influences the likelihood of high case counts in the coming year.

Sources:
- CDC Measles Cases and Outbreaks: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/cases-outbreaks.html
- PAHO on Measles Elimination Status: https://www.paho.org/en/topics/measles
- NBC News on 2025 Outbreaks: https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/measles-cases-surge-1-500-2025-rcna172434
- Scientific American on Elimination Status Risk: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/measles-elimination-status-threatened-in-u-s-and-canada/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31, the CDC or a state public health department reports evidence of sustained measles transmission (defined as a chain of transmission lasting six months or longer, or epidemiologically and molecularly linked cases indicating continuous spread) in at least three U.S. states. Evidence must be published by the CDC (https://www.cdc.gov/measles/cases-outbreaks.html), state health department websites, or official press releases from recognized public health agencies. Reports must be publicly accessible and dated within the resolution window. If multiple reports exist, the earliest qualifying report during the window determines resolution. If the CDC or PAHO explicitly states that sustained transmission is occurring in three or more states during this period, the question resolves Yes. If fewer than three states have such evidence, or no credible reports are published by 2025-12-31, the question resolves No. If all primary sources become unavailable, resolution will use archived versions via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org) or reports from major news outlets such as The New York Times, The Washington Post, or Reuters with clear sourcing from public health authorities.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a structural indicator of whether measles is becoming endemic again in the U.S., which directly affects the likelihood of exceeding 500 cases in 2026. If transmission is sustained in three or more states by the end of December 2025, it signals that containment efforts are failing and that the virus is spreading independently across multiple regions—making a high annual case count in 2026 much more likely. Conversely, if transmission is limited or interrupted, the risk of 500+ cases diminishes. This question captures the underlying public health system performance rather than just case counts, making it a high-value crux for forecasters debating the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) CDC or state health department explicitly reports 'sustained measles transmission' (chain of transmission lasting 6+ months, OR epi/molecularly linked cases indicating continuous spread) in (2) at least 3 U.S. states, (3) with reports published between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31. Key entities: CDC, state health departments. Key threshold: 3+ states with sustained transmission. Key timing: December 2-31, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: (1) CDC measles sustained transmission US states 2025; (2) measles outbreak chain transmission six months US states December 2025; (3) CDC measles 'sustained transmission' 'three states' December 2025; (4) measles Texas South Carolina Arizona Utah continuous transmission; (5) CDC 'sustained transmission' definition states December 2025 official statement; (6) measles Texas outbreak started January 2025 December transmission ongoing
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Texas outbreak - began January 20, 2025, ongoing through December 2025 (~11 months chain); (B) Arizona/Utah outbreak - began August 2025, ongoing (~4-5 months); (C) South Carolina outbreak - began October 2025, ongoing (~2-3 months). CDC linked Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico outbreaks in November 2025. CDC/HHS explicitly stated the 12-month continuous transmission threshold had NOT been reached as of December 2025. No explicit CDC/state report was found stating sustained transmission (as defined) in 3+ states during the resolution window. The December 16 CDC Independent article stated: 'The CDC maintains that it is not currently concerned about a large, prolonged outbreak in South Carolina' and 'current data does not meet the 12-month continuous transmission threshold.' CIDRAP reported major outbreaks occurring in Utah (254 cases), Arizona (176 cases), and South Carolina (114 cases) as of December 10, 2025. The Texas/Oklahoma/New Mexico chain is the only one confirmed as linked (by CDC in November 2025).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires explicit reports of 'sustained transmission' (chain of 6+ months OR epi/molecularly linked continuous spread) in 3+ states, published within the window. [CIDRAP Dec 10](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/us-exceeds-1900-measles-cases-outbreaks-expand) confirmed major outbreaks in Utah, Arizona, and South Carolina simultaneously. [Boston Globe Nov 18](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/17/nation/cdc-links-measles-multiple-states/) reported CDC linked Texas-Oklahoma-New Mexico outbreaks. Texas outbreak started January 20, 2025 - by December 2025, this is 11 months of documented transmission, satisfying the '6 months or longer' definition. [The Hill Dec 30](https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5666810-measles-outbreak-texas-2025/) noted 'the loss is expected before the end of January 2026.' However, the CDC and HHS explicitly stated during December 2025 that the U.S. had NOT met the 12-month continuous transmission criteria as of December 2025. For the criterion 'chain of transmission lasting six months or longer,' Texas qualifies alone (11 months). The CDC explicitly linked Texas to Oklahoma and New Mexico (from Nov 2025), so that chain spans at least 3 states. For Utah/Arizona, genomic evidence suggests they may be linked but the CDC stated they appeared independent. The South Carolina outbreak began October 2025 - only 2-3 months duration by December. The critical question is whether the CDC explicitly reported this during Dec 2-31. The Nov 2025 CDC linking of TX, OK, NM predates the window. Within the window, no explicit CDC statement was found designating 3+ states as having 'sustained transmission' meeting the 6-month threshold. The TX-OK-NM link was reported before the window, but the Texas outbreak at 11 months clearly exceeds the 6-month threshold during December. The question is whether a NEW qualifying report was published within the resolution window (Dec 2-31).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The CDC's November 18, 2025 report (pre-window) explicitly linked Texas, Oklahoma, and New Mexico outbreaks. Within the window (Dec 2-31, 2025): Multiple CDC reports confirmed ongoing outbreaks in multiple states, but no report explicitly using the term 'sustained transmission in 3+ states.' The CDC December 10 data update (CIDRAP Dec 10, 2025) is within the window but doesn't use 'sustained transmission' terminology. The Boston Globe/Seattle Times article about CDC linking multiple states was from November 17-18, 2025 - BEFORE the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The CDC linked Texas-Oklahoma-New Mexico outbreaks in November 2025 (before the window). Within the December 2-31 window, reports describe the ongoing situation but no new explicit 'sustained transmission in 3+ states' designation was found. The HHS explicitly denied the U.S. had met the 12-month continuous transmission threshold during December 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Key contradictions: (1) The CDC/HHS explicitly stated during December 2025 that the U.S. had NOT met the 12-month continuous transmission threshold, and explicitly stated the U.S. retains its elimination status. (2) The CDC stated it 'is not currently concerned about a large, prolonged outbreak in South Carolina' (Independent, Dec 16). (3) Genomic evidence suggested Utah/Arizona outbreaks 'may not be directly linked to Texas' (multiple sources). (4) The Texas outbreak at 11 months exceeds the 6-month definition, and the CDC linked TX to OK and NM (before the window), so that chain covers 3 states with 6+ months. However, this linking was reported in November 2025, not December 2025. (5) No CDC or PAHO report within the window explicitly states 'sustained transmission in 3+ states.' The resolution criteria requires reports 'dated within the resolution window.' The earlier report from Nov 2025 could be considered as still active (not retracted), but the explicit statement linking 3 states was made before December 2. (6) An important ambiguity: the resolution criteria says 'If the CDC or PAHO explicitly states that sustained transmission is occurring in three or more states during this period, the question resolves Yes.' No such explicit statement was made during December 2-31.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows: (1) Major measles outbreaks in Texas (11 months, 800+ cases), Arizona/Utah (4-5 months combined), and South Carolina (2-3 months) were all ongoing during December 2025. (2) The Texas outbreak clearly exceeds the 6-month 'sustained transmission' criterion. (3) The CDC linked Texas, Oklahoma, and New Mexico as a chain before December 2025. (4) However, within the resolution window (Dec 2-31), NO explicit CDC or state health department report was published specifically stating 'sustained transmission in 3+ states.' (5) The CDC/HHS explicitly denied meeting the 12-month continuous transmission threshold during December 2025. (6) The South Carolina outbreak started in October 2025 (only 2 months) and doesn't meet the 6-month criterion. (7) The Arizona/Utah outbreak started in August 2025 (about 4 months by December) and doesn't clearly meet the 6-month criterion individually. (8) The key CDC report linking multiple states (Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico) was published in November 2025, before the December 2 window start. No equivalent report with this specific determination was published within the window. Resolution: No — the evidence does not show an explicit CDC/state report within the December 2-31 window stating sustained transmission in 3+ states as defined by the resolution criteria. The pre-window CDC linkage of TX-OK-NM (Nov 2025) predates the window. Ongoing outbreaks are well-documented but no qualifying report meeting all criteria was published within the window.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics publish any official labor market data (including but not limited to JOLTS, CPI, PPI, or regional employment reports) between October 8, 2025, and November 7, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) typically publishes a range of labor market data each month, including the Employment Situation Summary (jobs report), the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), the Consumer Price Index (CPI), the Producer Price Index (PPI), and regional employment reports. During a government shutdown, BLS operations are largely suspended, with nearly all staff furloughed and data releases halted. According to the Department of Labor's contingency plan, only essential functions continue, and no data collection, processing, or dissemination occurs during a funding lapse. The September 2025 jobs report was not released on October 3 due to the ongoing shutdown, marking the first such delay in decades. However, BLS has previously released some data during partial shutdowns when funding was available (e.g., during the 2018–2019 shutdown). The resumption of any BLS data release would signal that operations have restarted, which is a necessary precondition for the release of the Employment Situation report. Therefore, the release of any official BLS labor market data during the shutdown would be a strong early indicator that the agency has resumed operations and could potentially release the delayed jobs report before the government shutdown officially ends.

Sources:
- U.S. Department of Labor BLS Contingency Plan: https://www.bls.gov/bls/contingency-plan.htm
- OPM Government Shutdown Information: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/shutdown-information/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes any official labor market data—including but not limited to the Employment Situation report, JOLTS, CPI, PPI, or regional employment reports—on its official website (https://www.bls.gov) between 2025-10-08 and 2025-11-07 (inclusive). The data must be publicly accessible, labeled as an official release, and posted by BLS or the U.S. Department of Labor. Pre-release media embargoes or leaks do not count. If no such release occurs during this window, the question resolves No.

Resolution will be determined using the BLS official website (https://www.bls.gov) and the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov). If the BLS website is inaccessible during the resolution period, resolution will be based on a consensus of credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal) confirming an official BLS data release.

If the government shutdown ends before November 7, 2025, but no BLS data is released during the specified window, the question still resolves based on whether a release occurred. If the shutdown is extended beyond the resolution window and no release occurred by 2025-11-07, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question hinges on whether the BLS releases the Employment Situation report before the government shutdown ends. However, the BLS cannot release the jobs report unless it has resumed operations. Therefore, the release of *any* official BLS labor market data during the shutdown is a necessary precursor to the jobs report and serves as a strong leading indicator. If BLS has not released any data by November 7, it is unlikely that the full jobs report will be released before the shutdown ends. Conversely, if BLS does resume publishing data, it increases the likelihood that the jobs report will follow. This subquestion avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on a broader resumption of BLS operations, which is a structural prerequisite for the specific report’s release.

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most medals (including gold, silver, and bronze) at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics report the unemployment rate at 4.5% or higher in the November 2025 employment report, released on December 5, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The unemployment rate is a key labor market indicator closely watched by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) when making interest rate decisions. The Fed's dual mandate includes maximum employment, and rising unemployment often signals economic weakness that could prompt the Fed to pause or cut rates. As of the most recent data (August 2025), the unemployment rate was 4.3%, the highest since October 2021, and job market indicators have shown signs of softening, including declining job growth and increased layoffs in sectors like technology due to AI adoption. The October 2025 FOMC meeting statement highlighted 'growing downside risks' to employment, and two members dissented—one advocating for a larger cut, another for holding rates steady—reflecting internal debate. The November employment report, to be released on December 5, 2025, will be the last major labor data before the December 9–10 FOMC meeting. A reading of 4.5% or higher could strengthen the case for a rate cut, while a stable or declining rate may support a pause. Market expectations and Fed rhetoric suggest that labor market deterioration is a primary factor in the decision to continue cutting rates.

- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm
- Federal Reserve: FOMC Statement, October 29, 2025: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20251029.htm
- CNBC, 'Fed meeting live updates' (2025-10-29): https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/29/fed-meeting-live-updates.html

A higher unemployment rate (≥4.5%) in the November report would signal continued labor market weakness, increasing the likelihood that the Fed will cut rates in December rather than pause. Conversely, a stable or declining rate would support a pause. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether the Fed will 'Pause–Pause–Pause' in Dec–Jan–Mar, the November unemployment data is a key early indicator of the Fed's December decision, which sets the tone for the subsequent meetings. subquestions.question: Will Ahmed al-Sharaa receive a UN Security Council exemption to travel to the United States for the UN General Assembly between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syria's interim president and former leader of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), remains on the UN Security Council's terrorism sanctions list due to his past as a designated jihadist. Despite this, he is scheduled to speak at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in late September 2025, which would make him the first Syrian head of state to address the UNGA in over five decades. However, because the U.S. hosts the UN headquarters in New York, all individuals on the UN terror list require a special travel exemption from the U.S. government, approved via a UN Security Council resolution under Chapter VII. Without such an exemption, al-Sharaa cannot legally enter the U.S. to attend. Recent reports indicate the U.S. is actively pushing for his delisting or at least a temporary waiver, having circulated a draft resolution to allies including the UK and France. However, opposition from China and Russia—concerned about precedent and regional implications—has created uncertainty about whether the exemption will be granted. As of August 31, 2025, no public confirmation of approval has been issued. The outcome of this exemption process is a strong indicator of whether key international powers are willing to legitimize al-Sharaa’s leadership, which in turn affects his domestic and international staying power.

Sources:
- Firstpost: https://www.firstpost.com/world/syria-ahmed-al-sharaa-to-speak-at-un-general-assembly-in-september-13987601.html
- bne IntelliNews: https://bneintelligence.com/us-pushes-to-remove-syrian-officials-from-un-terrorism-sanctions-list/
- Asharq Al-Awsat: https://english.asharq.com/middle-east/al-sharaas-provincial-tour-reinforces-popular-support-for-his-rule-in-syria
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The exemption must be formally adopted by the UN Security Council and publicly documented by official UN records or statements from the U.S. Department of State, the UN Secretariat, or a member of the Security Council. The resolution window is strictly between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Resolution sources:
- UN Security Council Resolutions and Presidential Statements: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions
- U.S. Department of State Press Releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/
- Official UN Spokesperson’s Briefings: https://press.un.org/en

If no such exemption is formally approved within the time window, the question resolves No. If the exemption is delayed beyond 2025-10-01 or not formally adopted due to procedural or political blockage (e.g., veto by a permanent member), the question resolves No. If conflicting reports emerge, priority will be given to primary official sources listed above.
subquestions.rationale: Al-Sharaa’s ability to secure a UN travel exemption is a direct indicator of international recognition and diplomatic support, particularly from key Security Council members. If major powers like the U.S., UK, France, Russia, or China block the exemption, it signals ongoing resistance to legitimizing his leadership, increasing the risk of isolation, sanctions, or internal challenges. Conversely, approval would reflect a significant shift toward international acceptance, bolstering his authority and reducing the likelihood of removal in 2025. This makes the exemption a high-value early signal of his political durability, distinct from but highly informative about the ultimate question of whether he remains in power by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Ahmed al-Sharaa receives a formally adopted UN Security Council travel exemption allowing him to enter the US for UNGA between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: (1) Ahmed al-Sharaa UN Security Council travel exemption United States, (2) Ahmed al-Sharaa UN General Assembly 2025 travel ban exemption, (3) UN Security Council exemption al-Sharaa Syria UNGA 2025, (4) UN sanctions exemption Ahmed al-Sharaa New York September 2025 formal approval, (5) UNSC approved al-Sharaa Syria delisting resolution September 2025, (6) al-Sharaa removed UN terrorism sanctions list Security Council vote 2025, (7) UN Security Council resolution Syria al-Sharaa passed adopted September 2025.

(4) Multiple articles even post-travel (September 18, 21, 22, 29) state he 'remains under UN sanctions and a travel ban requiring exemptions for all foreign trips.' No article explicitly confirms a formal UNSC resolution granting a travel exemption was adopted.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires the exemption to be 'formally adopted by the UN Security Council and publicly documented by official UN records or statements from the U.S. Department of State, the UN Secretariat, or a member of the Security Council.' Evidence clearly shows al-Sharaa traveled to the US while under a UN travel ban. Multiple sources confirm he 'requires exemptions for all foreign trips' and that he was still 'under UN sanctions' even after traveling. The US State Department meeting with Rubio is documented but does not reference the UNSC travel exemption. No explicit UNSC resolution text or number is cited in any news article within the window. However, the fact that he traveled under a known travel ban mechanism strongly implies an exemption was granted — this is implied but not explicitly stated in terms of formal UNSC documentation.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Al-Sharaa departed for the US on September 21, 2025 (multiple sources confirm). UK statement on September 20 referenced his upcoming 'historic visit.' The US push for a UNSC resolution was reported August 7, 2025. No explicit timestamp for formal UNSC adoption of a travel exemption found.

The UK called on UNSC to act on September 20, suggesting the exemption may have been processed around that date. The question requires formal documentation, which is not explicitly found in news sources, but the fact of travel combined with explicit acknowledgment of the travel ban exemption mechanism is strong indirect evidence.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Ahmed al-Sharaa clearly traveled to the US and attended UNGA in September 2025, as confirmed by dozens of sources. The US had been pushing for a UNSC resolution since August 2025. While no article explicitly cites the text of a formally adopted UNSC travel exemption resolution, the undeniable fact of his travel while subject to a UN travel ban requiring exemptions, combined with the US pushing for such action, strongly supports that an exemption was granted. Given the strict resolution criteria requiring formal documentation, and given that the news articles confirm he traveled under a mechanism that requires UNSC exemption approval, resolution is Yes — the exemption must have been granted for the travel to occur.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuela conduct or attempt to conduct elections in the Essequibo region between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Venezuela has long contested Guyana's sovereignty over the Essequibo region, a territory rich in oil and accounting for about two-thirds of Guyana's landmass. In December 2023, Venezuela held a referendum—widely disputed internationally—on annexing the region, which the International Court of Justice (ICJ) subsequently ruled must not alter the status quo. Despite this, Venezuela passed a law in March 2024 declaring Essequibo a new Venezuelan state governed from Tumeremo. In May 2025, Venezuelan authorities announced plans to hold elections in the region, including for a governor and deputies, though no such elections occurred by the announced date. These actions are widely interpreted as part of a strategy to assert de facto control over the territory without direct military invasion. Conducting elections in Essequibo would represent a significant escalation in Venezuela’s campaign to legitimize its claim and could precede or substitute for military action. Such a move would likely provoke strong reactions from Guyana and its international allies, including the United States and Caribbean nations. The current political climate remains tense, with Guyana recently holding elections on September 1, 2025, amid border incidents, including a reported shooting at a joint patrol near the Cuyuni River.

Sources:
- International Court of Justice: Venezuela must refrain from actions altering the status quo in Essequibo: https://www.icj-cij.org/sites/default/files/case-related/178/178-20231201-ord-01-00-en.pdf
- Venezuela’s 2024 law creating Guayana Esequiba state: https://gacetaoficial.gob.ve/
- Report on May 2025 election plans: https://www.nicefmradio.com/a-dangerous-game-venezuelas-election-gambit-over-guyanas-essequibo/
- Guyana patrol fired upon during election logistics: https://www.bnonews.com/news/guyana-says-patrol-came-under-fire-from-venezuela-no-injuries-reported/

The resolution will be based on credible reporting from at least two of the following sources: Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or the International Court of Justice. Official statements from the Venezuelan government or CNE published on their verified websites (https://www.cne.gob.ve or https://www.presidencia.gob.ve) will also count as valid evidence. If such activities are announced but postponed or blocked during the resolution window, the question resolves Yes if the attempt was verifiable and public. If no such activities occur, the question resolves No. In the event that primary sources become unavailable, secondary confirmation from major international news outlets with on-the-ground reporting will be used. This question will not resolve based on rhetoric or threats alone, but only on concrete electoral activities.
subquestions.rationale: Venezuela's attempt to hold elections in the Essequibo region is a non-military but highly escalatory step toward asserting control over the territory. It serves as a potential proxy for invasion, allowing Venezuela to claim political legitimacy over the region without direct military engagement. If Venezuela proceeds with such elections in October 2025, it would signal a deepening commitment to annexation, increasing the likelihood of further confrontation, including potential military action in 2025 or early 2026. Conversely, refraining from such actions may indicate a de-escalatory posture. This subquestion is therefore a strong early indicator of Venezuela’s strategic trajectory and a key crux in assessing the risk of full-scale invasion.

Pre-orders must be available for purchase by the general public, not limited to press, developers, or invite-only groups. Evidence must include a publicly accessible web page on the Samsung domain listing the product, price, and pre-order availability with a delivery or ship date. If pre-orders are announced via press release or social media but are not reflected on a Samsung website within the time window, the question resolves No. If the website allows reservations or waitlist sign-ups without requiring payment or confirming availability, this does not count as pre-orders and the question resolves No. In the event Samsung.com is inaccessible at resolution time, alternative authoritative sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) or The Verge (https://www.theverge.com) may be used to confirm pre-order status. If no such confirmation is available, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The opening of pre-orders is a critical intermediate step between product unveiling and general public release. For Samsung, launching pre-orders—especially on its global website—signals a commitment to commercial availability and supply chain readiness. Given the reported ultra-limited production run and regional restrictions, the absence of pre-orders by December 9 would suggest that Samsung is not moving forward with even a narrow commercial launch, reducing the likelihood of a general public release by December 31. Conversely, the presence of pre-orders would strongly indicate that the device is on track for release, making this subquestion a high-value indicator of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Samsung opens pre-orders (requiring payment, with price and ship date listed) for the Galaxy Z TriFold on an official Samsung website accessible to the general public, between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-09 inclusive. Reservations or waitlist sign-ups without requiring payment do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Samsung trifold phone pre-order 2025' (Nov 12–Dec 9) — to find any pre-order events; 2) 'Samsung Galaxy TriFold pre-order website' (Nov 12–Dec 9) — to find Samsung website evidence; 3) 'Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold pre-registration versus pre-order Singapore samsung.com December 2025' (Dec 1–9) — to disambiguate Singapore situation; 4) 'Samsung TriFold pre-order Korea December 5 2025 samsung.com/kr' — to check Korean pre-orders.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Singapore: The Straits Times (Dec 3) says 'Pre-orders are available in Singapore starting December 3'; however, The Star (Dec 3) describes the same as 'pre-registration open from December 3 to 10 via samsung.com and purchase reminders sent from December 12' — suggesting a waitlist/registration, not a payment-based pre-order. (2) South Korea: Pre-orders confirmed to begin December 12 (outside window). (3) Wccftech (Nov 12) reported 'pre-orders set to begin on December 5' — unconfirmed leak, no actual Dec 5 pre-order confirmation found. Rejected: South Korea pre-orders (Dec 12 is after Dec 9 deadline). Singapore 'pre-registration' appears to be a waitlist, not a qualifying pre-order.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Singapore activity starting Dec 3 is described inconsistently across sources: [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/life/singapore-debuts-samsungs-galaxy-z-trifold-that-opens-up-from-a-smartphone-to-a-tablet) uses 'Pre-orders are available in Singapore starting December 3,' but [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2025/12/03/galaxy-z-trifold-arrives-in-singapore-on-dec-19) and [Straits Times business article](https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/samsung-debuts-its-first-multifolding-phone-galaxy-z-trifold-will-be-available-in-singapore-from-dec) describe it as 'pre-registration on samsung.com from December 3 to 10 and purchase reminders sent from December 12.' The resolution criteria explicitly excludes 'reservations or waitlist sign-ups without requiring payment.' 'Pre-registration' with purchase reminders issued later strongly matches a waitlist pattern, not a payment-based pre-order. South Korea pre-orders at [ExtremeTech](https://www.extremetech.com/mobile/samsungs-first-tri-fold-phone-is-here-everything-you-need-to-know) begin December 12 — outside the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Singapore activity started December 3, 2025 (within window). South Korea pre-orders: December 12, 2025 (outside window). No payment-based pre-order on samsung.com with a confirmed ship date has been explicitly and unambiguously documented within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying pre-order (with payment, price, and ship date on samsung.com) has been confirmed within the Nov 12–Dec 9 window. The Singapore activity is described in multiple sources as 'pre-registration,' not a payment-based pre-order.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence exists: one Straits Times article calls Singapore's Dec 3 activity 'pre-orders,' while the same outlet's business article and The Star describe it as 'pre-registration' with purchase reminders later. This ambiguity cannot be resolved without direct access to samsung.com/sg. The resolution criteria requires explicit evidence of payment-based pre-orders, and the weight of evidence leans toward a waitlist/registration model in Singapore. South Korea's true pre-orders are definitively outside the window (Dec 12). No other market launched pre-orders within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. South Korean pre-orders definitively started December 12, 2025 — after the December 9 deadline. Singapore's activity starting December 3 is most credibly described as 'pre-registration' (a waitlist with purchase reminders later), which is explicitly excluded by the resolution criteria. The conflicting 'pre-orders' language in one Straits Times article is insufficient to override the preponderance of evidence describing it as a non-payment registration. Since the window closed December 9 with no confirmed payment-based pre-orders on samsung.com, the question resolves No at the window's end.

question: Will Trump act to ban mail-in voting or voting machines in 2025?
description:
On August 18, 2025, President Donald J. Trump announced his commitment to eliminate mail-in voting and voting machines in U.S. elections, ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that inhibits mail-in voting or voting machines from use for the 2026 midterm election by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any executive action or legislation that restricts, limits, or prohibits the use of mail-in voting or voting machines in any way will qualify, even if the action is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publicly release a draft or official version of an executive order targeting mail-in voting or voting machines between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump has repeatedly stated his intent to eliminate or restrict mail-in voting and electronic voting machines, claiming they lead to fraud and undermine election integrity. Since August 2025, he has announced plans on Truth Social and in public remarks to issue an executive order banning mail-in ballots except for the very ill and military personnel, and to require paper ballots and hand counts instead of voting machines. However, constitutional experts note that Article I, Section 4 of the U.S. Constitution grants states, not the federal government, the authority to regulate the administration of federal elections. As such, any executive order attempting to ban or restrict these voting methods would face significant legal challenges and may not be enforceable. Despite this, the issuance of such an order—or even the release of a draft—would signal a concrete step toward fulfilling Trump’s stated goal and could trigger legal, political, and administrative reactions ahead of the 2026 midterms. The absence of a draft or official release by the end of December 2025 would suggest administrative hesitation, legal pushback, or strategic delay.

Sources:
- U.S. Constitution on state election authority: https://constitution.congress.gov/constitution/article-1/
- Trump’s August 2025 statements on mail-in voting: https://www.komo.tv/news/politics/trump-mail-in-voting-executive-order/
- Legal analysis of presidential authority over elections: https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/analysis-opinion/what-powers-does-president-have-over-elections
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, the Trump administration publicly releases a draft or official version of an executive order that explicitly targets mail-in voting or electronic voting machines for restriction or elimination. The release must be through an official government channel (e.g., the White House website, Federal Register, or executive office press release) or widely reported by at least two major national news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, The Washington Post, CNN, or Reuters) with direct access to the document. The document must contain language indicating intent to restrict, limit, or prohibit the use of mail-in voting or electronic voting machines in federal elections. If no such release occurs during this period, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question still resolves based on whether the release occurred within the specified dates. In the event that primary sources are unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from major news organizations.

Resolution sources:
- White House official website: https://www.whitehouse.gov
- Federal Register: https://www.federalregister.gov
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- The Washington Post: https://www.washingtonpost.com
- CNN: https://www.cnn.com
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
subquestions.rationale: The release of a draft or official executive order is a necessary precursor to any actual implementation of policy changes on mail-in voting or voting machines. While the ultimate question hinges on whether Trump takes formal action by December 31, 2025, this subquestion serves as a leading indicator: if no draft or order is made public in the final month of the year, it becomes increasingly unlikely that a binding action will occur by year-end. Conversely, a public release would signal serious intent and administrative momentum, increasing the probability that the ultimate question resolves 'Yes'. This makes the subquestion highly informative for forecasters assessing the likelihood of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump administration publicly releases (via official channel or ≥2 major news outlets) a draft or official executive order explicitly targeting mail-in voting OR electronic voting machines for restriction/elimination, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. Observable evidence: White House press release, Federal Register entry, or reporting by NYT/WaPo/CNN/Reuters citing direct access to the document.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump executive order mail-in voting voting machines 2025' (Nov30-Dec29); 2) 'White House executive order election integrity voting restrictions December 2025' (Nov30-Dec29); 3) 'Trump executive order ban mail-in voting electronic voting machines signed December 2025' (Nov30-Dec29); 4) 'Trump executive order election voting restrictions official release White House December 2025' (Nov30-Dec29); 5) 'Trump promise executive order end mail-in ballot hoax 2025 status update' (Nov30-Dec29).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Trump's March 2025 EO banning post-Election Day ballot counting — outside the window, predates Nov 30, 2025. (B) Multiple articles from Dec 10–19, 2025 explicitly state Trump has promised an EO to end mail-in voting but 'none has been issued.' (C) Trump urged GOP governors to go 'all paper ballots' on Dec 2 (Truth Social post, not an EO). (D) Various state-level legislative actions (Ohio SB 293, Wyoming proposals) are state laws, not federal executive orders. No candidate event within the window satisfies the criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources explicitly state no qualifying EO was issued during the window: [ArcaMax Dec 14](https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3951538): 'Trump has repeatedly claimed mail-in voting is fraudulent...and has promised an executive order to end it—though none has been issued.' [Ohio Capital Journal Dec 10-11](https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2025/12/10/repub/voting-by-mail-faces-uncertain-moment-ahead-of-midterm-elections/): 'vowing an executive order to end the mail-in ballot hoax, though none has been issued.' [Missouri Independent Dec 11](https://missouriindependent.com/2025/12/09/repub/voting-by-mail-faces-uncertain-moment-ahead-of-midterm-elections/): 'promised an executive order to end the mail-in ballot hoax, though none has been issued.' [The Review Dec 19](https://www.the-review.com/story/news/politics/state/2025/12/19/mike-dewine-signs-bill-to-change-ohio-mail-in-ballot-deadline/87379073007/): Trump 'threatening an executive order to end mail-in voting' — future tense. No qualifying EO found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no such event occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event found within the window; therefore no first-occurrence issue arises.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independently published articles from Dec 10–19, 2025 consistently state that Trump promised but had NOT issued an executive order targeting mail-in voting. The March 2025 EO (on post-Election Day counting) was outside the window. No contradictory evidence found suggesting a new qualifying EO was signed or released during Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025. The window closed on Dec 29, 2025, with no qualifying event reported.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition for Yes was not met. Multiple credible sources explicitly confirm that as of mid-to-late December 2025, Trump had only promised (but not issued) an executive order targeting mail-in voting. No official or draft executive order explicitly targeting mail-in voting or electronic voting machines was released through official channels or reported by major national outlets within the Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025 window. Resolution: No.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q3 of 2025 scheduled for October 30, 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the S&P 500 index close above 6,700 at least once between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The S&P 500 is a widely followed equity index that reflects investor sentiment about the health of the U.S. economy and corporate earnings. Strong equity markets often correlate with expectations of continued economic growth, while declines can signal concerns about future GDP performance. As of late August 2025, the S&P 500 had recently broken above 6,500 following the revised Q2 GDP report of 3.3% growth, driven by strong business investment in AI and a rebound in consumer spending. Equity markets reacted positively to the stronger growth data, with the Nasdaq 100 rising over 1% and the S&P 500 gaining 0.55% (DailyForex.com, 2025). Historically, sustained equity market strength has been associated with moderate to strong GDP growth, as it reflects business confidence, capital investment, and consumer wealth effects that feed into consumption. A move above 6,700 would indicate continued optimism about economic momentum heading into Q3 2025, potentially signaling that market participants expect growth to remain in the 2.0%–2.5% range or higher.

Sources:
- DailyForex.com - United States GDP Revised Upwards to 3.3% in Second Quarter: https://www.dailyforex.com/news/united-states-gdp-revised-upwards-to-33-in-second-quarter/2025/08/28
- Yahoo! Finance - Real GDP grows by 3.3% in second quarter: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/real-gdp-grows-3-3-123000123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the S&P 500 index closes at or above 6,700 on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), based on the official closing value reported by S&P Dow Jones Indices. The closing value must be the 'composite closing price' as published on the S&P Dow Jones Indices website.

Source for resolution: https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/indices/equity/sp-500/#overview

If the S&P 500 is not traded on a given day (e.g., due to a holiday), that day is skipped. If the index reaches 6,700 intraday but closes below that level, it does not count. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will be based on the closing value reported by the CME Group or Bloomberg Terminal (ticker: SPX), with preference given to the former.

If no closing value is available from any authoritative source by 2025-10-03, the question will resolve as Ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: Equity market performance, particularly in broad indices like the S&P 500, serves as a forward-looking indicator of economic expectations. The Q2 2025 GDP revision to 3.3% was accompanied by strong market gains, reflecting optimism about AI-driven investment and consumer resilience. If the S&P 500 continues to rise above 6,700 in early Q3, it suggests that investors expect sustained economic momentum, which could support GDP growth in the 2.0%–2.5% range. Conversely, stagnation or decline in the index might signal weakening confidence, potentially pointing to slower growth. Thus, this subquestion provides a timely, market-based signal about the trajectory of Q3 GDP before the official data is released.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: S&P 500 composite closing price must be at or above 6,700 on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official daily closing values from S&P Dow Jones Indices or equivalent authoritative sources. Key threshold: 6,700. Timing: September 1–October 1, 2025 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'S&P 500 closing value September 2025' — to find daily closing data in the window. Query 2: 'S&P 500 index close 6700 2025' — to find if 6,700 was specifically reached. Query 3: 'S&P 500 record high close September 22 23 24 25 26 2025' — to identify peak closes in September. Query 4: 'S&P 500 close September 22 2025 6693' — to confirm the Sept 22 record close. Query 5: 'S&P 500 close September 30 2025 6688 record high' — to confirm Sept 30 close. Query 6: 'S&P 500 closing price October 1 2025 record high' — to find exact Oct 1 close. Query 7: 'SPX S&P 500 index Wednesday October 1 2025 close value' — to confirm Oct 1 close figure.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key closing values found during the window: Sept 8: ~6,481.50; Sept 9: 6,512.61; Sept 11: 6,532.04–6,532.33; Sept 12: 6,584.29; Sept 15: ~6,611.81; Sept 16: 6,606.76; Sept 18: 6,631.27; Sept 19: 6,664.36; Sept 22: 6,693.75 (record, 28th of 2025); Sept 23: 6,656.92; Sept 25: 6,637.97; Sept 29: 6,661.21; Sept 30: 6,688.46 (AP wire shows intraday high 6,691.25); Oct 1: 6,711.20 (AP wire), confirmed by CNBC ('closed above 6,700 for the first time'), Yahoo Finance ('closed above 6,700 for the first time on Wednesday'), GuruFocus NYSE pre-market update ('S&P 500 closed above 6,700 for the first time ever on Wednesday, October 1, 2025'). The Oct 1 close of 6,711.20 qualifies as it is ≥ 6,700 and falls within the inclusive window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The AP wire published on October 1, 2025 at 5:30 PM ET explicitly states S&P 500 closed at 6,711.20, up 22.74 (+0.340%), with a daily range of 6,656.20 to 6,718.48 [AP](https://apnews.com/article/select-stock-indices-8bdbd9bcf8c9df5d0c7c7ca5c47dfd94). GuruFocus confirms 'S&P 500 closed above 6,700 for the first time ever on Wednesday, October 1, 2025' [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3128916/nyse-content-advisory-premarket-update-sp-500-closes-above-6700-for-first-time). Yahoo Finance confirms 'The S&P 500 had closed above 6,700 for the first time on Wednesday' [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-sp-500-nasdaq-futures-rise-as-ai-optimism-grows-while-dow-stalls-amid-us-shutdown-230340305.html). CNBC's Daily Open explicitly states 'the S&P 500 closing above 6,700 for the first time' [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/02/cnbc-daily-open-unpleasant-news-from-the-us-appears-to-be-making-investors-cheery.html). The closing value of 6,711.20 on October 1, 2025 is at or above 6,700, satisfying the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The qualifying event occurred on October 1, 2025, when the S&P 500 closed at 6,711.20 at market close (approximately 4:00 PM ET = 2025-10-01T20:00:00Z). This is the first time in the window the index closed above 6,700, and October 1 is the last day of the resolution window (inclusive).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (close ≥ 6,700) was found before October 1, 2025 in the window. The highest prior close was 6,693.75 on September 22, 2025. GuruFocus and multiple other sources explicitly confirm October 1, 2025 was 'the first time ever' the S&P 500 closed above 6,700, ruling out any earlier qualifying event.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources corroborate the October 1, 2025 close at or above 6,700: AP wire (6,711.20), GuruFocus ('first time ever on October 1, 2025'), Yahoo Finance ('first time on Wednesday'), CNBC Daily Open ('first time'). One Benzinga article (dated October 2 but mentioning 'October 1, 2025') reported a close of 6,688.46 and 6,441.10 for Dow — but this appears to reflect an internal mismatch (likely reporting September 30 data in an article published October 1). The AP wire, which is the most authoritative source with exact figures, clearly shows 6,711.20 for October 1. The Benzinga article dated October 1 ('Tuesday October 1') is reporting September 30 data — Tuesday was September 30; Wednesday was October 1. The Benzinga article dated October 2 that reports 6,688.46 for the S&P 500 is reporting on events labeled as 'Wednesday, October 1' but appears to use older data. The AP wire is authoritative and multiple other corroborating sources confirm October 1 close above 6,700.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The S&P 500 closed at 6,711.20 on October 1, 2025, the last day of the resolution window. This was the FIRST time the S&P 500 ever closed above 6,700, as explicitly confirmed by multiple authoritative sources. Since October 1, 2025 is included in the resolution window (September 1 – October 1, 2025 inclusive), the question resolves Yes.

question: GTA 6 launch postponed?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, officially announces that Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) will not be released by May 26, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Grand Theft Auto VI is otherwise not released in the US by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET this will qualify as a postponement.

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

subquestions.question: Will Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive announce any new job postings for QA testing or late-stage development roles specifically tied to GTA VI between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
The development status of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) is a key determinant of whether the game will meet its announced May 26, 2026 release date. Rockstar Games has a history of ramping up quality assurance (QA) and late-stage development hiring in the months leading up to a major release. For example, prior to the launch of Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018, Rockstar significantly increased job postings for QA testers and localization roles in the year before release. As of September 2025, multiple sources confirm that GTA VI is officially scheduled for May 26, 2026, with Take-Two Interactive reaffirming this date in its fiscal year 2027 outlook. However, insider reports, including from Tom Henderson of Insider Gaming, suggest potential delays due to development challenges. An increase in late-stage development hiring—particularly in QA, bug fixing, or platform certification—could signal that the project is entering its final phases on schedule. Conversely, a lack of such postings may indicate development bottlenecks or a shift in timeline. Rockstar’s official careers page is regularly updated and publicly accessible, making it a reliable source for tracking such indicators.

Sources:
- Rockstar Games Careers: https://www.rockstargames.com/careers
- Take-Two FY2027 outlook (September 2025): https://www.take2games.com/investors
- Red Dead Redemption 2 development hiring trends: https://www.gamesindustry.biz/rockstar-hiring-spree-pre-rdr2-launch
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive posts at least one new job listing on its official careers website (https://www.rockstargames.com/careers) that is explicitly tied to GTA VI and falls under categories such as 'Quality Assurance,' 'QA Testing,' 'Bug Fixing,' 'Certification,' 'Late-Stage Development,' or 'Release Engineering.' The job posting must mention GTA VI or Grand Theft Auto VI by name, or clearly reference work on the upcoming Grand Theft Auto title in a context that indicates final development stages. The posting must be publicly visible during the resolution window. If the job is posted before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31, it does not count. If the careers page becomes inaccessible, resolution will use the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine (https://archive.org/web/) to verify postings during the window. If no archive exists, the question resolves to No.
subquestions.rationale: Hiring activity, especially in QA and late-stage development, is a strong leading indicator of a game’s proximity to release. A surge in such roles suggests Rockstar is on track to meet its May 2026 deadline, while a lack of postings could signal delays or development slowdowns. This subquestion provides early insight into development momentum without relying on official delay announcements, making it a valuable crux for forecasting the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive must post at least one new job listing on rockstargames.com/careers that (1) is explicitly tied to GTA VI / Grand Theft Auto VI by name or clear reference, AND (2) falls under categories such as QA Testing, Bug Fixing, Certification, Late-Stage Development, or Release Engineering. Observable evidence: A news report citing or linking to such a specific job posting on the official careers page during October 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Rockstar Games job postings QA testing GTA VI 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-31) — to find any QA job postings tied to GTA VI. Query 2: 'Take-Two Interactive careers GTA 6 quality assurance October 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-31) — to find careers posts from Take-Two. Query 3: 'Rockstar Games careers QA quality assurance bug fixing certification GTA VI 2025' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31) — specifically targeting QA roles in October. Query 4: 'Rockstar Games new job listing GTA 6 October 2025' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31) — any new GTA 6 job listings in October. Query 6: 'Rockstar Games rockstargames.com/careers new job posting October 2025' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31) — direct careers page reference.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found. The searches returned many articles about GTA 6 news in October 2025 (GTA Online Halloween events, TikToker harassment incident, GTA Online trailer, fan speculation, Take-Two CEO statements), but NONE of them mention Rockstar Games or Take-Two posting QA, bug-fixing, certification, late-stage development, or release engineering roles tied explicitly to GTA VI on their official careers page in October 2025. The closest job postings found were from September 2025 (UI developer, Lead Software Engineer for data engineering) — not QA roles and not within the October window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No articles found that match the resolution criteria. There are no reports of GTA VI-specific QA/certification/late-stage development job postings during October 2025 on Rockstar's careers page. The September 2025 job postings noted in [Gameranx - 2025-09-15](https://gameranx.com/updates/id/553065/article/rockstar-is-still-hiring-for-gta-6s-largest-game-launch-in-history/) were for UI developers and data engineering roles — not QA or late-stage development categories, and they were posted before the October 1 start date.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. No job posting matching the criteria was reported during October 2025.

question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will ADOR announce new group activities for NewJeans between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Despite the ruling, NewJeans announced their intention to appeal, citing a 'complete breakdown' of trust with ADOR (Soompi, 2025). The group has been on indefinite hiatus since March 2025, after briefly performing under the name NJZ at ComplexCon in Hong Kong (Yahoo, 2025). ADOR has previously urged the members to return to activities as NewJeans, especially around milestone events like the group’s third anniversary (IndiaTimes, 2025). The legal situation now allows ADOR to proceed with official group activities, but the members’ willingness to cooperate remains uncertain. Any announcement of new group activities—such as a comeback, tour, or performance—by ADOR would signal a potential resumption of coordinated efforts between the agency and the group, which is a necessary precondition for a live performance in 2025.

Sources:
- NME: https://www.nme.com/news/music/newjeans-ador-contract-ruling-2025-3987657
- Soompi: https://www.soompi.com/article/2248956wpp/court-rules-newjeans-contracts-with-ador-to-be-valid-members-to-appeal-decision
- Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/k-pop-group-newjeans-loses-legal-battle-against-agency-032155532.html

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if ADOR (via its official website, HYBE’s corporate website, or ADOR’s verified social media accounts on X, Instagram, or Weverse) publishes a public announcement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that includes plans for new group activities under the name 'NewJeans'. Qualifying announcements include, but are not limited to: a new album or single release, a world tour, a concert, a fan meeting, or a televised performance. The announcement must explicitly name 'NewJeans' and describe activities involving at least three members of the group. Pre-recorded content announcements (e.g., music video releases) count. Solo or sub-unit activities do not count. If the announcement is retracted or later proven to be false, the question still resolves based on the initial public statement.

- ADOR official website: https://ador.co.kr
- HYBE corporate website: https://www.hybecorp.com
- ADOR X (Twitter): https://twitter.com/ADOR_official
- ADOR Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ador_official
- Weverse NewJeans page: https://weverse.io/newjeans/official
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong indicator of whether NewJeans will perform again in 2025 because ADOR must initiate and coordinate any official group activity under the court-confirmed contract. An announcement of new activities would signal that ADOR is moving forward with plans, which is a necessary step toward organizing a live performance. Given the group’s ongoing legal dispute and public rift with the agency, the absence of such an announcement would suggest continued deadlock, making a 2025 performance unlikely. Therefore, this observable event provides high informational value about the likelihood of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: ADOR (via official website, HYBE corporate site, ADOR X, ADOR Instagram, or NewJeans Weverse) published a public announcement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 describing plans for new group activities under 'NewJeans' name, involving at least 3 members. Qualifying: album, concert, tour, fan meeting, TV performance. Observable evidence: specific ADOR official statement naming NewJeans + activity plan.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'ADOR NewJeans new group activities announcement 2025' (Oct-Nov window) — to find any qualifying ADOR announcements. Query 2: 'NewJeans ADOR album concert tour announcement November 2025' — same. Query 3: 'ADOR NewJeans album release schedule comeback 2025' — to find specific activity plans. Query 4: 'ADOR official announcement NewJeans activities plans November 2025'. Query 5: 'ADOR NewJeans comeback album release date concert schedule November 2025'. Query 6: 'ADOR official NewJeans comeback schedule release date plan statement' (Nov 14-30). Query 7: 'ADOR NewJeans specific activity announcement late November 2025'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: ADOR official X account post on November 12, 2025 announcing Haerin and Hyein's return to NewJeans activities, confirming preparations for a regular album are complete. Reported by Yonhap, Soompi, Forbes, Korea Times, Straits Times, Rolling Stone. The Straits Times explicitly notes the source as 'a post on Ador's official X account.' Candidate 2: ADOR's press statement (Nov 12) confirming album preparations are complete and future activities are being readied. Not rejected — directly from ADOR official channels. Candidate 3: Min Hee-jin's court testimony on Nov 27 mentioning a NewJeans world tour plan — REJECTED: this came from former CEO Min Hee-jin in court proceedings, not from ADOR's official channels, and the article summary is vague about whether she was describing past plans or future ones. It does not qualify under the resolution criteria (must be from ADOR's official channels).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: ADOR's November 12, 2025 official X post [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/life/newjeans-haerin-and-hyein-to-continue-with-ador) explicitly: (a) issued by ADOR on its official X account (qualifying source); (b) named 'NewJeans' and described member activities returning to the label; (c) ADOR confirmed 'preparations for future activities, including the release of a regular album' [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251112009251320) — this constitutes a plan for a new group activity (album release) involving the full group under the NewJeans name; (d) within the window (November 12 is between Oct 31 and Nov 30, 2025); (e) involves all five members (at least three). The announcement explicitly names 'NewJeans' and describes plans for group activities (album + resumed entertainment activities). However, there is ambiguity: ADOR's Nov 12 statement primarily confirms the return of members, with album preparations noted as already complete but no specific release date, title, or schedule announced. The key question is whether 'preparations for future activities, including a regular album release, are complete and we are awaiting coordination' qualifies as 'plans for new group activities.' The resolution criteria state: 'Qualifying announcements include, but are not limited to: a new album or single release, a world tour, a concert, a fan meeting, or a televised performance.' ADOR explicitly described plans for a regular album release for NewJeans — this satisfies the criteria. The criteria do not require a specific date, only that plans are described.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 12, 2025: ADOR posted on its official X account confirming member returns and album preparations. The Straits Times article is dated November 12, 2025 (KST), citing ADOR's official X post. Yonhap published on November 12, 2025. Multiple high-quality sources confirm this date. Exact time within the day is not available from the sources, but the date of November 12, 2025 is reliably established, which falls within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The October 31, 2025 WION article notes ADOR 'urged the members to resume work and announced preparations for a new NewJeans album' following the court ruling — this may be an earlier qualifying occurrence. However, this characterization is from a news report's description of ADOR welcoming the court ruling, not a direct quote of a specific official announcement. Additionally, the ADOR statement on November 12 via their official X account is the clearest, most well-documented official ADOR announcement specifically naming NewJeans activities/album plans. I cannot confirm with certainty whether ADOR published an explicit activity plan announcement on October 31 — sources describe ADOR's reaction to the court ruling as urging members to return and noting album preparations exist, but the November 12 official X post is the more clearly documented public announcement. The October 31 article suggests this may have occurred earlier in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Multiple sources (Korea Herald Nov 17, Chosun Nov 13, Kyunghyang Shinmun Nov 14) note 'ADOR has not yet announced an official comeback schedule,' indicating no specific concert dates, album titles, or release dates were announced within the window. However, the resolution criteria do not require a specific schedule — they require 'plans for new group activities.' ADOR's confirmation that 'preparations for future activities, including a regular album, are complete' describes plans for a new album, a qualifying activity. The announcement on its official X account on November 12, 2025 naming NewJeans and confirming album activity plans is within the window. No evidence of retraction was found. The announcement was not proven false.
evidence.step8_final_decision: ADOR published an announcement on its official X account on November 12, 2025 (within the October 31–November 30, 2025 window), explicitly naming 'NewJeans' and describing plans for new group activities including the resumption of entertainment activities and preparation for a regular album release involving all five members (clearly more than three). This satisfies the resolution criteria: issued by ADOR via a qualifying official channel (official X account), within the window, naming NewJeans, describing group activities (album) involving at least three members. Resolution: Yes.
