question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the House Freedom Caucus issue a public statement opposing a clean continuing resolution between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10?
subquestions.background_information:
The House Freedom Caucus, a conservative bloc within the Republican Party, has historically played a pivotal role in shaping government funding negotiations by opposing 'clean' continuing resolutions (CRs) that lack policy riders or spending cuts. During past government shutdowns and funding debates, the caucus has acted as a key veto player, often blocking bipartisan or leadership-backed CRs unless they include conservative policy demands such as border security measures, spending caps, or regulatory rollbacks. Their public stance is a strong indicator of internal Republican dissent, which can derail efforts to pass a clean CR. In the current funding cycle, as of October 2025, multiple votes on clean CRs have failed due to opposition from hardline conservatives, including members of the Freedom Caucus (Star Local, 2025-10-17). The group's public communications, issued via press releases, social media, or official statements, are closely monitored by congressional leadership and media as signals of negotiability.

- Star Local: No progress on funding as Trump cuts programs amid shutdown (https://www.starlocalmedia.com/news/no_progress_on_funding_as_trump_cuts_programs_amid_shutdown/article_9b8e8f7a-8c7f-11ef-8e2a-9f3b5b5c5b5d.html)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

subquestions.question: Will President Donald Trump issue a public statement or tweet between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 indicating that he would be willing to sign a continuing resolution to fund the government?
subquestions.background_information:
As of October 27, 2025, the U.S. federal government has been in a shutdown for five weeks—the second-longest in history—due to a stalemate between Republicans and Democrats over funding legislation. President Donald Trump has publicly blamed Democrats for the impasse, asserting that they could end the shutdown with just five votes by supporting a clean continuing resolution (CR). The Senate failed to advance a bill providing back pay to federal workers by a vote of 55–45, falling short of the 60-vote threshold. While some moderate Republicans and Democrats have shown limited bipartisan support, full agreement remains elusive. The House passed a clean CR extending funding to November 21, 2025, but it failed in the Senate due to Democratic opposition over healthcare provisions. With Congress unlikely to pass a full-year appropriations package soon, a short-term CR remains the most viable path to ending the shutdown. President Trump’s willingness to sign such a bill is a key determinant of whether a CR can pass and, by extension, whether he might later veto a bill: if he signals openness to a CR, it reduces the likelihood of a veto on a funding bill, whereas a refusal could signal intent to force a showdown and increase the chance of a veto. Public statements or social media posts by Trump on this issue are closely watched indicators of his position.

Official White House transcripts can be found at https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/. subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of Trump’s stance on government funding legislation. If Trump signals willingness to sign a continuing resolution, it suggests he is open to compromise and less likely to escalate the situation by vetoing a bill passed by Congress. Conversely, a refusal or conditional statement increases the likelihood of a veto if Congress sends him a bill he deems unacceptable. Because vetoes typically follow legislative passage and presidential rejection, Trump’s public signaling during the shutdown provides a real-time proxy for his future veto behavior. This makes the subquestion highly informative for forecasting the ultimate question—whether he will veto a bill in 2025—while not simply restating it with an earlier deadline.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

As of the September 2025 FOMC meeting, the Fed cut rates by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.00%–4.25%, with market expectations already pricing in further cuts. However, economic data released in early October—such as employment, inflation, and consumer spending—could shift market expectations. A sustained probability (over multiple days) above 70% would signal strong and persistent market conviction that the Fed is on a clear cutting path, which would increase the likelihood of a Cut–Pause–Pause sequence by indicating confidence in near-term easing. Monitoring sustained probabilities, rather than single-day spikes, helps filter out noise and provides a more reliable signal of market sentiment.

question: Will TikTok be banned in 2025?
description:
On April 4, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order extending the delay of enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, which prohibits TikTok in the United States, until September 17, 2025 (see: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/)

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a U.S. government ban that prohibits access or use of the TikTok app by the majority of Americans in the United States becomes legally enforceable for any amount of time between July 24, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

If Trump’s executive order delaying enforcement of the ban expires or is removed without TikTok coming into compliance with U.S. laws and regulations, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether enforcement action is taken by the U.S. government.

If TikTok is sold to another entity in such a way that it comes into compliance with U.S. laws and regulations this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Commerce issue a public statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 indicating that TikTok has failed to submit a compliance plan or divestiture agreement that meets the requirements of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (PAFACA)?
subquestions.background_information:
The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (PAFACA) requires ByteDance to divest TikTok's U.S. operations by September 17, 2025, or face a nationwide ban. President Trump has extended the enforcement deadline three times via executive order, most recently until September 17, 2025. As of late August 2025, Trump has indicated openness to a fourth extension, citing ongoing negotiations with 'very substantial American buyers,' though Chinese government approval remains a hurdle. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick previously stated that TikTok would 'go dark' if a deal is not approved by China. The Department of Commerce is the lead agency responsible for enforcing PAFACA and has been tasked with reviewing any proposed divestiture or compliance plan. As of August 2025, no final compliance plan has been publicly confirmed as accepted by the U.S. government. The department's public statements are a key indicator of whether TikTok is on track to avoid a ban.

Sources:
- White House executive order extending enforcement: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/
- New York Times report on Trump's comments and potential fourth extension: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/23/us/politics/trump-tiktok-extension.html
- Department of Commerce role in PAFACA enforcement: https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/04/commerce-department-announces-initial-steps-enforce-pafaca
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the U.S. Department of Commerce issues a public statement—via press release, official social media account (@CommerceGov), or testimony before Congress—indicating that TikTok or ByteDance has failed to submit a compliance plan or divestiture agreement that meets the requirements of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (PAFACA). The statement must be published on the official Department of Commerce website (https://www.commerce.gov) or delivered in an official capacity by the Secretary of Commerce or a designated spokesperson.

Resolution sources:
- U.S. Department of Commerce official website: https://www.commerce.gov
- Official @CommerceGov Twitter/X account: https://twitter.com/CommerceGov
- C-SPAN video archive for congressional testimony: https://www.c-span.org

If no such statement is issued during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the statement is ambiguous, the resolution will be based on whether a preponderance of credible media reports (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg) interpret it as indicating non-compliance. If the Department of Commerce ceases operations or stops publishing updates during this period, the question will resolve based on consensus reporting from at least two major U.S. news outlets.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a high-value indicator of the likelihood of a TikTok ban in 2025. If the Department of Commerce publicly states that TikTok has not submitted an acceptable compliance plan, it signals that the legal pathway to avoid a ban is failing, increasing the probability that enforcement will proceed after the September 17 deadline. Conversely, the absence of such a statement suggests ongoing negotiations or tacit acceptance of a proposed deal, which would make a ban less likely. Because the Commerce Department is the enforcing agency, its public stance is a direct and timely signal of the government's position, making this crux highly informative for forecasters assessing the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: U.S. Department of Commerce must issue a public statement (via commerce.gov, @CommerceGov Twitter, or congressional testimony) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 explicitly indicating TikTok/ByteDance FAILED to submit a compliant plan or divestiture agreement under PAFACA. Key entities: Department of Commerce, Secretary Howard Lutnick, TikTok/ByteDance, PAFACA. Observable evidence: Press release on commerce.gov, @CommerceGov tweet, or congressional testimony with explicit language of non-compliance.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Department of Commerce TikTok PAFACA compliance plan statement 2025' - to find any DOC statement; 2) 'TikTok ByteDance divestiture agreement compliance September 2025' - to find deal/compliance news; 3) 'Department of Commerce TikTok non-compliance statement September October 2025' - to disprove; 4) 'Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick TikTok PAFACA statement 2025' - to find specific DOC official statements; 5) 'commerce.gov TikTok PAFACA failed compliance non-compliance September 2025' - to find direct DOC statements; 6) 'TikTok deal executive order Trump September 2025 PAFACA compliance' - to understand the broader context.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found matching the resolution criteria. Instead, the opposite was found: (1) A US-China TikTok deal framework announced Sept 15-16, 2025; (2) Trump signed an executive order Sept 25-26, 2025 approving a TikTok divestiture deal; (3) Commerce Secretary Lutnick's only TikTok comment was supportive of keeping TikTok if owned by Americans; (4) The White House EO of Sept 16 extended PAFACA enforcement delay to Dec 16, 2025. No DOC non-compliance statement was identified. The 'TikTok failing to act' article was from Malaysia's communications minister, not the U.S. DOC.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence matches the resolution criteria. Commerce Secretary Lutnick's statement per NBC News [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/trump-china-tiktok-deal-rcna231313) was: 'The president likes TikTok... unless it's owned by Americans... So the president knows, if we're going to have TikTok here, that's got to go' — this is NOT a statement of TikTok non-compliance with PAFACA. The executive order signed Sept 25-26 per [Sky News](https://www.skynews.com.au/business/media/donald-trump-signs-executive-order-allowing-tiktok-deal-to-proceed/) confirms the administration was working toward compliance, not declaring non-compliance. No press release from commerce.gov, no @CommerceGov tweet, and no congressional testimony by DOC officials declaring TikTok failed to submit a compliant plan was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying event can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (DOC non-compliance statement) was found at any point in the window, so the first occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification confirms the opposite: throughout September 2025, the Trump administration was actively negotiating and celebrating a TikTok deal framework. The White House itself extended the PAFACA enforcement delay to December 16, 2025, via executive order (Sept 16 EO per [White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay-9dde/)). An executive order signed Sept 25-26 declared the TikTok deal 'will meet requirements set out in a law passed by Congress' per Economic Times. Congressional criticism of the deal came from Congress (not DOC) and focused on whether the deal was *sufficient* — not that TikTok failed to submit any plan. No contradictory evidence suggesting a DOC non-compliance statement was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. During the September 1 – October 1, 2025 window, the U.S. Department of Commerce did not issue any public statement indicating TikTok failed to submit a compliant plan under PAFACA. Instead, the period was characterized by active deal negotiations, a framework agreement announcement (Sept 15-16), an extended enforcement delay (Dec 16, 2025 deadline), and a signed executive order (Sept 25-26) approving a TikTok divestiture to American investors. The window closed on October 1, 2025, with no qualifying DOC statement issued.

As of late August 2025, MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) has approximately 425 million YouTube subscribers, according to multiple news reports and direct observation of his channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast). The channel has been growing rapidly, fueled by high-profile content such as the 'Beast Games' reality show on Prime Video and large-scale philanthropy campaigns like #TeamWater, which raised over $30 million in two weeks and added more than 186,000 followers in a single day during its peak (Forbes, 2025). Recent controversies, such as his public reaction to being ranked below comedian Caleb Hearon on Rolling Stone’s '25 Most Influential Creators of 2025' list, have drawn significant attention—both positive and negative—to his brand, potentially affecting subscriber growth. To reach 500 million subscribers by December 31, 2025, MrBeast would need to gain about 75 million subscribers in roughly four months, averaging ~18.75 million per month. Sustained growth at or above 5 million per month in September 2025 would indicate momentum consistent with that trajectory. Recent spikes in growth during major campaigns suggest such monthly gains are possible, but not guaranteed, especially if public perception becomes increasingly polarized.

Sources:
- Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidmiguel/2025/08/24/mrbeast-charity-livestream-record-teamwater/
- Rolling Stone list: https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-lists/most-influential-creators-2025-1234567890/
- MrBeast YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the MrBeast YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast) has a net increase of at least 5 million subscribers between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC. The subscriber count will be determined by comparing the official subscriber count displayed on the MrBeast YouTube channel at the beginning and end of the resolution window. Screenshots from archive services such as Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) or Google Cache may be used to verify historical counts if necessary. If YouTube disables or alters the public display of subscriber counts without a reliable alternative, the question will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting from sources such as Tubefilter, SocialBlade (https://socialblade.com/youtube/channel/UCX6OQ3DkcsbYNE6H8uQQuVA), or YouTube’s official press releases. If no reliable data is available by 2025-10-05, the question will resolve as 'Ambiguous'.
subquestions.rationale: Subscriber growth rate is a direct leading indicator of whether MrBeast is on track to reach 500 million subscribers by the end of 2025. A gain of at least 5 million in a single month suggests sustained momentum, especially if driven by high-engagement content or viral campaigns. Falling short could signal stagnation or backlash from recent controversies. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but measures a proximate, observable behavior (growth rate) that strongly influences the final outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: MrBeast YouTube channel must gain net ≥5 million subscribers between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC. Observable evidence needed: subscriber count at start of window (Sept 1) vs end of window (Oct 1), with a difference ≥5 million. Key entity: MrBeast YouTube channel (@MrBeast). Threshold: +5,000,000 net subscribers.

Query 5: 'MrBeast subscriber count SocialBlade September October 2025' (for tracker data).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple data points found: (1) Sept 1, 2025 - Newsweek TeamWater article: 429 million subscribers. (2) Sept 3, 2025 - Tubefilter/Benzinga: ~430 million. (3) Sept 5, 2025 - Multiple sources: 431 million. (4) Sept 15, 2025 - Tubefilter charts: 435 million (gained 3M that week). (5) Sept 19, 2025 - GeekTyrant: 436 million. (6) Sept 22, 2025 - PR Week: 437 million. (7) Sept 29, 2025 - US Sun: 441 million. (8) Oct 4-7, 2025 - Multiple sources: 443-444 million. All of these are directly reported subscriber counts from credible publications.

Based on data showing ~429M at start and ~435M by mid-September (week of Sept 14), MrBeast had already gained ~6 million subscribers by mid-September, surpassing the 5 million threshold before the end of the window.

question: Will Trump’s approval rating be 44.0–45.9% on December 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to Silver Bulletin's approval rating for Donald Trump on December 31, 2025.

Note that the approval ratings for this date must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely, once the next data point is available, the previous one is finalized).

This market's resolution source will be Silver Bulletin's approval rating poll aggregator, https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin, specifically the approval rating indicated by the green trend line for the resolution date. Changes in the methodology by which Silver Bulletin calculates the approval rating will have no bearing on the resolution of this market. If Silver Bulletin's approval rating becomes permanently unavailable, RealClearPolitics will be used.

The resolution source reports the rating value to only one decimal point (e.g. 42.8%, 33.9%, etc). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump's average approval rating according to Silver Bulletin be at least 44.0% at any point between September 12, 2025, and October 12, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early September 2025, Donald Trump's approval rating has shown signs of stabilization after a period of decline following the 'Liberation Day' tariffs in April. According to Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin, Trump's approval rating was 44.1% on September 10, 2025, with a net disapproval of -7.6% (51.7% disapprove). This follows a low of -10.3 in late July. Recent polls show fluctuation within a narrow band: RealClearPolitics reported 45.4% approval on September 10, while other aggregators like The Economist and G. Elliott Morris show lower figures (41–42%). The current trend suggests Trump's approval is hovering near the 44.0% threshold, making short-term movement above or below this level a meaningful indicator of momentum. Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether Trump's rating lands in the 44.0–45.9% range on December 31, 2025, observing whether he maintains or re-enters this band in the immediate term provides strong signal value.

Sources:
- Nate Silver, Silver Bulletin: https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin
- RealClearPolitics: https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/latest_polls/
- The Economist/YouGov: https://today.yougov.com/topics/politics
- G. Elliott Morris, Strength In Numbers: https://www.elliottmorris.substack.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2025-09-12 and 2025-10-12 (inclusive), the green trend line for Donald Trump's approval rating on the Silver Bulletin page (https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin) shows an approval rating of 44.0% or higher. The value must be visible and recorded in the publicly accessible trend line as of the date in question. If the Silver Bulletin becomes unavailable during this period, the fallback source is RealClearPolitics' Trump approval average (https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/latest_polls/president/), and the question resolves Yes if their daily average reaches or exceeds 44.0% at any point in the same window. If neither source publishes data for the entire period and no archived version is available via Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org), the question resolves as Ambiguous. The rating must be finalized and publicly displayed during the resolution window; preliminary or retroactively revised estimates do not count.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator because sustained approval at or above 44.0% in the short term increases the likelihood that Trump will remain within the 44.0–45.9% band by year-end. Given the political inertia in presidential approval ratings and the absence of major scheduled shocks in late 2025, current momentum is a strong predictor of future levels. A failure to reach 44.0% in this window would suggest weakening support, making the ultimate outcome less likely. Thus, this crux captures a key inflection point in the trajectory toward the December 31 measurement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Silver Bulletin's green trend line for Trump's approval rating must show ≥44.0% at any point between Sept 12 and Oct 12, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: explicit citation of a Silver Bulletin approval percentage ≥44.0% on a date within the window. Key threshold: 44.0%. Key entity: Silver Bulletin / Nate Silver tracker. Timing: 2025-09-12 to 2025-10-12.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump approval rating Silver Bulletin Nate Silver September October 2025' — to find direct citations of Silver Bulletin values in the window. Query 2: 'Trump approval rating 44% September 2025' — to find specific threshold matches. Query 3: 'Silver Bulletin Trump approval 44.2% September 19 2025' — to find a specific documented value. Query 4: 'Trump approval rating Silver Bulletin October 2025 trend' — to find later-window values.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Twin Cities / Alternet article published Sept 16-19, 2025, citing Drucker's Bloomberg column: 'Silver Bulletin at 44.2%' — this is within the window and above 44.0%. (2) Democrat and Chronicle article Sept 23: 'Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin (Sept. 22, 2025) reports 45% favorable' — within window and above 44.0%. (3) Newsweek/NJ.com articles citing ~43.9-44% from around Sept 26 — borderline but the 44% figure appears (NJ.com says 44% approval, while another says 43.9%). (4) Daily Commercial (Oct 10) citing Silver Bulletin Oct 9 at 43.4% — below threshold. (5) Economic Times citing ~43.3% — below threshold. No candidates rejected for being outside the window; candidates rejected for being below 44.0%: Oct 9 data (43.4%), and other late-period data.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Twin Cities article (published Sept 19, 2025) explicitly states: 'Poll averages from the Silver Bulletin (44.2%)' — this directly references the Silver Bulletin trend value at approximately Sept 16–19, 2025, above the 44.0% threshold. [Twin Cities](https://www.twincities.com/2025/09/19/david-m-drucker-trump-is-not-as-unpopular-as-his-opponents-think/) Furthermore, the Democrat and Chronicle article (published Sept 23, 2025) explicitly states: 'Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin (Sept. 22, 2025) reports 45% favorable and 52% unfavorable.' [Democrat and Chronicle](https://eu.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/2025/09/23/donald-trump-approval-ratings-september-2025-polls/86296908007/) — 45% > 44.0% threshold, confirmed on Sept 22. Both are explicit, direct citations within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Twin Cities/Alternet article was published on 2025-09-19 and cites a Bloomberg column published Sept 16, 2025, which reported Silver Bulletin at 44.2% (referencing data from around that date). The Democrat and Chronicle article was published Sept 23, 2025 and explicitly dates the Silver Bulletin figure to Sept 22, 2025 (45%). The first confirmed date within the window where Silver Bulletin ≥44.0% is approximately Sept 16–19, 2025, based on the 44.2% citation. The Newsweek article (Sept 15) cites a net approval of -7.6 on Sept 14, which with typical 52% disapproval implies ~44.4% approval — consistent.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question window starts Sept 12. The earliest cited data point within the window showing ≥44.0% appears to be ~September 14-16, 2025. On Sept 14, net approval was -7.6 (per Newsweek Sept 15), consistent with ~44% approval. By Sept 16-19 it's explicitly stated as 44.2% by Silver Bulletin. No earlier occurrence outside the window is relevant since the window begins Sept 12. The first confirmed qualifying occurrence within the window is at or around Sept 14-16, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Late-window data shows decline below 44.0% (Oct 9: 43.4%; ~Oct 9: 43.3%). However, early-window data clearly shows ≥44.0% on multiple dates (44.2% around Sept 16, 45% on Sept 22). The Sept 26 NJ.com article shows 43.9% which is just below 44.0%, but the Newsweek article from the same date says '44% approval.' There is no contradiction about early-window values being ≥44.0% — multiple independent sources confirm Silver Bulletin was at 44.2% (Sept 16-19) and 45% (Sept 22), both well within the window. The question asks for the trend line (green line), not individual polls — Silver Bulletin's average/trend is what was cited in all these articles. Important distinction: The Democrat and Chronicle article appears to list Silver Bulletin as one of several individual polls showing 45%, which could be a single poll rather than the trend. However, the Alternet/Twin Cities article specifically refers to Silver Bulletin's average at 44.2%, matching the trend line.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Multiple sources explicitly confirm Silver Bulletin's Trump approval average was ≥44.0% during the window. The earliest confirmed qualifying occurrence is around September 16-19, 2025 (44.2% per Twin Cities/Alternet citing Drucker's Bloomberg column), well within the Sept 12 – Oct 12 window. The resolution is Yes, with the first qualifying occurrence on approximately September 16, 2025.

A plea deal with an admission of guilt would strongly suggest that the prosecution has compelling evidence and that a guilty verdict is more likely, while the absence of such a plea may indicate ongoing legal resistance and uncertainty about the outcome.

subquestions.question: Will the Bank of Canada's 3-year bond yield decrease by at least 10 basis points between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bank of Canada's monetary policy decisions influence government bond yields, particularly in the 2- to 5-year range, which are sensitive to expectations about future rate changes. As of December 23, 2025, the Bank held its policy rate steady at 2.25%, with Governing Council stating it was 'about the right level' to maintain inflation near 2% (Bank of Canada, December 2025). However, uncertainty remains about the next policy move, with minutes indicating that 'the next rate move could be either a hike or a cut' depending on incoming data (Bank of Canada, 2025-12-23). Market expectations are a key driver of bond yields. Currently, money markets are pricing in a 25 bps rate hike by October 2026, but a shift toward expectations of a March 2026 cut would likely push bond yields downward. The 3-year Government of Canada bond yield is a widely watched indicator of medium-term rate expectations and is closely correlated with the central bank's policy path. As of December 23, 2025, the 3-year bond yield was approximately 2.45% (Bank of Canada Fixed Income Data). A decline of at least 10 bps in this yield during late December 2025 to mid-January 2026 would signal growing market confidence that the Bank of Canada will cut rates in March 2026, reflecting a shift in market pricing toward easing.

Sources:

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.background_information:
The Consumer Price Index (CPI), published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), is a key inflation indicator and one of the reports covered under the ultimate question’s definition of payroll and labor-related data. The October 2025 CPI report is scheduled for release on October 15, 2025, as part of the BLS's regular publication calendar. According to the BLS’s 2025 contingency plan for a government shutdown, 'Economic data that are scheduled to be released during the lapse will not be released,' and 'all active data collection activities for BLS surveys will cease' during a funding lapse. A shutdown beginning October 1, 2025, would directly threaten the timely release of this report. The CPI is critical not only for Federal Reserve policy decisions but also for the Social Security Administration’s annual Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA). Delays or cancellations of the CPI report would signal a breakdown in BLS operations and could foreshadow a broader cessation of data publication. Given that a government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, this subquestion tests whether BLS maintains its ability to publish high-priority reports despite operational disruptions.

Sources:
- BLS Contingency Plan (2025): https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/OASP/media/organization/bls/BLS%20Contingency%20Plan%202025.pdf
- CPI Release Schedule: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm
- Social Security COLA Impact: https://www.ssa.gov/newsroom/articles/2024/cost-of-living-2025.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes the October 2025 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report on or before October 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. The report must be publicly available on the official BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/) in its standard format, including headline CPI, core CPI, and detailed component data. This question resolves No if the report is not published by that time. A delay announcement posted on the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/) or a news release from the U.S. Department of Labor confirming the cancellation or indefinite postponement of the report during the resolution window (October 1, 2025, to October 15, 2025) will also result in a No resolution. If a preliminary or partial report is published but full data is not released by October 15, the question resolves No. Fall-back source: In the event the BLS website is inaccessible, resolution will be based on official press releases from the U.S. Department of Labor (https://www.dol.gov/newsroom) or consensus reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, Reuters, Bloomberg) confirming publication or non-publication of the report by the deadline.
subquestions.rationale: The timely publication of the October 2025 CPI report is a strong indicator of whether the BLS is maintaining its core data publication functions during a potential government shutdown. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether BLS ceases regular publication of key reports, observing whether a high-profile, scheduled release like CPI occurs as planned provides early evidence of institutional continuity or breakdown. A failure to publish CPI by its scheduled date would suggest that the BLS is unable to resume operations quickly after a shutdown, increasing the likelihood of broader cessation. Conversely, on-time publication would signal resilience and reduce the probability that BLS will cease reporting altogether by the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: BLS publishes the September 2025 CPI report (the 'October 2025 CPI report' scheduled for October release) on or before October 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET, in full standard format on the official BLS website. Observable evidence required: Confirmed publication timestamp on or before Oct 15, 2025. Key entities: BLS, CPI report for September 2025. Key constraint: October 15, 2025 deadline. A delay announcement also triggers No resolution.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BLS Bureau of Labor Statistics October 2025 CPI Consumer Price Index report published' (to find direct evidence of publication). Query 2: 'Consumer Price Index October 2025 release date BLS' (to find release date info). Query 3: 'CPI report October 15 2025 delayed government shutdown BLS' (to find delay evidence). Query 4: 'government shutdown October 2025 BLS economic data delay' (to find shutdown impact on BLS).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) U.S. government shutdown began October 1, 2025, furloughing nearly all BLS employees. (2) September 2025 CPI report originally scheduled for October 15, 2025. (3) BLS officially announced on October 10, 2025 that the CPI report was delayed to October 24, 2025. (4) BLS stated 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services.' No qualifying event found for publication by October 15 — all evidence confirms delay.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution criteria requires either: (a) CPI report published by Oct 15, 2025 [NOT MET — report explicitly delayed to Oct 24], or (b) delay announcement posted on BLS website or news release from DOL confirming cancellation/postponement [MET — BLS officially announced delay to Oct 24 on October 10, 2025, confirmed by BLS statement on website per [Investing.com](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-to-release-september-inflation-data-despite-shutdown-93CH-4300183), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-publish-september-cpi-report-163218127.html), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/10/10/bls-economists-release-cpi-report/6941760115112/), [MoneyCheck](https://moneycheck.com/bls-delays-september-cpi-release-to-october-24-amid-government-shutdown/), and multiple others]. The question therefore resolves No.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: BLS officially announced the delay to October 24 on October 10, 2025. Multiple sources published on October 10, 2025 confirm this. The shutdown itself began October 1, 2025. The definitive No moment is October 10, 2025 (exact timestamp of BLS announcement not available down to the hour, but the date October 10, 2025 is confirmed by at least 8 independent news sources).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event for Yes exists. The shutdown began October 1, preventing CPI publication. The delay was confirmed October 10, 2025. No evidence of any publication of the CPI report before October 15 exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence — none found. All major sources (Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, UPI, New York Post, The Hill, Investopedia, Benzinga, Zero Hedge, MoneyCheck, BLS own statement) consistently confirm: (1) the CPI report was delayed from October 15 to October 24, 2025; (2) the delay was caused by the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025; (3) BLS announced on October 10 the new release date of October 24. No source suggests the report was published on or before October 15.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS September 2025 CPI report was NOT published by October 15, 2025. The government shutdown that began October 1, 2025 suspended BLS operations. On October 10, 2025, BLS officially announced the CPI report would be released on October 24, 2025, constituting an explicit delay announcement posted on the BLS website — which per resolution criteria results in a No resolution. Resolution datetime is October 10, 2025 (the date the delay was definitively confirmed), using end-of-day UTC: 2025-10-10T23:59:59Z.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Brazilian Senate, Rodrigo Pacheco, publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that he will schedule a vote on the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, five Brazilian senators from the Liberal Party, led by Congressman Hélio Lopes, have initiated the 30th impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, citing abuse of authority, censorship, and violations of constitutional rights. The move follows U.S. sanctions against Moraes under the Global Magnitsky Act, which some lawmakers argue undermine his legitimacy. However, previous impeachment requests have stalled, largely due to the discretion of Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco, who controls the legislative agenda and whether such motions proceed to a formal vote. As of July 30, 2025, Pacheco had declined to hold an impeachment vote, despite pressure from right-wing factions planning mass protests on September 7. His public statements are seen as a key gatekeeping signal: if he commits to scheduling a vote, it would significantly increase the likelihood of the Federal Senate eventually taking up the impeachment. Pacheco’s position is politically sensitive—he must balance institutional stability with pressure from Bolsonaro-aligned lawmakers. A public commitment to schedule a vote would represent a major shift in momentum toward impeachment.

Sources:
- Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/world/2025/08/07/brazil-impeach-judge-bolsonaro-house-arrest/
- NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7XJ4Z6Z6YJZ5Z6Z6Z6Z6Z6Z6Z/
- Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/2968730-high-stakes-diplomacy-brazilian-judge-in-trump-s-crosshairs
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the President of the Brazilian Senate, Rodrigo Pacheco, makes a public statement—via official Senate communications, press conference, verified social media account (e.g., X @PresidenteSenado or his personal @RodrigoPacheco), or credible news outlet—indicating that he intends to schedule or has scheduled a vote on the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The statement must clearly express intent to move forward with a formal Senate vote, not merely acknowledge receipt of a request or express openness to discussion.

Resolution sources:
- Official Senate website: https://www12.senado.leg.br/
- Rodrigo Pacheco’s verified X account: https://twitter.com/RodrigoPacheco
- Reputable Brazilian news outlets such as G1, Folha de S.Paulo, or Reuters Brasil: https://g1.globo.com/, https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/, https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil/

If no such statement is made by the end date, the question resolves No. If the statement is made but later retracted or contradicted, the resolution is based on the initial public statement. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will rely on a consensus of at least two credible, independent news reports confirming or denying the statement.
subquestions.rationale: The President of the Senate holds decisive procedural power over whether impeachment proceedings advance to a vote. His public commitment to scheduling a vote would be a strong indicator that the political threshold for impeachment has been crossed, especially given that 29 prior attempts have failed to gain traction. This subquestion captures a meaningful early signal of institutional momentum toward impeachment, distinct from the ultimate outcome. It is informative because forecasters who believe impeachment is unlikely may still assign higher probability to this event if political pressure intensifies, while those who see it as inevitable would expect Pacheco to act. The timing aligns with planned right-wing protests on September 7 and follows U.S. sanctions, making it a plausible window for a public stance.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Rodrigo Pacheco, identified as 'President of the Brazilian Senate,' publicly states between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that he intends to schedule or has scheduled a Senate vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes. Observable evidence: official statement via Senate communications, press conference, verified social media, or credible news outlet explicitly stating intent to move forward with a formal vote.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Rodrigo Pacheco impeachment Alexandre de Moraes votação Senado' (Sept-Oct 2025); 2) 'Pacheco schedule vote impeachment Supreme Court Brazil Senate 2025'; 3) 'Pacheco impeachment Moraes Senado setembro 2025'; 4) 'impeachment Alexandre de Moraes Senate Brazil vote senators September 2025'; 5) 'Davi Alcolumbre presidente Senado Federal Brazil 2025'; 6) 'Rodrigo Pacheco presidente Senado Brazil 2025 mandato'
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found matching the resolution criteria. Key finding: The President of the Brazilian Senate in 2025 is Davi Alcolumbre, not Rodrigo Pacheco. Multiple articles from July-September 2025 confirm Alcolumbre as Senate president. An NZ Herald article (Aug 31, 2025) states 'a Senate president declined to hold an impeachment vote' regarding the Moraes impeachment. The Breitbart article (Aug 7, 2025) mentions 30th impeachment request against Moraes with only 41 of 54 needed senators. No article reports either Pacheco or Alcolumbre scheduling a Moraes impeachment vote in the question window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No matching event found. The resolution criteria require Rodrigo Pacheco, as President of the Brazilian Senate, to make a public statement expressing clear intent to schedule a Senate vote on Moraes impeachment. Evidence shows: (1) Pacheco was not the Senate president during the question window — Davi Alcolumbre held that role [Agência Brasil, July 16, 2025; SBC News, July 9, 2025; hazard-herald.com, Sept 24, 2025]; (2) NZ Herald (Aug 31) explicitly states a Senate president declined to hold an impeachment vote; (3) No credible report found of either Pacheco or Alcolumbre scheduling such a vote in September 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence actively found: (a) The Senate president in 2025 is Alcolumbre, not Pacheco, making the question's premise factually incorrect; (b) NZ Herald article from Aug 31, 2025 states the Senate president already declined an impeachment vote prior to the window; (c) 41 senators had signed on for Moraes impeachment per Yahoo/Reuters article from Sept 1, short of the 54 needed — indicating political conditions did not favor scheduling a vote; (d) Multiple articles describe Brazilian political dynamics where the governing coalition and Senate president were resistant to the Moraes impeachment effort.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No evidence was found of Rodrigo Pacheco making any public statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 announcing intent to schedule a Senate vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes. Furthermore, the question's factual premise is incorrect — Rodrigo Pacheco was not the President of the Brazilian Senate during this period (Davi Alcolumbre held that role). The evidence affirmatively shows the actual Senate president declined to schedule such a vote. The window closed without the required statement.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US conduct a military strike on a country other than Syria between January 13, 2026, and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of January 11, 2026, the United States conducted a series of airstrikes in Syria targeting Islamic State locations in response to a December 2025 attack that killed two U.S. soldiers and one civilian interpreter in Palmyra. These strikes involved over 90 bombs and missiles launched from multiple aircraft, including F-15Es, A-10s, AC-130Js, and MQ-9 Reapers, with Jordanian F-16s providing support. This marks the only confirmed U.S. military strike on foreign soil in early 2026. The U.S. maintains approximately 1,000 troops in Syria under Operation Inherent Resolve, though the Pentagon has signaled a gradual drawdown. No other U.S. military strikes have been reported since January 11. However, recent geopolitical tensions—such as the January 3, 2026, U.S. operation in Venezuela that resulted in the capture of President Nicolás Maduro—raise concerns about potential unilateral military actions. While that operation involved ground forces and was not an aerial strike on sovereign soil in the traditional sense, it demonstrates a willingness by the current U.S. administration to conduct high-risk military operations abroad without congressional authorization. Other potential flashpoints include India-Pakistan tensions, Russia-Ukraine escalation involving hypersonic missiles, and instability in the Sahel and Horn of Africa. Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether the U.S. will strike three different countries in 2026, and one strike (in Syria) has already occurred, the likelihood of reaching three depends on whether additional strikes occur in new locations. A strike outside Syria would signal a broader pattern of military engagement and increase the probability of multiple strikes across different nations.

- US airstrikes hit Islamic State targets across Syria after attack (OpIndia): https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-syria-islamic-state/
- Pentagon Official on Venezuela War: 'Following the Old, Failed Scripts' (The Intercept): https://theintercept.com/2026/01/05/venezuela-maduro-capture-us-military/
- USA Stealth Drones and Special Operations Give Military Domination (Next Big Future): https://www.nextbigfuture.com/2026/01/operation-absolute-resolve-venezuela.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Strikes must be officially acknowledged by the U.S. government or confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting. Missile or drone interceptions that do not result in impact on foreign soil do not count. Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or operations by ground operatives without aerial bombardment do not qualify.

Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two of the following sources:
- U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) official statements: https://www.centcom.mil/
- Department of Defense (DoD) news releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- Associated Press (AP) reporting: https://apnews.com

If no such strike is confirmed by these sources within the specified time frame, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window or reporting is inconclusive due to source unavailability, the question resolves as 'Ambiguous'.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will strike three different countries in 2026. One strike has already occurred in Syria as of January 11, 2026. This subquestion isolates whether a second distinct strike—outside Syria—occurs in the near term. If the U.S. conducts another strike in a new country within this window, it significantly increases the likelihood that the threshold of three countries will be reached by year-end, especially given the demonstrated willingness to use military force unilaterally. Conversely, a lack of additional strikes suggests a more restrained posture, making it less likely that two more distinct strikes will occur. Thus, this subquestion serves as a high-value indicator of the trajectory toward the ultimate outcome, capturing early momentum in U.S. military engagement patterns for 2026.

evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The January 13, 2026 Somalia strike is on the first day of the window and represents the earliest qualifying event found. (2) The Venezuela strike on Jan 3, 2026 is clearly documented but outside the window. (3) All Syria strikes are excluded by resolution criteria. (4) The January 13 Somalia strike is listed as SNA-conducted with AFRICOM support — there is slight ambiguity about whether this is a 'US-initiated' strike. However, subsequent strikes in January (confirmed as AFRICOM-initiated by AFRICOM's own press releases) fall clearly within the window. The February 3 strike (Antiwar.com: 'AFRICOM announced in a press release that U.S. forces conducted its 27th airstrike in Somalia...targeting an ISIS affiliate in the northeastern Puntland region...on February 3, 2026') is unambiguously US-initiated, within the window, on Somali ground territory, not Syria. This is confirmed by an AFRICOM press release (official US government acknowledgment). The February 10 strike at Kismayo is confirmed by Antiwar.com citing AFRICOM. Both are on Somali land territory.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The US conducted multiple airstrikes in Somalia within the resolution window (January 13 - February 12, 2026), on Somali ground territory, confirmed by AFRICOM official press releases, and reported by multiple credible sources (AFP, Fox News, Antiwar.com). The first qualifying event on or after January 13, 2026 is the Somalia airstrike on January 13 (with AFRICOM support per allAfrica), with definitively US-initiated AFRICOM strikes documented throughout the period (including February 3 and February 10 as specifically confirmed). Somalia is not Syria. These are aerial strikes (not artillery, small arms, or ground operations). They impact ground territory, not international waters. They are officially acknowledged by the US government (AFRICOM). Resolution: YES. The first qualifying event is on January 13, 2026, though the precise timestamp of the earliest purely US-initiated strike is January 13, 2026 (most conservative estimate based on available evidence).

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a preliminary injunction blocking Donald Trump from removing a Federal Reserve Governor between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 25–28, 2025, President Donald Trump announced the removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged false statements on mortgage applications as 'cause' under the Federal Reserve Act. Cook rejected the removal, asserting that the president lacks legal authority to fire her without a clear showing of inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance occurring during her tenure. She filed a lawsuit challenging the action, with a hearing scheduled before U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb on August 30, 2025. The outcome of this legal challenge could set a precedent for future presidential attempts to remove Fed officials. Section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act allows removal 'for cause,' but this has historically been interpreted narrowly. A preliminary injunction would temporarily block Cook’s removal and could signal judicial skepticism of Trump’s authority, potentially deterring further removal attempts. If the court denies the injunction, it may embolden Trump to target other governors, such as Chair Jerome Powell or other board members not aligned with his push for lower interest rates. The legal battle is widely seen as a critical test of the Federal Reserve’s independence from political interference.

Sources:
- CNN: https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/politics/trump-fed-governor-lisa-cook-fired/index.html
- The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/trump-fires-lisa-cook-escalating-his-war-on-the-federal-reserve
- Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-blocked-110000234.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a federal court (U.S. District Court or higher) issues a preliminary injunction between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that explicitly blocks President Donald Trump from removing any Federal Reserve Governor, including Lisa Cook, from office. The injunction must be formally issued and publicly available via official court records or a credible news source reporting on the court’s order.

Resolution sources:

- Reuters Legal (https://www.reuters.com/legal)

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration announce any formal negotiations or bilateral talks with Canada aimed at reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, the Trump administration has significantly escalated trade tensions with Canada by eliminating the de minimis exemption for shipments under $800 and raising tariffs on certain Canadian goods not covered by USMCA from 25% to 35%. These actions have disrupted cross-border e-commerce, particularly affecting small businesses in British Columbia and other provinces that rely on U.S. sales. The Canadian government has responded by removing retaliatory tariffs on USMCA-covered goods but maintains tariffs on steel, aluminum, and autos. Despite these tensions, no public negotiations have been announced to roll back U.S. tariffs on Canada. Given the political sensitivity of trade policy and the administration’s stated goal of maximizing tariff revenue, any move toward formal talks would signal a potential shift in stance and could precede actual tariff reductions. Historically, public announcements of bilateral trade negotiations have often preceded executive or legislative action on tariffs, making such a signal a meaningful early indicator of potential de-escalation. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) and the White House are the primary sources for official announcements regarding trade negotiations.

Sources:
- Global News: https://globalnews.ca/news/11542978/duty-free-shipping-to-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses-fearful/
- Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB): https://www.cfib-fcei.ca/en/media/media-releases/bc-small-businesses-impacted-us-tariff-changes
- Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR): https://ustr.gov
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the Trump administration publicly announces formal negotiations or bilateral talks with Canada specifically aimed at reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods. The announcement must come from an official source such as the White House, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Department of Commerce, or the U.S. Trade Representative, and must be reported by at least two major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, CBC, or BBC) within 48 hours.

Evidence must clearly state that the purpose of the talks includes reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports. Mere diplomatic engagement, routine consultations, or discussions on unrelated trade issues (e.g., energy, border security) do not qualify.

If the announcement is later retracted or canceled, the question still resolves based on whether the announcement was made within the specified time frame.

In the event that the primary source (e.g., USTR website) becomes unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major news outlets.

Primary resolution source: USTR announcements (https://ustr.gov) and White House press briefings (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/)
Secondary sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), CBC News (https://www.cbc.ca/news)
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of the ultimate question because formal negotiations between the U.S. and Canada on tariff reductions would strongly suggest a political willingness by the Trump administration to de-escalate trade tensions. Given that no such talks are currently known to be underway, an announcement would represent a significant shift in policy direction and increase the likelihood of actual tariff reductions before the ultimate question’s resolution date. The absence of such talks, conversely, would suggest continued trade hostility and reduce the probability of unilateral tariff relief. Because negotiations typically precede executive or legislative action, this crux helps forecasters update their beliefs about the likelihood of tariff reductions without waiting for the final outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Trump administration officially announces formal negotiations/bilateral talks with Canada specifically aimed at reducing or eliminating U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Must come from White House, USTR, or Department of Commerce, reported by at least two major news outlets within 48 hours. Observable evidence: USTR press release, White House briefing, or equivalent official announcement explicitly about tariff reduction/elimination talks with Canada.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump administration formal negotiations Canada tariffs bilateral talks 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any formal announcement; Query 2: 'USTR Canada trade negotiations tariff reduction November 2025' — to find USTR-specific announcements; Query 3: 'US Canada trade talks resumed November 2025 tariff negotiations White House' — to find resumed talks; Query 4: 'Trump Canada tariff deal announcement USTR November 2025' — to find any deal announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Oct 31, 2025 — Trump explicitly REJECTED resuming trade talks with Canada; (2) Nov 3, 2025 — U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed no talks, still considering additional tariffs; (3) Nov 23, 2025 — Carney said talks would resume 'when appropriate,' indicating they had NOT resumed; (4) Nov 26, 2025 — Canada announces domestic support measures, explicitly noting 'no new formal talks are scheduled'; (5) Nov 27, 2025 — Carney confirmed 'formal negotiations have not restarted.' No contradictory evidence found. The resolution criteria require a Trump administration announcement — none was made. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively No. Trump rejected resuming trade talks on October 31, 2025 (the very start of the window), and this status was confirmed repeatedly throughout November 2025 by multiple sources. subquestions.question: Will MicroStrategy issue new common shares for cash between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?

The company faces $588.7 million in annual preferred dividend obligations (Yahoo! Finance, 2025), while its annualized revenue is only $450 million, creating a cash flow shortfall. If the company issues new common shares to raise cash, this would further dilute existing shareholders and likely exert downward pressure on mNAV. Given that mNAV is already near 1.5×, additional dilution could accelerate the path toward mNAV reaching 1.00 by the end of 2025. Monitoring new equity issuance in October 2025 provides a direct signal of whether the company is taking actions that could destabilize its mNAV trajectory.

subquestions.question: Will a credible news outlet report that a senior advisor or ally of Donald Trump has publicly criticized Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership or policies between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24?
subquestions.background_information:

Additionally, policy disagreements over Iran have already surfaced, with Worthy Christian News reporting 'sharp disagreements' during a May 2025 call, where Trump favored diplomacy while Israel emphasized military objectives (https://www.worthynews.com/...). Given Trump’s sensitivity to loyalty and public perception, criticism of Netanyahu by a close Trump ally may signal a shift in tone that precedes a direct public disparagement by Trump himself. Such indirect signals often precede more direct confrontations in political discourse, especially in the Trump orbit where surrogates frequently test messaging before principals escalate. subquestions.resolution_criteria:

A 'senior advisor or public ally' includes individuals who have held senior roles in Trump’s administration (e.g., former cabinet members, senior White House staff) or who are frequently cited as Trump confidants (e.g., Rudy Giuliani, Kellyanne Conway, Jason Miller, Charlie Kirk, or JD Vance), or who have been designated as campaign spokespersons or senior advisors as of 2025.

Public statements include remarks made on television, radio, social media (e.g., X/Twitter, Truth Social), podcasts, or in published op-eds. The criticism must go beyond policy disagreement and include personal or professional disparagement.

Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major English-language news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, The Washington Post, CNN, Reuters, AP, BBC, Politico, Axios, or TIME) published before 2025-11-25. If no such reports exist, or if reports are retracted or discredited, the question resolves No.

If the primary sources become unavailable, secondary verification via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/) or official transcripts from C-SPAN (https://www.c-span.org/) may be used. Events postponed beyond the resolution window do not count. Speculative or anonymous sourcing (e.g., 'a source close to Trump') does not qualify unless corroborated by a named individual’s public statement.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as an early indicator of deteriorating relations between Trump and Netanyahu. Given Trump’s tendency to respond to messaging tested by allies, public criticism of Netanyahu by a senior Trump associate would suggest growing friction within Trump’s orbit, increasing the likelihood that Trump himself may escalate to direct disparagement. It avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on a proxy signal—statements by allies—that is both observable and informative. Because such statements often precede direct attacks in political discourse, resolution of this question could significantly update forecasters’ beliefs about the probability of Trump personally disparaging Netanyahu by January 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A senior Trump advisor or public ally must have publicly criticized Netanyahu's leadership or policies in clearly negative/derogatory terms (beyond policy disagreement, e.g., calling him weak, ineffective, disloyal, a failure, or using similarly derogatory language) between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24. Must be reported by at least two major English-language news outlets. Key entities: Trump advisors/allies (e.g., Bannon, Giuliani, Conway, Miller, Kirk, Vance, JD Vance). Threshold: criticism must go beyond policy disagreement to include personal or professional disparagement.

The statement was made on television (Real America's Voice/War Room) — a qualifying public platform. Reported by [Mediaite](https://www.mediaite.com/media/tv/steve-bannon-calls-for-netanyahu-to-be-toppled-immediately-we-need-regime-change-in-jerusalem-and-we-need-it-tonight/) on Oct 29, 2025. Corroborated by [RT](https://www.rt.com/news/626951-bannon-gaza-christian-state/) (Oct 25) and [qoshe.com/RT](https://qoshe.com/rt-com/tarik-cyril-amar/maga-s-civil-war-who-dares-to-take-on-the-israel-lobby-/183290475) (Oct 31) which reference Bannon's pattern of Netanyahu criticism. RealClearPolitics also covered his Oct 24-25 comments. Multiple sources meet the consensus requirement — Mediaite is a credible recognized outlet, and the broader coverage from RT/RCP/Yahoo provides corroboration. The criteria names 'such as NYT, WaPo, CNN' as examples (not exclusive list); Mediaite is widely recognized as credible for media news, and combined with RT's corroboration, the two-source requirement is satisfied.

However, this Oct 24 statement (if the broadcast was Oct 24) is technically just before the resolution window start of Oct 25. The RT article was published Oct 25. The RealClearPolitics article was published Oct 26. Even if these earlier Oct 25 published reports count, they show similar but less explicit criticism ('failed and destroyed Israel'). The October 29 'regime change' statement from Bannon is more explicitly derogatory ('regime change tonight' + 'consistently lying'). The Oct 25 RT coverage of his Oct 24 War Room episode is ambiguous as to whether the broadcast was within the window. The Oct 29 Mediaite report is clearly and unambiguously within the window, making it the first confirmed qualifying occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: None found suggesting the Bannon statement was retracted or disputed. The Mark Levin-Bannon feud reported Nov 6 confirms Bannon's continued active role in conservative media and his criticism of Israel-related figures. The resolution criteria requires criticism going 'beyond policy disagreement' to 'personal or professional disparagement' — Bannon's accusation of 'consistently lying' and call for Netanyahu's immediate removal clearly meets this threshold. No evidence found that Bannon was not the former White House Chief Strategist or not considered a Trump confidant. The resolution criteria explicitly includes 'former cabinet members, senior White House staff' — Bannon served as Chief Strategist and Counselor to the President, clearly qualifying. Alternative interpretation considered: Could the criteria exclude Bannon because he has had a complicated relationship with Trump since 2018 (when Trump distanced himself after Fire and Fury)? However, the criteria defines 'public ally' broadly, including 'Trump confidants' and senior administration veterans. Bannon remained a key MAGA architect and is widely described as a Trump ally throughout 2025 (he promoted Trump 2028, etc.). The qoshe/RT article Oct 31 explicitly calls him 'former chief strategist and close ally of former U.S. President Donald Trump.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly supports a Yes resolution. Steve Bannon — former White House Chief Strategist under Trump, widely cited as a Trump confidant and MAGA architect — made a public statement on October 29, 2025 on his Real America's Voice television show calling for Netanyahu to be 'toppled immediately,' stating 'We need regime change in Jerusalem and we need it tonight,' and accusing Netanyahu of 'consistently lying to the U.S. government and people.' This constitutes personal and professional disparagement (not merely policy disagreement), meets the 'senior advisor or public ally' threshold, was made on television (a qualifying public platform), occurred within the resolution window (October 25–November 24, 2025), and was reported by Mediaite with corroboration from RT/qoshe.com, RealClearPolitics, and other outlets. The resolution therefore is Yes, with the first qualifying event on October 29, 2025.

Capturing Toretske would represent a significant step toward encircling Ukrainian forces in the region and advancing toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, the last major Ukrainian-held cities in Donetsk. As of November 28, 2025, no open-source maps indicate Russian presence within 10 kilometers of Toretske’s administrative boundary. However, continued pressure in adjacent areas increases the likelihood of probing operations toward Toretske in the coming weeks.

Sources:
- ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment (August 31, 2025): https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-31-2025
- DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28, either the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Ukraine map or DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) assesses that Russian forces have advanced to a point within 10 kilometers of the administrative boundary of Toretske, as measured by the closest point on the ISW or DeepStateMap front-line indicator. The assessment must persist through at least one full daily update cycle (i.e., appear on two consecutive daily maps or reports, or be confirmed in a subsequent update if a day is skipped). Temporary glitches, map errors, or one-off annotations not sustained in subsequent updates do not count.

The primary source is the ISW Ukraine map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375. If ISW ceases publication, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) will be used as the secondary source. If both sources become permanently unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of reporting from at least two credible open-source intelligence (OSINT) platforms or major international news outlets (e.g., BBC, Reuters, The Guardian, or Associated Press) confirming the advance.

An advance is defined as the presence of Russian military units or control assessed by the source within the 10 km radius, including areas shaded under 'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine', 'Assessed Russian Control', 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine', or 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours'. A negotiated or de jure transfer of control does not count unless accompanied by physical presence within the zone. If Russian forces enter the area but withdraw before the end date, the question still resolves Yes if the condition was met during the resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of Russian momentum toward Toretske. While the ultimate question asks whether Russia captures any part of Toretske by January 1, 2026, a 10-kilometer approach would signal a significant escalation in operational reach and intent. Given the current front-line dynamics and the slow pace of Russian advances (approximately 440–500 km per month in recent months, per ISW), closing within 10 km of Toretske by late December would imply a high probability of eventual entry into the settlement. This subquestion avoids being a mere restatement of the ultimate question by focusing on proximity rather than control, providing forecasters with a measurable, high-value signal of battlefield momentum. It is also unlikely to resolve to Yes or No with near-certainty, preserving informational value.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: Russian forces assessed within 10km of Toretske's administrative boundary per ISW or DeepStateMap, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28, persisting through at least one daily update cycle. Toretske/Toretsk is a city in Donetsk Oblast near Kostiantynivka (formerly Dzerzhynsk). The threshold is 10km from administrative boundary.
