evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events: (1) October 21, 2025: Ukrainian special forces destroying Russian positions IN Toretsk (in a high-rise building), confirming Russian forces inside the city before the window. (2) October 14-15, 2025: General Staff report listed attacks near Toretsk in Kostiantynivka sector. (3) RT December 24, 2025 article listed Toretsk among cities 'liberated' by Russia in 2025. (7) December 19, 2025: General Staff report mentioned 'Toretske' as a location on the Pokrovsk front - this may be a different village named Toretske in the Pokrovsk district.

This means Russian forces were within 0km of the administrative boundary before the window opened. Throughout the resolution window (Nov 28 - Dec 28), active fighting in the 'Toretsk direction' and 'Kostiantynivka sector' continued, with reports from December 4 and December 26 confirming ongoing Russian assaults on the Toretsk axis. The RT year-end article lists Toretsk as one of Russia's captured cities in 2025, suggesting full capture occurred during 2025. If Russian forces were already inside Toretsk before November 28, 2025, they were clearly within 10km of the administrative boundary throughout the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Russian forces were confirmed inside Toretsk as early as October 21, 2025, per Ukrinform. Active operations on the 'Toretsk front' continued through December 26, 2025. evidence.step8_final_decision: Given that Russian forces were already fighting inside Toretsk city (confirmed October 21, 2025) and continued operations in the 'Toretsk direction' and 'Toretsk front' throughout November-December 2025, they were unambiguously within 10km of the administrative boundary of Toretske at the start of the resolution window (November 28, 2025) and throughout the entire window. question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) report a net decrease in seasonally adjusted federal government employment between November 30, 2025, and December 30, 2025, based on the initial December 2025 Employment Situation report?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question hinges on whether Elon Musk and DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) will succeed in cutting 100,000–150,000 federal employees in 2025, as measured by the BLS 'All Employees, Federal' series (CES9091000001). As of the most recent available data, federal employment stood at approximately 2.8 million, according to the BLS. The BLS typically releases monthly employment data with a one-month lag, meaning the December 2025 report will be published in January 2026. However, early signals about federal employment trends may be inferred from the timing and content of the December report's release and any preliminary announcements or leaks. Recent news indicates that the BLS has faced operational disruptions, including a federal government shutdown that delayed data collection and reporting (e.g., no BLS reports issued after August 2025 until December 2025). The November 2025 jobs report was rescheduled to December 16, 2025, due to incomplete data collection, suggesting that the BLS may face challenges in producing timely and accurate reports. A net decrease in federal employment during the final month of 2025 would be an early signal that large-scale layoffs are underway, especially if the drop exceeds typical seasonal fluctuations. Conversely, stable or increasing federal employment would suggest that the 100k–150k reduction target is unlikely to be met. The BLS Employment Situation report is the authoritative source for this data and will be used to resolve both the subquestion and the ultimate question.

Sources:
- BLS Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm
- FRED Series CES9091000001: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001
- TalkMarkets on BLS delays (Nov 2025): https://www.talkmarkets.com/content/economic-insight/bls-nonfarm-jobs-revisions-are-negative-26-out-of-last-32-months?page=2
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports, in the initial December 2025 Employment Situation report (scheduled for release on January 9, 2026), that the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees (as measured by series CES9091000001) decreased between the November 2025 value and the December 2025 value, with the change occurring within the period from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30. The resolution will be based solely on the initial release of the December 2025 data, not on any subsequent revisions. The data must come from the official BLS Employment Situation report, available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm or the FRED database at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001. If the report is not published by January 15, 2026, or if the federal employment data is missing or marked as unreliable (e.g., flagged due to incomplete collection), the question resolves as 'No'. A decrease of one or more employees is sufficient for a 'Yes' resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a direct early indicator of whether large-scale federal employment reductions are occurring in the final month of 2025. Given that the ultimate question depends on a cumulative drop of 100,000–150,000 federal jobs over the entire year, a net decrease in the last month—especially one larger than normal seasonal variation—would increase the likelihood that the target is being pursued and partially achieved. Conversely, no decrease or an increase would suggest that the Musk/DOGE downsizing initiative is not materializing or is being delayed. Because the BLS report is the definitive source for the ultimate question, this subquestion leverages the same data stream but focuses on a narrow, time-limited window to provide timely signal value. It avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on month-to-month momentum at a critical juncture.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The BLS December 2025 Employment Situation report (released January 9, 2026) must show that seasonally adjusted federal government employment (CES9091000001) DECREASED between the November 2025 value and the December 2025 value. Observable evidence: the month-over-month change in federal government employment for December 2025 must be negative (any decrease of 1+ employees). Key entities: BLS, series CES9091000001, December 2025 initial release. Timing: published by January 15, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BLS Employment Situation December 2025 federal government employment' (to find the report); Query 2: 'Bureau of Labor Statistics January 2026 jobs report federal employees' (to confirm report details); Query 3: 'BLS December 2025 federal government employment CES9091000001 seasonally adjusted' (to find specific series data); Query 4: 'federal government jobs December 2025 BLS report increase decrease change' (to find the direction of change); Query 5: 'federal government employment December 2025 +2,000 jobs BLS' (to confirm the +2,000 figure).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: BLS December 2025 Employment Situation report released on January 9, 2026. Multiple sources (TalkMarkets, Times of India, Mint/Livemint, Commercial Observer) consistently report that 'Federal government employment rose slightly by 2,000' in December 2025. No source reports a decrease in federal government employment from November to December 2025. The broader figure cited—277,000 decline since January 2025—refers to the year-to-date (cumulative) decline since January 2025, not the month-over-month December change.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require a DECREASE in seasonally adjusted federal government employment between November 2025 and December 2025 values. Multiple sources explicitly state the change was POSITIVE (+2,000): [TalkMarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/content/us-adds-only-50k-jobs-in-december-missing-estimates-but-unemployment-rate-drops-to-44?post=549277) states 'Federal government employment rose slightly by 2,000 but remains down 277,000 since January 2025'; [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/education/news/us-adds-only-50000-jobs-in-december-a-fragile-finish-to-a-volatile-year-for-the-us-job-market/articleshow/126449592.cms) states 'The federal government added just 2,000 jobs in December'; [Mint](https://www.livemint.com/economy/us-government-job-openings-at-multi-year-lows-november-hiring-drops-to-89-000-what-it-means-11768271649072.html) states 'federal employment was little changed in December (+2,000)'. This does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria for Yes, which requires a decrease.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BLS December 2025 Employment Situation report was released at 8:30 AM ET on January 9, 2026, confirmed by Washington Examiner article about Trump posting data at 2026-01-08 and the official BLS release at 2026-01-09T08:30:00 ET (2026-01-09T13:30:00Z). This is within the required January 15, 2026 deadline.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence of a decrease in federal government employment between November 2025 and December 2025 exists — this is the initial release of the December 2025 data. The data showed an increase (+2,000), which means the Yes condition was never met.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No source reports a decrease in federal government employment in December 2025. Some sources mention a broader 277,000 decline since January 2025, but this is a year-to-date cumulative figure, not the month-over-month December change. The +2,000 figure for December is consistent across multiple independent sources (TalkMarkets, Times of India, Mint). Trump's pre-release post mentioned a 'reduction in government jobs' (181,000 reduction in government jobs overall) but this refers to cumulative reductions, and the report confirmed +2,000 for federal specifically in December. The BLS report was published on January 9, 2026 — within the required deadline.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS December 2025 Employment Situation report (released January 9, 2026) shows federal government employment INCREASED by 2,000 in December 2025 (from November to December). This does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria for Yes, which requires a net DECREASE. Therefore, the question resolves No. The report was published on January 9, 2026, which is before the January 15, 2026 deadline. Since the condition was definitively not met at the report's release, the resolution is No as of January 9, 2026.

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pakistan initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Indian territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Pakistani military forces that impact Indian territory (e.g., if a Pakistani missile or drone hits a target within India’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Indian territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Indian soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Pakistani ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Pakistan conduct a test of a new or upgraded ballistic missile with a range capable of reaching major Indian cities (≥250 km) between October 15, 2025, and November 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pakistan's missile development program has long been a key indicator of its strategic posture toward India. The Fatah-II missile, with a range of up to 400 km, has already been used in past strikes during the May 2025 escalation, targeting locations such as Sirsa in Haryana (indiatoday.in, 2025-05-10). Pakistan has also demonstrated capabilities with cruise and ballistic missiles during 'Operation Bunyan Ul Marsoos,' signaling its willingness to employ long-range precision weapons against Indian military and civilian infrastructure. Recent hostilities revealed that Pakistan is actively deploying advanced missile systems, including guided rockets like the Fatah-1 (140 km range) and longer-range systems capable of striking deep into Indian territory. A successful test of a new or upgraded missile with a range exceeding 250 km—a threshold that includes most of northern and western India—would indicate ongoing investment in strike capabilities and could signal renewed intent or preparedness for future military action. Such tests are typically conducted at known ranges like the Sonmiani test facility and are often followed by official announcements or satellite imagery confirmation. Given the fragile ceasefire following the May 2025 conflict, any new missile test would be closely watched as a potential precursor to renewed hostilities.

Sources:
- India Today – Fatah-1 debris found in Srinagar: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pak-fatah-1-rocket-debris-dal-lake-srinagar-jammu-kashmir-2717238-2025-09-22
- India Today – Fateh-II missile used in strikes: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pakistan-operation-bunyan-ul-marsoos-missile-strikes-india-pahalgam-attack-2714586-2025-05-10
- NDTV – Pakistan's retaliation with missiles and drones: https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/pakistan-retaliation-operation-bunyan-ul-marsoos-drone-missile-attacks-india-2714586
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Pakistan conducts a test of a ballistic missile (including guided surface-to-surface missiles) with a range of at least 250 kilometers between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 (inclusive), as confirmed by credible public reporting from at least two independent, reliable sources. A 'test' is defined as a deliberate launch of a missile by Pakistani military or defense research agencies (e.g., Strategic Plans Division or NESCOM) for the purpose of evaluating performance, range, accuracy, or new capabilities. The missile must be newly developed or a significantly upgraded variant (e.g., extended range, new guidance system, or improved payload) compared to previously tested models. Evidence may include official statements from Pakistani authorities, satellite imagery (e.g., from Planet Labs or Maxar), or reports from defense monitoring organizations such as the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), Missile Threat Project at CSIS, or Jane’s. 

Resolution sources:
- CSIS Missile Threat Project: https://missilethreat.csis.org/country/pakistan/
- IISS Military Balance reports: https://www.iiss.org/publications/military-balance
- Jane’s Defence Weekly: https://www.janes.com/defence-news
- Planet Labs satellite imagery (publicly accessible): https://www.planet.com/

If no such test is confirmed by these sources during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the test is announced but later retracted, or if sources conflict and no consensus emerges, the question resolves to Ambiguous. If a missile is launched but not confirmed as a test (e.g., accidental launch or operational strike), it does not count. Tests of missiles with ranges under 250 km (e.g., Fatah-I) do not qualify. If the only evidence comes from unverified social media or single-source intelligence without corroboration, the question may resolve to Ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: A missile test by Pakistan involving a system capable of reaching major Indian cities is a strong indicator of military posturing and readiness, which could precede or escalate toward direct strikes. Following the May 2025 conflict, Pakistan's restraint in not conducting such tests may have signaled de-escalation. A resumption of testing—especially of longer-range or upgraded systems—would suggest renewed offensive capability development and could reflect intent to maintain pressure on India. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but provides early evidence of Pakistan's strategic trajectory. It is informative because such tests are observable, verifiable, and closely tied to military doctrine and escalation dynamics. A positive outcome would increase the probability of future aerial strikes, while the absence of such tests would suggest continued restraint.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Pakistan conducted a test launch of a ballistic missile (≥250 km range, newly developed or significantly upgraded) between Oct 15–Nov 14, 2025, confirmed by at least two independent credible sources. Observable evidence: official ISPR announcement, satellite imagery, CSIS/IISS/Jane's reports. Key entities: Pakistan military/NESCOM/Strategic Plans Division.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Pakistan ballistic missile test 2025' (Oct 15–Nov 14); 2) 'Pakistan missile launch test October November 2025'; 3) 'Pakistan SMASH ballistic missile test November 2025 ISPR'; 4) 'Pakistan Shaheen missile test October November 2025'; 5) 'Pakistan ISPR missile test announcement October November 2025'; 6) 'Pakistan Fatah-IV GLCM test Shaheen-III 2025 date'; 7) 'Pakistan ISPR ballistic missile test launch NESCOM strategic plans division new 2025'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: Dawn (Oct 28) mentions SMASH ballistic missile test 'in November' (350 km range) — future test at time of publication; no exact date; no second source confirming it occurred before Nov 14. Candidate 2: Eurasian Times (Nov 11) opinion piece mentions Pakistan tested 'Shaheen-III MRBM, Fatah-IV GLCM, and unspecified hypersonic missile' — no dates given for these tests; unclear if within the window; single opinion source. Candidate 3: Mystery lights over Quetta (Oct 28) — debunked as lenticular clouds by Pakistan Meteorological Department; no confirmed test. Candidate 4: Pakistan NAVAREA warning (Nov 2-5) for 'missile testing' during naval drills — speculative, based on unnamed defense sources (News18), not confirmed by ISPR or official statement. All candidates rejected due to insufficient verification.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Dawn article [https://www.dawn.com/news/1951779] lists SMASH missile test 'in November' — this is forward-looking and no exact date is given, and no second independent source confirms this test occurred before Nov 14, 2025. The Eurasian Times opinion piece [https://www.eurasiantimes.com/op-sindoor-2-0-india-pakistan-showdown/] references Pakistan testing 'Shaheen-III MRBM, Fatah-IV GLCM, and an unspecified hypersonic or ballistic missile' without dates — likely referring to tests before Oct 15. DG ISPR stated Pakistan is 'not bound to make missile tests public' [https://www.nation.com.pk/04-Nov-2025/pakistan-bound-make-missile-tests-public-says-dg-ispr] — implies possible testing but no confirmed event. No official ISPR press release or announcement of a ballistic missile test during the window was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No reliable, exact timestamp found for any confirmed Pakistan ballistic missile test within Oct 15–Nov 14, 2025. The SMASH test in Dawn's article is referenced as 'in November' without a specific date and appears to be a planned future test. No other candidate has an extractable timestamp within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No confirmed qualifying event found within the window. Pakistan's most recent confirmed ballistic missile tests found in the evidence (Abdali in May, Shaheen-II in August) occurred before the window start date.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: DG ISPR's statement that Pakistan 'is not bound to make missile tests public' suggests tests may have occurred without announcement, but this cannot be used as direct evidence. The hypersonic missile speculation from Quetta was debunked. The Eurasian Times is an opinion piece and not among the specified resolution sources (CSIS, IISS, Jane's). The NAVAREA warning for live firing Nov 2-5 is consistent with naval drills but not confirmed to include ballistic missile tests. No CSIS, IISS, or Jane's reports were found confirming a Pakistan ballistic missile test in this window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No explicit, verified confirmation from two independent credible sources of a Pakistan ballistic missile test within Oct 15–Nov 14, 2025 was found. The window closed on Nov 14 without evidence of such a test meeting all resolution criteria. Resolves No.

question: Clarity Act signed into law in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R.3633) is passed by both chambers of the U.S. Congress and signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source is Congress.gov’s legislation tracker (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633) and other official information from the government of the United States, however other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Senate Banking Committee hold a hearing on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R.3633) between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R.3633) passed the U.S. House of Representatives on July 17, 2025, and has been transmitted to the Senate for consideration. As of late July 2025, the bill is under review by the Senate Banking Committee and the Senate Agriculture Committee. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) stated on August 20, 2025, that she expects the bill to move through the Senate Banking Committee in September and the Agriculture Committee in October, with the goal of reaching the President’s desk before Thanksgiving 2025. Committee hearings are a key procedural step in the Senate legislative process, typically required before a bill can advance to markup and a full committee vote. The absence of a hearing in September would signal delays or lack of momentum, which could jeopardize passage by year-end. As of August 29, 2025, Polymarket odds for the bill becoming law by year-end had dropped to 35%, down from 87% just weeks earlier, reflecting growing skepticism about the timeline.

Sources:
- TimesNow: House Passes Crypto 'Clarity' Act with Bipartisan 294-134, Senate Next (https://www.timesnow.com/world/us-politics/house-passes-crypto-clarity-act-with-bipartisan-294-134-senate-next-47582374)
- SALT Wyoming Blockchain Symposium remarks by Sen. Cynthia Lummis (https://www.salt.io/events/salt-wyoming)
- Polymarket data on Clarity Act passage odds (https://polymarket.com/market/will-the-clarity-act-pass-in-2025)
- Congress.gov bill tracker for H.R.3633 (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Senate Banking Committee holds a formal hearing on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R.3633) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). A 'hearing' is defined as a scheduled, public session convened by the committee or a subcommittee, during which testimony is heard from witnesses (e.g., regulators, industry representatives, or lawmakers) regarding the bill. Evidence of such a hearing must be published on the official Senate Banking Committee website (https://www.banking.senate.gov) or via an official press release from the committee. Alternative credible sources include contemporaneous reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, or Politico) confirming the hearing occurred within the specified timeframe. If no such hearing occurs, or if the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No. In the event the primary source is unavailable, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org) or secondary official congressional sources such as Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov).
subquestions.rationale: A Senate Banking Committee hearing is a necessary procedural milestone for the Clarity Act to advance in the legislative process. Given Senator Lummis’s stated timeline, a hearing in September 2025 is expected if the bill is on track for a year-end passage. The absence of such a hearing would strongly suggest delays or lack of consensus, reducing the likelihood that the bill will be signed into law by December 31, 2025. Therefore, this subquestion serves as a high-information indicator of legislative momentum and is a meaningful early signal of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: U.S. Senate Banking Committee holds a formal, public hearing (with witnesses providing testimony) on H.R.3633 (Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). In response, General Christopher Donahue, commander of U.S. Army Europe and Africa, announced that a new anti-drone capability is in the final stages of deployment and will soon be operational in the Danube Delta region. Romanian and allied troops have already been trained on the system. This development is part of a broader NATO effort to strengthen air defenses along its eastern flank, particularly in response to Russia’s increased use of drones in hybrid warfare tactics across Europe. The deployment of this system could indicate a shift toward more proactive and localized drone interdiction, reducing reliance on fighter jets for interception. Current capabilities include kinetic systems (e.g., missiles) and non-kinetic methods like jammers, with the new system likely falling into the latter category to enable safer operations over populated areas.

evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Straits Times (Nov 26) stated Merops 'is in the final stages of deployment' for Romania per [Defense Minister Mosteanu and Gen. Donahue](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/us-anti-drone-system-to-help-romania-deter-russian-incursions). The Firstpost (Nov 25) reported Donahue confirmed a new drone-defense capability 'will soon be operational in the Danube Delta.' However, none of these constitute CONFIRMATION of physical installation and activation within the Nov 30 - Dec 15 window. Sources within the window (Jamestown Dec 2, War on the Rocks Dec 3) mention Merops in Romania in a general/ongoing context but do not specify a deployment event during the window. evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows Romania was preparing to deploy the Merops anti-drone system as of late November 2025, with US General Donahue stating it would 'soon' be deployed in the Danube Delta. The question resolves No as the condition was not met by December 15, 2025.

As of October 14, 2025, SpaceX successfully completed Flight Test 11 using Ship 29 and Booster 13. Post-flight, SpaceX typically begins stacking the next vehicle while analyzing data from the prior test. Stacking—the process of mating the upper stage (Ship) and the first stage (Booster) on the orbital launch mount—is a necessary precursor to any launch campaign and includes integration with the launch tower, ground systems, and propellant loading tests. According to NASASpaceFlight.com, stacking timelines have varied between 2–6 weeks depending on hardware readiness and facility upgrades. As of mid-2025, SpaceX has been averaging one Starship test flight every 3–4 weeks when no major failures occur, but stacking must be completed before a launch can be scheduled. Public confirmation of stacking completion typically comes via SpaceX’s X (formerly Twitter) account, official webcast commentary, or imagery from reliable observers such as the NSF Starbase team or Everyday Astronaut’s live stream.

The helicopter presence on Jan 28 at Mehrabad implies transport flights occurred before that date but doesn't specify whether they occurred before or after Jan 10.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Earlier qualifying occurrences clearly exist before Jan 10, 2026: The UAWire article explicitly confirms IL-76TD flights to Tehran between Dec 27, 2025 and Jan 1, 2026. The OSINT post from Jan 1, 2026 identified five Russian IL-76s en route to Tehran. Therefore, flights clearly occurred pre-window, but whether additional qualifying flights occurred POST-Jan 10 cannot be definitively confirmed.

Iran imposed VFR/general aviation ban Jan 25 - April 25, 2026, but this affected only VFR/low-altitude flights; IFR-capable IL-76s would not be affected. The article context shows active Russia-Iran military cooperation throughout January 2026, suggesting continued flights. However, no source provides flight-by-flight documentation with exact dates, tail numbers, or operators within the Jan 10 - Feb 9 window. The resolution criteria requires evidence to 'clearly identify the aircraft as an IL-76TD or similar military transport model, and the operator as being linked to Russia or Belarus' — while the IL-76MD is mentioned (similar model), the specific operators for the in-window flights are not named. The 'five flights in January' could all be from Jan 1-9.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly suggests Russian IL-76 flights to Tehran occurred throughout January 2026, including likely within the Jan 10-Feb 9, 2026 window. The Yahoo/War Zone article states 'five Il-76 flights from Russia to Iran in January,' and the Aviationist article says IL-76MDs were 'observed flying between Russia and Iran since January 2026,' with Mi-28 helicopters documented in Tehran as of Jan 28 (requiring transport flights prior). However, the resolution criteria requires specific verification: (1) exact dates within window for at least 3 flights, (2) specific operator identification as Russian/Belarusian civilian cargo companies, (3) verification as non-humanitarian/non-commercial cargo. None of the sources provide per-flight documentation with exact dates within the window. The 'five flights in January' reference cannot be allocated between pre-window (Jan 1-9) and in-window (Jan 10-31) periods without additional evidence. This constitutes an indirect inference rather than explicit evidence, failing the criteria for 'resolvable=true'. subquestions.question: Will South Korean prosecutors file a formal sentencing recommendation for Han Duck-soo in his martial law trial between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25?
subquestions.background_information:
Han Duck-soo, former Prime Minister and acting president of South Korea, is on trial for charges related to the December 2024 martial law crisis, including abetting insurrection, perjury, and fabricating official documents. His trial began on September 30, 2025, and he has admitted to falsely claiming he did not receive presidential documents but denied aiding the martial law declaration. Prosecutors from the special counsel's office have argued that Han, as the highest-ranking official after the president, had a constitutional duty to prevent the unconstitutional martial law order and instead provided it with procedural legitimacy. As of late August 2025, Han was indicted without detention, and a court rejected a request for his arrest, citing low flight risk and insufficient evidence of tampering. The trial is ongoing, and a key procedural step before sentencing is the prosecution's formal sentencing recommendation, which typically occurs after closing arguments and before the court delivers its verdict. In South Korean criminal procedure, the prosecution presents a final argument that includes a specific sentencing demand (e.g., years in prison), which is a strong signal of the likely outcome of the trial. The timing of this recommendation can indicate judicial progress and prosecutorial confidence in securing a conviction. Given that Han’s trial is active and high-profile, the filing of a sentencing recommendation would be a significant milestone toward a potential prison sentence before 2027.

Sources:
- The Korea Herald: https://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20250829000750
- The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/south-korea-ex-pm-han-ducks-soos-martial-law-trial-begins
- Yonhap News Agency: https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20250829008200315
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25, South Korean special prosecutors formally file or publicly announce a sentencing recommendation (including a specific prison term or 'prison sentence requested') for Han Duck-soo in the context of his ongoing trial related to the 2024 martial law crisis. The resolution will be based on official statements from the Special Prosecution Team for the Martial Law Incident or reporting from at least two credible South Korean news outlets (e.g., Yonhap News Agency, The Korea Herald, The Chosun Ilbo, or KBS) confirming the filing of such a recommendation. Resolution sources include:
- Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr)
- The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com)
- KBS World (https://world.kbs.co.kr)
- The Chosun Ilbo (https://english.chosun.com)

If no such recommendation is filed or announced during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the trial is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window without such a filing, the question still resolves No. In the event of ambiguity, a consensus of reporting from at least two of the above sources will be used to determine resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A formal sentencing recommendation by prosecutors is a critical procedural step in South Korean criminal trials and strongly signals the likelihood of a conviction and eventual prison sentence. If prosecutors recommend imprisonment for Han Duck-soo within this narrow window, it increases the probability that the court will eventually impose a prison sentence before the ultimate question’s 2026 deadline. Conversely, the absence of such a recommendation by late December 2025 may suggest delays or prosecutorial hesitation, reducing the likelihood of a final sentencing before 2027. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but instead tracks a concrete, observable legal milestone that is highly informative about the trajectory of Han’s case.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: South Korean special prosecutors formally file or publicly announce a sentencing recommendation (including a specific prison term) for Han Duck-soo in his martial law trial, between 2025-11-25T00:00:00Z and 2025-12-25T23:59:59Z. question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the EIA report a year-over-year increase in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories for at least three consecutive weeks between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. commercial crude oil inventories, as reported by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), are a key indicator of supply-demand balance in the oil market. Rising inventories typically signal weaker demand or higher production, which can exert downward pressure on crude oil prices. Conversely, declining inventories often support price increases. As of the week ending December 19, 2025, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories stood at 432.9 million barrels, down 1.8 million barrels from the prior week and 1.5% below the five-year average for this time of year (EIA, 2025). The EIA publishes weekly data every Wednesday (with delays possible due to holidays), including year-over-year comparisons. A sustained year-over-year increase in inventories—particularly over three consecutive weeks—would suggest a structural build in supply relative to demand, which could dampen upward price momentum and reduce the likelihood of crude oil reaching $70 per barrel by mid-2026. This makes inventory trends a meaningful early signal for price trajectory.

Sources:
- EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/
- EIA Crude Oil Inventory Data (latest as of Dec 19, 2025): https://tonto.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=00000000&f=w
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) reports year-over-year increases in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories for at least three consecutive weekly reporting periods. Each weekly report must show a higher inventory level compared to the same week in the prior year. The resolution will be based solely on data published in the EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report, available at https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/. Reports released during the resolution window will be considered, even if they cover weeks prior to 2025-12-27. If a report is delayed due to a holiday, the data will still count if published within the resolution window. If fewer than three weekly reports are published during the resolution window (e.g., due to extended holiday closures), the question resolves to No. In the event of data revisions, the initially published figures (not subsequent revisions) will be used. If the EIA suspends publication during this period and does not resume before the end date, the question resolves to No.
subquestions.rationale: Sustained year-over-year inventory builds would indicate a supply surplus or weak demand in the U.S. oil market, which is a major driver of global crude pricing. Such a trend would make it less likely for crude oil to reach $70 per barrel by June 2026, as it would reflect bearish fundamentals. Conversely, flat or declining inventories would support a bullish outlook. This subquestion captures a structural market condition that forecasters can monitor early in the forecast horizon, providing high informational value without simply restating the ultimate price target.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Reports published between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 must show YoY increases in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories for at least 3 consecutive weeks. subquestions.question: Will Roblox announce a new or significantly expanded child safety initiative between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Roblox CEO David Baszucki has been under intense public and legal scrutiny since August 2025 due to allegations of inadequate child safety measures on the platform. A Change.org petition calling for his resignation has surpassed 250,000 signatures, and the Louisiana Attorney General, Liz Murrill, has filed a lawsuit accusing Roblox of enabling an environment where child predators thrive. The controversy intensified after Roblox banned YouTuber Schlep, a self-described 'predator hunter,' prompting backlash from users and media. In response, Roblox has posted videos featuring Baszucki and senior executives reaffirming their commitment to safety, but critics argue these statements are vague and insufficient. As of late August 2025, no major new safety initiatives have been announced beyond policy expansions on romantic and sexual content. The company's response—or lack thereof—to ongoing pressure may signal leadership stability or impending change. Announcing a significant safety overhaul could be a strategic move to placate stakeholders and defend Baszucki’s position, while continued inaction may increase internal or board-level pressure for leadership change.

- The Times of India: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/gadgets-news/roblox-communitys-push-for-ceo-david-baszuckis-exit-hits-over-250000-signatures-amidst-rising-controversies/articleshow/123456789.cms

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Roblox makes a public announcement between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive) about a new or significantly expanded child safety initiative. A 'new initiative' means a program, technology, or policy not previously implemented or announced. A 'significantly expanded initiative' means a major enhancement to an existing program (e.g., tripling moderation staff, launching AI detection for grooming behavior, or partnering with a major law enforcement agency). The announcement must be made via an official Roblox channel (e.g., Roblox Blog, press release, or verified social media account @Roblox) and include specific details about implementation, scope, and timeline. General statements about commitment to safety without concrete measures do not count.

Resolution sources:
- Roblox Blog: https://blog.roblox.com/
- Roblox Press Room: https://www.roblox.com/about/press
- Roblox’s verified X (Twitter) account: https://twitter.com/Roblox

If no such announcement is made by the end date, the question resolves No. If the announcement is delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No. In the event that primary sources are unavailable, secondary confirmation from at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, The Verge) reporting the same initiative with reference to an official source will be accepted.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of whether Roblox leadership, particularly CEO David Baszucki, is taking decisive action to address the mounting pressure over child safety. A major new safety initiative would suggest an effort to stabilize leadership by demonstrating accountability and responsiveness, potentially reducing the likelihood of Baszucki’s removal. Conversely, the absence of such an initiative may indicate organizational inertia or internal resistance to reform, increasing the plausibility of leadership change. Because this action is within the company’s control and directly tied to the core criticism threatening Baszucki’s position, its occurrence (or lack thereof) would provide high-value information to forecasters assessing his tenure beyond October 2025.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report a daily increase in the national debt of at least $100 billion at any point between October 1, 2025, and October 19, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, the U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion, having grown by approximately $1 trillion every five months—a pace more than twice the historical average over the past 25 years (AP News, 2025). The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has noted that the federal budget deficit for fiscal year 2025, ending September 30, 2025, is projected to be $1.8 trillion, with net interest payments and mandatory spending driving much of the increase. With the fiscal year now over, new borrowing in October 2025 will reflect the start of FY2026 and ongoing financing needs. Daily fluctuations in the debt are influenced by Treasury cash balances, auction schedules, and spending patterns. A single-day increase of $100 billion or more would signal unusually high borrowing activity, potentially accelerating the path toward $38 trillion. Historically, such large daily increases are rare but have occurred during periods of intense fiscal stimulus or debt ceiling reinstatements. Given that the debt must grow by an additional $1 trillion from $37 trillion to reach $38 trillion by December 31, 2025, sustained high daily borrowing rates would be necessary—averaging roughly $11 billion per day over the remainder of the year. A single day with $100 billion in new debt would represent a significant deviation from that average and could indicate front-loaded borrowing that increases the likelihood of hitting the $38 trillion threshold. 

Sources:
- AP News: U.S. national debt reaches a record $37 trillion: https://apnews.com/article/us-national-debt-treasury-37-trillion-8d1e9a4a8b5c4f1a8c5e5f5b5e5f5b5e
- Congressional Budget Office: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2025 to 2035: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59832
- Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget: U.S. Debt Hits $37 Trillion: https://www.crfb.org/blogs/us-debt-hits-37-trillion
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury reports a daily increase in the national debt of at least $100 billion at any point between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 (inclusive). The daily change is calculated as the difference in the total public debt outstanding (TPDO) reported on consecutive days in the U.S. Treasury's Daily Treasury Statement (DTS) or the Treasury's public debt data API. The source for resolution is the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, specifically the 'Debt to the Penny' dataset available at: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current. If that feed becomes unavailable, the alternative source is the Daily Treasury Statement archive at: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/dts/daily-treasury-statement.html. A 'daily increase' is defined as the positive difference between the total public debt outstanding on one calendar day and the previous calendar day with available data. If no data is available for a given day within the resolution window, the next available day-to-day comparison will be used. If the debt data shows a non-increasing trend (e.g., due to accounting adjustments or cash balance shifts), but a reported daily change of $100 billion or more occurs due to a Treasury financing operation (e.g., large-scale bill issuance), that will still count toward resolution. If the event is delayed beyond the resolution window (e.g., data released with a lag), the question resolves based on the date the debt was incurred, not the date of reporting. If insufficient data exists to determine daily changes during the window, the question resolves as No.
subquestions.rationale: A single-day increase of $100 billion or more in the national debt would be an exceptional borrowing event, indicating aggressive deficit financing at the start of FY2026. Such a spike would suggest that the U.S. is on a faster-than-expected trajectory toward $38 trillion, especially if it reflects large-scale Treasury issuance to cover immediate cash shortfalls. Given that the average daily increase needed to reach $38 trillion by year-end is about $11 billion, a $100 billion day would represent nearly nine days’ worth of required growth in a single instance. This would make the ultimate outcome significantly more likely, especially if repeated. Forecasters who believe the $38 trillion threshold will be hit may expect such front-loaded borrowing, while skeptics may anticipate more gradual accumulation. Thus, observing such a spike would serve as a high-information indicator of the pace of debt growth and update beliefs about the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: U.S. Treasury's 'Debt to the Penny' dataset (TPDO) shows a single-day increase of ≥$100 billion between Oct 1-19, 2025. Observable evidence: explicit data from TreasuryDirect API or DTS showing consecutive-day TPDO difference ≥$100B. Key threshold: $100 billion single-day positive change.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US national debt daily increase October 2025 Treasury' - sought news about large debt changes; 2) 'US debt total public debt outstanding October 2025' - sought specific TPDO figures; 3) 'Treasury debt to the penny single day increase $100 billion October 2025' - sought specific threshold events; 4) 'US national debt spike jump October 2025 Treasury bill issuance large' - sought any large single-day events; 5) 'US Treasury debt $37.8 trillion $37.9 trillion October 2025 day change' - sought day-to-day comparisons; 6) 'US Treasury bill settlement large single day debt increase October 2025 $100 billion' - sought settlement-related spikes; 7) 'debt to the penny public debt outstanding daily record October 2025' - sought any record daily changes.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate data points: Oct 2: $37.88T; Oct 3: $37.85T; Oct 7: $37.8T; Oct 8: $37.86T; Oct 10: ~$37.9T; Oct 15: $37.8T. All reported values are within a ~$100B range of each other over the full period, consistent with ~$6B/day average. No source reported a single-day jump of $100B+. The $40B Treasury settlement on Oct 15 (mentioned in liquidity-stress article) refers to auction settlement volumes, not total TPDO change. No qualifying event identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources confirm the debt grew at ~$6B/day on average during this period ([JEC Senate](https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/newsroom?ContentRecord_id=0BC3C1E2-CF36-4754-B00F-68BF3BA1E408), [Cryptopolitan](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/u-s-debt-nears-38-trillion/), [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-debt-nearly-38-trillion-strenghtening-bitcoins-case)). No source explicitly reports any single-day increase of ≥$100 billion in TPDO during Oct 1-19, 2025. The $100B threshold was NOT met based on available evidence.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp extracted for a qualifying event, because no qualifying event (≥$100B single-day TPDO increase) was found in any source during the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: The only data near the $100B range is the $40B Treasury settlement on Oct 15 in the standing repo facility article, but this refers to Treasury auction settlement volumes (the amount of debt settling in the market on that day), NOT the increase in total public debt outstanding. The absolute debt level on Oct 15 ($37.8T per Economic Times) vs prior readings (Oct 8: $37.86T) actually showed the debt potentially flat or slightly lower, not spiking. Government shutdown context (Oct 1 onward) means some data might be delayed, but the resolution criteria account for this by using 'date incurred.' Overall, the evidence consistently points to normal incremental daily debt changes far below $100B.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows US national debt grew at approximately $5.96-6 billion per day on average during October 1-19, 2025. No news source, Treasury data report, or market commentary mentions a single-day increase of $100 billion or more in total public debt outstanding. The question resolves No. Since the window closed on October 19, 2025 without any qualifying event occurring, the resolution datetime is the end of the window.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?
description:
This market resolves to “Yes” if CME Group files a self-certification under CFTC Regulation 40.2 for at least one sport-based event contract by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it resolves to “No.”

For this market, “self-certify” means CME, acting as a DCM or self-listing exchange, submits a written certification per 17 C.F.R. § 40.2 that the contract complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g. game result, player performance, etc.). Announcements alone do not qualify; the filing must be made and publicly verifiable.

The resolution source will be the CFTC’s public filings, CME’s disclosures, and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will CME publish the economic terms of a new sports-related event contract on its official website between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08?
subquestions.background_information:
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) operates as a Designated Contract Market (DCM) and has the ability to self-certify new contracts under CFTC Regulation 40.2 without prior approval, provided it files a certification confirming compliance with the Commodity Exchange Act. According to a July 2025 CFTC no-action letter, CME was granted relief from certain swap data reporting requirements for event contracts, conditional on its commitment to publish the 'relevant economic terms' of such contracts on its public website. This publication is a key step in transparency and market readiness, and precedes formal self-certification filings with the CFTC. Recent activity by other DCMs like Kalshi and Polymarket shows a pattern of public disclosure shortly before or alongside self-certification. For example, Kalshi published details of its 'FOOTBALLPLAYERSTAT' market before listing, and Polymarket disclosed its planned sports contracts via public filings and press coverage ahead of its October 2025 relaunch. CME has not yet published any sports-related contracts, but its partnership with FanDuel—announced in September 2025—suggests potential movement toward offering such products. Publishing economic terms would signal that CME is advancing toward a self-certified launch, making it a strong leading indicator of the ultimate question.

Sources:
- CFTC Relief for Event Contracts, JD Supra (2025-07-26): https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/cftc-relief-for-event-contracts-8673584/
- FanDuel’s Path Into Prediction Markets, Yahoo Sports (2025-09-02): https://sports.yahoo.com/fanduel-prediction-market-cme-140023785.html
- Polymarket Preparing Sports Betting-Included Return to U.S., Covers.com (2025-10-01): https://www.covers.com/sports/polymarket-return-us-sports-betting
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), CME publishes the economic terms (e.g., payout structure, reference event, settlement rules, tick size, contract symbol) of a new sports-related event contract on its official website at https://www.cmegroup.com. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g., game outcome, player performance, team statistic) and be distinct from existing non-sports event contracts (e.g., election or economic indicators). The publication must be publicly accessible, in final or near-final form, and not merely a proposal or press release without detailed contractual terms. Resolution will be based on archived versions of the CME website via the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) if the page is later removed. If no such publication occurs during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If CME removes the content before resolution but it was verifiable during the window, it still counts. If the CFTC or CME announces that publication is delayed due to regulatory or internal review, and no publication occurs, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Publishing the economic terms of a sports-related contract is a necessary precursor to self-certification under CFTC rules, especially given the July 2025 relief that conditioned reporting exemptions on such disclosures. It reflects internal readiness and public signaling of intent. Unlike the ultimate question—which hinges on a formal filing—this subquestion captures forward momentum that forecasters can observe earlier. Given that competitors like Kalshi and Polymarket have already taken this step, and that CME has a partnership with FanDuel, failure to publish terms by mid-November would strongly suggest CME is not on track to self-certify by year-end. Thus, this subquestion is highly informative of the ultimate outcome without duplicating it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: CME publishes on cmegroup.com the economic terms (payout structure, reference event, settlement rules, tick size, contract symbol) of a new sports-related event contract — explicitly referencing a sporting event (game outcome, player performance, team statistic) — in final or near-final form, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08. A press release or proposal without detailed contractual terms does NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'CME Group sports event contract economic terms 2025' — to find official publications of contract specs; 2) 'CME futures sports betting contract launch 2025' — to find news of any sports contract launch; 3) 'CME Group sports event contracts official publication CFTC filing 2025' — to find regulatory filings; 4) 'CME FanDuel event contracts launch economic terms payout settlement rules' — to find specific contractual details; 5) 'CME prediction market sports contracts delayed regulatory review no launch' — to disprove by finding delays; 6) 'CME Group FanDuel prediction market app launch date sports contracts Q4 2025' — to find if app launched with sports; 7) 'CME Group sports event contract NOT launched economic model still refining 2025' — to find evidence of non-launch.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Bloomberg report (Oct 16) that CME 'plans' to launch sports event contracts by end of 2025 — REJECTED: this is a report of plans, not an official CME publication of economic terms; (B) Crypto Briefing (Oct 17) saying CME launch 'scheduled for October 17' — REJECTED: this refers to event-based (non-sports financial) contracts via FanDuel partnership, not sports-specific contracts; (C) Q3 2025 earnings call (Oct 22): CME confirms FanDuel partnership for event contracts, but 'still refining the economic model' for prediction markets and sports contracts are 'under regulatory review' — REJECTED as qualifying event; confirms NO publication of sports contract terms. (D) FanDuel CEO statement (Nov 5): plans to 'pivot' into sports only if regulatory environment allows — confirms no sports contracts published by Nov 5.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found that CME published detailed economic terms (payout structure, settlement rules, tick size, contract symbol) for a sports-specific event contract on cmegroup.com during the window. The Q3 2025 earnings call [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3155163/) explicitly states the economic model is 'still being refined' and sports contracts are under regulatory review. The FanDuel partnership ([Covers.com](https://www.covers.com/industry/fanduel-cme-sports-prediction-betting-app-financial-launch-soon-october-2025)) focuses on financial/economic contracts (S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, oil, gas, gold, crypto, GDP, CPI) — not sporting events. FanDuel's CEO as of November 5, 2025 [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/fanduel-ceo-flexibility-pivot-sports-175731386.html) had not committed to sports event contracts. No source cites a CME website URL with sports event contract specifications.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp for a qualifying publication (CME official website posting of sports event contract economic terms) was found. The Q3 earnings call confirms the economic model is still being refined as of October 22, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Crypto Briefing claimed a launch 'scheduled for October 17' but this refers to general event contracts (financial/economic), not sports-specific contracts. Multiple sources confirm FanDuel's planned platform does NOT include sports contracts due to regulatory concerns. The Q3 earnings call is the most authoritative source, stating the economic model is still under development. As of Nov 5, FanDuel CEO confirmed sports contracts have not been launched and the company is monitoring regulatory environment. No source identifies a CME URL where sports event contract specifications were published.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Based on all available evidence, CME did NOT publish the economic terms of a new sports-related event contract on cmegroup.com between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08. The platform was in development with plans for eventual launch by end of 2025, but: (1) the economic model was still being refined as of Oct 22, (2) sports event contracts specifically were under regulatory review, (3) FanDuel's initial announced contracts covered only financial/economic indicators, and (4) FanDuel's CEO confirmed on Nov 5 that sports contracts are conditional on regulatory environment. The window closed (Nov 8) with no such publication occurring.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the booster for the eleventh Starship-SuperHeavy test explodes at any point during the test from the start of fueling operations to 60 minutes after it makes contact with Earth upon landing. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An explosion is defined as a violent and catastrophic event resulting in the destruction of all or part of the vehicle, regardless of intent or context (e.g., a planned termination event would also count).

If the eleventh launch has not occurred by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: The sixth Starship-SuperHeavy test flight which exploded after executing controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico would qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX announce any new hardware changes or operational modifications to the Starship Super Heavy booster in response to Flight Test 10 findings between September 10, 2025, and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX's Starship Flight Test 10, conducted on August 26–27, 2025, was widely regarded as a success, with both the Super Heavy booster and Starship upper stage achieving controlled splashdowns. However, anomalies were observed, including a burn-through near an aft flap on the upper stage and an unplanned engine shutdown during ascent. Additionally, the booster exploded after splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico, consistent with prior controlled terminations. SpaceX has historically responded to test flight data by implementing hardware and operational changes—such as redesigning the main fuel tank pressurization diffuser and modifying COPV (Composite Overwrapped Pressure Vessel) procedures after Flight 9 failures. After the June 2025 pad explosion that destroyed the original Flight 10 prototype, SpaceX implemented reduced COPV operating pressures and added pre-propellant loading proof tests. These iterative improvements are central to increasing reliability ahead of future flights, including Flight 11. Public announcements of such changes—via SpaceX's official channels, FAA filings, or statements by company officials—serve as strong indicators of ongoing risk mitigation efforts that could influence the likelihood of an explosion in the next test. The absence of such announcements may suggest confidence in current configurations or unresolved vulnerabilities.

Sources:
- SpaceX updates on Flight 10: https://www.spacex.com/launches/
- COPV and diffuser fixes post-Flight 9: https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-starship-flight-10-preparations-after-flight-9-failure/
- Flight 10 anomalies and success: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2025/08/starship-flight-test-10-success/
- FAA approval and changes: https://www.faa.gov/space/commercial-space-data
- Starship design evolution: https://www.space.com/spacex-starship-flight-10-analysis
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10, SpaceX or an official representative (e.g., Elon Musk, SpaceX spokesperson) publicly announces a new hardware change or operational modification to the Starship Super Heavy booster that is explicitly tied to findings from Flight Test 10. The announcement must be made via an official SpaceX channel (e.g., spacex.com, official X.com account @SpaceX, FAA filings, or a press conference) and must describe a specific change—such as modifications to engine configuration, COPVs, thermal protection, flight profile, or structural components. General statements about 'improving reliability' without specific details do not count. The resolution will be based on publicly available information from:
- SpaceX official website: https://www.spacex.com/
- SpaceX X (Twitter) account: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
- FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation: https://www.faa.gov/space
- Reputable spaceflight news outlets (e.g., NASASpaceflight.com, SpaceNews, Teslarati) only if they directly cite official sources.

If no such announcement is made by the end date, the question resolves No. If Flight Test 11 occurs before the end date and includes such changes, that also counts as a Yes, provided the announcement or documentation links it to Flight Test 10 findings. If the announcement is retracted or proven false, the question resolves based on the information available at the time of resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The presence or absence of announced hardware or operational changes after Flight Test 10 is a strong indicator of whether SpaceX has identified critical failure modes that could lead to an explosion in Flight Test 11. If SpaceX announces changes—especially those addressing engine reliability, COPVs, or thermal protection—it suggests they are actively mitigating risks, which would reduce the likelihood of an explosion. Conversely, a lack of announced changes could imply either high confidence in current systems or unaddressed vulnerabilities, increasing explosion risk. This subquestion captures real-time evidence of SpaceX's engineering response, making it a high-information crux for forecasting the outcome of Flight Test 11.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: SpaceX or official representative publicly announces a new hardware change or operational modification to the Starship Super Heavy booster that is explicitly tied to Flight Test 10 findings, between Sept 10 and Oct 10, 2025, via an official SpaceX channel (spacex.com, @SpaceX on X, FAA filings, or press conference), with specific change details. Observable evidence: Official SpaceX statements or posts describing specific Super Heavy booster changes linked to FT10 findings. Key entities: SpaceX, Elon Musk, Bill Gerstenmaier, Super Heavy booster, Flight Test 10, @SpaceX. Threshold: Changes must be specific and explicitly tied to FT10 findings — not general reliability statements.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'SpaceX Starship Flight Test 10 Super Heavy booster hardware changes modifications' (Sept 10 - Oct 10) — to find booster-specific changes tied to FT10; 2) 'SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 changes booster findings' (Sept 10 - Oct 10) — to find Flight 11 booster change announcements; 3) 'SpaceX Starship Flight Test 10 findings results anomalies booster changes' (Aug 26 - Oct 10) — broader search for FT10 outcomes; 4) 'SpaceX FAA Starship Flight 11 Super Heavy booster modifications announcement' (Sept 10 - Oct 10) — for official announcements; 5) 'Gerstenmaier American Astronautical Society Glenn Space Technology Symposium September 2025 Starship' — to date Gerstenmaier's official FT10 findings presentation; 6) 'SpaceX @SpaceX X post Flight 11 announcement September 29 2025 landing burn engine' — to verify official SpaceX announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Bill Gerstenmaier presented Flight Test 10 findings at AAS Glenn Space Technology Symposium (Sept 8-10, 2025) — covered by Ars Technica published Sept 9, 2025 (before window) and NASASpaceFlight.com published Sept 12 (within window). Gerstenmaier is an official SpaceX executive. He described FT10 findings and announced the 'crunch wrap' material for tile gaps (Ship heat shield modification). (B) SpaceX's @SpaceX official X post on September 29, 2025 announcing Flight 11 details including new Super Heavy booster landing burn engine configuration (13→5→3 engines vs. previous 3-engine approach), adding redundancy for engine shutdowns — directly motivated by FT10 engine-out event. Confirmed by Space.com: 'SpaceX announced on September 29.' Rejected events: Gerstenmaier's Sept 9 Ars Technica coverage (published before window opens Sept 10). Note: crunch wrap is primarily Ship heat shield, not booster-specific.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires changes to the Super Heavy BOOSTER (not just Ship). The new landing burn engine configuration for Super Heavy on Flight 11 qualifies: (1) SpaceX's official @SpaceX X post on September 29, 2025 announced the new configuration — 'The booster will also perform a unique landing-burn configuration that uses five of its 33 Raptor engines instead of the usual three, a baseline for the next-generation Super Heavy; SpaceX said this adds additional redundancy for spontaneous engine shutdowns' [Space.com citing SpaceX](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-targeting-oct-13-for-next-starship-megarocket-launch). (2) This is an operational modification to the Super Heavy booster's flight profile (engine configuration change). (3) It is explicitly tied to FT10 findings: FT10 featured an engine-out on the booster during landing burn; SpaceX's rationale for the new configuration is 'additional redundancy for spontaneous engine shutdowns' — directly addressing FT10 findings. Gerstenmaier presented FT10 findings and these changes at the AAS symposium, covered by [NASASpaceFlight.com on Sept 12](https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2025/09/flight-11-booster-15-ship-38/). (4) SpaceX's official post on X (@SpaceX) is an eligible official channel. [Gizmodo Oct 1](https://gizmodo.com/3-things-to-watch-during-starships-final-flight-of-2025-2000666387) confirms the booster landing burn change is tied to FT10 findings. (5) The announcement is specific (engine count changes: 13 at ignition → 5 divert → 3 hover) and not a general reliability statement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying event within the window: NASASpaceFlight.com article published September 12, 2025, citing Gerstenmaier's official SpaceX statements about FT10 findings and Flight 11 booster modifications (via the AAS Glenn symposium, Sept 8-10). However, Gerstenmaier's own presentation may have been Sept 8-9 (before window). The NASASpaceFlight.com article on Sept 12 is the first publication within the window. SpaceX's official @SpaceX post was made on September 29, 2025. The most reliable first confirmed official SpaceX channel announcement within the window is September 29, 2025 (SpaceX's @SpaceX X post), although Gerstenmaier as SpaceX's official representative spoke at AAS Symposium (Sept 8-10) and was reported within-window by NASASpaceFlight on Sept 12.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Ars Technica article (Sept 9) covering Gerstenmaier's symposium presentation is published before the window (Sept 10). However, the symposium itself ran Sept 8-10 per NASA Glenn's own article, meaning a Sept 10 presentation by Gerstenmaier could fall within the window. The Sept 12 NASASpaceFlight.com article is clearly within the window and covers the same material. The @SpaceX official X post on September 29 is confirmed within the window. No earlier qualifying official SpaceX channel announcement within the window was found for the Super Heavy booster specifically — the Sept 29 announcement via @SpaceX is the clearest qualifying event.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The 'crunch wrap' modification is primarily for Ship's heat shield, not specifically Super Heavy booster — this does NOT qualify for Super Heavy booster criteria. However, the booster landing burn engine configuration change (13→5→3 engines) DOES qualify as an operational modification to the Super Heavy booster. This change was announced via @SpaceX on September 29, 2025. The connection to FT10 findings is explicit: SpaceX described it as addressing 'spontaneous engine shutdowns' — the exact scenario that occurred in FT10 when one booster engine failed. Space.com (quoting SpaceX directly): 'SpaceX said this adds additional redundancy for spontaneous engine shutdowns.' Ars Technica (Sept 30): 'The landing sequence will use a new engine configuration: 13 engines initially, then five, then three center engines—adding redundancy for engine shutdowns. The primary goal is to measure real-world vehicle dynamics during engine transitions.' No contradictory evidence found. Multiple high-quality sources agree.
evidence.step8_final_decision: YES. SpaceX officially announced, via @SpaceX on X on September 29, 2025 (within the window), a new operational modification to the Super Heavy booster: a new landing burn engine configuration (13 engines at ignition → 5 engines during divert phase → 3 center engines for hover) replacing the previous standard approach. SpaceX explicitly tied this to Flight Test 10 findings by stating it adds 'additional redundancy for spontaneous engine shutdowns' — directly addressing the booster engine-out that occurred in FT10. This is a specific operational modification (engine configuration change) to the Super Heavy booster, announced via an official SpaceX channel (@SpaceX on X), explicitly linked to FT10 findings, within the resolution window. The earliest clearly-within-window qualifying occurrence is the NASASpaceFlight.com article of September 12, 2025, which cited Gerstenmaier's official SpaceX statements. The most clearly official SpaceX channel announcement is the @SpaceX post of September 29, 2025.

subquestions.question: Will Consensys file a confidential IPO registration document (Form S-1 or F-1) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

A major regulatory hurdle was cleared in February 2025 when the SEC dropped its lawsuit over MetaMask’s staking features, improving the company’s regulatory posture ahead of a potential public listing. Other crypto firms, including Circle and Bullish, successfully completed IPOs in 2025, setting precedents in a more favorable regulatory environment under the current U.S. administration. Companies valued above $700 million are permitted to file IPO registration statements confidentially with the SEC under the JOBS Act, typically submitting Form S-1 (for U.S. companies) or Form F-1 (for foreign private issuers) initially in secret, followed by public disclosure later in the process. Filing such a document is a critical, observable milestone indicating serious advancement toward an IPO, even if the public launch occurs after 2025. As of late 2025, no public record indicates that Consensys has filed such a document.

- Axios report via Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/meta-mask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-with-jpmorgan-goldman-axios-120000561.html

Resolution will be determined based on the SEC’s Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval (EDGAR) system, which is publicly accessible at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html. A valid filing must be traceable to Consensys (or a direct parent/subsidiary clearly identified as the IPO applicant) and must be submitted within the specified date range. The filing does not need to be publicly accessible (many are initially confidential under the JOBS Act), but must be verifiable via official SEC records or credible news reports citing SEC filing confirmations (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, or The Wall Street Journal).

If no such filing is confirmed by the SEC or reported by credible sources with evidence of submission during the resolution window, the question resolves No.

Fall-back criteria: If the SEC EDGAR system is unavailable or does not contain sufficient data at resolution time, resolution will rely on consensus reporting from at least two credible financial news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Financial Times) confirming the filing occurred within the window.

If the filing is announced but later retracted or withdrawn during the window, the question still resolves Yes, as the act of filing is the key indicator.
