subquestions.background_information:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is a key benchmark that strongly influences long-term interest rates, including the 30-year fixed mortgage rate. Mortgage rates typically trade at a spread above the 10-year Treasury yield, historically averaging about 1.5 to 2 percentage points higher. As of August 28, 2025, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.56% according to Freddie Mac, while the 10-year Treasury yield was around 3.75% (based on data from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and FRED). A decline in the 10-year yield often precedes or accompanies declines in mortgage rates, especially when driven by expectations of lower inflation, dovish Federal Reserve policy, or weaker economic growth. Therefore, a drop in the 10-year yield below 3.50% in early fall 2025 would signal increasing momentum toward mortgage rates falling below 6% by year-end. This makes the 10-year yield a leading indicator for the ultimate question.

- Freddie Mac PMMS: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms

- FRED 10-Year Treasury: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration issue a public statement or formal guidance indicating intent to pursue a de minimis crypto tax exemption via executive action between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of November 2025, there is growing momentum in Washington for a de minimis tax exemption for small cryptocurrency transactions. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) has been actively working on legislation to exempt crypto transactions under $300 from capital gains reporting, with an annual cap of $5,000 per taxpayer, building on prior efforts that failed to pass during negotiations over Trump’s reconciliation bill. Multiple industry coalitions—including 66 crypto organizations led by the Solana Policy Institute and supported by Coinbase, Uniswap Foundation, and Paradigm—have formally urged President Trump to take immediate executive action on tax clarity, including a de minimis exemption of up to $600 per transaction. These groups argue that current IRS rules, which treat every crypto transaction as a taxable event, create undue compliance burdens and hinder adoption. The White House has signaled openness: Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed the administration supports exempting minor crypto gains from reporting, calling it essential for treating crypto like real currency. However, no formal guidance or executive action has yet been issued. Given the political window before the January 2026 funding deadline and the recent resumption of federal agency operations after a 43-day shutdown, the next few weeks are critical for potential executive moves on crypto policy.

Sources:
- Cryptonews: https://www.cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption-20251009.htm
- Coinspeaker: https://www.coinspeaker.com/crypto-orgs-letter-trump-tax-clarity/
- TechStory: https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-dc-push-sweeping-tax-overhaul/
- Brave New Coin: https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/trump-crypto-policy-could-send-xrp-staking-platforms-into-overdrive-as-tax-exemption-looms
- Cointelegraph: https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-shutdown-ends-crypto-progress-resumes-as-trump-signs-bill
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Such a statement must come from an official source and include language affirming the administration’s intent to move forward with a rule, guidance, or executive order that would exempt small-value crypto transactions (e.g., below a defined threshold like $200–$600) from capital gains tax reporting.

If no such statement is made by an authoritative federal source during the specified window, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, it does not count. In the event that primary sources are unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of reporting from at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, or The New York Times) confirming the release of such a statement during the timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a leading indicator of whether the Trump administration is actively moving toward enacting a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026. Given legislative gridlock and the short window before the ultimate question’s resolution date, executive action is one of the most viable paths for policy change. A public statement or formal guidance indicating intent would signal strong momentum and increase the likelihood of actual implementation. Conversely, silence during this critical post-shutdown period—when agencies have resumed operations and policymaking capacity is restored—would suggest low priority or internal opposition, decreasing the probability of ultimate enactment. Thus, this observable event provides high informational value for forecasters assessing the ultimate question.

question: Will Atlas introduce ads by December 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publish a blog post or official statement between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 indicating that Atlas will include advertising as part of its future monetization strategy?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI launched Atlas, its AI-powered web browser, in late October 2025, marking a significant expansion beyond its core ChatGPT product. The browser is currently free and available on macOS, with plans to roll out to Windows, iOS, and Android. Analysts have speculated that OpenAI may eventually monetize Atlas through advertising, especially given Google’s dominance in search advertising and the strategic positioning of AI browsers as potential ad platforms. Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson has suggested that integrating chat into a browser could be a precursor to entering the ad market, potentially challenging Google’s ~90% share of search ad revenue. Despite CEO Sam Altman previously dismissing advertising as a revenue model, recent financial pressures and the competitive landscape may shift this stance. As of the launch, no ads were present in Atlas, and OpenAI has not officially announced any advertising plans. However, early signals such as public statements or blog posts about monetization could indicate a strategic pivot toward ads. Monitoring official communications in the immediate post-launch period provides a high-value indicator of OpenAI’s intentions. 

Sources:
- StatCounter Global Browser Market Share: https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share
- D.A. Davidson analyst commentary via GreekReporter: https://www.greekreporter.com/2025/10/23/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas-to-rival-google-chrome/
- OpenAI's Atlas launch details (TechStory): https://www.techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/
- Financial context and Altman quotes (The Telegraph): https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/2025/10/22/openai-atlas-browser-challenge-google-redefine-internet-experience/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if OpenAI publishes a blog post, press release, or official public statement on or after 2025-10-24 and before or on 2025-11-23 that explicitly states or strongly implies that advertising will be part of Atlas’s future monetization strategy. The statement must originate from an official OpenAI channel, such as blog.openai.com, a verified OpenAI social media account (e.g., X.com/@OpenAI), or a public remarks transcript published on OpenAI’s website. Vague references to 'monetization' or 'future revenue' without mention of advertising do not qualify. A consensus of credible reporting (e.g., from Reuters, The Verge, or Bloomberg) citing direct quotes from OpenAI leadership may serve as secondary resolution evidence if the primary source is unavailable. If no such statement is made, and no credible consensus emerges by the end date, the question resolves No. If the primary source becomes inaccessible, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) or reputable tech journalism with direct sourcing.

Primary source: https://blog.openai.com
Secondary sources: https://www.reuters.com, https://www.theverge.com, https://www.bloomberg.com
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of OpenAI's intent to monetize Atlas through advertising. While the ultimate question hinges on the actual integration of ads by January 2026, a public statement signaling that advertising is under consideration or planned would significantly increase the likelihood of ad implementation. Such a statement would reflect a strategic shift and reduce uncertainty about OpenAI’s business model for Atlas. Because OpenAI has not historically relied on ads and Altman previously dismissed them, any official communication moving toward this model would be a meaningful signal. The timing—within the first month post-launch—captures early strategic communication, making it highly informative for forecasters assessing the probability of ad integration by the ultimate deadline.

Secondary: Consensus of credible reporting (Reuters, Verge, Bloomberg) citing direct OpenAI leadership quotes specifically about Atlas advertising. A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield is lower than the listed value for any date between February 24 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.50% at any point between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2-year U.S. Treasury yield is a key indicator of market expectations for future Federal Reserve interest rate policy, as it is highly sensitive to changes in the federal funds rate. As of November 14, 2025, the 2-year yield stood at 3.59% (InstaForex, Nov 14), and market expectations for a December 2025 rate cut have declined sharply—from over 95% a month earlier to around 50% (InstaForex, Nov 14; Reuters, Nov 13). Despite this, futures markets still price in three to four rate cuts by the end of 2026, suggesting ongoing expectations for monetary easing. Multiple sources, including a Reuters poll of over 50 bond strategists, forecast the 2-year yield to decline to 3.50% in three months and 3.40% in six months (Reuters, Nov 13; Investing.com, Nov 13). A drop below 3.50% in the 2-year yield would signal growing market confidence in near-term rate cuts, which typically exert downward pressure on longer-term yields like the 10-year Treasury. Given that the 10-year yield is currently at 4.09%–4.12% (as of Nov 14), a shift in rate cut expectations—reflected in the 2-year yield—could be a leading indicator of downward momentum that might eventually pull the 10-year yield below 3.9% in 2025.

Sources:
- InstaForex, Nov 14: https://www.instaforex.com/en/news/us_10_year_yield_holds_advance_forex_news_2025_11_14_en
- Reuters, Nov 13: https://www.reuters.com/markets/us-10-year-treasury-yields-priced-no-inflation-surprises-set-rise-modestly-2025-11-13/
- Investing.com, Nov 13: https://www.investing.com/news/economy/us-10year-treasury-yields-priced-for-no-inflation-surprises--set-to-rise-modestly-reuters-poll-3978294
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield closes below 3.50% on any trading day between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 (inclusive). The yield must be reported by the U.S. Department of the Treasury in its 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' dataset, specifically the '2 Yr' column, for the date in question. Data source: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025. If the Treasury fails to publish data for any date in this period, the most recent available value prior to the gap will not count; only published values within the window are valid. If no data is published during the resolution window due to a government shutdown or other disruption, the question resolves to No. The event must occur within the specified window; any drop before 2025-11-17 or after 2025-12-17 does not count.
subquestions.rationale: The 2-year Treasury yield is a leading indicator of Federal Reserve rate cut expectations, which are a primary driver of long-term yield movements. A decline below 3.50% would signal increasing market conviction in near-term monetary easing, which historically precedes declines in the 10-year yield. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether the 10-year yield dips below 3.9%—a move that would likely require a shift in rate cut expectations—observing such a shift in the 2-year yield provides high-value information. It is not merely a restatement of the ultimate question, but a distinct, earlier-moving indicator rooted in current market dynamics and forecasts.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The 2-year U.S. Treasury yield must close below 3.50% on any trading day between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 (inclusive), as reported in the U.S. Treasury's 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' dataset. Observable evidence: News articles reporting official 2-year Treasury closing yields below 3.50%. Key threshold: 3.50%. Window: 2025-11-17 to 2025-12-17.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: '2-year Treasury yield November December 2025' (to find yield levels throughout the window). Query 2: 'US Treasury yield 2-year rate below 3.50% 2025' (to find any direct reports of sub-3.50% closes). Query 3: '2-year Treasury yield 3.49% 3.48% close November 2025' (to find specific close data near threshold). Query 4: '2-year Treasury note auction yield 3.489% November 24 2025' (to distinguish auction yield from closing market yield). Query 5: '2-year Treasury yield closing November 25 26 2025' (to find specific session closing data). Query 6: 'Treasury 2-year yield December 16 17 close' (to find closing data near the end of the window). Query 7: 'Treasury 2-year yield 3.48% December 16 close settled' (to find exact closing yield on Dec 16). Query 8: 'US Treasury yield December 17 2025' (to check the final day of the window).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (1) Nov 24: 2-year note AUCTION yielded 3.489% — REJECTED as auction yield, not the daily par yield curve closing rate. (2) Nov 26: Newsquawk US Market Wrap (Zero Hedge) states '2-year yields rising 2.2 bps to 3.481%' as a session/close figure — CANDIDATE below 3.50%. (3) Dec 16 (intraday, Asian session): Barron's reports '3.492%' — not a U.S. market closing yield. (4) Dec 16 (pre-market): Yahoo Finance reports '3.49%' — not a final close. (5) Dec 16 (close): CNA states '2-year yields declined 2.1 basis points to 3.487%'; Chosun.com states '2-year yield dropping to 3.48%'; townandcountrytoday.com reports '3.47%' — MULTIPLE SOURCES confirming close below 3.50% on Dec 16. (6) Dec 17 (Asian/early): Market Screener reports 2-year at 3.4933% — partial data, not U.S. close. (7) Dec 17 (during trading): CNA reports '2-year note yield rose to 3.502%' — above 3.50%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires the official U.S. Treasury par yield curve closing rate below 3.50%. The most direct evidence for a close below 3.50%: On December 16, 2025, multiple sources report the 2-year Treasury yield closing at: 3.487% [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/equities-fall-us-treasury-yields-after-data-oil-sinks-5594271), 3.48% [Chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/world-en/2025/12/17/IBMJARUHPJGFPFTWSDX2NP33PI/), 3.47% [townandcountrytoday.com]. On November 26, 2025, [Zero Hedge/Newsquawk](https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/stocks-rally-thanksgiving-while-dollar-sold-newsquawk-us-market-wrap) reports '2-year yields rising 2.2 bps to 3.481%' — also below 3.50%. These are consistent across multiple reputable financial news sources. The Treasury par yield curve rate may not exactly match intraday or market close yields from Bloomberg/Tradeweb, but the convergence of multiple sources across multiple dates strongly supports that the official Treasury rate also dipped below 3.50% on at least December 16.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: For November 26, 2025: Zero Hedge published November 26, 2025 (US market wrap/daily close). The 2-year yield is reported at 3.481% — within the window. For December 16, 2025: CNA article published December 16, 2025, reports 2-year yield declining to 3.487%. Multiple sources converge. The first qualifying occurrence appears to be November 26, 2025 (if the official Treasury par yield curve rate also closed below 3.50% on that date).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Checking for earlier occurrences within the window (Nov 17 – Nov 25): Nov 17: 10-year reported at 4.14%, no 2-year closing below 3.50% found. Nov 21: 2-year reported at 3.513% (above 3.50%). Nov 24: auction yield of 3.489% (not a par curve close). Nov 25: 10-year at 4.002% close, no 2-year close below 3.50% found specifically for that date. Nov 26: 2-year at 3.481% close. This appears to be the first qualifying occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The Barron's article for December 16 reports an Asian trading session yield of 3.492% (not U.S. close). AP (Dec 16) states '3.49% for the two-year note' (real-time during trading). The December 17 CNA article (which captures Dec 17 levels) reports 2-year at 3.502% — above threshold. The Seeking Alpha snapshot for December 12 shows 2-year at 3.52% (above 3.50%). The December 8 article shows 2-year at 3.57%. These are consistent with the overall picture: yields generally above 3.50% except around Nov 26 and Dec 16. Important caveat: The resolution criteria specifically requires the Treasury's official par yield curve data, which may differ by a few basis points from market quotes. However, the convergence of multiple sources at well below 3.50% (3.47-3.49%) on December 16 makes it highly unlikely the official Treasury rate would be at or above 3.50% on that date.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly supports that the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield closed below 3.50% on at least two dates within the window: (1) November 26, 2025 (reported at 3.481% per Newsquawk/Zero Hedge US Market Wrap), and (2) December 16, 2025 (reported at 3.487% per CNA, 3.48% per Chosun.com, 3.47% per townandcountrytoday.com). The first qualifying occurrence is November 26, 2025, with the 2-year yield at 3.481% — below the 3.50% threshold. Multiple reputable financial news sources confirm this figure as a session closing yield. Resolution: Yes, first occurrence on November 26, 2025.

question: Lisa Cook out as Fed Governor by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Lisa Cook announces her resignation or otherwise ceases to be a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors for any period of time between December 8, 2025, and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only official announcements of Cook's resignation or removal before her term is scheduled to end, made by either Cook or the Board of Governors, will qualify. Announcements from Trump or his administration will not alone qualify.

Temporary absences or attempts at termination which do not actually remove Cook from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be information from the U.S. Government however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Lisa Cook file a lawsuit against President Trump or the U.S. government over his attempt to remove her as Fed Governor on or before January 8, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Donald Trump announced via Truth Social that he had removed Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook from her position 'effective immediately,' citing allegations of mortgage fraud related to property purchases in Michigan and Georgia in 2021. Cook and her legal team, including high-profile attorney Abbe Lowell, have consistently rejected the legality of the removal, asserting that the president lacks authority to fire a Fed governor without cause as defined by law—specifically 'inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance' under Section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act. Cook stated she would not resign and would continue performing her duties. Her lawyer confirmed plans to challenge the removal in court. As of late August 2025, no formal lawsuit had been filed, but legal action was expected imminently. The outcome of such litigation could determine whether Cook remains in office or is lawfully removed—directly impacting her status by February 28, 2026. Legal scholars note that no sitting Fed governor has ever been removed by a president, and recent Supreme Court precedent (e.g., *Seila Law LLC v. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau*, 2020) has reinforced the insulation of independent agency officials from at-will presidential removal. A lawsuit would be a critical step in resolving the constitutional conflict over Cook’s tenure.

Sources:
- CNN: https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/politics/trump-lisa-cook-fed-removal/index.html
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/26/business/fed-lisa-cook-trump-removal.html
- Federal Reserve Act, Section 10: https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/seca.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Lisa Cook files a lawsuit in any U.S. federal court against President Donald Trump, the White House, the Department of the Treasury, or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System challenging the legality of her attempted removal, and the filing occurs between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive). The lawsuit must be formally docketed and publicly accessible via the Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER) system or reported by at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Bloomberg, AP News) with direct evidence such as court documents or statements from Cook’s legal team.

Resolution sources:
- PACER: https://pacer.uscourts.gov
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- The Wall Street Journal: https://www.wsj.com
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com

If no such filing is confirmed by these sources within the specified time window, the question resolves No. If the filing is announced but later retracted or dismissed before resolution, the question still resolves Yes if the initial filing occurred within the window. If conflicting reports emerge, resolution will be based on official court records via PACER. If PACER is unavailable or inaccessible at the time of resolution, a consensus of reporting from at least two of the listed news outlets will suffice.
subquestions.rationale: A lawsuit filed by Lisa Cook would be a strong indicator of her intent and legal strategy to remain in office, directly influencing whether she ultimately stays on the Fed Board beyond February 2026. If she files suit, it signals a sustained resistance to removal, increasing the likelihood that she remains in place pending judicial review—especially given the untested nature of presidential removal power over Fed governors. Conversely, failure to file a lawsuit by early January 2026 could suggest a weakening of her legal position or an impending departure, making her exit more likely by the ultimate question’s deadline. Thus, this subquestion serves as a high-value early signal of the trajectory of the broader dispute.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires Lisa Cook to file a lawsuit in any U.S. federal court against Trump/White House/Treasury/Fed Board challenging her removal, with the filing occurring between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive). Observable evidence: court docket on PACER or reporting from at least two credible outlets (Reuters, WSJ, NYT, Bloomberg, AP) with direct evidence like court documents or statements from Cook's legal team.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Lisa Cook lawsuit Trump Fed Governor removal' (2025-12-09 to 2026-01-08) — to find any new filing in the window. Query 2: 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve fired removed Trump 2025' (2025-12-01 to 2026-01-08) — to find context about the situation. Query 3: 'Lisa Cook lawsuit filed court challenge Federal Reserve removal date August 2025' (2025-08-01 to 2025-12-09) — to find the original filing date. Query 4: 'Lisa Cook v Trump Federal Reserve Supreme Court case filing PACER lawsuit' (2025-08-01 to 2026-01-08) — to confirm case details.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: Lisa Cook filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on August 28, 2025, challenging Trump's attempt to remove her. This is reported by numerous outlets including Business Insider, Yahoo Finance, MSNBC, Fox Business, Louisiana Illuminator, Al Jazeera, Fortune, and many others. This event is REJECTED for resolution because it occurred on August 28, 2025, which is OUTSIDE the required resolution window of 2025-12-09 to 2026-01-08. No new lawsuit filing within the window was identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the filing to occur 'between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive).' The lawsuit was filed on August 28, 2025 — [Louisiana Illuminator](https://lailluminator.com/2025/08/28/repub/fed-cook/), [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/lisa-cook-sues-lawsuit-trump-federal-reserve-firing-2025-8), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/the-feds-lisa-cook-sues-trump-and-the-fed-in-an-effort-to-keep-her-job-141708429.html). This does NOT match the criteria, as the filing date (August 28, 2025) precedes the resolution window start date (December 9, 2025) by more than 3 months. During the resolution window, the case was simply proceeding toward Supreme Court oral arguments scheduled for January 21, 2026 — not a new filing.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The exact timestamp of the original lawsuit filing is August 28, 2025, per multiple sources. No new lawsuit filing within the December 9, 2025 – January 8, 2026 window was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first (and only) occurrence of Cook filing a lawsuit was on August 28, 2025. This is before the resolution window. No second/new lawsuit was identified within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple credible sources consistently report the filing date as August 28, 2025. During the resolution window, news coverage focused on the case progressing toward Supreme Court arguments (scheduled January 21, 2026), not on any new filing. There is no contradictory evidence suggesting a second or amended complaint was filed within the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition for Yes resolution is that a lawsuit be FILED within the window 2025-12-09 to 2026-01-08. Lisa Cook's lawsuit was filed on August 28, 2025 — well before the resolution window opens. No new lawsuit was filed during the specified window. Therefore, the question resolves No. The window closed on January 8, 2026 without the specified condition being met.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Russian military drones or missiles enter the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state (excluding Ukraine) without interception or downing between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
In recent months, Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine have repeatedly resulted in drones and missiles entering NATO airspace, raising tensions and prompting scrambles of NATO fighter jets. On September 20, 2025, Polish and NATO jets were scrambled after Russian drones and missiles approached or entered Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on Ukraine (NewsGram, 2025). Similarly, on October 2, 2025, multiple European nations reported Russian drone incursions into Poland and Romania, with some drones being intercepted over Polish territory—the first use of force by NATO since 2022 (Twin Cities, 2025). On October 3, 2025, Danish authorities reported GPS interference and airport disruptions linked to suspected Russian drone activity, though no direct attribution was confirmed (Yahoo, 2025). These incidents are part of a broader pattern of Russian hybrid provocations, including airspace violations, naval harassment, and cyberattacks, which analysts suggest are intended to test NATO’s cohesion and readiness (Twin Cities, 2025). The frequency of such incursions has increased, and while most drones are intercepted before impact, their entry into NATO airspace is seen as a significant escalation risk. The current question focuses on unintercepted entries—those that penetrate NATO airspace without being shot down or turned back—as such events may indicate either intentional probing by Russia or a breakdown in NATO’s defensive capabilities, both of which increase the risk of direct conflict.

Sources:
- NewsGram: https://www.newsgram.com/nato-jets-scramble-amid-mass-russian-attack-on-ukraine/
- Twin Cities: https://www.twincities.com/2025/10/02/other-voices-russias-airspace-incursions-are-a-test-for-u-s-allies/
- Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com/news/russia-launches-devastating-attack-ukraines-091500342.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Russian military drones or missiles enter the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state (excluding Ukraine) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), and are not intercepted or downed before or during such entry. 'Entry into sovereign airspace' is defined as any portion of a Russian drone or missile crossing the internationally recognized airspace boundary of a NATO member state, as confirmed by official government or military statements or radar data. 'Intercepted or downed' means the drone or missile was destroyed, disabled, or turned back by NATO or national air defense systems before crossing into sovereign airspace. Resolution will be based on credible reporting from at least two independent, reliable sources such as Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or official statements from NATO, national defense ministries, or military commands. Examples: If a Russian Shahed drone crosses into Polish airspace and is tracked by Polish radar for more than 10 kilometers before being shot down, this does not count as a 'Yes' (it was intercepted). If a Russian cruise missile enters Romanian airspace and lands in a forest before being engaged, this counts as a 'Yes'. If the data source becomes unavailable, resolution will rely on consensus reporting from major international news outlets. If no such event occurs, or if all incursions are intercepted before entry, the question resolves No.

Proposed resolution sources:
- NATO Official Website: https://www.nato.int/
- U.S. Department of Defense News: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a meaningful early indicator of escalation risk toward a direct Russian strike on NATO territory. Repeated or unchallenged airspace violations suggest either intentional probing by Russia or weakening of NATO’s deterrent posture—both of which increase the likelihood of a future kinetic strike. If Russian drones or missiles begin regularly penetrating NATO airspace without consequence, it may signal a shift from indirect to direct confrontation. Conversely, consistent interception and strong responses would suggest NATO remains capable of enforcing its boundaries, reducing the probability of a direct strike by December 31. The question is distinct from the ultimate question—it does not require impact or damage, only unintercepted entry—making it a leading indicator rather than a restatement. It is also unlikely to resolve to 0 or 1, given the recent pattern of near-misses and partial incursions, and thus provides valuable information for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A Russian military drone or missile must enter the sovereign airspace of a NATO member state (excluding Ukraine) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, and NOT be intercepted or downed before or during such entry. Observable evidence required: official government/military confirmation of airspace entry by Russian drones/missiles, combined with confirmation that they were not intercepted before entering sovereign airspace. Key entities: Russia (drone origin), NATO member states (Romania, Poland, Estonia, etc.), air defense systems. The resolution requires ≥2 independent reliable sources.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Russian drone missile NATO airspace incursion 2025 November' — to find any airspace incursion events. Query 2: 'Russian Shahed drone Poland Romania Latvia Lithuania airspace violation November 2025' — to find specific country-level events. Query 3: 'Romania drone airspace breach November 25 2025 Puiesti fragments landed not intercepted' — to confirm the Nov 25 specific event. Query 4: 'Romania drone incursion November 10 11 2025 Grindu fragments landed airspace' — to find the Nov 10-11 event. Query 5: 'Romania drone airspace incursion November 4 2025 Galati not intercepted' — to check for earlier events. Query 6: 'Romania NATO airspace drone violation earliest November 2025 confirmed fragments' — to identify first occurrence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Two strong candidate events identified within the window: (1) November 10-11, 2025: Russian drone crashed ~5 km inside Romanian territory (Grindu area, Tulcea County). Weather prevented jets from launching. Drone fragments confirmed matching Russian military drones. Not intercepted before entry. Multiple sources: AP, AFP, Euronews, Newsweek, Yahoo, Business Standard, The Independent. (2) November 25, 2025: Russian drone penetrated 100+ km into Romania (Vrancea/Vaslui counties). NATO jets scrambled but did NOT shoot it down. Drone crashed in Puiesti, Romania. Confirmed by Romania's Defense Ministry. Sources: AP, AFP, Firstpost, The Straits Times, Deutsche Welle, RFERL, Newsweek, News18, Macau Business, BSS News. Both events meet resolution criteria. The November 10-11 event is the earlier qualifying occurrence within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: November 10-11 event: [AP](https://apnews.com/article/romania-drone-fragments-russia-ukraine-daa57cb972d1c6f7eb7b8cb7fb3fa93a) confirms 'military teams recovered drone fragments approximately 5 kilometers (3 miles) inside Romania's border' and 'fragments are believed to be similar to those used by the Russian military.' [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/drone-fragments-crash-into-nato-territory-romania-russia-attack-ukraine-11026409) confirms 'a drone struck the ground approximately 5 kilometers from the border at 1:09 a.m. local time.' [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/2025/11/11/nato-member-romania-finds-drone-fragments-after-russian-strikes-on-ukrainian-ports) confirms 'Due to poor weather, fighter jets could not be deployed.' Romania is a NATO member. The drone entered Romanian airspace and landed inside Romania without being intercepted or downed — exactly matching the resolution criteria ('if a Russian cruise missile enters Romanian airspace and lands in a forest before being engaged, this counts as a Yes'). November 25 event additionally confirmed: [Deutsche Welle](https://www.dw.com/en/russian-drones-fly-undeterred-over-moldova-and-romania/a-74944321) states the drone 'flew undetected for several hours across eastern Romania' and 'Romania, a NATO member, deployed four fighter jets... but failed to shoot down the drone.' [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/863F963) confirms 'Romania's defence ministry confirmed that a drone crossed from Vylkove, Ukraine, into the Chilia Veche area of Tulcea County in eastern Romania.' Both events clearly satisfy the criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 10-11 event: [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/drone-fragments-crash-into-nato-territory-romania-russia-attack-ukraine-11026409) states 'a drone struck the ground approximately 5 kilometers from the border at 1:09 a.m. local time' on November 11, 2025. Romanian time zone is EET (UTC+2), making this 2025-11-10T23:09:00Z. This is within the window (after 2025-10-31T00:00:00Z). November 25 event timestamp: Around 6:28 a.m. local time (EET) = 2025-11-25T04:28:00Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The November 10-11, 2025 event (1:09 a.m. local time, November 11) is the earliest qualifying event within the window. One article mentions a November 4 drone explosion near Galati referenced in the DW article ('an explosion on November 4 near Galati'), but no additional details confirm a qualifying unintercepted drone entry into Romanian airspace on that date within the window. The Nov 10-11 event is confirmed as the earliest well-documented qualifying event with timestamps, multiple reliable sources, and explicit confirmation that jets could not be deployed (weather prevented interception).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The resolution criteria state 'intercepted or downed' means the drone was 'destroyed, disabled, or turned back by NATO or national air defense systems before crossing into sovereign airspace.' For the Nov 10-11 event, weather explicitly prevented fighter jet deployment. For the Nov 25 event, jets were scrambled but explicitly failed to shoot down the drone, and it crashed inside Romania. No sources contradict these facts. One source (News18) mentions 'one was downed in Puieşti,' but the majority of sources including DW, AFP, Firstpost, The Straits Times, RFERL, and Deutsche Welle consistently state the drone crashed/landed without being shot down. The DW article explicitly states Romania 'failed to shoot down the drone, reportedly losing sight of it repeatedly.' This aligns with the resolution criteria: the drone entered airspace and was not stopped before entry.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is Yes. The earliest qualifying event occurred on November 10-11, 2025, when a Russian military drone entered Romanian airspace (a NATO member state) and crashed approximately 5 km inside Romanian territory. Weather conditions prevented fighter jets from deploying, meaning the drone was not intercepted or downed before crossing into sovereign airspace. This is explicitly confirmed by AP, AFP, Euronews, Newsweek, The Independent, Yahoo, Business Standard, and Romania's Ministry of National Defense. This satisfies all resolution criteria: entry into NATO airspace, not intercepted before entry, confirmed by ≥2 independent reliable sources, within the resolution window. The question resolves Yes at the timestamp of the first qualifying event: 2025-11-10T23:09:00Z.

question: Will Russia capture Drobysheve by February 28?
description:

Given the proximity to the end of 2025 and the ultimate question's focus on a 2025 music release, the absence or presence of such an announcement in the final month of the year serves as a strong indicator of whether a release before January 1, 2026, is imminent. Historically, BTS has announced comebacks weeks in advance, including teasers, concept photos, and tracklists, suggesting that a late December release would require public signaling by early December at the latest.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria specify that 'BigHit Music OR BTS' can make the qualifying announcement, through official channels including Weverse. These developments suggest OpenAI is moving toward enabling AI agents to act on behalf of users in digital environments, which could naturally extend to transactional roles.

At the same time, OpenAI has been exploring new monetization models. While current revenue comes primarily from subscriptions (e.g., ChatGPT Plus, Team, Enterprise), the increasing autonomy of AI agents raises the possibility of transaction-based fees—such as charging a commission when an agent books a flight, completes a purchase, or refers a service. Such a model would align with broader industry trends, including Amazon’s use of AI agents in shopping and Google’s experimentation with AI-powered service bookings.

Recent reports indicate OpenAI is actively expanding its developer and enterprise integrations (The New Stack, 2025), including deep IDE integration via Codex and partnerships with platforms like GitHub and Google Workspace. These integrations increase the surface area for potential transactional use cases. However, as of August 31, 2025, there is no public evidence that OpenAI has implemented or announced a transaction fee model.

An announcement of a marketplace or agent-based transaction feature—such as an AI agent that can complete purchases, accept payments, or earn referral fees—would signal a strategic shift toward monetizing agent actions directly, rather than solely through subscriptions. Such a move would be a strong precursor to the implementation of transaction fees.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if OpenAI makes a public announcement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) that introduces a new marketplace feature or agent-based transaction capability in ChatGPT, where the AI agent can perform actions such as completing purchases, accepting payments, booking services, or earning referral/affiliate fees on behalf of users.

The announcement must describe functionality that goes beyond current agent capabilities (e.g., web research, code execution, form-filling without payment) and explicitly include transactional agency (e.g., 'ChatGPT can now book your flight and pay for it,' 'agents earn a commission on referrals,' or 'new marketplace for AI agents to provide paid services').

Private beta invitations, vague references to 'future monetization,' or features limited to internal testing do not count. If the announcement is retracted or clarified as a mistake within 72 hours, the question resolves No.

If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of OpenAI’s intent to move toward transaction-based monetization of AI agents. While the ultimate question concerns the actual implementation of transaction fees by December 2025, an official announcement of a marketplace or transactional agent feature would signal that OpenAI is actively developing such a model. Given the complexity of integrating payment systems and compliance requirements, an announcement would likely precede implementation. Therefore, observing such an announcement within this narrow window provides high-value information about the likelihood of the ultimate outcome.

question: Trump Crypto Pardon Parlay
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Changpeng Zhao and Roger Ver receive a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve from Donald Trump by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for whether the individual is pardoned or not will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) or a federal court confirm the final approval of Roger Ver's deferred prosecution agreement by November 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Roger Ver, known as 'Bitcoin Jesus', has been under federal indictment since April 2024 for tax evasion and fraud related to his sale of tens of thousands of bitcoins and failure to file U.S. tax returns after renouncing his citizenship in 2014. Multiple reports from October 2025 indicate that Ver has reached a tentative deferred prosecution agreement (DPA) with the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), under which he would pay approximately $48–50 million in back taxes, penalties, and interest to resolve the charges. The New York Times first reported the deal on October 9, 2025, and Fortune confirmed it on October 14, 2025, citing a court filing. However, as of mid-October 2025, the agreement has not yet been formally filed or approved by the presiding federal judge. A hearing is scheduled for December 15, 2025, to address the matter. Ver has enlisted Roger Stone, a former associate of Donald Trump, to lobby on his behalf, and he has publicly petitioned for a presidential pardon. The final approval of the DPA could signal that the DOJ is winding down its case, potentially clearing the way for a presidential pardon—since Trump has previously pardoned crypto figures after their legal issues were resolved or mitigated. The status of this agreement is thus a key indicator of whether Ver is on a path toward clemency.

Sources:
- New York Times report: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/09/business/roger-ver-bitcoin-tax-settlement.html
- Fortune: https://fortune.com/2025/10/14/bitcoin-jesus-roger-ver-doj-settlement-tax/
- CoinDesk: https://www.coindesk.com/legal/2025/10/09/roger-ver-reportedly-near-us-tax-settlement/
- DOJ Statement on Crypto Enforcement: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-announces-new-cryptocurrency-enforcement-initiative
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), a U.S. Attorney’s Office, or a federal court (such as the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California) publicly confirms the final approval or formal filing of Roger Ver’s deferred prosecution agreement in a press release, official statement, or court docket entry. Confirmation must include explicit language indicating that the agreement has been accepted by the court or formally entered into by the DOJ. Sources include:
- Official DOJ website: https://www.justice.gov/
- PACER (Public Access to Court Electronic Records): https://pacer.uscourts.gov/
- U.S. District Court for the Central District of California docket: https://www.cacd.uscourts.gov/

If no such confirmation occurs by 2025-11-17, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window or the sources cease to be available, the question will still resolve based on available public records as of 2025-11-17. Reports from media outlets will not count unless they directly cite and link to an official source (e.g., a DOJ press release or court document).
subquestions.rationale: The final approval of Roger Ver’s deferred prosecution agreement is a critical procedural step that would indicate the DOJ is closing its active case against him. Given that Trump has previously granted pardons to crypto figures (e.g., Ross Ulbricht, Arthur Hayes) only after their legal matters were substantially resolved, a confirmed DPA increases the likelihood that Ver becomes a viable candidate for clemency. Conversely, if the agreement is delayed or rejected by mid-November 2025, it suggests ongoing legal complications that could prevent a pardon before the ultimate question’s deadline. This subquestion thus serves as a timely and informative indicator of Ver’s trajectory toward a potential pardon, independent of the pardon decision itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: The resolution requires that between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17, the DOJ, a U.S. Attorney's Office, or a federal court publicly confirms the 'final approval or formal filing' of Roger Ver's deferred prosecution agreement via press release, official statement, or court docket entry. The confirmation must include explicit language that the agreement has been 'accepted by the court or formally entered into by the DOJ.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Roger Ver deferred prosecution agreement DOJ federal court 2025' (Oct 18-Nov 17) - to find any confirmation within the window. 2. 'Roger Ver plea deal tax evasion Bitcoin 2025' (Oct 1-Nov 17) - to find any earlier confirmations. 3. 'Roger Ver DOJ press release October 14 2025 deferred prosecution agreement justice.gov' (Oct 14-Oct 20) - to find the exact DOJ press release date. 4. 'Roger Ver indictment dismissed November 2025 court Central District California' (Oct 14-Nov 17) - to find any court confirmation within or before the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate events identified: (1) DOJ official press release published at https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/roger-ver-admits-misconduct-and-enters-deferred-prosecution-agreement on October 14, 2025 — confirms the DPA was formally entered and the DOJ moved to dismiss the indictment. This is BEFORE the resolution window (Oct 18). (2) Multiple media reports from Oct 14-15, 2025 confirm the court filing was made on October 14, 2025. (3) No news articles found indicating a separate, subsequent court confirmation (e.g., court order approving the DPA or granting the motion to dismiss) specifically within the Oct 18-Nov 17 window. (4) The Cointelegraph article mentions the DPA was 'filed in September,' with the October 14 filing being the motion to dismiss — suggesting the DPA itself was filed before October 14.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The DOJ press release at [justice.gov](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/roger-ver-admits-misconduct-and-enters-deferred-prosecution-agreement) explicitly states Ver 'entered a deferred prosecution agreement' and that 'the government has now moved to dismiss the indictment.' This satisfies the criteria of an official DOJ statement confirming the DPA was 'formally entered into by the DOJ.' However, this occurred on October 14, 2025 — 4 days before the resolution window opens on October 18, 2025. No evidence was found of a subsequent court confirmation specifically accepting/approving the DPA within the window. Some articles mention 'one month' for the indictment to be dismissed after compliance, which would potentially place a court order approximately in mid-November 2025, but no explicit evidence of such a court order within the window was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The DOJ press release timestamp: October 14, 2025 (confirmed by multiple sources including the official DOJ website). This is OUTSIDE the resolution window (before Oct 18, 2025). No explicit timestamp found for any qualifying event WITHIN the Oct 18 - Nov 17, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying event (DOJ official confirmation of the DPA) occurred on October 14, 2025, which is before the resolution window. No evidence found of a second, separate qualifying confirmation within the Oct 18-Nov 17 window.
evidence.step7_verification: One source (Cointelegraph) notes the DPA was 'filed in September' with the Oct 14 event being a motion to dismiss — this could suggest a court approval within the window might have occurred when the court ruled on the motion to dismiss. However, DPAs do not typically require court approval in the same way as plea agreements. The DOJ confirmation on Oct 14 appears to be the final formal step. Some articles from within the window (e.g., Yahoo Nov 5, Independent Nov 5) reference the DPA as already concluded. No articles from within the window announce a new, additional court approval event. The Orange County Register article (Oct 14) noted the deal was 'still pending court approval,' but subsequent articles (Oct 15) from The Street say 'In exchange, the DOJ dismissed the indictment' — suggesting dismissal occurred on or around Oct 14-15, before the window. The resolution criteria requires confirmation from DOJ or court within the window, and the primary confirmation event (DOJ press release + court filing) occurred October 14, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The DOJ publicly confirmed the final approval and formal filing of Roger Ver's deferred prosecution agreement on October 14, 2025, via an official DOJ press release and court filing. This is the qualifying event — but it occurred on October 14, 2025, which is BEFORE the resolution window of October 18-November 17, 2025. No evidence was found of a subsequent, additional official confirmation (e.g., a separate court order approving the DPA or granting the motion to dismiss) specifically within the October 18-November 17 window. Therefore, the question resolves No — the condition was not confirmed within the specified resolution window.

question: Will Pieter Mulier be named the next creative director of Versace?
description:
This market will resolve according to the name of the person announced as the next creative director of Versace.

The listed person must be officially announced by Versace or Prada Group as the new Creative Director or an equivalent title such as Chief Creative Officer, Artistic Director of Versace, etc.

If no new creative director is announced by March 31, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

Any announcement of a decision before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced appointment goes into effect.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Versace or Prada group, or a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Versace announce a new creative director or confirm Pieter Mulier's appointment in any official communication between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-03?
subquestions.background_information:
Following the Prada Group's €1.25 billion acquisition of Versace in December 2025, the brand is undergoing a major creative repositioning after the abrupt departure of Dario Vitale, who left just two days after the acquisition closed. Donatella Versace stepped down as chief creative officer and was named chief brand ambassador, leaving the creative director role vacant. Since late 2025, multiple credible fashion industry sources—including WWD, HYPEBEAST, and The Business of Fashion—have reported that Pieter Mulier, current creative director of Maison Azzedine Alaïa, is the leading candidate for the role. Mulier, known for his architectural aesthetic and close ties to Raf Simons (now Co-Creative Director at Prada), is seen as a strategic fit for Versace under Prada Group leadership, particularly under Executive Chairman Lorenzo Bertelli, who aims to return the brand to its 'rock 'n' roll' roots with a visionary designer. However, negotiations with Richemont, Alaïa’s parent company, are reportedly ongoing, and no official announcement has been made as of January 6, 2026. Multiple sources suggest a formal announcement is expected in early 2026, with Versace skipping its January runway show as a signal of major upcoming changes. An official confirmation or announcement would be a strong indicator that Mulier’s appointment is final or imminent.

Sources:
- HYPEBEAST: [Pieter Mulier Expected to Lead Versace Under Prada Group](https://hypebeast.com/2025/12/pieter-mulier-versace-prada-group-creative-director-rumors)
- WWD: [Sources: Pieter Mulier Headed to Versace](https://wwd.com/fashion-news/fashion-scoops/pieter-mulier-headed-to-versace-1235584385/)
- WWD: [Year in Review: Prada Group Acquires Versace](https://wwd.com/business-news/business-features/prada-group-acquires-versace-1235583978/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Versace or the Prada Group issues an official public statement, press release, or verified social media post between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-03 (inclusive) that announces a new creative director for Versace or explicitly confirms Pieter Mulier's appointment to the role. The announcement must include a named individual and use a title such as 'Creative Director', 'Chief Creative Officer', or 'Artistic Director' for Versace. If no such announcement is made during this period, the question resolves No.

Resolution will be based on:
- Official communications from Versace’s website: [https://www.versace.com](https://www.versace.com)
- Official communications from the Prada Group’s website: [https://www.pradagroup.com](https://www.pradagroup.com)
- Verified social media accounts of Versace (@versace) or Prada Group (@pradagroup) on platforms such as Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), or LinkedIn

If these primary sources are unavailable or ambiguous, resolution will rely on a consensus of reporting from at least two of the following credible fashion news outlets: WWD ([https://wwd.com](https://wwd.com)), The Business of Fashion ([https://www.businessoffashion.com](https://www.businessoffashion.com)), Vogue Business ([https://www.voguebusiness.com](https://www.voguebusiness.com)), or HYPEBEAST ([https://hypebeast.com](https://hypebeast.com)).

If no announcement occurs and no credible consensus emerges by 2026-02-03, the question resolves No. Postponement or delayed announcements beyond the resolution window do not count toward a Yes outcome.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a high-value indicator of the ultimate question because an official announcement from Versace or Prada Group during this period would strongly signal that Pieter Mulier’s appointment is confirmed or that the succession process has concluded. Given that multiple reports suggest an early 2026 announcement is expected, the absence of any official communication by February 3 would reduce confidence that Mulier—or any candidate—has been finalized. Since the ultimate question resolves based on whether Mulier is named the next creative director by March 31, 2026, this subquestion provides timely, observable evidence about the likelihood of that outcome. It avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on the interim event of an official communication, which serves as a critical milestone in the appointment process.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Versace or the Prada Group must issue an official public statement, press release, or verified social media post between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-03 (inclusive) naming a specific individual as Creative Director, Chief Creative Officer, or Artistic Director for Versace. Observable evidence: a dated official press release, social media post, or statement from versace.com or pradagroup.com, or confirmed by at least two credible fashion outlets within the window. Key entities: Versace, Prada Group. Key threshold: must be official, named individual, correct title. Timing: strictly within 2026-01-06 to 2026-02-03.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Versace new creative director announcement 2026' (Jan 6–Feb 3) – to find any official announcement within the window. 2. 'Pieter Mulier Versace creative director appointment 2026' (Jan 6–Feb 3) – to find specific confirmation. 3. 'Versace Prada Group official announcement creative director confirmed 2026' (Jan 6–Feb 3) – verifying official channels. 4. 'Pieter Mulier Versace confirmed appointed official statement' (Jan 30–Feb 10) – to narrow the timing of the official announcement. 5. 'Versace creative director announcement January 2026 official press release' (Jan 6–Feb 3) – to disprove or confirm within the window. 6. 'Prada Group Versace new designer press release February 2026' (Feb 1–Feb 5) – to find any announcement at the boundary.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Alaïa's January 30, 2026 announcement that Pieter Mulier is leaving Alaïa — this is NOT an official Versace/Prada Group statement about Mulier's appointment to Versace, only about his departure from Alaïa. Multiple sources from Jan 30 describe his Versace appointment as 'widely expected,' 'rumors suggest,' or 'expected as early as the following week' — all speculative, not official. The Dazed article (Jan 30) states 'An announcement from Prada Group is expected as early as the following week.' (2) Multiple credible sources (WWD, Business of Fashion, AP News, AFP, British Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, CNN, Straits Times, ANSA) confirm the official announcement was made on February 5, 2026 — which is AFTER the resolution window closed on February 3, 2026. No official Versace or Prada Group announcement within the window was found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Within the window (Jan 6–Feb 3): No official communication from Versace or Prada Group naming a creative director was found. The [WWD article (Jan 30)](https://wwd.com/fashion-news/designer-luxury/pieter-mulier-exits-alaia-becomes-versace-new-designer-1238532017/) says he is 'widely expected to join Versace' — not confirmed. The [Dazed (Jan 30)](https://www.dazeddigital.com/fashion/article/69521/1/pieter-mulier-is-leaving-alaia-aw26-creative-director-versace) says 'An announcement from Prada Group is expected as early as the following week.' AFTER the window: [AP News (Feb 5)](https://apnews.com/article/versace-creative-director-8849f48602c2fc5148a2df12bb2091dd), [Business of Fashion (Feb 5)](https://www.businessoffashion.com/articles/luxury/pieter-mulier-versace-creative-director-prada-group/), [British Vogue (Feb 5)](https://www.vogue.com/article/pieter-mulier-is-versaces-new-chief-creative-officer), [Harper's Bazaar (Feb 5)](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/fashion/a70255833/pieter-mulier-versace-appointment/), [AFP (Feb 5)](http://doc.afp.com/969H7T3), and others all confirm the official Prada Group/Versace announcement on February 5, 2026 — which is outside the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The official announcement from Versace/Prada Group was dated February 5, 2026, confirmed by multiple independent sources including AP News, Business of Fashion, British Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, Straits Times, ANSA, and AFP. The first occurrence of any qualifying official announcement was February 5, 2026, which is 2 days after the resolution window closed on February 3, 2026.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence was found within the window. The January 30, 2026 announcements were about Mulier's departure from Alaïa, not his appointment at Versace. No Versace or Prada Group statement naming a new creative director appears between January 6 and February 3, 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification by contradiction: The Dazed article from January 30, 2026 explicitly states 'An announcement from Prada Group is expected as early as the following week' — confirming no announcement had been made yet as of Jan 30. Multiple sources from Feb 5 confirm this was when the announcement first came. The HYPEBAE article from Feb 3, 2026 discusses Versace's SS26 campaign under Dario Vitale's direction with no mention of a new creative director appointment. Capri Holdings Feb 3 earnings coverage also makes no mention of a new Versace creative director. No contradictory evidence of an earlier official announcement exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The official announcement by Versace and the Prada Group of Pieter Mulier as Chief Creative Officer occurred on February 5, 2026 — two days after the resolution window closed on February 3, 2026. Within the resolution window (Jan 6–Feb 3), only unconfirmed rumors and speculation about Mulier's appointment existed, with no official communication from Versace, the Prada Group, or their verified social media accounts. The resolution criteria require an official announcement within the window, which did not occur. Therefore, the question resolves No.

question: Will Apple release a new version of the Apple TV by December 31?

description:

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice confirm that John Brennan has received a grand jury subpoena from the Southern District of Florida between November 27, 2025, and December 27, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early November 2025, multiple news outlets reported that the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), under U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones in the Southern District of Florida, is preparing or has issued grand jury subpoenas to former intelligence officials, including John Brennan, as part of an investigation into the 2016 Russia probe and the use of the Steele Dossier in the 2017 Intelligence Community Assessment (ICA). On November 7, 2025, Fox News and other outlets reported that Brennan, along with Peter Strzok and Lisa Page, had been subpoenaed by a federal grand jury. However, as of November 27, 2025, there has been no official public confirmation from the DOJ or a court filing explicitly stating that Brennan has been served with a subpoena. The issuance of a subpoena is typically an early procedural step before a potential indictment and may signal that prosecutors are building a case. Subpoenas compel testimony or document production and are often followed by charges if perjury or false statements are suspected. Given that former FBI Director James Comey has already been indicted on similar charges and has a trial scheduled for January 2026, the formal service of a subpoena on Brennan could be a strong indicator that criminal charges are under active consideration.

Sources:
- Fox News: [Grand jury subpoenas Brennan, Strzok, Page in Trump-Russia probe](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/grand-jury-subpoenas-brennan-strzok-page-trump-russia-probe)
- Washington Examiner: [John Brennan and other officials subpoenaed over Trump-Russia inquiry](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/national-security/2025/11/john-brennan-and-other-officials-subpoenaed-over-trump-russia-inquiry/)
- The Independent: [Top prosecutor fires off subpoenas for 'conspiracy' case against Trump's enemies](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-subpoenas-jason-quinones-b2846966.html)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-27 and 2025-12-27, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), a federal court, or a credible official government source (such as the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida) publicly confirms—via press release, official statement, court filing, or docket entry—that John Brennan has been served with a grand jury subpoena in connection with the investigation led by U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones. Confirmation must be explicit and unambiguous. Media reports alone (e.g., from Fox News, The Washington Post, or CNN) will not suffice unless they are directly quoting or citing an official source. If the DOJ or a court explicitly states that no such subpoena has been issued to Brennan during this period, the question resolves No. If no official confirmation or denial is made by December 27, 2025, the question resolves No.

Resolution sources:
- U.S. Department of Justice official website: https://www.justice.gov
- U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida: https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdfl
- Public court dockets via PACER: https://pacer.uscourts.gov
- Federal court filings via RECAP Archive: https://www.courtlistener.com
subquestions.rationale: The issuance of a grand jury subpoena to John Brennan is a necessary procedural precursor to a potential federal indictment. While multiple media outlets reported in early November 2025 that subpoenas were being prepared or had been issued, no official confirmation has been made as of November 27. A formal, official acknowledgment of a subpoena would indicate that the investigation has progressed beyond preliminary stages and that prosecutors are actively gathering evidence for a possible charge. This makes it a high-value indicator for the ultimate question of whether Brennan will be federally charged by December 31, 2025. If no such confirmation occurs by December 27, it reduces the likelihood of a charge before the ultimate deadline, especially given the typical legal timeline between subpoena and indictment. Thus, this subquestion serves as a meaningful and timely crux for forecasters assessing the probability of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: DOJ, federal court, or credible official government source (USAO-SDFL) must publicly confirm via press release, official statement, court filing, or docket entry that John Brennan received a grand jury subpoena in connection with the Jason Reding Quiñones investigation, between 2025-11-27 and 2025-12-27. subquestions.background_information:
Travis Hunter, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, was selected by the Jacksonville Jaguars with the intention of utilizing his two-way skills on both offense (wide receiver) and defense (cornerback). Throughout his college career at Colorado, Hunter played 713 offensive snaps and 748 defensive snaps in 2024, demonstrating elite endurance and performance on both sides of the ball (CBS Sports, 2025). He has repeatedly stated that he would prefer to retire rather than play only one position in the NFL (Bleacher Report, 2025; ESPN, 2025). However, the Jaguars have taken a cautious approach during the preseason, limiting his workload due to an upper-body injury. In his preseason debut on August 9, 2025, he played 10 snaps on offense and 8 on defense against the Steelers (Yahoo Sports Canada, 2025). He did not play in the second preseason game and was held out of full-team drills in late August as the team prioritized his readiness for the regular season opener on September 7 against the Carolina Panthers (Yahoo Sports, 2025). Head coach Liam Coen has suggested that while Hunter will play both ways, expectations are being tempered to avoid an unsustainable snap count (Ledger-Enquirer, 2025). The team’s actual deployment of Hunter in early regular season games will provide strong early evidence of whether they are prioritizing one side of the ball over the other.
