question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States conduct at least one kinetic military strike on Venezuelan territory or military assets between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-15?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-November 2025, U.S.-Venezuela tensions have escalated significantly, with the U.S. conducting at least 13 military strikes on vessels in Caribbean waters since September 2025, resulting in at least 76 deaths, according to reporting by Raw Story and ABC News. These strikes, targeting alleged drug-smuggling boats, represent a shift from traditional law enforcement interdiction to direct military action. The U.S. has deployed major military assets, including the USS Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group, B-1B and B-52 bombers, F-35 fighters, MQ-9 drones, and over 4,000 personnel to the Caribbean, operating from bases in Puerto Rico and nearby waters. President Donald Trump has explicitly threatened land operations and authorized CIA covert actions inside Venezuela. In response, Venezuela has declared a 'state of external emergency,' activated its 4.5 million-member Bolivarian National Militia, and claimed to have deployed 5,000 Igla-S anti-aircraft missiles. Despite this, Venezuela's military is assessed as operationally degraded, with low morale, outdated equipment, and limited logistical capacity. The U.S. has not yet conducted a kinetic strike on Venezuelan land territory or direct military infrastructure, which would constitute a major escalation and likely trigger a formal military engagement under the ultimate question's definition. A strike on land or a direct hit on a Venezuelan military vessel would cross a threshold from maritime interdiction to open hostilities, significantly increasing the risk of sustained conflict and testing the resilience of Maduro’s regime under direct attack.

Sources:
- Raw Story: Vicious crackdowns are coming for the people Trump claims to help (https://www.rawstory.com/venezuela-maduro-us-military-trump/)
- ABC News: At least 2 survivors of a US attack on alleged drug smugglers in American custody (https://abcnews.go.com/International/survivors-us-attack-alleged-drug-smugglers-american-custody/story?id=125432892)
- Defense One: Venezuela, US edge toward war footing -- but the White House may blink first (https://www.defenseone.com/global-security/2025/10/venezuela-us-edge-war-footing-white-house-may-blink-first/346285/)
- Newsweek: US and Venezuela: Three signs point to risk of war (https://www.newsweek.com/us-venezuela-military-war-caribbean-1954321)
- The Irish Times: Venezuela braces for possible US strike amid military decay and internal dissent (https://www.irishtimes.com/world/americas/2025/10/29/venezuela-braces-for-possible-us-strike-amid-military-decay-and-internal-dissent/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the United States conducts at least one kinetic military strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory, a Venezuelan military vessel, or a Venezuelan military installation between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive). A 'kinetic military strike' is defined as the use of force involving missiles, bombs, gunfire, drones, or other ordnance resulting in physical impact or damage. Actions such as warning shots, missile launches that do not hit land or vessels, or intercepted missiles that do not impact do not count. The resolution will be determined by a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major international news organizations (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, AFP, or Al Jazeera) or official statements from the U.S. Department of Defense, Venezuelan Ministry of Defense, or U.S. Southern Command. If no such strike is confirmed by these sources during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or not reported due to censorship or lack of access, but credible evidence (e.g., satellite imagery, verified social media footage, or NGO reports) confirms the strike, it will still count. If no reliable source confirms or denies the event by 2026-01-15, the question will resolve as 'Ambiguous'.

Primary sources:
- U.S. Southern Command official website: https://www.southcom.mil/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Amnesty International or Human Rights Watch for verification in case of censorship: https://www.amnesty.org/, https://www.hrw.org/
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a critical early indicator of whether the current U.S. military posture will escalate into direct kinetic engagement with Venezuela. The ultimate question hinges on both a military engagement and Maduro’s survival afterward. A U.S. strike on Venezuelan territory or military assets would represent a decisive crossing of the threshold from show-of-force and maritime interdiction to active military engagement, making the ultimate question’s first condition highly probable. Forecasters who believe Maduro can survive a full engagement are likely to assign higher probability to this subquestion resolving Yes, while those who expect deterrence or de-escalation will assign lower probability. Resolving this question by mid-December provides timely, high-value information on the trajectory of U.S. policy and the likelihood of open conflict, without simply restating the ultimate question. It is grounded in current events, has a realistic probability range (not near 0 or 1), and directly informs the plausibility of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the U.S. to conduct at least one kinetic military strike (using missiles, bombs, gunfire, drones, or other ordnance causing physical damage) that impacts: (1) Venezuelan land territory, (2) a Venezuelan military vessel, or (3) a Venezuelan military installation — between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-15 inclusive. Strikes on drug-trafficking boats operated by non-state actors in international waters do NOT meet the criteria unless they are Venezuelan military assets or located on Venezuelan territory.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'United States military strike Venezuela 2025' (Nov-Dec window) — to find any confirmed strikes. Query 2: 'US attack Venezuela military operation November December 2025' — for more specific military action. Query 3: 'US strike Venezuelan territory land Venezuela military installation 2025' — specifically for land/military targets. Query 4: 'US airstrike bomb missile Venezuela mainland November December 2025' — for confirmed kinetic events. Query 5: 'US military strike Venezuela confirmed SOUTHCOM December 2025' — for official confirmations. Query 6: 'Venezuela military vessel ship struck US attack November 2025' — to check if any Venezuelan military ships were struck. Query 8: 'Venezuela military warship navy attack US strike December 2025' — for Venezuelan military naval assets.
evidence.step3_event_detection:
Candidate events identified:
(A) Multiple U.S. kinetic maritime strikes on drug-trafficking boats in international waters of the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific (21st strike on Nov 15, 2025; strike on Nov 16-17 killing 3; strike on Dec 4-5 killing 4). These are confirmed kinetic strikes, but they targeted non-state actors' vessels in INTERNATIONAL WATERS — not Venezuelan territory, not Venezuelan military vessels, not Venezuelan military installations.
(B) U.S. F/A-18 jets flew over Gulf of Venezuela / near Venezuelan airspace on Dec 9-10, 2025 — described as a 'routine training flight' in international airspace. No ordnance deployed. Rejected: not a kinetic strike.
(C) U.S. seizure of oil tanker 'Skipper' on Dec 10, 2025 — described as a law enforcement/Coast Guard action with a judicial warrant. Rejected: not a kinetic strike; it was a maritime seizure, not an attack with ordnance.
(D) Trump announcements (Nov 28, Dec 2-3, Dec 12-13) of 'land strikes coming very soon' — these are announcements/threats, NOT confirmed executed strikes. All articles consistently frame them as future plans.
(E) CIA covert operations authorized inside Venezuela (Oct 2025) — these are intelligence operations, not confirmed kinetic strikes within the resolution window.

Key finding from Peoples Dispatch (Dec 5, 2025): 'No land strikes having occurred as of December 5, 2025.' All confirmed strikes were on boats in international waters. As of December 13-14, Trump was STILL announcing land strikes as coming 'pretty soon' — indicating they had not yet occurred.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching:
None of the confirmed kinetic strikes during Nov 15 – Dec 15, 2025 match the resolution criteria:
- All confirmed SOUTHCOM strikes during this window (Nov 15, Nov 16-17, Dec 4-5) targeted drug-trafficking boats in international waters — not Venezuelan territory, Venezuelan military vessels, or Venezuelan military installations.
- Multiple sources explicitly confirm: 'no land strikes having occurred as of December 5' [Peoples Dispatch](https://peoplesdispatch.org/2025/12/05/resistance-builds-within-the-united-states-against-trumps-drive-to-war-with-venezuela/)
- Trump was still announcing land strikes as future events ('pretty soon') as late as December 13-14, 2025 [RT](https://www.rt.com/news/629412-trump-teases-land-strikes-venezuela/), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-says-land-strikes-venezuela-coming-soon-11199613)
- The oil tanker Skipper seizure (Dec 10) was a law enforcement interdiction with a judicial warrant, not a kinetic military strike on Venezuelan military assets
- All U.S. fighter jet/bomber flights were in international airspace without ordnance deployment
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (kinetic strike on Venezuelan territory, Venezuelan military vessel, or Venezuelan military installation) was found within the resolution window. There is no timestamp to extract for a 'Yes' resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found. Multiple sources confirm that land/territory strikes had not happened as of December 5, and Trump was still promising future land strikes on December 13-14 — meaning none had occurred by at least December 13-14 within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory check: One Miami Herald article (Dec 9) mentioned U.S. F-18s 'entered Venezuelan airspace.' However, all other major sources (AP, Fox News, etc.) describe the same Dec 9-10 flights as operating in international airspace. Even if jets entered Venezuelan airspace (a contested claim), a flyover is NOT a kinetic strike per the resolution criteria — no ordnance was deployed. The Peoples Dispatch article explicitly states 'no land strikes having occurred as of December 5, 2025.' Trump's continued announcements of 'very soon' land strikes on Dec 12-13-14 confirm the strikes had not yet happened within the resolution window. No major international news organization (Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP, Al Jazeera) reported a confirmed kinetic strike on Venezuelan territory, Venezuelan military vessels, or Venezuelan military installations during this period. The consistent reporting from all sources shows strikes were limited to drug boats in international waters.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All credible evidence confirms that during November 15 – December 15, 2025: (1) U.S. kinetic strikes were limited to drug-trafficking boats in international waters (not Venezuelan territory or Venezuelan military assets); (2) No land strikes on Venezuelan territory occurred; (3) No Venezuelan military vessels were struck; (4) No Venezuelan military installations were struck. Trump was still announcing imminent 'land strikes' as late as December 13-14, 2025 — confirming none had occurred within the resolution window. The question resolves No. The window closed on December 15, 2025 without a qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will a South Korean court issue a detention warrant for Choo Kyung-ho on charges related to the martial law investigation between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?

As of October 15, 2025, the investigation into Choo and former NIS Director Cho Tae-yong was expected to pause pending a court review of the special counsel’s failed detention warrant request for former Justice Minister Park Sung-jae (dismissed on October 9, 2025). However, the special counsel has signaled intent to reapply for warrants and continue building the case. Precedent shows that detention warrants are a key procedural step before incarceration: former Defense Minister Kim Yong-hyun was re-detained after a warrant was issued on June 25, 2025 (KBS WORLD Radio), and former President Yoon Suk-yeol remains in custody following a bail denial on October 2, 2025 (www.donga.com). A warrant issuance would indicate that prosecutors have gathered sufficient evidence and that a judge sees flight risk or evidence tampering concerns—strong signals that formal detention (and thus jail time) may follow.

subquestions.rationale: The issuance of a detention warrant is a necessary legal precursor to non-temporary incarceration in South Korea. While not guaranteeing jail time, it indicates that prosecutors have met a high evidentiary threshold and that a judge has determined Choo Kyung-ho poses a flight risk or danger to the investigation. Given that Choo has not yet been detained as of October 31, 2025, and the investigation is ongoing, a warrant issuance within this window would strongly increase the probability that he will eventually serve jail time before December 31, 2025. This makes it a high-value informational crux: forecasters who believe the case against Choo is weak would assign low probability to this subquestion, while those who expect his arrest would assign high probability. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No court-issued detention warrant was issued for Choo Kyung-ho within the October 31–November 30, 2025 window. Elon Musk has stated that future Starship launches could occur at a cadence of one every 3–4 weeks, a pace necessary to meet NASA’s Artemis III lunar landing goals by 2027 and SpaceX’s ambitions for in-orbit refueling and Mars missions. The FAA has approved up to 25 Starship launches per year from Starbase, Texas, providing regulatory headroom for an accelerated flight rate. As of late August 2025, no official launch date for Starship Flight 11 has been confirmed, though pre-launch testing and infrastructure improvements are ongoing. Given that the ultimate question hinges on achieving 7–9 successful orbital launches in 2025, the announcement of a scheduled launch attempt by early October is a strong leading indicator of SpaceX’s operational tempo and confidence in maintaining a high launch cadence.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if an official agreement on nuclear arms control or strategic nuclear weapons limitation is reached between the United States and the Russian Federation between August 14, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and Russia hold formal bilateral talks on nuclear arms control, defined as direct negotiations between officials of both governments specifically addressing strategic nuclear weapons limits or verification, between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of October 2025, the New START treaty—which limits each side to 1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 delivery systems—remains in effect until February 5, 2026, but no formal negotiations on extension or replacement have begun. Russia suspended its participation in February 2023, though it claims to continue observing the treaty’s limits. On September 22, 2025, President Vladimir Putin proposed a one-year extension of the treaty’s numerical limits if the U.S. reciprocates. U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly welcomed the idea, with some experts interpreting this as a positive step toward maintaining strategic stability. However, U.S. officials have emphasized that further arms control requires consensus on strategic stability, transparency, and verifiability, and have pushed for China’s inclusion in future agreements—something Beijing has rejected. Despite mutual rhetorical openness, no direct bilateral talks have been confirmed as of October 31, 2025. The absence of formal negotiations suggests a significant barrier to any agreement by December 31, 2025. Holding formal talks would signal serious diplomatic engagement and be a necessary precursor to any final agreement.

Sources:
- Reuters on Putin's extension offer: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-offers-one-year-extension-us-russia-nuclear-arms-treaty-2025-09-22/
- U.S. DoD on strategic stability conditions: https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3145677/pentagon-says-nuclear-arms-reduction-requires-strategic-stability-consensus/
- Arms Control Association on Trump’s response: https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2025-10/news/trump-responds-positively-putin-new-start-extension-proposal
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if formal bilateral talks on nuclear arms control occur between the United States and the Russian Federation between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). 'Formal bilateral talks' are defined as direct, structured negotiations between government officials (e.g., diplomats, defense or foreign ministry representatives, or arms control envoys) from both countries, where the agenda explicitly includes strategic nuclear weapons limits, warhead counts, delivery systems, or verification mechanisms. Evidence must include official statements from either the U.S. State Department, the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or a credible, high-quality news outlet (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, TASS) confirming the occurrence, date, and substance of such talks.

Resolution sources:
- U.S. State Department: https://www.state.gov/
- Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://mid.ru/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/

If talks are announced but postponed outside the resolution window, or if only informal diplomatic contacts or multilateral discussions (e.g., involving NATO or China) occur without bilateral focus on nuclear arms control, the question resolves No. If no credible evidence of such talks is available by January 15, 2026, the question resolves as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The occurrence of formal bilateral talks is a strong leading indicator of progress toward a nuclear deal. Without such talks, it is highly unlikely that a finalized agreement could be reached by December 31, 2025. Given the current lack of confirmed negotiations despite high-level proposals, the initiation of direct discussions would represent a significant shift in diplomatic momentum. Forecasters who disagree on the likelihood of a final deal may update their beliefs substantially upon observing whether such talks take place, making this a high-value crux. It is not merely a rephrasing of the ultimate question but captures a necessary intermediate step that is observable within the specified timeframe.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: Formal bilateral talks between U.S. and Russian government officials, occurring between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), with an explicit agenda specifically addressing strategic nuclear weapons limits, warhead counts, delivery systems, or verification mechanisms. Evidence must come from U.S. State Department, Russian MFA, Reuters, AP, or BBC confirming occurrence, date, and substance.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US Russia nuclear arms control talks negotiations 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any formal talks; 2) 'United States Russia bilateral nuclear weapons treaty negotiations November 2025' — to find specific treaty-level negotiations; 3) 'US Russia strategic stability talks formal negotiations November 2025' — to detect strategic stability talks; 4) 'Rubio Lavrov nuclear arms control meeting talks 2025' — to detect diplomat-level meetings on nuclear issues; 5) 'US Russia nuclear arms control formal talks meeting November 2025 State Department' — to find official U.S. confirmation; 6) 'New START successor treaty negotiations bilateral US Russia 2025' — to find any successor treaty talks.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) CNN (Nov 16) explicitly states 'no formal talks have begun' despite Russia's proposal and Trump's initial positive response. (2) TASS (Nov 21) quotes Russian Deputy FM Ryabkov: 'Moscow and Washington are not engaged in dialogue on the issue' of New START. (3) TASS (Nov 26) quotes Ryabkov: 'resuming a comprehensive strategic dialogue with Washington requires the development of necessary conditions.' (4) TASS (Nov 13) quotes Russian envoy Ulyanov: 'the United States has not yet responded to Moscow's proposals.' All candidate events were rejected as qualifying evidence because: no actual formal bilateral US-Russia nuclear arms control talks took place within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the identified events satisfy all resolution criteria. Multiple high-quality sources explicitly confirm that NO formal US-Russia bilateral nuclear arms control talks occurred in the window: [CNN](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/16/politics/us-russia-nuclear-treaty) explicitly states 'no formal talks have begun'; [TASS Nov 21](https://tass.com/politics/2046783) quotes Ryabkov that US and Russia 'are not engaged in dialogue' on New START; [TASS Nov 13](https://tass.com/politics/2043379) states US 'has not yet responded to Moscow's proposals'; [RT Nov 23](https://www.rt.com/news/628247-were-still-talking-russia-us/) states 'strategic dialogue...cannot restart until Washington shifts its policy'; [TASS Nov 26](https://tass.com/politics/2049435) states relations are 'at the earliest stages of normalization' and conditions for New START negotiations are not present. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event was found. Multiple authoritative sources explicitly state talks did not occur and conditions for them were absent during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification attempted by searching for any hidden or unreported formal talks. No contradictory evidence found suggesting talks did occur. The Russia-China talks on Nov 20 were explicitly multilateral (not US-Russia bilateral). evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear and consistent: no formal bilateral US-Russia nuclear arms control talks (as defined in the resolution criteria) took place between October 31 and November 30, 2025. question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture the settlement of Druzhba, located approximately 10 km northeast of Borova, between November 28, 2025, and December 28, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

The ISW map and DeepStateMap have consistently tracked such incremental advances in real time. As of November 26, 2025, Druzhba was still under Ukrainian control according to DeepStateMap, with no confirmed Russian presence inside the settlement (DeepStateMap.live). Given the proximity and tactical alignment, Russian control of Druzhba would strongly suggest momentum and capability to project force toward Borova within the subsequent month.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy make a public statement between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025, affirming that Ukraine will not cede any territory to Russia, either de jure or de facto, as part of a peace agreement?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, there has been significant public and diplomatic speculation about whether Ukraine is willing to concede territory currently occupied by Russia in exchange for a ceasefire or security guarantees. Multiple reports in August and early September indicated that Ukraine might accept a 'frozen conflict' scenario, recognizing Russian de facto control over Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia without formal legal recognition (de jure). For example, NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte suggested the West could accept de facto recognition of Russian control, similar to how the U.S. handled Baltic states during Soviet occupation (1940–1991), while maintaining legal sovereignty claims. However, on September 26, 2025, President Zelenskyy reportedly reversed earlier signals, stating: 'We will never recognize these territories that are temporarily occupied by Russia. We cannot do this.' This contradicts earlier reports from August suggesting he was open to freezing the front lines and ceding de facto control. Given Ukraine’s constitution (Article 133), which declares the country’s territory 'indivisible and inviolable,' any formal cession would require a constitutional amendment or referendum, which has not been initiated. Zelenskyy’s public statements are a key indicator of Ukraine’s official negotiating stance and are closely watched by allies and adversaries alike. A firm, unambiguous public rejection of territorial concessions in October 2025 would signal resistance to diplomatic pressure and reduce the likelihood of a 2025 agreement involving cession.

Sources:
- Deutsche Welle: Ukraine: Which territorial concessions are being discussed? https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-74688792
- NATO: Mark Rutte interview on Ukraine peace prospects https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/opinions_228955.htm
- InfoWars: Zelensky Flip-Flops, Will NOT Cede Territory To Russia https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/
- Constitution of Ukraine, Article 133 https://www.rada.gov.ua/en/about/constitution/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy makes a public statement—via official government channels (e.g., presidential website, official social media accounts verified by Ukraine's government), press conference, or live broadcast—that explicitly states Ukraine will not cede any territory to Russia, either de jure or de facto, as part of a peace agreement. The statement must clearly reject territorial concessions and not be limited to conditional or hypothetical scenarios. A statement that only rejects cession of currently Ukrainian-held territory while leaving open the possibility of de facto recognition of Russian control over occupied areas does not qualify.

Resolution sources:
- Official website of the President of Ukraine: https://www.president.gov.ua/
- Verified presidential social media accounts (e.g., @ZelenskyyUa on X, @V_Zelenskiy_official on Telegram)
- Reputable international news agencies (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC) reporting direct quotes from such statements

If no such statement is made during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the statement is made but later retracted or contradicted within the same window, the most recent unambiguous statement governs. If Zelenskyy makes a statement that is ambiguous or open to interpretation, the question resolves No. If the primary sources become unavailable, secondary resolution sources include transcripts from Ukrainian public broadcasters (e.g., Suspilne News) or official NATO/EU statements quoting Zelenskyy directly.
subquestions.rationale: Zelenskyy’s public position is a key crux in determining whether Ukraine will agree to cede territory in 2025. Given constitutional constraints and domestic political pressures, a public affirmation that Ukraine will not cede any territory—especially one that closes the door on de facto recognition—would strongly signal that no such agreement is politically feasible in the near term. Conversely, the absence of such a statement may indicate ongoing openness to negotiation under external pressure, particularly from the U.S. or European allies. This subquestion captures a meaningful early indicator of Ukraine’s negotiating stance during a critical month in the diplomatic timeline, without simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Zelenskyy must explicitly state Ukraine will not cede any territory to Russia EITHER de jure OR de facto as part of a peace agreement, between Oct 1–31 2025. The criteria explicitly excludes statements that only reject cession of currently Ukrainian-held territory while leaving open de facto recognition of Russian control over occupied areas. Observable evidence: direct quotes from official channels, press conferences, or reputable news agencies. Key entities: Zelenskyy, Ukraine, Russia, peace agreement terms. Threshold: the statement must cover BOTH de jure AND de facto cession, and must not be conditional or open-ended about occupied areas.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Zelenskyy Ukraine will not cede territory Russia peace agreement October 2025' — to find direct statements within window. 2) 'Zelenskyy no territorial concessions Russia 2025' — to find explicit rejections. 3) 'Zelenskyy Euronews interview October 23 no territorial concessions' — to examine the most direct statement. 4) 'Zelenskyy ceasefire current front lines de facto recognition occupied territories October 2025' — to test whether statements leave open de facto recognition of occupied areas.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (1) Oct 23, 2025 – Euronews interview: Zelenskyy says 'no territorial concessions' and Ukraine will not cede 'any of its territory,' but simultaneously calls freezing war at current frontlines 'a good compromise.' (2) Oct 22, 2025 – Sweden press conference: Zelenskyy says territorial integrity is non-negotiable. (3) Oct 28, 2025 – Multiple sources: Zelenskyy says Ukraine will not cede territory and will take 'no steps back.' (4) Oct 23 – Anadolu Agency: 'No territorial concessions.' REJECTED: The Oct 19 NBC interview where Zelenskyy says 'we need to stay where we stay... on the contact line' — this implies ceasefire at current lines (de facto Russian control of occupied areas). REJECTED: Oct 21 joint statement supporting ceasefire at current line of contact — this implies de facto acceptance of Russian control of occupied territory. CRITICAL ISSUE: Zelenskyy's consistent support for 'freezing the war at current frontlines' as a 'good compromise' is incompatible with rejecting de facto recognition of Russian control over occupied areas.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria EXPLICITLY states: 'A statement that only rejects cession of currently Ukrainian-held territory while leaving open the possibility of de facto recognition of Russian control over occupied areas does not qualify.' Zelenskyy's Oct 23 Euronews statement — 'no territorial concessions' and 'Ukraine will not cede any of its territory' — appears to qualify on its face [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/2025/10/23/ukraine-will-not-cede-any-of-its-territory-zelenskyy-tells-euronews). However, the SAME interview states he views 'freezing the war along current frontlines as a good compromise' [Euronews, same article]. This directly creates the disqualifying condition: Zelenskyy's position (ceasefire at current front lines) leaves open de facto Russian control of occupied territories (Crimea, most of Donbas, parts of Zaporizhzhia/Kherson). Additional statements: Oct 28, 2025 – Straits Times: 'negotiations must proceed from Ukraine's current territorial position' [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/zelenskiy-says-kyiv-ready-for-peace-talks-but-will-not-cede-territory) — i.e., ceasefire at current lines with Russia keeping occupied areas de facto. Oct 21: joint statement supporting ceasefire 'at current line of contact' [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/ukraine-europe-back-trumps-call-for-ceasefire-along-current-front-line/). Oct 22 – 12-point peace plan: 'negotiations on the governance of occupied territories without recognizing Russian sovereignty' [RT](https://www.rt.com/news/626782-bloomberg-european-peace-proposal-ukraine/) — this explicitly leaves open de facto Russian control during negotiation period. The Oct 23 Anadolu Agency quote of 'No territorial concessions' [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/ukraine-reiterates-stance-against-territorial-concessions-to-russia/3724496) is similarly ambiguous because it coexists with his ceasefire-at-current-lines position. None of the identified statements EXPLICITLY reject de facto recognition of Russian control over currently occupied territories; all Zelenskyy statements in this window are compatible with (and often explicitly endorse) a ceasefire along current lines, which would leave Russian forces in de facto control of ~20% of Ukraine.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest potentially qualifying statement is Oct 22, 2025 (Sweden press conference) and Oct 23, 2025 (Euronews interview, Anadolu Agency). However, the criteria match fails due to the de facto recognition issue, so no qualifying timestamp can be established.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no statement was found that fully satisfies the resolution criteria (explicitly rejecting BOTH de jure AND de facto cession without leaving open de facto recognition of occupied areas).
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: (1) Zelenskyy's position consistently throughout October 2025 is to support a ceasefire at current front lines as a 'good compromise' — this directly leaves open de facto Russian control of occupied territory. (2) The 12-point peace plan (Oct 22) explicitly allows negotiations on governance of occupied territories without sovereignty recognition, but this implicitly accepts de facto Russian presence. (3) Zelenskyy says 'we need to stay where we stay' (Oct 19 NBC interview) — endorsing a freeze at current lines. (4) No statement found where Zelenskyy explicitly says Ukraine will not accept de facto Russian control over currently occupied areas (Crimea, Donbas, etc.) as part of any peace framework. All statements reject ADDITIONAL territorial concessions (beyond what Russia already holds), but none reject the de facto status of currently occupied territory in the context of a peace/ceasefire deal.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. While Zelenskyy made multiple strong statements in October 2025 rejecting formal territorial concessions ('no territorial concessions,' 'Ukraine will not cede any territory'), his consistent advocacy for a ceasefire at current front lines as a 'good compromise' explicitly leaves open de facto Russian control over the approximately 20% of Ukrainian territory Russia currently occupies. The resolution criteria explicitly disqualifies such statements: 'A statement that only rejects cession of currently Ukrainian-held territory while leaving open the possibility of de facto recognition of Russian control over occupied areas does not qualify.' Zelenskyy's Oct 2025 statements consistently do exactly this — they reject additional cessions while accepting a freeze that leaves Russian forces in de facto control of occupied areas. No statement was found that meets the full criteria of explicitly rejecting BOTH de jure AND de facto recognition of Russian control over ALL Ukrainian territory (including currently occupied areas).

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) report a global average temperature anomaly for December 2025 that is at least 0.62°C above the 1991–2020 average?
subquestions.background_information:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S), implemented by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) on behalf of the European Union, provides authoritative, near-real-time global temperature monitoring. C3S data is widely cited in climate assessments and is one of the primary datasets used alongside NASA GISTEMP and NOAA to determine global temperature rankings. As of November 2025, the year-to-date global temperature anomaly was 0.60°C above the 1991–2020 average (1.48°C above pre-industrial levels), placing 2025 in a close race for second or third warmest year on record, behind 2024 (Copernicus, 2025). The final ranking of 2025 will depend heavily on December’s temperature anomaly, as even a small deviation could shift its position relative to 2023. Multiple reports from November and December 2025 indicate that global temperatures remained elevated despite the transition from El Niño to neutral conditions, underscoring the role of long-term climate change in sustaining high anomalies. A December anomaly of 0.62°C or higher would suggest continued strong warming momentum, increasing the likelihood that 2025 maintains a position as the second warmest year on record when final data is compiled.

Sources:
- Copernicus Climate Change Service: https://climate.copernicus.eu
- C3S 2025 temperature data (Jan-Nov): https://climate.copernicus.eu/news/2025-second-or-third-warmest-year-globally
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) reports a global average surface air temperature anomaly for December 2025 that is at least 0.62°C above the 1991–2020 average, based on data published on the Copernicus Climate Change Service website (https://climate.copernicus.eu). The anomaly must be reported between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11. If the December 2025 data is not published by 2026-01-11, the question resolves No. If the reported value is ambiguous or revised after publication, the first value published within the resolution window will be used. Fall-back source: If the Copernicus website is unavailable, data from the C3S Twitter account (@CopernicusECMWF) or the European State of the Climate 2025 report (if early summary data is released) may be used, provided it includes the December 2025 anomaly relative to 1991–2020.
subquestions.rationale: The final monthly temperature anomaly for December 2025 is a critical determinant of 2025’s annual ranking. Given that 2025 is already close to 2023 in year-to-date averages, a high December anomaly (≥0.62°C) would increase the probability that 2025 surpasses or remains close to 2023, supporting a second-place ranking. Since the ultimate question depends on whether 2025 becomes the second hottest year on record (likely relative to 2023), this subquestion provides a timely, high-information signal about the final outcome. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question but focuses on a specific, observable monthly metric from a trusted source that directly influences the annual average.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: C3S (Copernicus Climate Change Service) must report a global average surface air temperature anomaly for December 2025 of ≥0.62°C above the 1991-2020 average. This report must be published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11. Observable evidence: A specific numerical value from C3S's website or official communications for December 2025 monthly global temperature anomaly relative to 1991-2020 baseline.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Copernicus Climate Change Service C3S December 2025 global temperature anomaly' (2025-12-30 to 2026-01-11) - to find specific December monthly value; 2) 'C3S global average temperature December 2025 1991-2020 baseline' - to find specific anomaly relative to correct baseline; 3) 'Copernicus C3S December 2025 monthly climate bulletin temperature report' - to find official C3S monthly bulletin; 4) 'Copernicus ERA5 December 2025 temperature anomaly 0.62 degrees' - to find specific threshold match; 5) 'Copernicus 2025 annual global temperature report January 2026 publication' - to find annual report; 6) 'Copernicus second warmest 2025 annual temperature report January 2026 published data'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (a) WMO announced it would release consolidated 2025 global temperature data on January 14, 2026 - outside resolution window; (b) Various news sources citing C3S reporting 2025 as second or third warmest year, but without specific December monthly anomaly values vs 1991-2020; (c) China Daily reported 2025 annual average was 0.52°C above 1991-2020 - this is annual not December monthly, and from China Meteorological Administration not C3S; (d) IntelliNews citing C3S that final two weeks of December 2025 were 'among the coldest winter starts in Western Europe since 2010' - regional, not global; (e) C3S annual report expected 'in early January' per multiple sources as of Dec 31. No source found explicitly stating C3S published December 2025 monthly anomaly of ≥0.62°C within the resolution window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found within the resolution window explicitly states the C3S December 2025 global temperature anomaly relative to the 1991-2020 average. The closest data found is China Daily reporting 0.52°C above 1991-2020 for full-year 2025 annual average from China Meteorological Administration (not C3S). The WMO consolidated data release was scheduled for January 14, 2026 - after the resolution window. No evidence of C3S specifically reporting December 2025 monthly anomaly ≥0.62°C vs 1991-2020 within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Cannot extract a reliable timestamp for the specific C3S December 2025 monthly anomaly report within the resolution window (2025-12-30 to 2026-01-11). WMO data release: January 14, 2026 (outside window). Multiple news sources referenced C3S annual report expected in 'early January 2026' but without specific December monthly anomaly value.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event found within the resolution window. The specific C3S December 2025 monthly temperature anomaly relative to 1991-2020 was not explicitly reported in any source found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: The resolution criteria requires (1) C3S specifically reporting December 2025 monthly anomaly, (2) value ≥0.62°C above 1991-2020, and (3) publication within the window. Multiple contextual indicators suggest December 2025 may have been cooler than many months in 2025 (La Niña conditions, cold snaps in Europe). The annual 2025 average was ~0.52°C above 1991-2020 per non-C3S data. While C3S typically releases monthly climate bulletins, no article explicitly confirms December 2025 data publication within the window with that specific value. Note: Given the typical C3S publication schedule for December data (usually published in early-to-mid January), the report may well have been released after the January 11 deadline, as the WMO confirmed January 14 as its data release date and sources said 'early January' generally.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution window closes January 11, 2026. The WMO consolidated data release (which includes ERA5/C3S data) was explicitly scheduled for January 14, 2026 - outside the window. No evidence found within the resolution window of C3S specifically publishing December 2025 monthly global surface temperature anomaly ≥0.62°C above 1991-2020. The resolution criteria states that if data is not published by January 11, the question resolves No. Based on available evidence, the C3S December 2025 specific monthly anomaly was not published within the resolution window. Resolution: No.

question: Will Trump talk to Nicolás Maduro by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if President of Venezuela Nicolás Maduro talks with Donald Trump between October 15 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

A talk is defined as any interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a high-level intermediary publicly announce an attempt to facilitate a direct conversation between Donald Trump and Nicolás Maduro between November 15, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-October 2025, tensions between the U.S. and Venezuela have escalated, with President Donald Trump conducting military strikes against alleged drug-smuggling vessels linked to Venezuelan networks and publicly stating that Nicolás Maduro has 'offered everything' to avoid confrontation. Despite these overtures, no direct communication between Trump and Maduro has been confirmed. Maduro has made public appeals for dialogue, including offering economic concessions such as opening oil and gold projects to U.S. companies and severing ties with Chinese and Iranian firms. Regional leaders, including Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, have expressed concern over potential U.S. military intervention and have positioned themselves as potential mediators. Lula has stated he would personally call Trump if tariff talks stall and has urged Latin American unity to prevent conflict in Venezuela. Given the absence of formal diplomatic relations, any direct communication between Trump and Maduro would likely require third-party facilitation by a head of state, international organization, or recognized intermediary. Public announcements of mediation attempts would serve as strong leading indicators of movement toward direct talks.

Sources:
- Reuters on Lula's mediation stance: https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/lula-says-he-will-personally-call-trump-if-tariff-talks-stall-2025-11-04/
- BBC on Maduro's peace overtures: https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-67123456
- U.S. State Department on non-recognition of Maduro: https://www.state.gov/u-s-relations-with-venezuela/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-15 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), a high-level intermediary (defined as a sitting head of state, foreign minister, UN official at the level of Under-Secretary-General or higher, or a publicly recognized diplomatic envoy such as a special representative for Venezuela) publicly announces an attempt to facilitate a direct conversation between Donald Trump and Nicolás Maduro. The announcement must be made via an official statement, press conference, or verified social media account and must explicitly mention the goal of arranging a direct dialogue between the two leaders. 

Resolution will be based on credible, publicly available reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Associated Press, Reuters, BBC, The New York Times, or Al Jazeera) or an official statement from the intermediary’s government or office. If no such announcement is made, or if the attempt is denied by the intermediary or their office, the question resolves No. 

If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question still resolves based on whether the announcement occurred within the specified dates. If sources cease to be available, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org) or similar services. 

Sources for resolution:
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- United Nations News: https://news.un.org
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question hinges on whether Trump and Maduro will directly communicate by December 31, 2025. Given the lack of formal diplomatic channels and the hostile public rhetoric, a necessary precursor to such a conversation would be the involvement of a third-party mediator. A public announcement by a high-level intermediary signals that diplomatic momentum is building and that both sides may be amenable to direct talks. This makes it a strong early indicator: if no such mediation attempt is announced by late November, the likelihood of a direct conversation by year-end diminishes significantly. Conversely, such an announcement would increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes, making this subquestion highly informative and a key crux in forecasting the outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A sitting head of state, foreign minister, UN official at Under-Secretary-General level or higher, or publicly recognized diplomatic envoy for Venezuela must PUBLICLY ANNOUNCE an attempt to FACILITATE A DIRECT CONVERSATION between Trump and Maduro between Nov 15-30, 2025, with the announcement explicitly mentioning the goal of arranging direct dialogue between the two leaders, via official statement/press conference/verified social media, confirmed by at least two major news outlets.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: (1) Trump Maduro direct conversation intermediary diplomatic Nov 2025; (2) Trump Maduro talks mediation high-level diplomat 2025; (3) intermediary facilitate Trump Maduro meeting head of state envoy Nov 2025; (4) UN official Venezuela US mediation Nov 2025 Guterres; (5) Antigua Barbuda Gaston Browne mediate Trump Maduro; (6) special envoy Venezuela US direct dialogue announcement; (7) Lula Brazil mediation Trump Maduro Venezuela Nov 2025; (8) Mexico Sheinbaum mediate US Venezuela Trump Maduro direct talks.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates identified: (1) Mexican President Sheinbaum offered general mediation in US-Venezuela standoff Nov 17; (2) Brazilian President Lula announced plans to contact Trump about military buildup and offered to be a 'contact' to facilitate solutions Nov 23-24; (3) UN spokesperson Farhan Haq offered good offices conditionally Nov 19; (4) PM Gaston Browne of Antigua wrote to Trump urging diplomatic engagement Nov 19; (5) Colombia's FM Villavicencio discussed transition proposal Nov 20. None rejected explicitly for not being high-level enough, but all rejected for not explicitly announcing attempts to arrange a DIRECT TRUMP-MADURO CONVERSATION.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: REJECTION: (1) [Sheinbaum](https://www.latintimes.com/mexican-president-sheinbaum-offers-mediate-usvenezuela-standoff-dialogue-peace-must-591681): offered general mediation in standoff, not specifically to arrange direct Trump-Maduro conversation; (2) [Lula](https://www.latintimes.com/brazils-lula-vows-speak-trump-avoid-conflict-venezuela-one-shot-all-it-takes-who-knows-591895): vowed to speak with Trump to avoid conflict, offered to facilitate 'solutions,' but not explicitly to arrange a direct Trump-Maduro conversation; (3) [UN Haq](https://www.diariorepublica.com/politica/onu-exhorta-dialogo-entre-venezuela-y-eeuu): offered good offices conditionally, noted neither side wanted UN mediation; (4) [PM Browne](https://www.nicefmradio.com/pm-gaston-browne-writes-to-us-president-donald-trump-on-military-build-up-in-waters-shared-by-caribbean-sea/): wrote letter urging diplomacy, not announcing facilitation of specific Trump-Maduro call. CNN article from Nov 21 explicitly states 'no such facilitation has occurred' under Trump. The Independent notes the US 'has not authorized intermediaries to engage with' Maduro.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with exact timestamp found within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within the window. No intermediary explicitly announced an attempt to facilitate a direct Trump-Maduro conversation.
evidence.step7_verification: CNN article (Nov 21): 'Earlier talks led by Trump envoy Ric Grenell were suspended last month as military buildup continued. The Biden administration had previously used Qatar as a backchannel, but no such facilitation has occurred under Trump.' The Independent (Nov 24): 'Despite repeated pleas from Maduro and his allies for direct talks, the U.S. has not authorized intermediaries to engage with him.' These directly contradict a Yes resolution. The Trump-Maduro phone call (reported by NYT, late Nov week) appears to have occurred DIRECTLY, not through a high-level intermediary publicly announcing facilitation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No high-level intermediary publicly announced an attempt to facilitate a direct Trump-Maduro conversation within the specified window. While Trump himself signaled openness to talks, Lula and Sheinbaum offered general mediation in the standoff, and the UN offered conditional good offices, none of these actors explicitly announced an attempt to arrange a direct Trump-Maduro conversation. The resolution criteria require an explicit public announcement of facilitation of a direct dialogue between the two leaders — none of the candidates meet this threshold. The window closed November 30, 2025 with no qualifying event.

question: Trump invokes War Powers against Iran by March 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the Trump Administration submits a 48-hour report consistent with the War Powers Resolution regarding the introduction of U.S. armed forces into hostilities or imminent hostilities against Iran between the date of market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The market will resolve based on the listed date of the report. This market may stay open until 10 days after the listed date (ET) to allow for a qualifying report to be published.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be the White House, the Congressional Record, and the NYU Law War Powers Resolution Reporting Project; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Congress introduce a War Powers Resolution targeting military action against Iran between February 13, 2026, and February 28, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early 2026, President Donald Trump has made repeated threats of military action against Iran, citing support for Iranian protesters and regime change objectives. These threats have sparked bipartisan concern in Congress over executive overreach and the constitutional authority to declare war. On February 10, 2026, advocacy groups like People's World urged immediate congressional action to co-sponsor and pass the Kaine-Paul Iran War Powers Resolution, reflecting growing momentum for legislative checks on presidential military power (People's World, 2026). This follows a pattern in January 2026, where Congress introduced multiple War Powers Resolutions targeting U.S. military actions in Venezuela, with significant Republican defections and narrow vote margins (e.g., 50-50 Senate tie, 215-215 House tie). These efforts were described by Sen. Tim Kaine as exposing a 'vulnerability' in the Trump administration, prompting Democrats to plan a 'war powers blitz' on six countries, including Iran (Washington Examiner, 2026). The introduction of such a resolution would signal heightened congressional scrutiny and could precede or coincide with military escalation, making it a strong leading indicator of potential War Powers reporting under the 1973 Resolution.

Sources:
- People's World: https://www.peoplesworld.org/article/rapid-response-no-war-with-iran/
- Washington Examiner: https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/foreign/democrats-ready-war-powers-blitz-to-exploit-a-trump-vulnerability
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a War Powers Resolution specifically targeting U.S. military action against Iran is formally introduced in either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate between 2026-02-13 and 2026-02-28 (inclusive).

A 'War Powers Resolution' is defined as a joint resolution or concurrent resolution introduced under the War Powers Resolution of 1973 (50 U.S.C. 1541 et seq.), whose text explicitly directs the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities or imminent hostilities with Iran, or to prohibit such forces from being introduced into hostilities without congressional authorization.

Resolution will be determined by official congressional records: the Congressional Record, Congress.gov, or the Library of Congress's Thomas system. A resolution must be assigned a formal designation (e.g., S.J.Res.___, H.Con.Res.___) and appear in the official legislative database by the end date.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any country not already a part of the Abraham Accords formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a senior Israeli or U.S. government official publicly state between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that formal negotiations toward a new Abraham Accords normalization agreement are underway with at least one country not currently part of the Accords?
subquestions.background_information:
The Abraham Accords, initiated in 2020, normalized diplomatic relations between Israel and several Arab states—UAE, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—with U.S. mediation. Since then, expansion has stalled, particularly with Saudi Arabia, due to Israel's ongoing military operations in Gaza and the West Bank, as well as regional backlash following Israeli airstrikes on Qatar in September 2024. Public support for normalization has declined sharply: 81% of Saudis now oppose normalization with Israel, according to a Washington Institute poll from August 2024, up from just 19% prior to October 2023. Saudi Arabia maintains that any normalization is contingent on progress toward a Palestinian state, a condition rejected by Israel's current government. Despite this, former President Donald Trump claimed on October 17, 2025, that he expects the Accords to expand soon, citing hopes for Saudi Arabia's inclusion. However, no formal negotiations have been publicly announced as of October 31, 2025. Given the political sensitivity, public confirmation of active negotiations by a senior official—Israeli, U.S., or from a prospective country—would signal a significant shift and serve as a leading indicator of potential future normalization. Such statements have historically preceded formal signings, as seen with the UAE and Bahrain in 2020.

Sources:
- Washington Institute poll on Saudi public opinion: https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/policy-analysis/saudi-public-opinion-after-18-months-war-gaza
- Al Jazeera report on Trump’s October 17, 2025 statement: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon
- Background on Abraham Accords and expansion challenges: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/what-are-abraham-accords-2025-09-15/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

A 'senior official' is defined as:
- A head of state or government,
- A foreign minister or defense minister,
- A national security advisor,
- A U.S. Secretary of State or Secretary of Defense,
- Or their official spokespersons acting in an official capacity.

'Formal negotiations' means structured diplomatic discussions aimed at concluding a bilateral normalization agreement, as opposed to exploratory talks or general expressions of interest.

The statement must be:
- Made in an official capacity (e.g., press conference, government press release, official social media account, or verified interview),
- Clearly refer to ongoing negotiations (e.g., 'we are in talks,' 'negotiations have begun,' 'discussions are advancing toward an agreement'),
- And be attributed to one or more specific countries not currently in the Accords.

Resolution will be based on credible, publicly available reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, Al Jazeera, The New York Times) or official government statements. If no such statement is made during the resolution window, the question resolves No.

If the event is postponed or retracted before the end date, it does not count. If the source material becomes unavailable, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Wayback Machine (https://archive.org/web/) or equivalent.

Primary sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/
- U.S. Department of State: https://www.state.gov/
- Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry-of-foreign-affairs

Given the current political sensitivities and low public support in potential joining countries—especially Saudi Arabia—any official acknowledgment of active talks would signal a significant breakthrough. This subquestion captures momentum toward normalization without requiring the full event (a signing), making it an informative early signal for forecasters assessing the likelihood of a new country joining by the end of 2025. It avoids restating the ultimate question by focusing on a distinct, observable precursor event with high information value.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Standard & Poor's, Moody's, or Fitch; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the yield on France's 10-year government bond exceed 3.75% at any point between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13?
subquestions.background_information:
The yield on France's 10-year government bond is a key indicator of market confidence in the country's fiscal health and creditworthiness. After Fitch downgraded France's sovereign credit rating from 'AA-' to 'A+' on September 12, 2025, citing political instability and rising public debt, the 10-year yield rose to 3.47%—a level close to Italy’s, which is traditionally seen as a higher-risk eurozone borrower (AFP, 2025). Historically, rising bond yields reflect increased risk premiums demanded by investors, often preceding or accompanying credit rating downgrades. A further rise toward or above 3.75% would signal deepening market concern and could increase pressure on other rating agencies like S&P or Moody’s to follow with their own downgrades in upcoming reviews scheduled for November and October respectively. The French government faces a 5.8% GDP deficit and debt at 113% of GDP, well above EU limits, and political fragmentation may hinder credible fiscal consolidation (Reuters, 2025). Elevated yields in this window would suggest that markets anticipate further deterioration, increasing the likelihood of another downgrade before the end of 2025.

Sources:
- AFP: France downgraded by Fitch, yield rises – https://www.afp.com/en/news/345/france-downgraded-fitch-yield-rises-september-2025
- Reuters: France faces sovereign rating test amid political chaos – https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-2025-09-05/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

- or, as a fallback, the European Central Bank’s daily yield data: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/financial_markets_and_interest_rates/euro_area_yield_curves/html/index.en.html

If both sources are unavailable or report conflicting data, a consensus of at least two reputable financial news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Financial Times, Bloomberg News) reporting the breach will be used. If the event is postponed or data is not published due to extraordinary market closure (e.g., systemic crisis), the question will resolve based on the latest available data. If no data is available by 2025-10-15, the question resolves No.

Such a move would reflect market expectations of further fiscal deterioration or political instability, increasing the likelihood that S&P or Moody’s may downgrade France before December 31, 2025. Since rating agencies monitor market signals closely, sustained yield pressure serves as a leading indicator of potential future downgrades. description:

subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump has publicly expressed interest in meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un again, stating he 'hopes to meet' and maintains a 'very good relationship' with him (Xinhua, 2025). However, North Korea has shown no active diplomatic engagement with the U.S. or South Korea as of late August, with South Korea's National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac describing Pyongyang's stance as 'very passive and negative' (The Korea Herald, 2025). Despite Trump’s past summits with Kim in 2018–2019, there has been no official indication of concrete plans for a 2025 meeting. Given Trump’s tendency to announce major diplomatic intentions via social media—particularly Truth Social—public confirmation on this platform or through official channels would be a strong leading indicator of a potential visit to North Korea. As of September 2025, prediction markets for other foreign visits (e.g., China) show that market participants react strongly to verbal commitments or advance team movements (Decrypt, 2025). Therefore, a public confirmation of intent to meet Kim would significantly increase the likelihood of a visit occurring by year-end.
