question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla release a software update labeled 'FSD V14' or equivalent that is described as enabling unsupervised driving on public roads between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla has repeatedly claimed progress toward unsupervised full self-driving (FSD), but as of late August 2025, all public deployments still require human supervision. The current FSD system is classified as Level 2 automation, meaning drivers must remain attentive and ready to take over at any time. Elon Musk has publicly stated that the next major FSD update, potentially called 'FSD V14', could roll out as early as September 2025 and might be 'two to three times safer than human drivers'. This update is expected to include a 10x increase in neural network parameters, improved handling of edge cases, and better performance in complex urban environments. Musk has previously tied such updates to the possibility of removing the need for driver supervision. However, past announcements have not led to meaningful improvements—e.g., in some evaluations, FSD's miles between disengagements remained around 900, far below the threshold needed for safe unsupervised operation. A public software release labeled as enabling unsupervised driving—even if not yet broadly deployed—would signal a critical shift in Tesla’s technical or regulatory posture. Such a move would likely precede or accompany any broader rollout of unsupervised FSD by June 2026.

Sources:
- Electrek: Tesla launches FSD (Supervised) in Australia and New Zealand (https://electrek.co/2025/08/28/tesla-fsd-supervised-australia-new-zealand/)
- Digital Trends: Tesla FSD trip from SF to LA (https://www.digitaltrends.com/cars/tesla-fsd-sf-to-la-video/)
- Lifeboat Foundation: Elon Announces MOST Powerful FSD Update Ever (https://lifeboat.com/ex/elon.announces.most.powerful.fsd.update.ever)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, Tesla (via official channels such as a software release note, CEO statement, investor presentation, or press release) releases a software update labeled 'FSD V14' or equivalent (e.g., 'FSD 14.0', 'Next-Gen FSD', or any name implying a major version upgrade) and explicitly describes it as enabling unsupervised driving on public roads—i.e., operation without the need for a human driver to monitor or intervene. The description must include language indicating that no active supervision is required (e.g., 'no driver needed', 'fully autonomous', 'no human oversight required').

Resolution sources:
- Tesla official software release notes (https://www.tesla.com/support/software-updates)
- Tesla CEO Elon Musk’s verified X (formerly Twitter) account (https://twitter.com/elonmusk)
- Official Tesla blog (https://www.tesla.com/blog)
- Major reputable tech or automotive news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, Electrek, The Verge) reporting on such a release with direct quotes or documentation.

If the update is announced but released outside the resolution window, or if the update is released without claims of enabling unsupervised driving, the question resolves No. If Tesla releases a version labeled 'FSD V14' but describes it only as improving supervised driving (e.g., 'better lane keeping' or 'improved navigation'), the question resolves No. In case of conflicting reports, resolution will be based on a preponderance of credible evidence from the sources listed above.
subquestions.rationale: A software update labeled as enabling unsupervised driving—even if not yet deployed at scale—would be a strong leading indicator that Tesla believes it has achieved a technical or regulatory breakthrough necessary for the ultimate outcome. Given that all current FSD deployments require supervision, such a public declaration would represent a material shift in Tesla’s position and increase the likelihood that unsupervised FSD could be broadly released by June 2026. This subquestion avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on a specific, near-term technical milestone (a named software release with specific claims) rather than full deployment. It is also informative because forecasters who expect unsupervised FSD by mid-2026 should assign a higher probability to such an update occurring in late 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, Tesla must (1) release a software update labeled 'FSD V14' or equivalent, AND (2) explicitly describe it as enabling unsupervised driving on public roads with language like 'no driver needed,' 'fully autonomous,' or 'no human oversight required.' Observable evidence: Official Tesla release notes, Musk statements, Tesla blog, or major outlets confirming both release and unsupervised driving claim within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Tesla FSD V14 software update release 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) — to find V14 release events; 2) 'Tesla Full Self-Driving unsupervised autonomous public roads September 2025' — to find unsupervised claims; 3) 'Tesla FSD V14 release date official unsupervised autonomous' — to find criteria match; 4) 'Tesla FSD 14.0 release testers wide rollout September October 2025' — to find earliest release date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Notebookcheck (Sept 25): 'Tesla is set to release FSD Version 14.0 in a wide rollout next week' — this is a future announcement, not a release within the window. (B) Autoevolution (Sept 26): 'The new build will first be released to early testers—primarily Tesla employees—next week [early Oct], regular customers by mid-November' — no release within window. (C) Investor's Business Daily (Oct 4): FSD V14 release 'coming Monday' (Oct 6) due to last-minute bug — outside the window. (D) Teslarati/Next Big Future (Oct 7): FSD V14.1 actually rolled out Oct 6-7, 2025 — outside window. (E) ABCmoney (Sept 5) claiming 'Level 4 autonomy milestone' — single low-credibility source contradicted by all major outlets. All events either fall outside the window or do not meet the unsupervised criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No source confirms FSD V14 was released within Sept 1-Oct 1, 2025 with unsupervised driving claims. [Autoevolution (Sept 26)](https://www.autoevolution.com/news/fsd-v14-should-get-to-early-testers-in-days-regular-customers-will-get-it-much-later-258168.html) confirms release to early testers was still 'next week' from Sept 26, meaning early October. [Notebookcheck (Sept 25)](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Tesla-FSD-V14-wide-release-as-Elon-Musk-says-update-will-feel-Sentient-by-V14-2.1124357.0.html) says wide rollout is 'next week.' Even when released, V14.1 is explicitly described as still requiring supervision — not unsupervised. The [Forbes (Oct 1)](https://www.forbes.com/sites/bernardmarr/2025/10/01/is-autonomous-driving-ever-going-to-happen/) article confirms no company has received full public road permits in the U.S. and Tesla's FSD 'still requires a vigilant human driver.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: FSD V14 was not released within the Sept 1-Oct 1, 2025 window. The earliest confirmed release timestamp is October 6-7, 2025, per multiple sources. No timestamp within the resolution window confirms V14 release.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (FSD V14 release with unsupervised driving claims) exists within the September 1-October 1, 2025 window. The release occurred after the window closed.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: ABCmoney.co.uk (Sept 5) claims 'Level 4 autonomy milestone' — but this is contradicted by Electrek (Sept 5, higher credibility) which reports Tesla 'abandoning' full autonomy promise; Forbes (Oct 1); VICE (Sept 25); Yahoo (Sept 30); NBC News (Sept 16); IBD (Oct 4) all confirming FSD remains supervised. The ABCmoney article is not from a major reputable outlet and appears unreliable. The resolution criteria specifically require 'major reputable tech or automotive news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, Electrek, The Verge).' evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. FSD V14 was not released within the September 1-October 1, 2025 window — it was released to early testers on October 6-7, 2025, outside the window. Furthermore, even when released, it was explicitly labeled 'FSD (Supervised)' and did not claim to enable unsupervised driving on public roads. Both required criteria (release within window AND unsupervised driving description) fail. The window closed on October 1, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirm in an official statement or press briefing between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that the Trump administration is negotiating a formal security guarantee with Ukraine that includes binding military defense obligations equivalent to NATO Article 5?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Andrii Yermak, head of Ukrainian President Zelenskyy’s office, to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, with a draft framework expected to be finalized soon (Українська правда, 2025-08-22). The military component of these talks includes intelligence sharing, weapons supply, and training, but the critical 'backstop mechanism'—a U.S. commitment to respond militarily if Ukraine is attacked—remains unformalized. European allies have conditioned their own security commitments on U.S. backing, calling for 'guaranteed guarantees' (Європейська правда, 2025-08-22). Despite 26 countries reportedly committing to a postwar reassurance force (Foreign Policy, 2025-09-04), the U.S. has not committed to a binding defense obligation, with President Trump ruling out ground troop deployment but leaving open the possibility of air support. The absence of a U.S. commitment has stalled broader agreements. Given this context, a public confirmation by Secretary Rubio that the U.S. is actively negotiating a formal, binding defense guarantee would signal a significant shift in U.S. policy and serve as a strong leading indicator of a final agreement by the end of 2025.

Sources:
- Українська правда: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/2025/08/22/7523456/
- Європейська правда: https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/2025/08/22/7523457/
- Foreign Policy: https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/09/04/ukraine-security-guarantees-troop-deployment-macron/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio issues an official statement, press briefing, or interview in which he confirms that the Trump administration is negotiating a formal security guarantee with Ukraine that includes binding military defense obligations equivalent in character to NATO Article 5—specifically, a commitment to respond militarily if Ukraine is attacked. The statement must be made in an official capacity and published by a credible news outlet or on the U.S. Department of State website. A qualifying statement must go beyond general expressions of support or references to existing cooperation (e.g., the June 2024 bilateral agreement) and must explicitly refer to negotiations on a new, binding defense commitment. If no such statement is made during the resolution window, the question resolves No.

Resolution sources:
- U.S. Department of State official website: https://www.state.gov/
- Major news outlets such as Reuters, Associated Press, The New York Times, or BBC: https://www.reuters.com/, https://www.apnews.com/, https://www.nytimes.com/, https://www.bbc.com/news

If the primary source becomes unavailable, secondary confirmation from two or more reputable news organizations reporting the same statement will suffice. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves based on whether the statement was made within the specified dates.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a high-value indicator because Secretary Rubio, as the top U.S. diplomat, is directly involved in negotiations with Ukraine and European allies. His public confirmation of ongoing talks about a binding defense guarantee would signal that the Trump administration has moved beyond exploratory discussions and is actively pursuing a formal commitment—strong evidence that a final agreement may be reached by the end of 2025. Given that previous statements have stopped short of confirming such negotiations, a clear affirmation would represent a material shift in U.S. policy and increase the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving 'Yes'.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Secretary of State Marco Rubio must issue an official statement/briefing confirming the Trump administration is negotiating a FORMAL security guarantee for Ukraine with BINDING military defense obligations EQUIVALENT to NATO Article 5 — specifically a commitment to respond militarily if Ukraine is attacked. The statement must be made in official capacity, published by credible outlets or State.gov, and go beyond general support or existing cooperation, explicitly referring to negotiations on a NEW, BINDING defense commitment. Window: 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Marco Rubio Ukraine security guarantee NATO Article 5 binding military defense' (Oct 31-Nov 30, 2025) — to find direct statements; 2) 'Rubio Ukraine formal security commitment negotiations 2025' — to find official announcements; 3) 'Rubio Ukraine Article 5 equivalent binding military commitment official statement' — to find press briefings with specific language; 4) 'State Department Ukraine security guarantee binding defense obligation November 2025' — to find official State Dept statements; 5) 'Rubio Ukraine peace plan security guarantee vague not binding November 2025' — to find contradicting evidence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Rubio defended the 28-point peace plan as a 'strong framework' (Nov 21-23, 2025). (B) Rubio attended Geneva talks and issued joint U.S.-Ukraine statement on 'updated and refined peace framework' (Nov 23-24, 2025). (C) The 28-point plan includes a security framework 'modeled on' NATO Article 5, but sources explicitly note it does NOT obligate U.S. military response. (D) Rubio at press briefing declined to disclose details, noted 'no agreement yet.' (E) Rubio told EU officials security guarantees should come AFTER a peace deal is signed (RT/Politico, Nov 27). Rejected: None of these events constitute Rubio explicitly confirming negotiations on 'binding military defense obligations equivalent to NATO Article 5.' The security framework in the plan explicitly allows the U.S. president to 'determine' a response — not obligate one — which analysts and the NY Post explicitly describe as falling short of Article 5.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match found. Key evidence: [NY Post](https://nypost.com/2025/11/21/world-news/trumps-nato-style-security-deal-offered-to-ukraine-amounts-to-less-than-a-guarantee/): 'The proposal does not obligate the U.S. to act, meaning intervention is not guaranteed.' [Philadelphia Inquirer](https://www.inquirer.com/opinion/ukraine-peace-deal-putin-war-trump-20251126.html): The plan offers 'only vague security assurances modeled on NATO Article 5—without binding commitments.' [CSIS](https://www.csis.org/analysis/unfinished-plan-peace-ukraine-provision-provision): The plan contains 'weaker security guarantees.' [CBS News/Ukrainian Ambassador](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/olga-stefanishyna-ukrainian-ambassador-us-face-the-nation-transcript-11-23-2025/): The separate security document is described as 'similar in spirit to Article 5' but 'not a formal treaty.' Rubio's actual statements reference 'durable and enforceable peace,' 'security guarantees,' and progress in negotiations — but never explicitly confirm negotiations on 'binding military defense obligations EQUIVALENT to NATO Article 5.' The resolution criteria requires going beyond general expressions and explicitly referring to NEW, BINDING defense commitments equivalent to Article 5. Rubio never said this.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. Rubio's most specific statements during the window (Nov 21-27, 2025) describe a 'strong framework' and progress in negotiations, but do not include explicit confirmation of binding Article 5-equivalent military obligations.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found, because no qualifying occurrence exists at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly supports No resolution: (1) The U.S. peace plan explicitly falls SHORT of Article 5 — the U.S. president 'determines' response rather than being obligated. (2) Ukraine and its allies are SEEKING Article 5-equivalent guarantees, indicating the U.S. has NOT committed to them. (3) Rubio told EU officials security guarantees come AFTER a deal, separate from the current framework. (4) Multiple analysts and reports from Reuters, AP, NY Post, CSIS, Philadelphia Inquirer all confirm the proposed guarantees are NOT binding in the Article 5 sense. (5) Rubio himself declined to disclose details at the Nov 24 Geneva press briefing. (6) Reports note Rubio was 'excluded from the process' at key stages. No contradictory evidence points toward Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. Throughout the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window, Secretary Rubio made numerous statements about Ukraine peace negotiations, security guarantees, and a 'strong framework.' However, no statement by Rubio explicitly confirmed that the Trump administration was negotiating a formal security guarantee with Ukraine that includes BINDING military defense obligations EQUIVALENT to NATO Article 5 (i.e., a commitment to respond militarily if Ukraine is attacked). Multiple high-quality sources explicitly confirm the opposite: the proposed security guarantee explicitly falls short of Article 5, is non-binding, and does not obligate U.S. military action. Ukraine was still SEEKING such guarantees, indicating they had not been agreed to. The question resolves No, with the window closing on November 30, 2025 as no definitively earlier foreclosing event was identified.

question: Isar Aerospace successful orbital launch in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any launch attempt of the Spectrum rocket, developed by Isar Aerospace, results in a payload reaching a stable Earth orbit by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

"Reaching stable orbit" is defined as the successful insertion of a payload into a sustained low Earth orbit (LEO) or higher, where the payload completes at least one full revolution around Earth.

subquestions.question: Will Isar Aerospace publicly announce a confirmed launch date for a Spectrum rocket mission between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?

Isar Aerospace has been developing the Spectrum rocket as part of its mission to provide independent European access to space. The company conducted its first launch attempt in March 2025 from Norway's Andøya Spaceport, which ended in a failure seconds after liftoff. However, the company described the test as valuable for gathering data and has stated that vehicles 2 and 3 are already in production. In September 2025, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the European Commission confirmed two missions scheduled to fly on Isar Aerospace's Spectrum launcher under the Flight Ticket Initiative, including a debris removal demonstration by Infinite Orbits and a cubesat integration mission by ISISPACE. These missions indicate existing customer payloads are ready for launch, but no official launch date has been announced as of October 31, 2025. Publicly confirming a launch date would signal that the company has completed key pre-launch milestones, including vehicle integration, range availability, and regulatory approvals—critical steps toward achieving orbital flight by the end of 2025. A confirmed launch date increases the likelihood of an actual launch attempt occurring within the remaining window of the ultimate question.

Without such an announcement, logistical and regulatory constraints make a launch before year-end increasingly unlikely. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question but captures a critical intermediate milestone—public commitment to a launch schedule—that reflects internal readiness and coordination with launch infrastructure and customers.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q4 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index be above 105.0 in the January 2026 release?
subquestions.background_information:
Consumer confidence is a leading indicator of economic activity and spending behavior, which directly influences GDP growth. The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index measures how optimistic consumers are about the economy, based on their assessment of current business and labor market conditions, as well as their short-term expectations. As of November 2025, the index stood at 100.2, down from 104.0 in January 2025, reflecting ongoing concerns about inflation, tariffs, and labor market softness. The December 2025 reading is expected to be released in early January 2026. Sustained consumer confidence above 105 typically correlates with robust consumer spending, a key driver of GDP. Given that consumer spending accounted for much of the 4.3% GDP growth in Q3 2025, continued strength in confidence could signal resilience heading into Q4. Conversely, a reading below 105 may indicate weakening demand, potentially dragging Q4 GDP below the 2.0%–2.5% target range.

Sources:
- Conference Board Consumer Confidence Press Release, November 2025: https://www.conference-board.org/data/consumerconfidence.cfm
- Analysis of consumer spending and GDP drivers in Q3 2025: https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-third-quarter-2025-advance-estimate
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index, as reported in the January 2026 release, is above 105.0. The index must be published by The Conference Board between 2025-12-29 and 2026-01-28. The release is typically issued on the last Tuesday of each month; the January 2026 release is expected around January 27, 2026. Resolution will be based solely on the headline index value (not components or revisions) from the official report available at: https://www.conference-board.org/data/consumerconfidence.cfm. If the report is not published by 2026-01-28 due to unforeseen circumstances (e.g., government disruption), the question will resolve as 'No.' This question resolves based on data released between 2025-12-29 and 2026-01-28.
subquestions.rationale: Consumer confidence is a leading indicator of household spending, which accounts for about 70% of U.S. GDP. The ultimate question hinges on whether Q4 2025 GDP growth falls within a narrow 2.0%–2.5% range. Given the strong 4.3% growth in Q3 was largely driven by consumer spending, a rebound in confidence above 105 in January 2026 would suggest sustained consumer momentum into Q4, increasing the likelihood of growth in the target range. Conversely, persistently low confidence would signal weakening demand, making it less likely that Q4 growth remains in that band. This subquestion provides early insight into consumer behavior before the Q4 GDP advance estimate is released on January 29, 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (headline value) must be ABOVE 105.0, published between 2025-12-29 and 2026-01-28. Observable evidence required: the official headline index number from the January 2026 Conference Board release. Key threshold: >105.0.

question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if police officers, security forces, or military personnel belonging to neither Israel nor a Palestinian entity begin an officially acknowledged police, military, peacekeeping, and/or security operation on the ground within Gaza by December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The foreign personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify. 

Entering Israeli controlled buffer zones will not qualify.  

Egyptian or other forces operating solely along the Egyptian/Gaza border will not qualify regardless of if they cross the border. 

Foreign personnel carrying out individual special operations, diplomatic missions, or solely humanitarian operations will not qualify.

Qualifying deployments must involve active-duty personnel of at least one foreign state or international institution (e.g., the UN or multinational missions) who are officially sent to Gaza for an operational role (e.g., peacekeeping, convoy escort, detention, logistical support). To qualify, the deployment must occur within the specified timeframe; mere announcements will not suffice.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a UN Security Council resolution authorizing a multinational International Stabilization Force (ISF) for Gaza be adopted between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15?
subquestions.background_information:
The prospect of foreign intervention in Gaza hinges significantly on the establishment of a legal and internationally recognized framework for deployment. Recent developments indicate that a multinational International Stabilization Force (ISF) could be deployed to Gaza as part of the second phase of the Trump-backed ceasefire plan. On October 14, 2025, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul confirmed that initial talks are underway with Russia and China to secure their support for a UN Security Council resolution that would authorize such a force. The resolution is seen as essential for legitimizing the deployment of foreign security forces in Gaza, as without it, any intervention would lack international legal standing. Egypt has signaled conditional support for such a force, provided it operates under a UN mandate with a clear political framework. The UN Security Council previously adopted Resolution 2735 on June 14, 2024, calling for an immediate ceasefire, but it did not authorize a peacekeeping or stabilization force. The current push seeks to go beyond that by establishing enforcement or monitoring mechanisms under Chapter VI or VII of the UN Charter. Adoption of such a resolution would require at least nine affirmative votes and no veto from any of the five permanent members (US, UK, France, Russia, China). Given recent diplomatic outreach to Russia and China, and the US's active role in brokering the ceasefire, the timing of such a resolution is now considered plausible within the next month. As of October 15, 2025, no such resolution has been formally tabled or adopted.

Sources:
- Anadolu Ajansı: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3357265
- Middle East Monitor: https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250826-joint-forces-to-govern-gaza-mission-and-repercussions/
- UN Security Council Resolution 2735: https://undocs.org/S/RES/2735(2024)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a resolution is formally adopted by the United Nations Security Council between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive) that explicitly authorizes the deployment of a multinational International Stabilization Force (ISF) or equivalent foreign security, peacekeeping, or monitoring force with operational presence in the Gaza Strip. The resolution must be legally binding and passed with at least nine affirmative votes and no veto from any of the five permanent members (US, UK, France, Russia, China). The force must be mandated to operate within the terrestrial territory of Gaza for purposes such as ceasefire monitoring, security, disarmament, or stabilization. The resolution must be published in the official UN documents system (https://undocs.org) and reported by major news outlets such as Reuters, AP, or BBC. If no such resolution is adopted by the end date, the question resolves No. In the event the UN Security Council adjourns or delays consideration of such a resolution beyond the end date, the question still resolves based on whether adoption occurred within the specified window. If the resolution is adopted but later repealed or suspended, it still counts as a Yes if adopted within the timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: The adoption of a UN Security Council resolution authorizing a multinational force is a critical prerequisite for any large-scale, officially acknowledged foreign intervention in Gaza. While the ultimate question concerns physical deployment of foreign forces by the end of 2025, this subquestion tracks a key political and legal milestone that must precede such deployment. If the resolution fails—especially due to a veto by Russia or China—it would significantly reduce the likelihood of foreign intervention, as it would remove the primary legal pathway for international forces to enter Gaza. Conversely, adoption would signal strong multilateral consensus and dramatically increase the probability of actual deployment. Thus, this subquestion serves as a high-value informational crux: forecasters who update on its outcome would meaningfully shift their probability estimates for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: UNSC formally adopts a resolution between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive) explicitly authorizing deployment of a multinational ISF or equivalent force with operational presence in Gaza. Must have ≥9 affirmative votes and no veto from P5 (US, UK, France, Russia, China). Must be legally binding. Observable evidence: Official UN document, major news outlet reporting, vote count and date.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'UN Security Council resolution Gaza International Stabilization Force ISF 2025' (Oct-Nov 2025) — to find adoption. 2) 'UNSC vote Gaza peacekeeping force resolution October November 2025' — general search. 3) 'UN Security Council Resolution 2803 Gaza adopted vote November 17 2025' — specific resolution search. 4) 'UN Security Council Gaza ISF resolution vote adopted November 2025' — to confirm vote date. 5) 'UN Security Council Gaza resolution vote November 15 2025' — to check if vote occurred on the deadline date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: UN Security Council Resolution 2803, adopting a US-drafted resolution authorizing an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza. Multiple credible sources confirm this resolution was adopted with 13 votes in favor, Russia and China abstaining (no veto). The key disputed question is the exact date: some AFP early reports from November 15 referred to 'Monday, November 15' as the vote date, but November 15, 2025 was a Saturday, not a Monday. The actual Monday after November 15 was November 17, 2025. All subsequent, confirmed reporting from the actual vote day (AFP, CNA, France Diplomatie, The Express Tribune, Tempo.co, Anadolu Agency, RT, 5pillarsuk, etc.) confirms the adoption date as November 17, 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution 2803 satisfies all substantive criteria: (1) explicitly authorizes deployment of a 'temporary International Stabilization Force (ISF)' in Gaza; (2) passed with 13 affirmative votes and no veto (Russia and China abstained); (3) legally binding with Chapter VII-equivalent authority ('all necessary measures'); (4) mandated to operate within Gaza for purposes of security, disarmament, and stabilization. Sources: [AFP adoption report](http://doc.afp.com/84BQ7G4), [France Diplomatie](https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/french-foreign-policy/france-and-the-united-nations/news-and-events/news/article/united-nations-adoption-of-security-council-resolution-2803-on-the-gaza-peace), [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/trump-gaza-plan-un-security-council-vote-nov-17-5469426), [5pillarsuk](https://5pillarsuk.com/2025/11/18/un-security-council-adopts-resolution-backing-trumps-gaza-international-stabilisation-force/). HOWEVER, the adoption date is November 17, 2025 — which is OUTSIDE the resolution window (Oct 16 – Nov 15, 2025).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The resolution was adopted on November 17, 2025 (Monday). This is confirmed by: AFP (November 17 adoption report), France Diplomatie (November 18 confirmation of November 17 vote), Telegraph India (November 23 analysis stating 'November 17, 2025'), 5pillarsuk ('November 17, 2025'), KTVZ/CNN ('November 17, 2025'), The Express Tribune ('November 17, 2025'), Tempo.co ('November 17, 2025'). The pre-vote AFP report from November 15, 2025, stated 'set to vote on Monday' — which turned out to be November 17. The resolution window closes November 15, 2025 at 23:59:59 UTC. The vote occurred on November 17, 2025, which is after the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists within the October 16 – November 15 window. The US draft was only circulated November 6–7, formal UNSC negotiations began November 7, and the vote was not scheduled until November 17. No other ISF-related resolution was adopted in this period.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some AFP pre-vote articles from November 15, 2025, cited 'Monday, November 15' as the vote date, but November 15, 2025 was a Saturday — this is an error in those early reports. The actual vote was Monday, November 17. This is confirmed by: CNA (correctly identifying Nov 17 as Monday), The Hindu (Nov 17), and all post-vote reporting (from Nov 17-18 onward) confirming adoption on Nov 17. No credible source reports a vote occurring on or before November 15, 2025. The question window definitively closes before the adoption of Resolution 2803.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution 2803 was adopted on November 17, 2025, which is 2 days AFTER the resolution window closed on November 15, 2025. As of November 15, 2025 (the end of the window), no qualifying UNSC resolution had been adopted. The vote was scheduled but had not yet occurred. The condition for Yes was not met within the window. Resolution: No. The window closed at 2025-11-15T23:59:59Z without any qualifying resolution having been adopted.

question: U.S. recognizes Russian sovereignty over Crimea in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. government formally recognizes Russian sovereignty over the majority of the Crimean peninsula by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Donald Trump's March 25, 2019, recognition of Israel's sovereignty over the Golan Heights is an example of a qualifying action. 

Statement of intents, or announcements of planned recognition will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Secretary of State make a public statement indicating openness to recognizing Russian sovereignty over Crimea between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. has consistently opposed the recognition of territorial changes achieved by force, including Russia’s 2014 annexation of Crimea. Since then, successive U.S. administrations have reaffirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity through statements, sanctions, and diplomatic actions. However, recent developments under the Trump administration have raised questions about a potential shift in policy. In August 2025, a Russian expert claimed that President Trump’s statement that Crimea 'cannot be returned to Ukraine' amounted to a 'de facto' recognition of Russian sovereignty (TASS, 2025). Former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo criticized any potential recognition as a 'mistake of epic proportions' and warned it would undermine U.S. credibility (The Hill, 2025). The U.S. has previously recognized territorial claims by allies—such as Israel’s sovereignty over the Golan Heights in 2019 and Morocco’s claim over Western Sahara in 2020—which some analysts argue sets a precedent that could be extended to Crimea if geopolitical incentives align (New Lines Magazine, 2025). A public statement by the Secretary of State indicating openness to recognizing Russian sovereignty would represent a significant departure from prior policy and could signal a shift toward formal recognition in the near term.

Current state: As of October 2025, the official U.S. position remains non-recognition of Crimea’s annexation. The State Department’s website continues to list Crimea as part of Ukraine, and no senior U.S. official has publicly endorsed recognition of Russian sovereignty.

Sources:
- New Lines Magazine: https://newlinesmag.com/opinion/putins-wouldnt-be-the-first-illegal-conquests-the-white-house-has-endorsed/
- The Hill: https://thehill.com/policy/national-security/5382897-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/
- TASS: https://tass.com/world/1823457
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the U.S. Secretary of State makes a public statement—via press conference, official transcript, social media post from an official @StateDept or @SecBlinken account, or written testimony—that explicitly indicates openness to recognizing Russian sovereignty over Crimea. Indications of openness include phrases such as 'we are considering recognition,' 'Crimea may remain part of Russia,' or 'the status quo should be accepted,' provided they suggest a willingness to depart from current U.S. policy of non-recognition.

The statement must be attributable to the Secretary of State personally and not merely reflect a hypothetical or third-party view. Vague or ambiguous remarks (e.g., 'all options are on the table') without clear indication of openness will not count.

Resolution sources:

question: Trump eliminates capital gains tax on crypto in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to eliminate capital gains tax on any cryptocurrency assets by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If capital gains is eliminated only for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration release a formal proposal or draft legislation that includes the elimination of capital gains tax on cryptocurrency assets between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-2025, the Trump administration has taken several notable steps to position the U.S. as a global leader in cryptocurrency policy. President Trump signed the GENIUS Act into law on July 18, 2025, establishing a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins and signaling strong support for digital assets (Invezz, 2025). He also issued an executive order on August 7, 2025, allowing cryptocurrencies to be included in 401(k) retirement accounts, further demonstrating administrative momentum toward crypto integration (ValueWalk, 2025). Additionally, there have been reports of legislative efforts, such as a 'Hail Mary' attempt to include a crypto tax exemption in the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (OBBB), which would provide a de minimis exemption for small crypto transactions (Decrypt, 2025). However, as of September 2025, no formal proposal to eliminate capital gains taxes on crypto—either broadly or for specific assets—has been made public. The administration’s Working Group on Digital Asset Markets, chaired by David Sacks, was tasked with delivering a regulatory framework within 180 days of its formation, a deadline that likely falls in early October 2025, making this period critical for new policy announcements (Crowdfund Insider, 2025). Given that tax legislation typically requires formal proposal before enactment, the release of such a draft would be a necessary precursor to the ultimate outcome of eliminating capital gains taxes on crypto by the end of 2025.

Sources:
- Invezz: https://www.invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

In the event that a proposal is announced but later retracted or clarified as non-binding without formal release, it still counts toward a Yes resolution if it was publicly disseminated in official channels. If the primary sources become unavailable, secondary authoritative reporting from at least two major news organizations will be used.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla announce the removal of human safety monitors from its Robotaxi pilot program in either Austin or San Francisco between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late June and July 2025, Tesla launched limited Robotaxi pilot programs in Austin, Texas, and planned a rollout in San Francisco, California. However, both programs involve human 'safety monitors'—either in the passenger seat or acting as drivers—contrary to Elon Musk's earlier promises of fully driverless operation. In Austin, Tesla deployed 10–20 Model Y vehicles with safety monitors in the front passenger seat, operating within a geofenced area and under strict conditions such as good weather and daytime hours (CNA, 2025). Similarly, in San Francisco, Tesla has not obtained permits for fully autonomous operation and instead uses human drivers with supervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, limiting service to select participants (Business Insider, 2025; Planetizen, 2025). Regulatory bodies like the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) have explicitly stated Tesla lacks authorization for autonomous operation, even with safety drivers. Texas law now requires permits for driverless operation, effective September 1, 2025, adding regulatory pressure (CNA, 2025). The presence of human monitors is a key barrier to meeting the definition of a 'driverless' service in the ultimate question. Therefore, any public announcement from Tesla indicating the removal of these human monitors—especially in the context of regulatory approval—would be a strong leading indicator that Tesla is moving toward true driverless operation before the end of 2025.

Sources:
- CNA: Tesla's robotaxi trial in Austin amid new Texas rules - https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/texas-tesla-robotaxi-autonomous-vehicle-law-5168521
- Business Insider: Tesla's robotaxi service in California uses safety drivers - https://www.businessinsider.com/tesla-robotaxi-service-safety-driver-california-2025-7
- Planetizen: Tesla's robotaxi launch disputed by California regulators - https://www.planetizen.com/news/2025/07/134877-tesla-announced-human-assisted-robotaxi-launch-san-francisco-state-regulators-say-otherwise
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08, Tesla makes a public announcement—via official press release, Elon Musk post on X (formerly Twitter), or credible media report citing Tesla representatives—that it has removed or will imminently remove human safety monitors (including passenger-seat monitors or driver-seat operators) from its Robotaxi pilot program in either Austin, Texas, or San Francisco, California. The announcement must explicitly state that vehicles will operate without any human actively controlling or monitoring the vehicle under normal conditions, consistent with the definition of 'driverless' in the ultimate question. 

Resolution sources: Official Tesla communications (https://www.tesla.com/blog), Elon Musk’s X account (https://twitter.com/elonmusk), and credible news outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), The Verge (https://www.theverge.com), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com) reporting with direct attribution to Tesla. 

If no such announcement is made during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the announcement is made but later retracted or contradicted by Tesla, the resolution will be based on the initial announcement unless it is clearly rescinded within the resolution window. If Tesla claims removal of monitors but third-party verification (e.g., rider reports, video evidence) contradicts this, the question still resolves Yes if the announcement itself meets the criteria. 

If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question remains resolvable based on whether the announcement occurred within the specified dates.
subquestions.rationale: The presence of human safety monitors is currently the primary obstacle preventing Tesla’s Robotaxi service from qualifying as 'driverless' under the ultimate question’s criteria. A public announcement removing these monitors would signal that Tesla believes it has either achieved sufficient technological readiness or obtained regulatory approval to operate without human intervention—both of which are necessary conditions for a full driverless launch by the end of 2025. Given that Texas’s new autonomous vehicle law takes effect on September 1, 2025, this week represents a plausible window for Tesla to announce compliance or deployment plans. Therefore, this subquestion acts as a high-value informational crux: if Tesla announces the removal of human monitors, forecasters should significantly increase their probability on the ultimate question resolving Yes; if no such announcement occurs, it strengthens the case that a true driverless launch before year-end is unlikely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Tesla must make a public announcement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 that it has removed OR will imminently remove human safety monitors from its Robotaxi in Austin or San Francisco. (3) Tesla expanded Robotaxi service area and opened app to public — REJECTED: Irrelevant to monitor removal. No candidate events satisfy the resolution criteria.

[TESLARATI](https://www.teslarati.com/elon-musk-tesla-will-take-safety-drivers-out-robotaxi-heres-when/): Musk said 'there should be no safety driver by end of year' — future promise, not imminent removal. The resolution criteria requires that vehicles 'will operate without any human actively controlling or monitoring the vehicle under normal conditions.' This was explicitly NOT announced; the opposite occurred — monitors were maintained or repositioned.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. During September 1-8, 2025, Tesla made no announcement of removing human safety monitors from its Robotaxi program. All credible sources confirm safety monitors were present throughout the resolution window in both Austin and San Francisco/Bay Area. question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the House Rules Committee adopt a special rule allowing floor consideration of a minibus spending package that funds at least three of the remaining nine appropriations bills between January 9 and January 29, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. government faces a funding deadline of January 30, 2026, after which a lapse in appropriations could trigger another government shutdown. As of early January 2026, Congress has not passed any of the nine remaining full-year appropriations bills, relying instead on stopgap funding. A key procedural hurdle for advancing spending legislation in the House is the House Rules Committee, which must adopt a special rule to bring any minibus or omnibus spending package to the floor for a vote. On January 6, 2026, lawmakers unveiled a $174 billion bipartisan 'minibus' package funding the Departments of Commerce, Justice, Energy, Interior, and the EPA, with a House Rules Committee meeting expected on January 7 and a possible floor vote on January 9. The passage of such a rule is a critical early indicator that Congress is moving toward averting a shutdown. Recent reports suggest bipartisan progress, but hardline Republicans and Democratic holds on Senate packages could still delay momentum. The House operates with a narrow Republican majority, making internal party cohesion essential for advancing legislation. The Rules Committee's action is a leading indicator of whether Speaker Mike Johnson can maintain control of his caucus and move forward on spending bills—key to both avoiding a shutdown and maintaining Republican credibility ahead of the 2026 midterms.

subquestions.question: Will initial jobless claims in the United States average below 230,000 per week between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29?
subquestions.background_information:
Initial jobless claims are a high-frequency economic indicator that reflects the number of individuals filing for unemployment insurance for the first time. This metric is widely regarded as a timely signal of labor market health, which in turn is a key driver of consumer spending—the largest component of U.S. GDP. A rising trend in jobless claims often precedes economic slowdowns or recessions, while low and stable claims suggest labor market resilience and support for continued economic growth. As of the week ending October 25, 2025, initial jobless claims were reported at 225,000 (seasonally adjusted), consistent with a stable labor market (U.S. Department of Labor, 2025). Recent GDP data for Q2 2025 showed strong growth at 3.8% in the final estimate, rebounding from a 0.6% decline in Q1, with consumer spending and AI-driven investment contributing significantly (BEA, 2025). However, forecasters remain cautious about the sustainability of growth into late 2025 and early 2026, particularly given tariff-related headwinds and potential weakening in business investment. Monitoring labor market tightness via jobless claims during November 2025 provides an early signal of whether the economy is maintaining momentum or beginning to weaken ahead of the Q4 2025 GDP release.

Sources:
- U.S. Department of Labor – Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims: https://oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/claims.asp
- U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis – GDPNow: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the weekly seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims in the United States, as reported by the U.S. Department of Labor, average below 230,000 per week for all weeks with data released between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29 (inclusive). The relevant data will be obtained from the official Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report published by the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Unemployment Insurance (OUI). The average will be calculated using the reported values for each week where the claims data are published during the resolution window. For example, if claims are reported on November 6 (covering the week ending October 30), November 13 (week ending November 6), November 20 (week ending November 13), and November 27 (week ending November 20), those four values will be averaged. If the average is strictly less than 230,000, the question resolves Yes. If the average is 230,000 or higher, it resolves No. Data source: https://oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/claims.asp. In the event that the U.S. Department of Labor fails to publish a report during the resolution window, the most recent available data point prior to the gap will not be extrapolated; only actual published values during the window will be used. If no data are published during the window, the question will resolve as Ambiguous. Delays in data release beyond the normal schedule (e.g., due to government shutdown) that result in no reports being issued during the window will also lead to an Ambiguous resolution.
subquestions.rationale: Labor market strength is a leading indicator of consumer spending health, which accounts for about 70% of U.S. GDP. A rise in initial jobless claims above 230,000 could signal weakening labor conditions, potentially leading to reduced consumer spending and increasing the likelihood of negative GDP growth in Q4 2025. Conversely, claims remaining below this threshold suggest labor market resilience, supporting continued growth. This subquestion provides timely, high-frequency insight into economic momentum during a critical period just before the end of Q4 2025, making it a valuable crux for forecasters assessing the risk of a contraction.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the average of weekly seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims, as officially reported by the DOL and published between Oct 30-Nov 29, 2025, to be strictly below 230,000. Key complication: a government shutdown ended ~Nov 12-13, 2025, disrupting normal Thursday release schedule. The DOL backfilled data online around Nov 18-20, and the first formal press release in the window was Nov 20.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Multiple queries for 'initial jobless claims November 2025', 'backfilled data shutdown', 'week ending November 15/22 2025', specific claim numbers, DOL report dates.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Reports within window: (1) Backfilled data posted online ~Nov 18 for week ending Oct 18 = 232,000; DOL announced remaining backfilled data to post by Nov 20. (2) Nov 20 official press release: week ending Nov 15 = 220,000 (previous week Nov 8 = 228,000 revised). (3) Nov 26 official press release: week ending Nov 22 = 216,000 (previous revised 222,000). All other backfilled weeks during shutdown were not explicitly confirmed with specific seasonally-adjusted numbers, though Morningstar said 'relatively modest.'
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Data points explicitly published within window: Oct 18 week = 232,000 [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/us-initial-jobless-claims-stood-at-232-000-in-october-18-week-202511181515); Nov 8 week = 228,000 (revised, per CalculatedRisk [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/11/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims_26.html)); Nov 15 week = 220,000 [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/11/weekly-initial-unemployment-claims.html); Nov 22 week = 216,000 [NASDAQ](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/us-weekly-jobless-claims-unexpectedly-dip-seven-month-low). Even using all confirmed data: (232+228+220+216)/4 = 224,000 < 230,000. Even if additional backfilled weeks (Oct 25, Nov 1) are included at ~228,000 each: (232+228+228+228+220+216)/6 = 225,333 < 230,000.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Nov 20, 2025 (first formal press release in window); Nov 26, 2025 (second formal press release, released early due to Thanksgiving). Backfilled data posted online ~Nov 18, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence — the resolution window opens Oct 30. No formal DOL press releases issued between Oct 30 and Nov 17 due to government shutdown. The first data points within the window were backfilled data ~Nov 18.
evidence.step7_verification: Potential issue: the resolution criteria might only count formal 'Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Reports' (press releases), not backfilled online database updates. If only formal Nov 20 (220,000) and Nov 26 (216,000) press releases count: average = 218,000 < 230,000 → Yes. No scenario identified where the average exceeds or equals 230,000. The 4-week moving average reported on Nov 26 was 223,750, consistent with all underlying values being well below 230,000.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Under any reasonable interpretation of which data points fall within the resolution window, the average of initial jobless claims is well below 230,000. The highest confirmed value is 232,000 (week ending Oct 18), but all other values (228,000, 222,000, 220,000, 216,000) pull the average well below 230,000. The question resolves Yes. subquestions.background_information:
Pokrovsk is a strategically important logistics hub in Donetsk Oblast, serving as a key node for Ukrainian supply lines in the eastern theater. Russian forces have been attempting to encircle and capture the city since mid-2024, with advances in nearby settlements such as Novoekonomichnoye and near Lysovka. As of late September 2025, Russian troops were reported to be within approximately 10 kilometers of Pokrovsk’s city center (ISW, September 25, 2025 update). The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) consistently tracks Russian advances and publishes daily assessments based on geolocated evidence, including imagery and open-source intelligence. The current front line remains fluid, with incremental Russian gains in the face of strong Ukrainian resistance. Capturing the train station—located on the eastern edge of Pokrovsk—would likely require prior advances into the city’s outer defensive perimeter. Therefore, progress within 5 km of the city center would indicate a significant breakthrough and serve as a strong precursor to capturing key infrastructure such as the train station. As of September 30, 2025, no Russian advances have been confirmed within this 5 km radius of the administrative center.

Sources:
- ISW Daily Assessments: https://www.understandingwar.org/
- DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/
- Geolocation of Pokrovsk administrative center: https://maps.app.goo.gl/5XmR5jv9KjJY6vFq8
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The 5 km radius is measured using great-circle distance from that point.

Resolution will be based solely on ISW reporting. If ISW ceases publication during this period, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as a secondary source, provided it includes geolocated visual evidence of positions within the 5 km radius. If neither source is available or provides sufficient information, the question will resolve to 'No'.

Advances reported by Russian sources, Ukrainian sources, or media outlets not affiliated with ISW or DeepStateMap will not count toward resolution unless explicitly cited and corroborated by ISW. Temporary probes or reconnaissance elements without sustained control do not qualify—ISW must describe the position as held or contested by Russian forces.

If the event occurs outside the specified date range, the question resolves to 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a meaningful early indicator of Russian progress toward capturing the Pokrovsk train station. The train station lies approximately 4.5 km east of the city center, meaning that any confirmed advance within 5 km of the center would place Russian forces in close proximity to the station and suggest a breakthrough in Ukrainian defenses. Given the high intensity of fighting in the area and the logistical challenges of advancing under fire, such a development would significantly increase the likelihood of capturing key infrastructure like the train station before the ultimate question’s resolution date. Conversely, the absence of such an advance by October 21 would suggest stalled momentum and reduce the probability of a successful capture by October 24. The use of ISW as a primary source ensures objectivity and consistency with the ultimate question’s resolution logic.

The primary resolution source for whether the individual is pardoned or not will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will public statements or credible leaks indicate that Sam Bankman-Fried or his representatives have formally requested a presidential pardon from Donald Trump between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Sam Bankman-Fried, the former CEO of FTX, is currently serving a 25-year prison sentence after being convicted in 2023 on seven felony counts related to fraud and conspiracy. His appeal is scheduled for November 4, 2025, in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit. There has been growing speculation that Bankman-Fried or his family may seek a presidential pardon from President Donald Trump, who returned to office in January 2025 and has previously granted clemency to figures in the crypto space, including Ross Ulbricht and the BitMEX co-founders. According to reports, Bankman-Fried’s parents have been in discussions with individuals connected to the Trump administration about the possibility of a pardon. A formal pardon request typically involves submission through the Office of the Pardon Attorney, though presidents can also act on informal appeals. Public signals—such as statements from legal representatives, family members, or leaks to credible media—can serve as early indicators that such a request is being pursued. As of September 2025, no official confirmation of a formal pardon application has been made.

Sources:
- The Crypto Basic: https://thecryptobasic.com/2025/09/12/sam-bankman-fried-appeal-hearing-set-for-november-in-new-york/
- Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/billybambrough/2025/05/28/trump-makes-news-with-more-pardons-and-commutations/
- Decrypt: https://decrypt.co/245675/trump-pardon-crypto-founders-sbf-cz-roger-ver
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, there is a credible public statement or leak indicating that Sam Bankman-Fried or his legal representatives have formally requested a presidential pardon from Donald Trump. Credible sources include:
- Direct statements from Sam Bankman-Fried’s legal team (e.g., Mark Cohen or other attorneys of record), his family, or their official representatives;
- Reporting from at least two reputable news outlets (e.g., The New York Times, Reuters, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, Associated Press) citing government officials, legal sources, or documents;
- Official filings with the U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Pardon Attorney, if publicly accessible.

The resolution will not count speculative commentary, unsubstantiated rumors, or social media posts without named sourcing. If the event is postponed or occurs outside the resolution window, the question resolves No. In the event of ambiguity, priority will be given to primary sources and consensus reporting.

Resolution sources:
- U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Pardon Attorney: https://www.justice.gov/pardon
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
subquestions.rationale: A formal pardon request is a necessary precursor to any presidential pardon. If no such request has been made or signaled by October 31, 2025, it becomes less likely—though not impossible—that Trump will issue a pardon by the end of 2025. Given the typical processing time and political considerations, a public indication of a formal request within this window would significantly increase the likelihood that the pardon is under active consideration, thereby providing strong evidence about the trajectory of the ultimate question. This subquestion captures early actionable intent rather than outcome, making it a high-value crux for forecasters.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: SBF or his legal representatives (e.g., Mark Cohen) formally requested a presidential pardon from Trump during October 2025. Observable evidence required: direct statements from legal team/family (named), OR reporting from 2+ reputable outlets (NYT, Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, AP) citing government/legal sources or documents, OR official DOJ filings. Key constraints: must be a 'formal' request, not informal lobbying or social media posts without named sourcing.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Sam Bankman-Fried presidential pardon Trump request 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find any reporting of a formal request. Query 2: 'SBF pardon Trump formal request October 2025' — same purpose. Query 3: 'Sam Bankman-Fried Mark Cohen legal team formal pardon petition filed October 2025' — to find named legal team statements. Query 4: 'SBF pardon attorney Office Pardon Attorney DOJ filing clemency petition 2025' — to find DOJ filings. Query 5: 'Sam Bankman-Fried clemency request Trump White House confirmed formal petition October 2025' — to find official confirmation. Query 6: 'SBF parents Joseph Bankman Barbara Fried Trump pardon petition formal request' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find family-sourced formal requests.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) SBF media campaign via Tucker Carlson podcast and GETTR posts expressing desire for clemency — rejected as social media/informal (not formal legal request). (2) SBF's parents 'quietly lobbying Trump allies' — referenced in multiple sources but described as informal/exploratory, no formal request confirmed. (3) Laura Loomer's claims of 'massive well-funded lobbying effort' — explicitly described as unsubstantiated by Decrypt analysis; no formal filings in public record. (4) Cryptopolitan/Benzinga references to SBF 'petitioning Trump for clemency' — these appear to refer to social media GETTR posts, not formal legal petitions. (5) Polymarket odds spike after CZ pardon (Oct 23-24) — purely speculative market activity, not evidence of formal request. All candidates rejected for failing to meet the 'formal request' standard with required sourcing.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event meets the resolution criteria. Multiple sources explicitly state that no formal request exists: [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/344233/laura-loomer-stokes-speculation-trump-sbf-pardon) states 'no official petition or White House statement confirms progress beyond exploratory discussions'; 'no firms are registered under the Lobbying Disclosure Act for a Bankman-Fried pardon; the Justice Department's 2025 clemency list does not include him.' [CCN](https://www.ccn.com/news/crypto/sam-bankman-fried-pardon-warnings-coordinated-lobbying-effort/) states 'no official indication exists that the Trump administration is considering a pardon: the Department of Justice and White House have not commented, no clemency filings are in the public record.' No reporting from NYT, Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, or AP confirming a formal request was found. No named attorney statements confirming formal filing were found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying formal pardon request event, as no such event was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly supports No resolution: Multiple credible crypto/news outlets (Decrypt, CCN, Cointelegraph) explicitly investigated and found no formal pardon request. The Decrypt article specifically notes 'no direct contact with Trump's team has been confirmed.' The NBC News article on White House clemency process (Oct 24, 2025) does not mention SBF among those with formal requests. SBF's GETTR posts and social media activity are explicitly excluded by the resolution criteria ('social media posts without named sourcing'). Informal lobbying by parents does not meet the 'formal request' standard. No DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney filings are mentioned for SBF.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly indicates that while there was informal lobbying activity, media campaigns, and speculation about a potential SBF pardon during October 2025, no formal pardon request meeting the resolution criteria was made. Multiple credible sources explicitly investigated and found no formal filings, no White House confirmation, and no named legal team statements confirming a formal request. The resolution criteria require a formal request (from named legal representatives or backed by 2+ major outlets with named sourcing, or DOJ filings), and this standard was definitively not met during the October 2025 window. The question resolves No.

question: Will Claude 5 be released by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Anthropic's Claude 5 model is made available to the general public by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes," Claude 5 must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by Anthropic as being accessible to the general public.

Claude 5 refers to a product explicitly named Claude 5 (e.g. Claude 5.0 would count), or one that is recognized as a successor to Claude 4, similar to the progression from Claude 2 to Claude 3. Products labeled as Claude 4.5 or similar will not count for this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Anthropic, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Anthropic publish a blog post or official statement between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 indicating active development or upcoming release of a new flagship model beyond Claude Sonnet 4.5 (e.g., references to 'Claude 5', 'next-generation model', or 'successor to Claude 4')?
subquestions.background_information:
As of September 29–30, 2025, Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 4.5, the latest iteration in its model lineup, positioning it as the 'best coding model in the world' with significant improvements in autonomous operation (up to 30 hours), benchmark performance (61.4% on SWE-bench Verified and OSWorld), and alignment (reduced sycophancy, deception, and power-seeking behaviors) [1]. The release followed closely after Claude Opus 4.1, indicating a rapid development cycle. Despite these updates, there has been no official mention of a 'Claude 5' or any successor model beyond the 4.x series. However, given the competitive AI landscape—especially with OpenAI’s GPT-5 reportedly outperforming Claude on some benchmarks—Anthropic may be under pressure to signal progress toward a next-generation model to maintain developer and enterprise interest [5]. Historically, Anthropic has used blog posts and official statements to preview or confirm major model developments, such as the launch of Sonnet 4.5 [6]. Therefore, any public communication between October 1 and October 31, 2025, that references development toward a model clearly positioned as a successor to the current 4.x series could serve as an early indicator that Claude 5 is in the pipeline and potentially on track for a 2025 release.

Sources:
- Analytics India Magazine: https://analyticsindiamag.com/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-touts-it-as-best-coding-model-in-the-world/
- TechRadar: https://www.techradar.com/pro/anthropic-s-claude-sonnet-4-5-is-available-now-the-best-ai-model-in-the-world-for-real-world-agents-coding-and-computer-use
- The Times of India: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-calls-it-best-coding-model-in-the-world/articleshow/124567890.cms
