- Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-45-its-130000235.html
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/29/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-its-best-ai-model-for-coding/
- Economic Times: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/internet/claude-sonnet-4-5-launched-by-anthropic-new-features-upgrades-free-access-and-more/articleshow/124567891.cms
- Free Press Journal: https://www.freepressjournal.in/technology/claude-sonnet-4-5-launched-whats-new-with-anthropic-s-latest-ai-model
- The New Stack: https://thenewstack.io/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), Anthropic publishes a blog post, press release, or official statement on its website (https://www.anthropic.com), official social media accounts (e.g., @anthropic on X/Twitter, LinkedIn, or YouTube), or through a verified spokesperson quoted in a credible news outlet (e.g., TechCrunch, The Verge, Reuters, Bloomberg), that explicitly references:
- The development or upcoming release of a new flagship model beyond Claude 4.x (e.g., 'Claude 5', 'next-generation model', 'successor to Claude 4', or similar phrasing);
- Or, internal progress toward a model clearly intended as the next major version in the Claude series (e.g., 'we are building the next version of Claude' or 'preparing for a major model release in 2025').

The statement must come from Anthropic or a named executive and not be speculative, third-party commentary, or user-generated content. References to minor updates (e.g., 'Claude 4.6') or agent-specific improvements (e.g., 'Claude Code enhancements') do not count.

If no such statement is published during the specified window, the question resolves No.

Fall-back criteria: If Anthropic’s blog or social media accounts become inaccessible during the resolution period, resolution will rely on consensus reporting from at least two credible tech news outlets (e.g., TechCrunch, The Verge, Bloomberg) confirming the existence and content of such a statement.

Delayed or ambiguous announcements (e.g., 'we’re working on something big' without model-specific context) do not qualify.

Primary source: https://www.anthropic.com/news
Secondary sources for verification: https://techcrunch.com, https://www.theverge.com, https://www.bloomberg.com, https://www.reuters.com
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of whether Anthropic is on track to release Claude 5 by the end of 2025. Given that the company has not yet announced any such model, a public signal of active development or imminent release within October 2025 would significantly increase the likelihood that Claude 5 is in final stages and on schedule. Conversely, silence during this period—especially after the recent launch of Sonnet 4.5—might suggest delays or a slower roadmap, reducing the probability of a year-end release. Because Anthropic has historically used official communications to manage expectations and signal progress, this observable event serves as a high-value crux for forecasters assessing the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: Anthropic publishes (Oct 1–31, 2025) an official blog post, press release, social media post, or verified spokesperson quote in credible outlet that explicitly references: (a) development or upcoming release of a model beyond Claude 4.x (e.g., 'Claude 5', 'next-generation model', 'successor to Claude 4'); OR (b) internal progress toward the next major version. Statement must come from Anthropic or named executive, not speculative/third-party. Minor updates (e.g., 'Claude 4.6') do not count. Key entities: Anthropic, named executives (Dario Amodei, Jared Kaplan, etc.). Timing: 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Anthropic Claude 5 announcement 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to find explicit Claude 5 references; 2) 'Anthropic next generation model flagship release 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to find next-gen model statements; 3) 'Anthropic Claude 5 OR next major version OR successor to Claude 4' (Oct 1–31) — variations; 4) 'Jared Kaplan Anthropic new Opus model year-end 2025 IBM' (Oct 1–31) — to find executive statements about upcoming models; 5) 'Anthropic Dario Amodei Claude 5 OR beyond Claude 4 OR next major model October 2025' — to find statements from top executives; 6) 'Anthropic Opus 4.5 OR Opus 5 OR Claude 5 new flagship model 2025' — to find specific model version references.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Jared Kaplan (Anthropic CSO) stated 'a new Opus version is in development, expected before year-end' — reported by Cryptopolitan (Oct 7, 2025) and Economic Times (Oct 7, 2025), in context of IBM-Anthropic partnership announcement. (2) Maginative article (Oct 15) citing 'an Anthropic spokesperson' saying 'a new Opus update expected by year-end or early 2026.' All other October 2025 Anthropic announcements are about: Claude Sonnet 4.5 (already released), Claude Haiku 4.5 (released Oct 15), Claude Skills feature, Claude Code expansion, Claude for Life Sciences, India expansion, etc. No references to 'Claude 5,' 'beyond Claude 4,' or 'next major version beyond Claude 4.x' found anywhere. Rejected events: All mentions of 'new Opus version' are referring to a next iteration within the Claude 4 Opus line (Opus 4.x), not a model beyond Claude 4.x. The Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 releases are Claude 4.x minor updates, explicitly excluded.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The most relevant candidate is Jared Kaplan's statement about 'a new Opus version in development, expected before year-end' per [Cryptopolitan](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/ibm-stock-surges-4-on-anthropic-ai/) and [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/ibm-stock-jumps-4-after-partnership-with-anthropics-claude-to-expand-ai-capabilities/articleshow/124366870.cms). HOWEVER, this does NOT meet the resolution criteria because: (a) 'A new Opus version' refers to an update within Claude 4.x (e.g., Opus 4.5), NOT a model 'beyond Claude 4.x'; (b) The resolution criteria explicitly excludes 'References to minor updates (e.g., "Claude 4.6")' — an Opus 4.x update would fall in this category; (c) Anthropic's model family at the time consists of Claude 4.x models (Opus 4.1, Sonnet 4, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5), and a 'new Opus version' is next in that family, not a Claude 5 or beyond Claude 4; (d) Neither the Cryptopolitan nor Economic Times article uses phrasing like 'Claude 5,' 'beyond Claude 4,' 'successor to Claude 4,' or 'next major version' — the criteria's required language. No other statement during October 2025 from Anthropic or its executives references a model beyond Claude 4.x.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Jared Kaplan's statement was reported on October 7, 2025, per Cryptopolitan and Economic Times. However, this statement does not satisfy the resolution criteria (see Step 4). No qualifying statement with an extractable timestamp was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple angles: (1) Searched for 'Claude 5' references — none found from Anthropic during October 2025; (2) Checked all Anthropic executive statements — Dario Amodei, Jared Kaplan, Mike Krieger all mentioned Claude 4.x models only; (3) The 'new Opus version' statement from Kaplan refers to Claude 4.x Opus updates, consistent with Anthropic's cadence of Opus 4.1 (Aug 2025), Sonnet 4.5 (Sep 2025), Haiku 4.5 (Oct 2025), suggesting 'new Opus' = Opus 4.5 or similar, not Claude 5; (4) Multiple articles confirm Anthropic's focus in October 2025 was on existing Claude 4.x products (Skills, Life Sciences, Code expansion, India/Korea offices); (5) No contradictory evidence found that Claude 5 was announced — the absence is consistent across all 40+ articles reviewed. The resolution criteria is unambiguous: 'beyond Claude 4.x' is required, and no such statement was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. During October 2025, Anthropic's only statement from a named executive about a forthcoming model was Jared Kaplan's reference to 'a new Opus version expected by year-end,' which refers to a Claude 4.x update (likely Opus 4.5), not a model 'beyond Claude 4.x' as required by the resolution criteria. No statement mentioning 'Claude 5,' 'next-generation model beyond Claude 4,' 'successor to Claude 4,' or equivalent language was found from Anthropic or its executives during the October 1–31, 2025 window. The window closed without any qualifying statement.

question: Will Russia capture Huliaipole by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the intersection between T-04-01 and Heroiv Ukrainy Vulytsia located in Huliaipole by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET.

The intersection station will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date, the market will resolve to “No”.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the intersection, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture the village of Solodke, located approximately 7 km north of Huliaipole, between November 23, 2025, and December 23, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Solodke is a village in Zaporizhzhia Oblast located approximately 7 kilometers north of Huliaipole, making it a strategically relevant location in the ongoing Russian offensive toward Huliaipole. Recent open-source intelligence indicates that Russian forces have made incremental gains in the northern approaches to Huliaipole. On November 10, 2025, DeepState reported that Russian forces had fully occupied Uspenivka and were in the process of absorbing Rivnopillia, with confirmed occupation of Solodke under verification. By November 12, DeepState noted that Solodke was under partial or full Russian control, suggesting ongoing consolidation in the area. The capture of Solodke would represent a significant step toward establishing a direct northern axis of advance on Huliaipole, reducing the defensive buffer for Ukrainian forces in the city. As of November 22, 2025, the Finnish OSINT group Black Bird assessed that Russia is employing a doctrine of reinforcing success in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, having captured over 15 villages since September, and may attempt to flank Huliaipole from the north while pinning down Ukrainian defenders from the east and south. The current status of Solodke remains ambiguous but leans toward partial Russian control, making its full formal capture a meaningful indicator of momentum toward Huliaipole.

Sources:
- DeepState report on Uspenivka and Solodke: https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-ato/3918220-deepstate-prognozu-zaporiga-zapocatili-uspenivku.html
- Black Bird OSINT assessment: https://kyivindependent.com/russia-likely-captured-over-15-villages-in-zaporizhzhia-obl-since-september-osint-group-says/
- Ukrainska Pravda on Russian advances: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/11/12/7543223/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-23 and 2025-12-23 (inclusive), credible open-source reporting confirms that Russian forces have captured the village of Solodke, located approximately 7 km north of Huliaipole in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. 'Capture' is defined as Russian forces establishing uncontested control over the settlement, with Ukrainian forces no longer holding any part of it, as evidenced by visual confirmation (e.g., geolocated imagery, drone footage), official claims corroborated by battlefield mapping, or consensus among at least two independent OSINT sources (e.g., DeepStateMap, ISW, Black Bird). The primary resolution source will be DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) and the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Ukraine Conflict Updates (https://www.understandingwar.org/). If both sources are unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting from at least two of the following outlets—Kyiv Independent, BBC Monitoring, or Reuters—will be used. Temporary incursions or contested control do not qualify; the village must be under stable Russian control by the end date. If Russian forces withdraw after capture, the question still resolves Yes. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No. Any data source discontinuation will trigger use of fallback sources as specified.
subquestions.rationale: The capture of Solodke is a geographically and operationally proximate indicator of Russian progress toward Huliaipole. Located just 7 km north, Solodke lies on a direct axis of advance and its capture would eliminate a key defensive node protecting Huliaipole’s northern flank. Recent reports suggest Russian forces are consolidating control in this area, and a confirmed capture of Solodke would signal both the capability and intent to continue advancing toward Huliaipole. Forecasters who believe Russia is gaining momentum in Zaporizhzhia Oblast would assign a higher probability to Solodke’s capture, which in turn increases the likelihood of Huliaipole’s capture by the ultimate question’s end date. Conversely, failure to capture Solodke by December 23 would suggest stalled momentum, providing meaningful evidence that Huliaipole may not fall by December 28. Thus, this subquestion serves as a high-value, time-sensitive crux for the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Russian forces establish uncontested control over Solodke (~7km north of Huliaipole, Zaporizhzhia Oblast) between 2025-11-23 and 2025-12-23 (inclusive). Observable evidence: DeepStateMap update marking Solodke as Russian-controlled, ISW confirmation, or consensus from at least two credible OSINT sources. Key entities: Solodke village, Polohy district, Zaporizhzhia Oblast; Russian forces; DeepState, ISW as primary sources.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Solodke village Huliaipole Russian forces capture Zaporizhzhia 2025' (general search, Nov 23–Dec 23); 2. 'Solodke Zaporizhzhia Oblast Russia Ukraine frontline control' (Nov 1–Dec 23); 3. 'Solodke captured Russian control December 2025 Zaporizhzhia'; 4. 'Solodke ISW DeepState Russian occupation November December 2025'; 5. 'Solodke DeepState ISW control December 2025 Huliaipole north'; 6. 'Russian Defense Ministry Solodke capture announcement 2025' (Nov 23–Dec 23).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates: (A) Russian Defense Ministry claim (Nov 14, 2025 — before window): RuMoD claimed Solodke was captured during the past week as part of a list of settlements including Novouspenivske, Nove, Solodke, Rybne. This is BEFORE the resolution window and was unverified/disputed by Ukraine. (B) Nov 10, 2025 (before window): DeepState reported 'confirmed occupation of Solodke under verification' — still unresolved, before window. (C) Nov 12, 2025 (before window): DeepState reported Solodke 'under partial or full Russian control' — contested. (D) Nov 13, 2025 (before window): DeepState reported advances 'near Solodke', with Ukrainian forces fighting in Solodke. (E) Nov 21-27, 2025 (within window): Ukrainian oblast governor reports Russian UAV and artillery strikes on Solodke — suggests contested status or Ukrainian control. (F) Dec 7, 2025 (within window): DeepState reports Russian forces 'advanced near Solodke' — 'advancing near' language suggests not yet captured. (G) Dec 9, 2025 (within window): Solodke listed among settlements still being attacked by Russian forces (872 attacks, including Solodke) — if under Russian control, Ukraine would not report incoming Russian attacks on it from their perspective. Candidates A-D are before the window. Candidates E-G suggest contested or Ukrainian status within the window. No explicit capture confirmation within the window from DeepState or ISW.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require: (1) capture confirmed between Nov 23–Dec 23, 2025; (2) visual confirmation or official claims corroborated by battlefield mapping; (3) consensus from at least two independent OSINT sources or DeepState/ISW specifically. The Dec 7, 2025 [DeepState report via Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/12/07/8010769/) states 'advanced near Solodke' — this is NOT a capture confirmation; 'advanced near' means the front moved closer but not that the village was taken. The ongoing Russian strikes on Solodke on Dec 9, 2025 [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/12/10/8011178/) are consistent with Solodke still being in the frontline area and potentially still under Ukrainian control or contested. No source explicitly states that Solodke was captured and under uncontested Russian control during the resolution window. The earlier Russian MoD claim (Nov 14) predates the window and was disputed. No DeepState or ISW confirmation of Solodke's capture within the window was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp of a qualifying capture event (within Nov 23–Dec 23, 2025) can be extracted. The Dec 7, 2025 DeepState report describes 'advances near Solodke,' not capture. No other source within the window explicitly states Solodke was captured and under uncontested Russian control.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying capture event was identified within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Ukraine's oblast governor reports Russian strikes on Solodke on Nov 27 and Dec 9, suggesting it was still in the combat zone and not under stable Russian control. (2) DeepState's Dec 7 language of 'advanced near' vs. 'occupied' is significant — DeepState uses 'occupied' when a settlement is captured (as seen for Rivnopillia, Yablukove, Kamianske, etc.). (3) The earlier Russian MoD claim of Solodke capture (Nov 14) predates the window and was contested by Ukrainian forces who reportedly cleared Solodke around Nov 9. (4) A Nov 12 DeepState report called Solodke 'under partial or full Russian control' — suggesting even before the window it was ambiguous. (5) No ISW report confirms Solodke as Russian-captured within the window. The evidence strongly suggests the question resolves No — Solodke was not confirmed as captured within the resolution window by the primary sources (DeepState, ISW).
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. The condition for Yes — explicit confirmation from DeepState or ISW (or two other credible sources) that Russian forces established uncontested control over Solodke between Nov 23–Dec 23, 2025 — was not met. Within the window: DeepState reported 'advances near Solodke' (Dec 7) rather than occupation; Ukrainian authorities reported Russian strikes hitting Solodke (Nov 27, Dec 9), suggesting contested status; no ISW report confirms capture. The earlier Russian MoD claim (Nov 14) predates the window and was disputed/unverified. question: Will Trump visit Gaza by Dec 31?

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump announce plans to visit Gaza during his Middle East trip between October 14, 2025, and November 13, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early October 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump has been actively involved in brokering a peace agreement between Israel and Hamas, with high-level diplomatic talks occurring in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt. Trump has already announced potential travel to the Middle East, including possible visits to Israel and Egypt, and has publicly stated he 'might visit Gaza soon' (October 8, 2025). His envoy, Steve Witkoff, visited a U.S.-Israel coordination site in northern Gaza on October 11, 2025, signaling deepening U.S. involvement in postwar stabilization (Newsweek). Trump is scheduled to address the Knesset in Israel and co-chair a summit in Egypt with regional leaders. While no official announcement of a Gaza visit has been made, his public statements and the momentum of the peace process suggest such a visit could be under consideration as a symbolic or diplomatic gesture. A presidential visit to Gaza would be highly significant—only Bill Clinton has done so (in 1998)—and would likely require extensive security and logistical planning, making a prior public announcement a necessary precursor. Given that Trump has not yet confirmed such a visit, an announcement during this period would be a strong indicator of intent and feasibility.

Sources:
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/trump-envoy-gaza-ceasefire-1948723
- EJPress: https://ejpress.org/israel-must-stop-bombing-gaza-immediately-hamas-ready-for-a-lasting-peace-trump-says/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13, Donald Trump makes a public statement—via official White House channels, a verified social media account (e.g., @POTUS on X.com), or a live press conference—announcing his intention or confirmed plans to visit the Gaza Strip. The statement must include explicit language indicating intent to visit Gaza (e.g., 'I will visit Gaza,' 'I plan to go to Gaza,' or 'My trip will include Gaza'). Vague or speculative remarks (e.g., 'I might go to Gaza' or 'It's a possibility') do not count toward resolution.

Resolution will be based on credible media reports from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, CNN, Al Jazeera) or an official statement from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or Trump’s verified social media account (https://twitter.com/POTUS). If no such announcement is made by the end date, the question resolves No.

If the announcement is made but later retracted or postponed beyond the resolution window, the question still resolves Yes as long as the announcement occurred within the timeframe. If the primary sources become unavailable, secondary sources such as archived versions via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org) will be used.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator of the ultimate outcome—whether Trump will actually visit Gaza by December 31, 2025. Given the security, diplomatic, and logistical complexity of a U.S. president visiting a war-affected area like Gaza, a formal announcement would signal serious intent and planning. Without such an announcement, the likelihood of an impromptu visit is extremely low. Therefore, the absence of an announcement during this critical window—when peace talks are ongoing and Trump is already traveling in the region—would significantly reduce the probability of the ultimate event occurring. Conversely, an announcement would increase confidence that the visit is being actively considered or scheduled, making this a high-value informational crux for forecasters.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Trump makes a public statement explicitly indicating intention to visit Gaza (e.g., 'I will visit Gaza') via official White House channels, verified social media, or live press conference. Statement must occur between Oct 14–Nov 13, 2025. Vague remarks ('I might go,' 'it's a possibility') do not qualify. Confirmed by at least two major news outlets or official sources.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: Trump's Time magazine interview conducted October 15, 2025 (published October 23, 2025), in which Trump stated 'Yeah, I will' in direct response to a question about visiting Gaza. Reported by TASS (Oct 23), New York Post (Oct 23), Times of Israel (Oct 23), AFP (Oct 23), and others. No earlier qualifying event found. Reported by: [New York Post](https://nypost.com/2025/10/23/us-news/trump-says-i-will-visit-gaza-calls-respect-for-president-most-important-factor-in-peace-deal/): 'Trump says I will visit Gaza' and confirmed the Time magazine interview published October 23, 2025. [AFP via Inquirer](https://globalnation.inquirer.net/296088/us-pressures-israel-on-west-bank-rubio-voices-confidence-in-gaza-truce): corroborates the October 15 interview published October 23. evidence.step8_final_decision: Trump explicitly stated 'Yeah, I will' in direct response to a question about visiting Gaza in a Time magazine interview conducted October 15, 2025 and published October 23, 2025 — within the Oct 14–Nov 13, 2025 resolution window. This constitutes explicit language indicating intent to visit Gaza, confirmed by multiple major news outlets (TASS, New York Post, Times of Israel, AFP). subquestions.question: Will Iran suspend cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) by restricting access to nuclear facilities or ending monitoring activities between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran has repeatedly signaled potential escalatory steps in response to the reactivation of UN sanctions via the 'snapback' mechanism by France, Germany, and the UK. Multiple Iranian lawmakers, including Hossein-Ali Haji-Deligani and Manouchehr Mottaki, have stated that withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) is being actively considered and that a draft bill for withdrawal is under preparation in parliament. As part of a broader three-part emergency plan, Iran may also suspend negotiations with the U.S. and European powers and end cooperation with the IAEA, including halting inspections and monitoring activities. According to Mehr News Agency and Tasnim News, such measures are framed as retaliatory actions if sanctions are reimposed. The IAEA has historically served as a key verification body for Iran’s nuclear activities, and a suspension of cooperation would represent a significant break from current compliance protocols, potentially signaling a prelude to formal NPT withdrawal. As of August 2025, Iran continues to allow some IAEA access, though tensions have increased following recent airstrikes on Iranian nuclear sites and stalled diplomatic talks.

Sources:
- Mehr News Agency: https://en.mehrnews.com/news/222128/Iran-s-parl-launches-emergency-plan-to-exit-NPT
- Tasnim News Agency: https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2025/08/29/3332229/Iran-s-Parliament-Drafts-Plan-to-Withdraw-from-NPT
- International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) - Iran Verification and Monitoring: https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/focus/iran
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, Iran suspends cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) by either: (1) formally announcing the restriction or termination of IAEA access to declared nuclear facilities; (2) actively denying IAEA inspectors access to monitored sites; or (3) ceasing the transmission of monitoring data from surveillance equipment (e.g., cameras, seals) installed under IAEA agreements. The suspension must be officially confirmed by either the IAEA or the Iranian government.

Resolution will be based on reports from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Board of Governors statements, official IAEA press releases, or credible, corroborated reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, or AFP) that confirm the suspension occurred within the specified timeframe.

If the Iranian government announces a suspension after the end date of 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No. In the event that the IAEA or other primary sources cease reporting on Iran’s compliance during this period, secondary sources such as the U.S. Department of State, Arms Control Association, or Federation of American Scientists will be used to determine resolution.

Primary source: IAEA Press Releases and Reports – https://www.iaea.org/newscenter
Secondary sources: Reuters – https://www.reuters.com, Associated Press – https://apnews.com
subquestions.rationale: A suspension of IAEA monitoring or inspection activities would be a significant escalatory step toward full withdrawal from the NPT, as it would break key verification obligations under the treaty. Historical precedent (e.g., Iran’s 2021 restriction of IAEA access) shows that such moves often precede broader treaty withdrawals or nuclear policy shifts. Given that Iranian lawmakers have explicitly linked NPT withdrawal to ending IAEA cooperation, observing this action within the next month provides strong evidence about the likelihood of formal NPT withdrawal by the end of 2025. It is a distinct, observable indicator that is not merely a rephrasing of the ultimate question, and its resolution is time-bound and verifiable using authoritative sources.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Iran formally announces restriction or termination of IAEA access to declared nuclear facilities; OR actively denies IAEA inspectors access to monitored sites; OR ceases transmission of monitoring data from surveillance equipment. Must be officially confirmed by IAEA or Iranian government. Window: 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Iran IAEA cooperation suspended nuclear facilities access 2025' — to find any suspension announcement. Query 2: 'Iran IAEA inspectors denied access nuclear monitoring September 2025' — to confirm access denial events. Query 3: 'Iran IAEA suspension cooperation September 21 2025 UN sanctions snapback' — to find SNSC announcement specifically. Query 4: 'Iran Supreme National Security Council IAEA suspension official announcement September 2025' — to confirm official government announcement. Query 5: 'IAEA confirmed Iran suspension nuclear monitoring access denied September October 2025' — to find IAEA-side confirmation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Sept 9-10 Cairo framework: Iran-IAEA signed cooperation document but Iran's FM explicitly stated 'no access is given to IAEA inspectors' — this is ambiguous as a suspension announcement (it describes existing state but was framed as a new cooperation framework). (2) Sept 20-21: Iran's SNSC formally announced via IRNA that E3's snapback activation 'will effectively suspend' cooperation with the IAEA — explicit formal government announcement of suspension. This is the primary qualifying event. (3) Sept 22-23: IAEA chief Grossi confirmed 'difficult juncture,' consistent with suspension. SNSC announcement rejected as ambiguous only for criterion (3) but clearly satisfies criterion (1) as a formal announcement of suspension.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The SNSC's statement 'Cooperation with the Agency will be suspended in connection with the actions of the European countries' [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2019311) is a formal announcement by the Iranian government of suspension of cooperation. The SNSC is Iran's highest security body; the statement was transmitted via state news agency IRNA. This satisfies criterion (1): 'formally announcing the restriction or termination of IAEA access to declared nuclear facilities.' Confirmed by: [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/21/iran-says-e3-move-to-trigger-sanctions-will-halt-cooperation-with-iaea), [RT](https://www.rt.com/news/625014-iran-halt-cooperation-un-nuclear-watchdog/), [CGTN](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2025-09-21/Iran-to-halt-cooperation-with-IAEA-after-UNSC-fails-to-lift-sanctions-1GQ7i4fzU8o/p.html), [spacewar.com/AFP](https://www.spacewar.com/afp/250920193015.im4fwd2d.html), [Hurriyet Daily News](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/iran-says-cooperation-with-iaea-suspended-213841) — well over two major outlets.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The SNSC announcement was dated September 20, 2025 (Hurriyet Daily News: 'Sept. 20'; CGTN: 'the following day' after Sept. 19 UNSC vote), with most other sources reporting September 21, 2025 as the publication date. The announcement itself was on 2025-09-20. Exact ISO 8601: 2025-09-20T00:00:00Z (the date the SNSC announced the suspension, with publication confirmed on 2025-09-21).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence found within the September 1–October 1 window. The June 2025 suspension predates the window. The Cairo agreement (Sept. 9-10) was a cooperation attempt, not a suspension announcement. The September 20-21 SNSC announcement is the first formal government declaration of suspension within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The September 9-10 Cairo framework could suggest Iran was cooperating, not suspending. However, even at Cairo, access was denied to Fordo and Natanz, and Iran's FM stated 'currently no access is given.' The SNSC's September 20-21 announcement is distinct from Cairo — it was a formal declaration following the UNSC vote. The IAEA chief's 'difficult juncture' comment (Sept. 22-23) is consistent with, not contradictory to, a suspension. No evidence found of the SNSC announcement being retracted within the window. Multiple corroborating sources (Al Jazeera, TASS, RT, CGTN, AFP-sourced, Hurriyet) all confirm the SNSC statement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Iran's Supreme National Security Council formally announced the suspension of IAEA cooperation on September 20-21, 2025, within the resolution window. The announcement was made via state news agency IRNA, satisfying the 'officially confirmed by the Iranian government' requirement. Multiple major international outlets (Al Jazeera, AFP, TASS, CGTN) corroborate this. The announcement explicitly states 'Cooperation with the Agency will be suspended,' directly satisfying resolution criterion (1). Resolution: YES.

subquestions.question: Will a tropical wave emerging from the west coast of Africa be designated as having at least a 40% chance of development into a tropical cyclone by the National Hurricane Center between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-11?
subquestions.background_information:
Tropical waves moving off the west coast of Africa are a primary source of Atlantic hurricane season activity, especially during the peak months of August and September. However, such waves can still contribute to storm formation into October. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) monitors these disturbances and assigns a probability of development over a 48-hour and 7-day window. A 40% or higher development chance indicates a significant likelihood of tropical cyclone formation, which increases the probability of additional named storms. As of August 31, 2025, the NHC was monitoring a tropical wave with a 30% chance of development (below the 40% threshold), suggesting that activity was present but not yet at a high-confidence level (Redding Record Searchlight, 2025). Given that the 2025 season has already seen at least one named storm (Hurricane Erin), and NOAA predicted 13–19 named storms for the season, continued African easterly wave activity in early October is a key indicator of whether the season will remain active enough to exceed 12 named storms. Monitoring NHC development probabilities provides an early signal of whether conditions are favorable for additional storm formation.

Sources:
- Redding Record Searchlight: https://www.redding.com/story/news/2025/08/31/national-hurricane-center-eyes-tropical-wave-in-atlantic-see-tracker/83625680007/
- National Hurricane Center: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/
- NOAA 2025 Hurricane Season Outlook: https://www.noaa.gov/media-release/noaa-predicts-above-normal-2025-atlantic-hurricane-season
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-11, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) issues a Tropical Weather Outlook (TWO) that designates a tropical wave emerging from the west coast of Africa as having a 'High' chance (≥40% probability) of development into a tropical cyclone within 48 hours or 7 days. The TWO must explicitly reference a system originating from the African coast and assign the ≥40% development chance during the specified window. The resolution will be based on the official NHC Tropical Weather Outlooks archived at: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2025/. If no such designation occurs during the period, the question resolves No. If the NHC discontinues publication of TWOs during the resolution window, the question will resolve based on the most recent publicly available data from the NHC website (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/) or, as a fallback, from the National Weather Service’s archived data at https://www.weather.gov/archive/. Events postponed beyond 2025-10-11 will not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The formation of named storms in the Atlantic, particularly in October, is often preceded by tropical waves off the west coast of Africa. A high development probability (≥40%) from the NHC indicates favorable atmospheric and oceanic conditions for tropical cyclone formation, which increases the likelihood of additional named storms. Since the ultimate question hinges on whether fewer than 12 named storms occur in the 2025 season, observing whether such high-probability systems emerge in early October serves as an early indicator of ongoing seasonal activity. If no such systems are identified, it suggests a declining likelihood of reaching or exceeding 12 named storms, thus providing valuable information to forecasters assessing the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: NHC issues a Tropical Weather Outlook (TWO) between Oct 1-11, 2025 assigning ≥40% probability of tropical cyclone development (within 48 hours OR 7 days) to a tropical wave explicitly originating from/emerging from the west coast of Africa. Observable evidence: NHC TWO documents or news reports citing the specific probability and African origin of the system.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'National Hurricane Center tropical wave Africa development chance October 2025' (to find general NHC monitoring reports) 2) 'NHC Tropical Weather Outlook African coast tropical cyclone October 2025' (to find direct TWO references) 3) 'Invest 95L Cape Verde tropical wave Africa NHC October 5 2025' (to confirm specific system identification) 4) 'NHC tropical wave Africa 50% 60% development October 4 2025 TWO' (to find earliest ≥40% occurrence) 5) 'NHC TWO tropical weather outlook October 4 2025 Africa wave 50% development' (to find exact timing)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (A) Oct 3 TWO: NHC raised odds of African tropical wave to 40% within 7 days (Orlando Sentinel: 'NHC increased the odds of a tropical wave off Africa developing into a tropical depression or storm to 40% within the next seven days'). (B) Oct 4 TWO: NHC assigned 50% chance to 'tropical wave between western Africa and the Cape Verde Islands' for 7-day development (WESH, News 4 Jax, Orlando Sentinel). Also 60% per WFLX Fox TV-29. (C) Oct 5 TWO: Invest 95L (same system, now designated) received 40% within 48 hours and 70% within 7 days (multiple sources). No earlier qualifying events found (Oct 1-2 articles show only 20% development chance for African wave). No candidate events were rejected — all clearly satisfy criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Exact criteria match confirmed: (1) System origin: The tropical wave is explicitly described as 'a tropical wave off Africa' (Orlando Sentinel, Oct 3), 'a tropical wave moving off the coast of Africa' (multiple Oct 4 sources), and 'a tropical wave originating off the coast of Africa' (FOX 13 Tampa Bay, Oct 6 for Invest 95L). (2) Development probability: ≥40% threshold met on Oct 3 (40% within 7 days per [Orlando Sentinel](https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2025/10/03/florida-under-new-tropical-threat-while-nhc-tracks-2-systems-plus-hurricane-imelda/)), Oct 4 (50% within 7 days per [WESH](https://www.wesh.com/article/florida-tropical-development-rain-all-weekend/68823344) and [News 4 Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/weather/2025/10/04/watching-the-tropics-two-systems-being-monitored-for-possible-development/)), and Oct 5 (40% within 48 hours per [WKMG](https://www.clickorlando.com/weather/2025/10/05/invest-95l-getting-better-organized-could-develop-this-week/) and [ArcaMax](https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3874877)). (3) NHC Tropical Weather Outlook: All reports reference official NHC TWO. (4) Timing: October 3-5, all within Oct 1-11 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying occurrence: The Orlando Sentinel article from Oct 3 references '40% within the next seven days' from the NHC TWO on October 3, 2025. WESH Oct 4 reports '50% chance' from 'between western Africa and the Cape Verde Islands.' The 8 a.m. TWO on October 3, 2025 appears to be when the ≥40% threshold was first crossed, as Oct 2 articles show only 20% and Oct 3 Orlando Sentinel reports 40%. Exact timestamp of NHC TWO: October 3, 2025 (8 a.m. EDT = 2025-10-03T12:00:00Z, though the article itself is dated Oct 3 without an exact publication time — the NHC issues TWOs at 2am, 8am, 2pm, 8pm EDT; the 8am EDT issuance = 12:00 UTC).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Searched for earlier qualifying events. Oct 2 reports (WESH, WKMG, NBC Miami, WOGX) all show only '20% chance of development over the next seven days' for the African tropical wave — below the 40% threshold. Oct 1 shows no African wave at ≥40%. Therefore, October 3, 2025 is confirmed as the FIRST occurrence of ≥40% development chance for an African tropical wave in the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Oct 3, 2025 articles show conflicting percentages (some say 30% per WFLA, some say 40% per Orlando Sentinel — these likely represent different TWO issuances during the same day, or different reporting of 7-day vs 48-hour probabilities). However, the Orlando Sentinel article explicitly states '40% within the next seven days' for the African wave on Oct 3. The Oct 4 WESH report from the 8 a.m. TWO October 4 explicitly states '50% chance' for the wave 'between western Africa and the Cape Verde Islands.' This is unambiguous and clearly ≥40%. The FOX 13 article explicitly describes Invest 95L as 'a tropical wave originating off the coast of Africa.' No contradictory evidence showing the wave did NOT originate from Africa exists. The resolution criteria asks about waves 'emerging from the west coast of Africa' — the Cape Verde Islands are just off the west coast of Africa, and all sources confirm the wave tracked off Africa's west coast.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = YES. The NHC issued Tropical Weather Outlooks between Oct 3-5, 2025 (within the Oct 1-11 window) designating a tropical wave emerging from the west coast of Africa as having ≥40% probability of development into a tropical cyclone within 7 days. The earliest qualifying occurrence was October 3, 2025 (40% per Orlando Sentinel referencing the NHC TWO). This was further confirmed on Oct 4 (50%) and Oct 5 (40% within 48 hours, 70% within 7 days for Invest 95L). The system was consistently described as originating from the African coast. All resolution criteria are met.

question: Will Trump announce a national housing emergency in 2025?
description:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump administration may declare a national housing emergency this fall to address high housing costs.(see: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/)

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration release a detailed policy proposal or executive order draft addressing the housing crisis, explicitly framed as preparation for a potential national emergency declaration, between November 2, 2025, and December 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the Trump administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall' to address high housing costs and limited supply, sparking speculation about imminent action (Reuters, 2025). Since then, multiple outlets have reported that the administration is evaluating options such as standardizing zoning codes, reducing closing costs, and granting tariff exemptions on construction materials—measures that could be implemented under emergency powers (Yahoo! Finance, 2025; Newsweek, 2025). While no formal declaration has been made, the administration has signaled urgency, particularly with the 2026 midterms approaching. Historically, the release of detailed policy drafts or executive order frameworks has preceded formal emergency declarations. For example, the draft executive order on immigration in 2017 was circulated weeks before the official emergency was declared. The existence of such a document would signal serious intent and bureaucratic momentum toward an actual declaration, making it a strong leading indicator.

Sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/
- Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-120000500.html
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/housing-market-tipping-point-trump-2025-1536328
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-02 and 2025-12-02, the Trump administration releases a detailed policy proposal, white paper, or draft executive order that explicitly frames housing affordability as a national crisis and outlines emergency-level actions under the National Emergencies Act (NEA), and is published through an official government channel (e.g., White House website, Treasury Department press release, Federal Register draft, or official social media account of a senior administration official).

The document must:
- Be authored or officially released by a federal agency or White House office;
- Mention 'national emergency,' 'emergency powers,' or 'NEA' in connection with housing;
- Include at least two specific policy actions that would require emergency authority (e.g., federal land use override, tariff suspension, or funding reallocation without congressional approval).

Resolution sources:
- White House official website: https://www.whitehouse.gov
- U.S. Department of the Treasury: https://home.treasury.gov
- Federal Register: https://www.federalregister.gov
- Official @POTUS or @ScottBessent Twitter/X accounts: https://twitter.com/POTUS, https://twitter.com/ScottBessent

If no such document is released during the specified period, the question resolves No. If the document is announced but not published by the end date, or if the source material becomes unavailable, the resolution will rely on archived versions via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/web/) or reputable news organizations with direct access to the document (e.g., AP, Reuters, Bloomberg).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong leading indicator because the release of a formal policy draft or executive order framework signals that the administration has moved beyond rhetorical consideration into active preparation for a national emergency declaration. Such internal coordination typically precedes a formal announcement by weeks. Given that the ultimate question hinges on whether Trump actually declares an emergency, evidence of bureaucratic momentum—especially through official channels—would significantly increase the likelihood of the ultimate outcome. Conversely, the absence of such a document by December 2 suggests that the administration is not advancing the plan, reducing the probability of a declaration by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: official document from federal agency/White House, mentioning 'national emergency,' 'emergency powers,' or 'NEA' in connection with housing, with at least two specific emergency-authority policy actions, published between 2025-11-02 and 2025-12-02 via official government channel.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) Trump housing crisis national emergency declaration executive order 2025; 2) Bessent national housing emergency declaration; 3) White House housing emergency NEA National Emergencies Act draft; 4) Trump housing emergency executive order zoning federal land federal register; 5) Bessent predicted national housing emergency declaration 2025
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key findings: (a) Washington Examiner Nov 11 article states 'Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent previously predicted a national housing emergency declaration, though no timeline was provided' — this is a verbal prediction, not an official document. (b) Daily Caller Nov 10 opinion piece by ACG Analytics researchers calls on Trump to declare National Housing Emergency — third-party advocacy, not official. (c) Trump administration working on 50-year mortgages — not framed as emergency action under NEA. (d) Various HUD policy changes related to homelessness programs — not framed as NEA emergency. (e) Trump's 'emergency price relief' EO was from January 2025 (before window). No candidate events meet criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No document found that: (1) was authored/officially released by a federal agency or White House office during the window; (2) mentions 'national emergency,' 'emergency powers,' or 'NEA' in connection with housing; AND (3) includes at least two specific policy actions requiring emergency authority. The Bessent prediction was verbal commentary on a TV show, not an official document. The ACG Analytics op-ed was a private advocacy piece. HUD's CoC program changes did not invoke emergency authority.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying document timestamp could be extracted because no qualifying document was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple searches covering the full Nov 2 - Dec 2, 2025 window found no evidence of an official government publication meeting the resolution criteria. The closest item — Bessent's prediction of a housing emergency declaration — is a verbal statement on CNN (Nov 2) and referenced in news coverage, not an official policy document. Trump's affordability-related actions in this period focused on 50-year mortgages, HUD CoC program changes, and food tariff rollbacks — none framed explicitly under NEA/emergency powers for housing.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require an official government document meeting specific requirements. No such document was published during the November 2 - December 2, 2025 window. The question resolves No. The window closed without the condition being met.

question: Will Trump meet with Putin by December 31?
description:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in person at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson near Anchorage, Alaska, for a summit focused on potential peace terms in Ukraine. 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Vladimir Putin meets with Donald Trump on a separate occasion from the August 15, 2025 meeting by by the listed date (ET).  Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Encounters that are part of, or a continuation of, the August 15 meeting will not qualify, even if they occur on a different day (e.g. August 16).

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both Putin and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. State Department or Kremlin announce plans for a follow-up meeting between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a summit in Anchorage, Alaska, focused on potential peace terms in the Ukraine war. The meeting lasted approximately three hours and was described by both leaders as 'productive' and 'constructive,' but no formal agreement was reached. During and after the summit, both sides indicated openness to further dialogue. Putin suggested a potential follow-up meeting in Moscow, to which Trump responded ambiguously, saying, 'People aren't going to like that' (Salon, 2025). Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov emphasized that details were being withheld to protect the peace process, calling the talks 'meaningful' and 'very constructive' (TASS, 2025). Given the lack of a concrete agreement, the scheduling of a follow-up meeting would signal continued diplomatic momentum and a mutual interest in advancing negotiations—key prerequisites for another in-person encounter. As of September 1, 2025, no official plans for a second meeting have been announced. The likelihood of such an announcement in the immediate aftermath of the summit serves as a strong early indicator of whether another meeting is being seriously pursued.

Sources:
- Salon: No deal in Alaska: Trump, Putin talk peace, with no resolution - https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-trump-putin-talk-peace-with-no-resolution/
- TASS: Kremlin says it keeps details of Putin-Trump summit under wraps to protect peace process - https://tass.com/politics/1825673
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either the U.S. State Department, the Kremlin, or both issue an official public statement announcing plans for a follow-up meeting between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. The announcement must specify intent to meet again, either by naming a date, location, or timeframe (e.g., 'the leaders agreed to meet again in the fall'), or by confirming that planning is underway (e.g., 'working-level discussions are ongoing to schedule a second summit').

Resolution will be based on credible, publicly available statements from:
- The official website of the U.S. State Department: https://www.state.gov/
- The official website of the President of the Russian Federation (Kremlin): http://en.kremlin.ru/
- Or, if neither publishes a relevant statement, secondary confirmation via two or more reputable news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, or Bloomberg) reporting the same announcement with attribution to official sources.

If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If the announcement is made but later retracted or postponed beyond the resolution window, it still counts as Yes if it was publicly issued during the specified period. If the source material becomes unavailable, resolution will rely on archived versions via the Internet Archive (https://archive.org) or equivalent trusted repositories.
subquestions.rationale: The announcement of plans for a follow-up meeting is a strong leading indicator of whether another Trump-Putin meeting is likely. Without such signals, the probability of a second in-person encounter diminishes significantly due to political, logistical, and diplomatic constraints. Given that the August 15 meeting ended without a deal but with expressions of goodwill, the next observable step in the diplomatic process would be scheduling further talks. This subquestion captures that momentum—or lack thereof—early, providing high informational value for forecasting the ultimate question. It avoids simply restating the ultimate question by focusing on an intermediate, observable action (official announcement) rather than the event itself (a meeting).

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between September 1–October 1, 2025, either the U.S. State Department OR the Kremlin (or both) must issue an official public statement announcing plans for a follow-up Trump-Putin meeting. The announcement must specify intent to meet again by naming: (a) a date, (b) a location, OR (c) a timeframe; OR confirming that planning is underway (e.g., 'working-level discussions are ongoing to schedule a second summit'). Observable evidence: Official statement on state.gov, en.kremlin.ru, or two+ reputable outlets reporting same announcement with official attribution.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Putin follow-up meeting announcement State Department Kremlin 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) — to find official announcements; 2) 'Trump Putin second summit planned scheduled 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) — to find confirmation; 3) 'Kremlin official announcement Trump Putin second meeting September 2025' — to find Kremlin statement; 4) 'State Department Kremlin confirm plan Trump Putin meeting date location fall 2025' — to find official confirmation; 5) 'Trump Putin meeting confirmed scheduled October November 2025' (Sep 25–Oct 1) — to find late-window announcements; 6) 'Peskov Trump invitation Moscow Putin meeting planned confirmed' (Sep 20–Oct 1) — to assess Kremlin stance; 7) 'Vance Russia refused meetings Trump bilateral September 2025' (Sep 25–Oct 1) — to check contradictory signals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Sep 5: Peskov says meeting 'could' happen — conditional, not an announcement of plans. REJECTED: does not meet threshold. (2) Sep 17: Peskov explicitly says 'no plans' for Trump-Putin meeting. REJECTED as qualifying Yes event; actually negates Yes. (3) Sep 19: Russian Deputy FM Ryabkov says Kremlin 'aims' for fall US talks, but 'White House and Kremlin have not officially confirmed reports of a new meeting date and venue.' REJECTED: no official confirmation. (4) Sep 28: Peskov says Putin's invitation to Trump is 'not shelved' — open invitation, not a confirmed plan. REJECTED: No date, location, or confirmed timeframe. (5) Sep 28: Vance says Russia 'refused' bilateral and trilateral meetings with US. REJECTS any Yes possibility. (6) Sep 29 qoshe/DW article: describes Trump-Putin meeting 'scheduled next Friday in Alaska' — but this appears to be a misdated or confused reference to the August 15 Alaska summit, given no other sources corroborate a new Alaska meeting announcement during late September; context and other simultaneous evidence strongly suggest this refers to the original August meeting. REJECTED as evidence of new announcement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event exactly satisfies the resolution criteria. The Kremlin's statements during September 2025 oscillated between conditional openness (Peskov, Sep 5: 'could' meet; Sep 28: invitation 'not shelved') and explicit denial of plans (Peskov, Sep 17: 'no high-level meetings are planned'). Vance explicitly stated Russia 'refused' bilateral meetings with Trump ([RT](https://www.rt.com/news/625523-vance-russia-refused-meetings/) Sep 28). The uawire.org article (Sep 19) explicitly notes 'The White House and the Kremlin have not officially confirmed the reports of a new meeting date and venue.' The qoshe.com/DW article (Sep 29) about a meeting 'next Friday in Alaska' appears inconsistent with all contemporaneous reporting and likely refers to the original August 15 summit, not a new announcement. No State Department statement confirming a follow-up Trump-Putin meeting was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying announcement with a precise, reliable timestamp was found within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence of an official announcement with date/location/timeframe was found at any point in the window. The absence of a qualifying event is consistent across all search results.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence examined: (1) Multiple Kremlin statements express openness to a future Trump-Putin meeting but none constitute official 'plans' with date/location/timeframe as required. (2) Sep 17 Peskov explicitly says no meeting planned — directly contradicts any positive signals from Sep 5. (3) Sep 28 Vance says Russia 'refused' bilateral/trilateral meetings, consistent with no plans being announced. (4) Sep 30 Trump 'still hopes' for Putin-Zelensky meeting (not a Trump-Putin bilateral), indicating no Trump-Putin meeting was confirmed. (5) The qoshe.com/DW article dated Sep 29 mentioning a meeting 'next Friday in Alaska' is an anomaly; other evidence does not corroborate a new Trump-Putin Alaska meeting announcement during this window, and the article appears to be either misdated or referring to the original August summit. The preponderance of evidence strongly supports no qualifying announcement having been made.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Throughout the September 1–October 1, 2025 window, no official statement from the U.S. State Department or the Kremlin was issued announcing confirmed plans for a follow-up Trump-Putin meeting with a specific date, location, or timeframe. Kremlin statements ranged from conditional openness (Sep 5) to explicit denial of plans (Sep 17) to an unaccepted standing invitation (Sep 28). U.S. officials (Vance, Sep 28) stated Russia had 'refused' bilateral meetings. No second Trump-Putin summit was officially scheduled or announced during this period. Resolution: No.

subquestions.question: Will Turkey publicly issue a formal diplomatic condemnation of an Israeli military operation in Syria or the broader Middle East between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Turkey and Israel have experienced fluctuating relations in recent years, particularly due to their opposing stances on Gaza, Syria, and regional influence. As of mid-2025, tensions have been elevated due to Israeli military operations in Syria—particularly those near Druze communities—and in Yemen, which Ankara views as part of a broader regional escalation. Turkish officials, including Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, have previously warned of the risks of direct military encounters in Syrian airspace and have called for deconfliction mechanisms (Forbes, 2025). Despite indirect communication facilitated by Azerbaijan, no formal coordination agreement has been publicly confirmed. Diplomatic condemnations by Turkey of Israeli actions have historically preceded or accompanied heightened tensions; for example, Turkey recalled its ambassador from Israel following the 2021 Gaza conflict. A formal condemnation—defined as an official statement issued by the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs or by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan—would signal deteriorating bilateral relations and could increase the risk of miscalculation or military friction in shared operational theaters such as Syria.

Recent developments, including Israel’s August 28, 2025 strike on Sanaa, have been framed as indirect warnings to regional actors, including Turkey (The Times of Israel, 2025). Given Turkey’s strategic partnership with Qatar and its support for Palestinian causes, Ankara is likely to respond diplomatically to any perceived escalation by Israel that threatens regional stability or Muslim populations. Such a response could serve as a leading indicator of deteriorating military restraint between the two nations.

Sources:
- Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidhambling/2025/05/12/the-risk-of-israeli-turkish-mock-dogfights-over-syria/
- The Times of Israel: https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/israel-strikes-sanaa-a-geopolitical-turning-point-beyond-yemen/
- Turkish Minute: https://turkishminute.com/2025/05/19/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs or President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan issues a formal public statement that explicitly condemns an Israeli military operation in Syria or another Middle Eastern country (e.g., Yemen, Iran, Lebanon) as aggressive, disproportionate, or illegal under international law.

A 'formal public statement' includes:
- A press release published on the official website of the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mfa.gov.tr)
- A speech or tweet from President Erdoğan that contains explicit condemnation (via https://www.tccb.gov.tr or his verified X account: https://twitter.com/RT_Erdogan)
- A statement delivered by Turkey’s ambassador to the UN or another international body that is officially reported by credible news outlets such as Reuters, AP, or BBC.

The statement must clearly refer to a specific Israeli military action (e.g., airstrikes, naval operations) and use language indicating official disapproval (e.g., 'condemn', 'strongly protest', 'categorically reject').

Resolution sources:
- Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://www.mfa.gov.tr
- Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye: https://www.tccb.gov.tr
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com

If no such statement is issued during the resolution window, the question resolves No. If the source material becomes unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of at least two credible, independent media reports confirming the absence or presence of such a statement.
subquestions.rationale: A formal diplomatic condemnation by Turkey of an Israeli military operation would indicate escalating bilateral tensions and a breakdown in diplomatic restraint, increasing the likelihood of miscalculation or direct military encounters in overlapping operational zones such as Syria. While not a military clash itself, such a condemnation serves as a meaningful early warning signal that the political environment is deteriorating, reducing the threshold for future military confrontation. Given ongoing Israeli operations in Syria and Yemen, and Turkey’s vocal regional posture, this indicator is both timely and sensitive to shifts in the relationship that could precede armed conflict.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the Turkish MFA or President Erdoğan must issue a formal public statement explicitly condemning a specific Israeli military operation in Syria or another Middle Eastern country (e.g., Yemen, Iran, Lebanon, Qatar), using language of official disapproval ('condemn', 'strongly protest', 'categorically reject'). Observable evidence: press release on mfa.gov.tr, speech/statement from Erdoğan, or official statements reported by Reuters, AP, BBC, or equivalent credible outlets. Key entities: Turkish MFA, Erdoğan. Timing: within resolution window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Turkey condemns Israel military operation Syria September 2025' — to find MFA/Erdoğan condemnations of Israeli ops in Syria. 2) 'Erdogan condemnation Israel airstrike Middle East 2025' — broader search for Erdoğan's condemnations. 3) 'Turkey foreign ministry condemns Israel airstrikes Syria September 2025 formal statement' — MFA-specific search. 4) 'Erdogan UNGA speech condemn Israel Syria Lebanon Yemen September 23 2025' — UNGA speech search. 5) 'Turkey condemns Israel attack Qatar Doha September 9 2025' — specific Qatar incident. 6) 'Turkey MFA statement condemn Israel September 16 2025 Gaza ground offensive' — Gaza ground offensive search. 7) 'Turkey condemns Israel September 1 2 3 2025 formal statement MFA' — earliest occurrence check.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) September 9, 2025: Turkish MFA issued formal statement condemning Israeli airstrike in Doha, Qatar — reported by Anadolu Agency, Qatar News Agency, Middle East Eye, Daily Sabah, Devdiscourse. (2) September 16, 2025: Turkish MFA condemned Israel's ground offensive in Gaza City as 'new stage in genocidal plans' — reported by Anadolu Agency, Hurriyet Daily News. (3) September 23, 2025: Erdoğan at UNGA condemned Israeli strikes in Syria, Iran, Yemen, Lebanon, and Qatar — reported by Times of Israel, India Today, Hurriyet Daily News. (4) September 2, 2025: Turkish parliament resolution condemning Israeli occupation — rejected as it comes from the Grand National Assembly, not MFA or Erdoğan, and does not reference a specific Israeli military operation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The September 9, 2025 statement by the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs EXACTLY matches the resolution criteria: (a) It is from the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (qualifying source per resolution criteria); (b) It condemns a specific Israeli military action — the airstrike on Doha, Qatar on September 9, 2025; (c) Qatar qualifies as 'another Middle Eastern country'; (d) The statement uses explicit condemnation language: 'This is clear evidence that Israel has adopted expansionist policies in the region and embraces terrorism as a state policy' and called it 'a despicable violation of its sovereignty and national security'; (e) Reported by multiple credible outlets including Anadolu Agency [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/turkiye-condemns-israeli-strike-on-hamas-delegation-in-qatar-during-ceasefire-talks/3682729], Qatar News Agency [https://qna.org.qa/en/news/news-details?id=turkiye-condemns-israeli-attack-on-residential-compound-in-doha&date=9/09/2025], Middle East Eye [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/turkey-israel-embraces-terrorism-state-policy], and Daily Sabah [https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/diplomacy/turkiye-denounces-israeli-strike-on-doha-as-genocide-driven-aggression]. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan separately 'categorically rejected any aggression that threatens the security and safety of the State of Qatar' per Qatar News Agency on September 14.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 9, 2025. One source (Devdiscourse) timestamps it at 'September 09 2025 15:01'. Multiple other sources confirm same date. This is within the resolution window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying MFA/Erdoğan statement found within window. The September 2 parliamentary resolution (from Grand National Assembly, not MFA or Erdoğan) does not qualify as it is from a different institution and references general occupation practices rather than a specific Israeli military operation. evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. Multiple independent credible sources (Anadolu Agency, Qatar News Agency, Middle East Eye, Daily Sabah, Devdiscourse, The Peninsula) all confirm the September 9, 2025 Turkish MFA formal condemnation. The condemnation references a specific Israeli military action (the September 9 airstrike on Doha). Qatar is explicitly named in the resolution criteria as an example ('another Middle Eastern country'). The language used ('despicable violation,' 'expansionist policies,' 'terrorism as a state policy') clearly constitutes official disapproval. A follow-up confirmation was also found in Foreign Minister Fidan's statement on September 14 at the Arab-Islamic ministerial meeting in Doha, where he 'strongly condemned the Israeli attack, and categorically rejected any aggression' (per Qatar News Agency).
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves YES. On September 9, 2025, the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal public statement explicitly condemning Israel's airstrike on Doha, Qatar — a Middle Eastern country explicitly named as an example in the resolution criteria. The statement used language of explicit condemnation ('despicable violation of its sovereignty,' 'clear evidence that Israel has adopted expansionist policies in the region and embraces terrorism as a state policy') and referred to a specific Israeli military action (airstrike on Doha targeting Hamas delegation). This was reported by multiple credible outlets including Anadolu Agency, Qatar News Agency, Middle East Eye, and Daily Sabah. This is the first qualifying occurrence within the window. All evidence requirements are satisfied.

The occurrence of these talks is therefore a strong indicator of whether the planned Hungary meeting is progressing beyond rhetorical statements toward concrete diplomatic planning.
